sourceDefinition: is originally A^abawN , (S, Msb, K,) as is shown by the first of its dual forms and of its pl. forms mentioned below; (S, Msb;) and signifies A father [in the ordinary sense: and also as meaning (assumed tropical:) an ancestor ]: (M:) as also ↓ A^abFA , a dial. var., (M, K,) the same in the nom. and accus. and gen. cases, like qafFA : (M:) and A^ab~N is a dial. var. of the same, [the second letter being doubled to compensate for the w suppressed, as is the case in A^ax~N , (TA voce A^axN )] but is rare. (Msb.) Accord. to the dial. commonly obtaining, when you use it as a prefixed noun, you decline it with the letters w and A and Y , saying, h`*aAA^abuwhu [ This is his father ], (Msb,) and A^abuwka [ thy father ]; (M;) and raA^ayotu A^abaAhu [ I saw his father ]; and mararotu biA^abiyhi [ I passed by his father ]: (Msb:) but accord. to one dial., you say, h`*aA A^abaAhu , (Msb:) and A^abaAka ; (M;) and raA^ayotu A^abaAhu ; and mararotu biA^abaAhu : (Msb:) and accord. to one dial., which is the rarest of all, it is defective in every case, like yadN and damN ; (Msb;) and [thus] you say, h`*aA A^abuwka [&c.]. (M.) The dual is A^abawaAni , (S, M, Msb,) meaning [ two fathers, and] father and mother; and some say A^abaAni : (S, M:) you say, humaAA^abawaAhu , meaning They two are his father and mother; and in poetry you may say, humaA A^abaAhu ; and in like manner, raA^ayotu A^abayohi [ I saw his father and mother ], (T,) and A^abayoka [ thy father and mother ]; (S;) but the usual, or chaste, form is raA^ayotu A^abawayohi . (T.) The pl. is A=baA='N , (T, S, M, Msb, K,) the best form, (T,) and A^abuwna , (T, S, M, K,) and A^ubuw~N (M, K, [in the CK AlAabowN is erroneously put for AlA^ubuw~N ,]) and A^ubuw~apN , (Lh, T, S, M, K, *) like EumuwmapN and xuw^uwlapN : (T, S:) you say, h`w^ulaA='i A^abuwkumo , meaning A=baAw^ukumo [ These are your fathers ]; (T;) and hence, in the Kur [ii. 127], accord. to one reading, waA_il`ha A^abiyka A_ibr`hiyma waA_isom`Eiyla waA_isoH`qa [ And the God of thy fathers, Abraham and Ishmael and Isaac ], meaning the pl. of A^bN , i. e. A^abiynaka , of which the n is suppressed because the noun is prefixed [to the pronoun]; (S;) and some of the Arabs say, A^abuw~atunaA A^akoramu AlA=baA='i [ Our fathers are the most generous of fathers ]. (T.) The dim. is ↓ A^ub~aY~N ; originally A^ubayowN , with the final radical letter restored. (Msb.) ― -b2- maA yadoriY lahu mino A^abK , and maA A^abN , mean- ing He knows not who is his father, and what is his father, are sayings mentioned by Lh on the authority of Ks. (M.) ― -b3- laA A^abaA lika , (T, S, M, K, &c.,) [accord. to the dial. of him who says A^abFA instead of A^abN ,] as also laA A^aba laka , and laA A^abaAka , (S, K,) [the last, accord. to J, because the l (meaning the l in lk in the preceding phrases) is as though it were redundant, but he seems not to have known the dial. var. A^abFA , and I rather think that laA A^abaAka , is for laA A^aboqaY A@ll~`hu A^abaAka , or the like,] and laA A^abaka , (Mbr, Sgh, K,) and laAba laka , (K,) which is for laA A^aba laka , (M,) means Thou art, in my estimation, one deserving of its being said to him, Mayest thou have no father! it is used in the manner of a proverb, is of frequent occurrence in poetry, (M,) is said to him who has a father and to him who has not a father, and is an imprecation as to the meaning, of necessity, though enunciative as to the letter; (M, K;) and hence the saying of Jereer, yaA tayomu tayoma EadiY~K laA A^abaA lakumo [ O Teym, Teym of 'Ades, may ye have no father! ]; which is the strongest evidence of its being a proverb, and not having a literal meaning; for all of [the tribe of] Teym could not have one father, but all of them were fit objects of imprecation and rough speech: (M:) it is an expression of praise: (S:) [i. e.] it is an imprecation against him to whom it is addressed, not, however, said with the desire of its having effect, but on an occasion of intense love, like laA A^um~a laka , &c.: (Har p. 165:) and sometimes in dispraise, like laA A^um~a laka : and in wonder, like lil~hi dar~uka : (TA:) or, as A Heyth says, on the authority of Aboo-Sa'eed Ed- Dareer, it expresses the utmost degree of reviling; [meaning Thou hast no known father; ] and laA A^um~a laka expresses reviling also, but means Thou hast no free, or ingenuous, mother: (Meyd in Har p. 165: [see A^um~a :]) sometimes it means Strive, or exert thyself, in thine affair; for he who has a father relies upon him in some circumstances of his case: (TA:) accord. to Kh, it means Thou hast none to stand thee in stead of thyself: (ISh, TA:) Fr says that it is a phrase used by the Arabs [parenthetically, i.e.,] to divide their speech: (TA:) [thus, for instance,] Zufar Ibn-El-Hárith says, A^ariyniY silaAHiY laA A^abaA laka A_in~aniY A^araY AlHaroba laA tazodaAdu A_il~aA tamaAdiyaA [ Show thou me my weapons: ( mayest thou have no father! or thou hast no father: &c.:) verily I see the war, or battle, increases not save in perseverance ]. (TA.) [Aboo-'Alee, as cited in the M, observes that the A (meaning the final A ) in A^abaA , in the phrase laA A^abaA laka , indicates that it is a prefixed noun, and determinate; whereas the l in lk together with the government exercised upon the noun by lA indicates that it is, on the contrary, indeterminate, and separate from what follows it: but it seems that he was unacquainted with the dial. var. A^ab~aA ; for laA A^abaA laka in the dial. of him who uses the form A^ab~aA instead of A^abN is the same grammatically as laA A^aba laka in the dial. of him who uses the form A^abN .] Suleymán Ibn-'Abd-El-Melik heard an Arab of the desert, in a year of drought, say, A^anozilo EalayonaA Algayova laA A^abaA laka , and Suleymán put the best construction upon it, [as though it meant, Send down upon us rain: Thou hast no father ], and said, I testify that He hath no father nor female companion nor offspring. (TA.) They say also, in paying honour [to a person], laA A^aba li$aAniy^ika , and laA A^aba li$aAniy^ika , (TA,) i. e. May thy hater have no father! or, accord. to ISk, each is a metonymical expression for laA A^abaA laka . (S in art. $nA^ , q. v.) ― -b4- One also says, on the occasion of an occurrence that is approved and commended, by way of expressing wonder and praise, lal~ihi A^abuwka , meaning To God, purely, is attributable [ the excellence of ] thy father, seeing that he begat thee a generous son, and produced the like of thee! (TA;) [or to God be attributed ( the excellence of ) thy father! ] it means that to God [alone] belongs the power to create the like of this man [to whom it relates], from whom has proceeded this wonderful action. (Har p. 44.) ― -b5- And hiYa binotu A^abiyhaA , meaning She resembles her father in strength of mind, or spirit, and sharpness of disposition, and in hastening, or striving to be first, to do things: said of Hafsah, by 'Áïsheh. (TA.) ― -b6- biA^abiY , (TA,) or biA^abiY A^anota , (T in art. bA^ ,) [said to a person,] means [ fudiyta biA^abiY Mayest thou be ransomed with my father! (see the next sentence but one;) or] A^afodiyka biA^abiY [ I will ransom thee with my father ]; (T ubi suprà;) or A^anota mafodiY~N biA^abiY Thou art, or shalt be, ransomed with my father ]; or fadayutuka biA^abiY [ I have in my heart ransomed thee, or I would ransom thee, with my father ]; the b being dependent upon a word suppressed, which, accord. to some, is a [pass. participial] noun, and accord. to others, a verb; and this word is suppressed because of the frequent usage of the phrase. (TA.) You say also, biA^abiY A^anota wa A^um~iY [ With my father mayest thou be ransomed, and with my mother! ]. (TA.) And biA^abiY mano wadadt~uhu , i. e. fudiYa biA^abiY mano wadadt~uhu [ May he whom I love be ransomed with my father! ], meaning may he [ my father ] be made a ransom for him [ whom I love ]! (El-Wáhidee on the Deewán of El-Mutanebbee, in De Sacy's Chrest. Arabe, sec. ed. vol. iii. p. 35 of the Arabic text.) Sometimes they change the Y into A : a poet says, waqado zaEamuwA A^an~iY jaziEotu EalayohimaA wahalo jazaEN A^ano qulotu waA biA^abaA humaA [ And they have asserted that I have become impatient on account of them two: but is it an evidence of impatience that I said, Alas, with my father may they two be ransomed? ]; meaning waA biA^abiY humaA . (S.) And some of the Arabs used to say, waA biA^abaA A^anota [ Alas, with my father mayest thou be ransomed! ]: this, says AM, being like yaA wayolataA for yaA wayolatiY ; as also yaA bayobaA , with the hemzeh changed into Y , originally yaA biA^abaA , meaning yaAbiA^abiY : and hence what is related, in a trad., of Umm- 'Ateeyeh; that she used not to mention the Prophet without saying, biyabaA [for biA^abi huwa ]. (TA in art. bA^ .) A woman said, yaA biA^abiY A^anota wa yaA fawoqa Albiyabo [ O thou to whom I would say, With my father mayest thou be ransomed! and O thou who art above him to whom I would address the saying, With my father mayest thou be ransomed! ]; respecting which Fr observes that the two words [ bi and A^ab ] are made as one [by prefixing the article] because of their frequent occurrence; (S;) and Aboo-'Alee says that the Y in biyab is substituted for ' , not necessarily; but ISk quotes the words as commencing with yaA biyabaA , which is the right reading, in order that this expression may agree with Albiy^abo , which is derived from it: EtTebreezee, however, relates Abu-l-'Alà's reciting the words as ending with Albiy^abo ; saying that this is compounded from the phrase biA^abiy , and that therefore the ' is preserved. (TA.) [See also the first paragraph in art. bA^ .] ― -b7- You say also, yaA A^abati [meaning O my father ], (S, M, K,) as in yaA A^abati AfoEalo [ O my father, do thou such a thing]; (S;) and yaA A^abata ; (S, M, K;) and yaAA^abatu ; (Z in the Ksh xii. 4;) and yaA A^abaho (S, M, K) when you pause after it. (S, M.) The p , [here written t ,] (Kh, M,) the sign of the fem. gender, (S, Z,) is substituted for the [pronominal] affix Y , (Kh, S, M, Z,) as in yaAA^um~ati ; (S;) and is like the p in EamapN and xaAlapN , as is shown by your saying, in pausing, yaA A^abahN , like as you say, yaA xaAlapN : (Kh, M:) the annexing of the fem. t to a masc. noun in this case is allowable, like as it is in HamaAmapN *akarN and $aApN *akarN and rajulN raboEapN and galaAmN yafaEapN : its being made a substitute for the affix Y is allowable because each of these is an augmentative added at the end of a noun: and the kesreh is the same that is in the phrase yaA A^abiY : (Z ubi suprà:) the t does not fall from Ab in the phrase yaA A^abati when there is no pause after it, though it [sometimes] does from A^um~ in the like phrase in that case, because the former word, being of [only] two letters, is as though it were defective. (S.) yaA A^abata is for yaA A^abataA , (Aboo-'Othmán El-Mázinee, S, * M, [the latter expression mentioned also in the K, but not as being the original of the former,]) the A [and h ] being suppressed; (the same Aboo- 'Othmán and M;) or for yaA A^abataA , the A being suppressed, like as the Y is in yaA gulaAmi ; or it may be after the manner of yaAA^abiYa . (Z ubi suprà.) yaA A^abatu is thus pronounced after the usual manner of a noun ending with the fem. p , without regard to the fact that the t is in the former a substitute for the suffix Y . (Z ubi suprà.) yaA A^abaho is said in a case of pause, except in the Kur-án, in which, in this case, you say, yaA A^abaho , following the written text; and some of the Arabs pronounce the fem. p , in a case of pause, t [in other instances], thus saying, yaA TaloHatu . (S.) yaA A^abaAhu is also said; (M, K;) though scarcely ever. (M.) A poet uses the expression yaA A^abaAta , for yaA A^abataAho : (S, M:) IB says that this is used only by poetic license, in a case of necessity in verse. (TA.) ― -b8- A^abN is tropically applied to signify (tropical:) A grandfather, or any ancestor. (Msb.) ― -b9- It is also applied to signify (assumed tropical:) A paternal uncle; as in the Kur ii. 127, quoted before. (M.) ― -b10- [It is also (like A^um~ and Aibon and binot ) prefixed to nouns of various significations. Most of the compounds thus formed will be found explained in the arts. to which belong the nouns that occupy the second place. The following are among the more common, and are therefore here mentioned, as exs. of different kinds.] ― -b11- A^abuw AlmaroA^api (assumed tropical:) The woman's husband: (Ibn-Habeeb, M:) it is said in the TS that AlA^abu , in certain of the dials., signifies the husband: MF deems this meaning strange. (TA.) A^abuw AlmavowaY (assumed tropical:) The master of the dwelling, or of the place of abode: (TA:) and (assumed tropical:) the guest. (K in art. vwY .) A^abuw AlA^aDoyaAfi (assumed tropical:) The very hospitable man. (TA.) ― -b12- A^abuw AlHaArivi (assumed tropical:) The lion. (TA.) A^abuw jaEodapa (assumed tropical:) The wolf. (TA.) A^abuw AlHuSayoni (assumed tropical:) The fox. (TA.) ― -b13- A^abuw jaAbir (assumed tropical:) Bread. (S and K in art. jbr .) ― -b14- A^abuw maAlikK (assumed tropical:) Extreme old age: (TA:) and (assumed tropical:) hunger. (MF in art. jbr .)

(M.) ― -b3- laA A^abaA lika , (T, S, M, K, &c.,) [accord. to the dial. of him who says A^abFA instead of A^abN ,] as also laA A^aba laka , and laA A^abaAka , (S, K,) [the last, accord. to J, because the l (meaning the l in lk in the preceding phrases) is as though it were redundant, but he seems not to have known the dial. var. A^abFA , and I rather think that laA A^abaAka , is for laA A^aboqaY A@ll~`hu A^abaAka , or the like,] and laA A^abaka , (Mbr, Sgh, K,) and laAba laka , (K,) which is for laA A^aba laka , (M,) means Thou art, in my estimation, one deserving of its being said to him, Mayest thou have no father! it is used in the manner of a proverb, is of frequent occurrence in poetry, (M,) is said to him who has a father and to him who has not a father, and is an imprecation as to the meaning, of necessity, though enunciative as to the letter; (M, K;) and hence the saying of Jereer, yaA tayomu tayoma EadiY~K laA A^abaA lakumo [ O Teym, Teym of 'Ades, may ye have no father! ]; which is the strongest evidence of its being a proverb, and not having a literal meaning; for all of [the tribe of] Teym could not have one father, but all of them were fit objects of imprecation and rough speech: (M:) it is an expression of praise: (S:) [i. e.] it is an imprecation against him to whom it is addressed, not, however, said with the desire of its having effect, but on an occasion of intense love, like laA A^um~a laka , &c.: (Har p. 165:) and sometimes in dispraise, like laA A^um~a laka : and in wonder, like lil~hi dar~uka : (TA:) or, as A Heyth says, on the authority of Aboo-Sa'eed Ed- Dareer, it expresses the utmost degree of reviling; [meaning Thou hast no known father; ] and laA A^um~a laka expresses reviling also, but means Thou hast no free, or ingenuous, mother: (Meyd in Har p. 165: [see A^um~a :]) sometimes it means Strive, or exert thyself, in thine affair; for he who has a father relies upon him in some circumstances of his case: (TA:) accord. to Kh, it means Thou hast none to stand thee in stead of thyself: (ISh, TA:) Fr says that it is a phrase used by the Arabs [parenthetically, i.e.,] to divide their speech: (TA:) [thus, for instance,] Zufar Ibn-El-Hárith says, A^ariyniY silaAHiY laA A^abaA laka A_in~aniY A^araY AlHaroba laA tazodaAdu A_il~aA tamaAdiyaA [ Show thou me my weapons: ( mayest thou have no father! or thou hast no father: &c.:) verily I see the war, or battle, increases not save in perseverance ]. (TA.) [Aboo-'Alee, as cited in the M, observes that the A (meaning the final A ) in A^abaA , in the phrase laA A^abaA laka , indicates that it is a prefixed noun, and determinate; whereas the l in lk together with the government exercised upon the noun by lA indicates that it is, on the contrary, indeterminate, and separate from what follows it: but it seems that he was unacquainted with the dial. var. A^ab~aA ; for laA A^abaA laka in the dial. of him who uses the form A^ab~aA instead of A^abN is the same grammatically as laA A^aba laka in the dial. of him who uses the form A^abN .] Suleymán Ibn-'Abd-El-Melik heard an Arab of the desert, in a year of drought, say, A^anozilo EalayonaA Algayova laA A^abaA laka , and Suleymán put the best construction upon it, [as though it meant, Send down upon us rain: Thou hast no father ], and said, I testify that He hath no father nor female companion nor offspring. (TA.) They say also, in paying honour [to a person], laA A^aba li$aAniy^ika , and laA A^aba li$aAniy^ika , (TA,) i. e. May thy hater have no father! or, accord. to ISk, each is a metonymical expression for laA A^abaA laka . (S in art. $nA^ , q. v.) ― -b4- One also says, on the occasion of an occurrence that is approved and commended, by way of expressing wonder and praise, lal~ihi A^abuwka , meaning To God, purely, is attributable [ the excellence of ] thy father, seeing that he begat thee a generous son, and produced the like of thee! (TA;) [or to God be attributed ( the excellence of ) thy father! ] it means that to God [alone] belongs the power to create the like of this man [to whom it relates], from whom has proceeded this wonderful action. (Har p. 44.) ― -b5- And hiYa binotu A^abiyhaA , meaning She resembles her father in strength of mind, or spirit, and sharpness of disposition, and in hastening, or striving to be first, to do things: said of Hafsah, by 'Áïsheh. (TA.) ― -b6- biA^abiY , (TA,) or biA^abiY A^anota , (T in art. bA^ ,) [said to a person,] means [ fudiyta biA^abiY Mayest thou be ransomed with my father! (see the next sentence but one;) or] A^afodiyka biA^abiY [ I will ransom thee with my father ]; (T ubi suprà;) or A^anota mafodiY~N biA^abiY Thou art, or shalt be, ransomed with my father ]; or fadayutuka biA^abiY [ I have in my heart ransomed thee, or I would ransom thee, with my father ]; the b being dependent upon a word suppressed, which, accord. to some, is a [pass. participial] noun, and accord. to others, a verb; and this word is suppressed because of the frequent usage of the phrase. (TA.) You say also, biA^abiY A^anota wa A^um~iY [ With my father mayest thou be ransomed, and with my mother! ]. (TA.) And biA^abiY mano wadadt~uhu , i. e. fudiYa biA^abiY mano wadadt~uhu [ May he whom I love be ransomed with my father! ], meaning may he [ my father ] be made a ransom for him [ whom I love ]! (El-Wáhidee on the Deewán of El-Mutanebbee, in De Sacy's Chrest. Arabe, sec. ed. vol. iii. p. 35 of the Arabic text.) Sometimes they change the Y into A : a poet says, waqado zaEamuwA A^an~iY jaziEotu EalayohimaA wahalo jazaEN A^ano qulotu waA biA^abaA humaA [ And they have asserted that I have become impatient on account of them two: but is it an evidence of impatience that I said, Alas, with my father may they two be ransomed? ]; meaning waA biA^abiY humaA . (S.) And some of the Arabs used to say, waA biA^abaA A^anota [ Alas, with my father mayest thou be ransomed! ]: this, says AM, being like yaA wayolataA for yaA wayolatiY ; as also yaA bayobaA , with the hemzeh changed into Y , originally yaA biA^abaA , meaning yaAbiA^abiY : and hence what is related, in a trad., of Umm- 'Ateeyeh; that she used not to mention the Prophet without saying, biyabaA [for biA^abi huwa ]. (TA in art. bA^ .) A woman said, yaA biA^abiY A^anota wa yaA fawoqa Albiyabo [ O thou to whom I would say, With my father mayest thou be ransomed! and O thou who art above him to whom I would address the saying, With my father mayest thou be ransomed! ]; respecting which Fr observes that the two words [ bi and A^ab ] are made as one [by prefixing the article] because of their frequent occurrence; (S;) and Aboo-'Alee says that the Y in biyab is substituted for ' , not necessarily; but ISk quotes the words as commencing with yaA biyabaA , which is the right reading, in order that this expression may agree with Albiy^abo , which is derived from it: EtTebreezee, however, relates Abu-l-'Alà's reciting the words as ending with Albiy^abo ; saying that this is compounded from the phrase biA^abiy , and that therefore the ' is preserved. (TA.) [See also the first paragraph in art. bA^ .] ― -b7- You say also, yaA A^abati [meaning O my father ], (S, M, K,) as in yaA A^abati AfoEalo [ O my father, do thou such a thing]; (S;) and yaA A^abata ; (S, M, K;) and yaAA^abatu ; (Z in the Ksh xii. 4;) and yaA A^abaho (S, M, K) when you pause after it. (S, M.) The p , [here written t ,] (Kh, M,) the sign of the fem. gender, (S, Z,) is substituted for the [pronominal] affix Y , (Kh, S, M, Z,) as in yaAA^um~ati ; (S;) and is like the p in EamapN and xaAlapN , as is shown by your saying, in pausing, yaA A^abahN , like as you say, yaA xaAlapN : (Kh, M:) the annexing of the fem. t to a masc. noun in this case is allowable, like as it is in HamaAmapN *akarN and $aApN *akarN and rajulN raboEapN and galaAmN yafaEapN : its being made a substitute for the affix Y is allowable because each of these is an augmentative added at the end of a noun: and the kesreh is the same that is in the phrase yaA A^abiY : (Z ubi suprà:) the t does not fall from Ab in the phrase yaA A^abati when there is no pause after it, though it [sometimes] does from A^um~ in the like phrase in that case, because the former word, being of [only] two letters, is as though it were defective. (S.) yaA A^abata is for yaA A^abataA , (Aboo-'Othmán El-Mázinee, S, * M, [the latter expression mentioned also in the K, but not as being the original of the former,]) the A [and h ] being suppressed; (the same Aboo- 'Othmán and M;) or for yaA A^abataA , the A being suppressed, like as the Y is in yaA gulaAmi ; or it may be after the manner of yaAA^abiYa . (Z ubi suprà.) yaA A^abatu is thus pronounced after the usual manner of a noun ending with the fem. p , without regard to the fact that the t is in the former a substitute for the suffix Y . (Z ubi suprà.) yaA A^abaho is said in a case of pause, except in the Kur-án, in which, in this case, you say, yaA A^abaho , following the written text; and some of the Arabs pronounce the fem. p , in a case of pause, t [in other instances], thus saying, yaA TaloHatu . (S.) yaA A^abaAhu is also said; (M, K;) though scarcely ever. (M.) A poet uses the expression yaA A^abaAta , for yaA A^abataAho : (S, M:) IB says that this is used only by poetic license, in a case of necessity in verse. (TA.) ― -b8- A^abN is tropically applied to signify (tropical:) A grandfather, or any ancestor. (Msb.) ― -b9- It is also applied to signify (assumed tropical:) A paternal uncle; as in the Kur ii. 127, quoted before. (M.) ― -b10- [It is also (like A^um~ and Aibon and binot ) prefixed to nouns of various significations. Most of the compounds thus formed will be found explained in the arts. to which belong the nouns that occupy the second place. The following are among the more common, and are therefore here mentioned, as exs. of different kinds.] ― -b11- A^abuw AlmaroA^api (assumed tropical:) The woman's husband: (Ibn-Habeeb, M:) it is said in the TS that AlA^abu , in certain of the dials., signifies the husband: MF deems this meaning strange. (TA.) A^abuw AlmavowaY (assumed tropical:) The master of the dwelling, or of the place of abode: (TA:) and (assumed tropical:) the guest. (K in art. vwY .) A^abuw AlA^aDoyaAfi (assumed tropical:) The very hospitable man. (TA.) ― -b12- A^abuw AlHaArivi (assumed tropical:) The lion. (TA.) A^abuw jaEodapa (assumed tropical:) The wolf. (TA.) A^abuw AlHuSayoni (assumed tropical:) The fox. (TA.) ― -b13- A^abuw jaAbir (assumed tropical:) Bread. (S and K in art. jbr .) ― -b14- A^abuw maAlikK (assumed tropical:) Extreme old age: (TA:) and (assumed tropical:) hunger. (MF in art. jbr .)

sourceDefinition: , (S, A, L, &c.,) in the first pers. of which, A^axa*otu , [and the like,] the * is generally changed into t , and incorporated into the [augmentative] t , [but in pronunciation only, for one writes A^axa*t~u and the like,] aor. , imperative xu*o , originally A@w^oxu*o , (S, L,) which latter form sometimes occurs, [but with w in the place of w^o when the A is pronounced with damm,] (TA,) inf. n. A^axo*N (S, L, Msb, K, &c.) and taA^oxaA*N , (S, L, K,) the latter having an intensive signification; (MF;) and waxa*a is a dial. var., as mentioned by Ibn-Umm-Kásim and others on the authority of AHei; (MF in art. tx* ;) He took; he took with his hand; he took hold of; (S, A, L, Msb, K;) a thing. (S, L.) You say, xu*i AlxiTaAma and xu*o biAlxiTaAma Take thou, or take thou with thy hand, or take thou hold of, the nose-rein of the camel: (S, L, Msb:) the b in the latter phrase being redundant. (Msb.) [And A^axa*a biyadihi , lit. He took his hand, or arm; meaning (assumed tropical:) he aided, or assisted, him: a phrase of frequent occurrence.] And A^axa*a EalaYyadi fulaAnK (assumed tropical:) He prevented, restrained, or withheld, such a one from doing that which he desired; as though he laid hold upon his hand, or arm: (L:) and A^axa*a EalaY yadihi duwna maA yuriyudhu [signifies the same]. (K in art. lgd .) ― -b2- Also, inf. n. A^axo*N , He took, or received; contr. of A^aEoTay . (L.) [Hence,] A^axa*a Eanohu , (assumed tropical:) He received from him traditions, and the like. (TA passim.) ― -b3- (assumed tropical:) [ He took, or derived, or deduced, a word, a phrase, and a meaning.] ― -b4- (tropical:) He took, received, or admitted, willingly, or with approbation; he accepted. (B, MF.) So in the Kur [vii. 198], xu*i AlEafowa (tropical:) [ Take thou willingly, or accept thou, superfluous property, or such as is easily spared by others]. (MF.) So too in the same [iii. 75], wa A^axa*t~umo Ealay *`likumo A_iSoriY (tropical:) [ And do ye accept my covenant to that effect? ]. (B.) [And in the phrases, A^axa*onaA miyvaAqakumo biAlEamali bimaA fiy Alt~awoAraApi , (Jel ii. 60,) and Ealay AlEam~li bmA fy AltwArp , (Idem ii. 87,) (assumed tropical:) We accepted your covenant to do according to what is in the Book of the Law revealed to Moses. ] xu*o Eanoka [is elliptical, and] means xu*o maA A^aquwlu wadaE Eanoka Al$~aka wAlmirA='a (assumed tropical:) [ Accept thou what I say, and dismiss from thee doubt and obstinate disputation ]. (S, L.) ― -b5- He took a thing to, or for, himself; took possession of it; got, or acquired, it; syn. HaAza ; (Z, Er-Rághib, B;) which, accord. to Z and Er-Rághib and others, is the primary signification; (MF;) and HaS~ala . (B.) [See also 8.] ― -b6- [ He took and kept; ] he retained; he detained: as in the Kur [xii. 78], faxu*o A^aHadanaA makaAnahu [ Therefore retain thou one of us in his stead ]. (B.) ― -b7- [ He took, as meaning he took away. Hence,] A^axa*a minohu Als~ayoru Journeying, or travel, took from him strength; ( Alquw~apa being understood;) weakened him. (Har p. 529.) And A^axa*a mina Al$~aAribi , (Mgh,) and mina Al$~aEari , (Msb,) He clipped, or cut off from, (Mgh, Msb,) the mustache, (Mgh,) and the hair. (Msb.) ― -b8- He, or it, took by force; or seized: (B:) (assumed tropical:) he, or it, overcame, overpowered, or subdued: said by some to be the primary signification. (MF.) [See also A^axa*ahu Ealow~aA , &c., in art. Elw : and A^axa*ahu mino fawoqu , &c., in art. fwq .] It is said in the Kur [ii. 256], laA taA^oxu*uhu sinapi wa laA nawomN (assumed tropical:) Neither drowsiness nor sleep shall seize [or overcome ] Him. (B.) [And you say, A^axa*atohu riEodapN (assumed tropical:) A tremour seized, took, affected, or influenced, him. And A^axa*ahu baTonuhu (assumed tropical:) His belly affected him with a desire to evacuate it. ] You say also, A^axa*a fiyhi Al$~araAbu (assumed tropical:) The wine affected him, or influenced him, so that he became intoxicated. (TA in art. vml .) And A^axa*a Alr~aA^osa (Msb in art. swr , &c.) and A^axa*a biAlr~aA^osi (K in art. HmY , &c.) (assumed tropical:) [ It had an overpowering influence upon the head ]; meaning wine. (Msb, K.) And A^axa*a biAlHaloqi [ It (food, &c.) choked ]. (IAar in art. n$b in the TA, and S in art. b$E , &c.) And laA yaA^oxu*u fiyhi qawolu qaAy^ilK (assumed tropical:) [ Nothing that any one may say will have any power, or effect, or influence, upon him ]; meaning that he obeyeth no one. (L in art. lyt .) ― -b9- He took captive. (L, Msb, B.) So in the Kur [ix. 5], faA@qotuluwA A@lmu$orikiyna Hayovu wajadt~umuwhumo waxu*uwhumo [ Then slay ye the believers in a plurality of gods wherever, or whenever, ye find them, and take them captives ]. (Bd, L, B.) ― -b10- See also 2, in three places. ― -b11- He gained the mastery over a person, and killed, or slew, him; (Zj, L;) as also ↓ A=xa*a : (L:) or simply, (assumed tropical:) he killed, or slew. (B.) It is said in the Kur [xl. 5], waham~ato k~ulu A^um~apK birasuwlihimo liyaA^oxu*uwhu , meaning [ And every nation hath purposed against their apostle ] that they might gain the mastery over him, and slay him; (Zj, L;) or (assumed tropical:) that they might slay him. (B.) ― -b12- (assumed tropical:) He (God, Msb) destroyed a person: (Msb, MF:) and (assumed tropical:) extirpated, or exterminated. (MF.) faA^axa*ahumu A@ll~`hu bi*unuwbihimo [in the Kur iii. 9 and xl. 22] means But God destroyed them for their sins. (Jel.) ― -b13- (tropical:) He punished, or chastised; (L, Msb, B, K, MF;) as also ↓ A=xa*a : (L, Msb, MF:) as in the phrases, A^axa*ahu bi*anobihi (Msb, K *) and bihi ↓ A=xa*ahu , inf. n. of the latter muw^aAxa*apN , (S, L, Msb, K,) (tropical:) he punished, or chastised, him for his sin, or offence: (Msb:) and A^uxi*a bi*anobihi means (assumed tropical:) he was restrained and requited and punished for his sin, or offence: (L:) or, accord. to some, A^axa*a signifies he extirpated, or exterminated; and ↓ A=x* he punished, or chastised, without extirpating, or exterminating. (MF.) [For ↓ A=x* ,] some say waAxa*a , (S, L,) which is not allowable, (K,) accord. to some; but accord. to others, it is a chaste form; (MF;) of the dial. of El-Yemen, and used by certain of the seven readers [of the Kur-án] in the instance of laA yuwaAxi*ukumu A@ll~`hu [ii. 225 and v. 91]; and the inf. N. in that dial. Is muwaAxa*apN , and the imperative is waAxi*o . (Msb.) ― -b14- (tropical:) He made a violent assault upon a person, and wounded him much. (K, TA.) [You say also, A^axa*ahu bilisaAnihi , meaning (assumed tropical:) He assailed him with his tongue; vituperated him; spoke against him. ] ― -b15- [ He took, took to, or adopted. ] You say, A^axa*a A^axa*ahumo and A_ixo*ahumo &c.: see A^axo*N , below. And A^axa*a fiY Tariyqi ka*aA [ He took such a road ]: and A^axa*a Eano yamiynihi A^awo yasaArihi [ he took the way by, or on, the right of him, or it, or the left of him, or it ]. (S in art. nZr .) [And A^axa*a biAlHazomi , and fiy AlHazomi , (the former the more common, the latter occurring in art. HwT in the K,) (assumed tropical:) He took the course prescribed by prudence, discretion, precaution, or good judgment; he used precaution: and, like A^axa*a biAlv~iqahi , (assumed tropical:) he took the sure course in his affair.] And A^axa*a Hi*orahu (assumed tropical:) He took care; became cautious, or vigilant. (Bd in iv. 73 and 103.) [And A^axa*a bimaA qaAla fulaAnN (assumed tropical:) He took to, or adopted and followed, or adhered to, what such a one said: see Har p. 367; where it is said that Ax* when thus used is made trans. by means of b because it implies the meaning of ta$ab~ava .] ― -b16- He took to, set about, began, or commenced; as in the saying, A^axa*a yafoEalu ka*aA He took to, set about, began, or commenced, doing such a thing; in which case, accord. to Sb, Ax* is one of those verbs which do not admit of one's putting the act. part. n. in the place of the verb which is its enunciative: [i. e., one may not say faAEilFA in the place of yfEl in the phrase above:] and as in A^axa*a fiY ka*aA He began, commenced, or entered upon, such a thing. (L.) ― -b17- [It is used in a variety of other phrases, in which the primary meaning is more or less apparent; and several of these will be found explained with other words occurring therein. The following instances may be here added.] ― -b18- TariyqN yaA^oxu*u fiY ramolapK [ A road leading into, or through, a tract of sand ]. (K in art. frz .) And A^axa*a bihimu AlT~ariyqu fiY gayori AlmaHaj~api [ The road lead them otherwise than in the beaten track ]. (T * and A in art. bhrj .) ― -b19- maA A^axa*atoka EayoniY muno*u HiynK (assumed tropical:) My eye hath not seen thee for some time; like maAZafiratoka . (T in art. Zfr .) And maA fiy AlHaY~i A^aHadN taA^oxu*uhu Eayoniy [explained to me by Ibr D as meaning (assumed tropical:) There is not in the tribe any one whom my eye regards as worthy of notice or respect by reason of his greatness therein]. (TA in art. jhr .) ― -b20- A^axa*otu Einodahu yadaY , and maEorwfAF : see 8. -A2- A^axi*a , aor. , inf. n. A^axa*N , (S, L, K,) He (a young camel) suffered heaviness of the stomach, and indigestion, from the milk: (S:) or became disordered in his belly, and affected with heaviness of the stomach, and indigestion, from taking much milk. (L.) ― -b2- He (a camel, L, K, or a sheep or goat, L) became affected by madness, or demoniacal possession; (K;) or by what resembled that. (L.) ― -b3- A^axi*ato Eayonuhu , aor. , inf. n. A^axa*N , His eye became affected by inflammation, pain, and swelling, or ophthalmia. (Ibn-Es-Seed, L, K. *) -A3- A^axu*a , aor. , inf. n. A^uxuw*apN , It (milk) was, or became, sour. (K.) [See A=xi*N .]

HSr : [in the CK, incorrectly, Aaxa*at and Alquluwbu :]) and Ax* biqalobihi [ He, or it, captivated his heart; or] he [or it ] pleased him, or excited his admiration. (TA in art. Alh .) -A2- A^x~* All~abana , inf. n. as above, He made the milk sour. (K.) [See A=xi*N .]

sourceDefinition: [written with the disjunctive alif Aiytaxa*a ] occurs in its original form; and is changed into A@t~axa*a [with the disjunctive alif Ait~axa*a ]; this being of the measure AftEl from A^axo*u , the [radical] ' being softened, and changed into t , and incorporated [into the augmentative t ]: hence, when it had come to be much used in the form of AftEl [thus changed], they imagined the [former] t to be a radical letter [unchanged], and formed from it a verb of the measure faEila , aor. yafoEalu ; saying, taxi*a , aor. yatoxa*u , (S, L, Msb, *) inf. n. taxa*N and taxo*N : (Msb:) and ↓ A@sotaxa*a [written with the disjunctive alif Aisotaxa*a ], of which exs. will be found below, is also used for At~x* ; one of the two t s being changed into s , like as s is changed into t in sit~N [for sidosN ]: or Astx* may be of the measure AstfEl from taxi*a ; one of the two t s being suppressed; after the manner of those who say Zalotu for Zalilotu : (S, L:) and IAth says that At~x* , in like manner, is of the measure AftEl from taxi*a ; not from A^axa*a : (L and K in art. tx* :) but IAth is not one who should contradict J, whose opinion on this point is corroborated by the fact that they say A@t~azara from A_izaArN , and A@t~amana from A^amonN , and A@t~ahala from A^aholN ; and there are other instances of the same kind: or, accord. to some, At~x* is from waxa*a , a dial. var. of A^axa*a , and is originally Aiwotaxa*a . (MF.) [The various significations of At~x* and taxi*a and Astx* will be here given under one head.] ― -b2- You say, A_iy^otaxa*uwA fiY AlqitaAli , (S, L, K, *) and fY AlHarobi , (Msb,) with two hemzehs, (S, L, K,) or, correctly, A_iytaxa*uwA , with one hemzeh, [or Aiytaxa*uwA ,] as two hemzehs cannot occur together in one word, (marginal note in a copy of the S,) [but in a case of wasl, the first hemzeh being suppressed, the second remains unchanged,] They took, or seized, ( A^axa*uwA ,) one another (S, L, Msb, K) in fight, (S, L,) and in war; (Msb;) and so Ait~axa*uwA . A^axa*a , (K in art. tx* , and B and TA in the present art.,) as meaning He took a thing to, or for, himself; took possession of it; got, or acquired, it; syn. HaAza and HaS~ala . (B, TA.) Some read, [in the Kur, xviii. 76,] lataxi*ota Ealayohi A^ajorAF [ Thou mightest assuredly have taken for thyself a recompense for it ]: (S, L, K in art. tx* , and TA in the present art.:) this is the reading of Mujáhid, (Fr, TA,) and is authorized by I'Ab, and is that of Aboo-'Amr Ibn-El-'Alà and AZ, and so it is written in the model-copy of the Kur, and so the readers [in general] read: (AM, L, TA:) so read Ibn-Ketheer and the Basrees; he and Yaakoob and Hafs pronouncing the * ; the others incorporating it [into the t ]: (Bd:) some read lAA@t~axa*t~a ; (L and K in art. tx* ;) but these read at variance with the scripture. And taxi*a , aor. , inf. n. taxa*N and taxo*N , also signifies He gained, acquired, or earned, wealth, (L, and Msb in arts. Ax* and tx* ,) or a thing. (Msb.) ― -b4- Ealayohimo yadFA ↓ Astx* and Einodahumo signify alike, i. q. At~x* [ He did to them a benefit, or favour; as though he earned one for himself in prospect, making it to be incumbent on them as a debt to him]: (ISh:) and Ait~axa*otu Einodahu maEorwfFA means [in like manner, as also Endh mErwfA ↓ A^axa*otu , and yad~aA , (and Ait~axa*a fiyhi HusonAF has a similar meaning; see Kur xviii. 85;)] I did to him a benefit, or favour; syn. sourceDefinition: inf. n. of A^axa*a , q. v. ― -b2- (assumed tropical:) A way, or manner, of life; as also ↓ A_ixo*N . (S, L, K.) You say, *ahaba banuw fulaAnK wamano A^axa*a A^axo*ahumo , (S, L, K, *) and ↓ A_ixo*ahumo , (L, K,) the former of the dial. of Temeem, and the latter of the dial. of El-Hijáz, (TA,) meaning (assumed tropical:) The sons of such a one went away, or passed away, and those who took to their way of life, (S, L, K,) and adopted their manners, or dispositions: (K:) and mano A^axa*a A^axo*uhumo and ↓ A_ixo*uhumo , and mano A^axa*a A^axo*uhumo [in the CK Aaxo*uhumo ] and ↓ A_ixo*uhumo , signify [virtually] the same: (K:) or mano A^axa*ahu A^axo*uhumo and ↓ A_ixo*uhumo signify [properly] mano A^axa*ahu A^axo*uhumo wasiyratuhumo [ those whom their way of life took, or influenced ]. (ISk, S L.) One says also, A@sotuEomila fulaAnN Eala Al$~aAmi ↓ wamaA A^axa*a A_ixo*ahu , with kesr, meaning (assumed tropical:) [ Such a one was appointed prefect over Syria, ] and he did not take to that good way of life which it was incumbent on him to adopt: you should not say A^axo*ahu : (AA, S, L:) or it means and what was adjacent to it: (Fr, L:) or, accord. to the Wá'ee, one says, in this case, ↓ wamaA A^axa*a A_ixo*ahu and A^axo*uhu and ↓ A^uxo*uhu , with kesr and fet-h and damm [to the hemzeh, and with the * marfooah, as in instances before]. (Et-Tedmuree, MF.) One also says, ↓ lawo kunota min~aA laA^axa*t~a biA_xo*inaA , (S, L,) with kesr to the A , (L,) [in a copy of the S biA^axo*inaA , which seems to be also allowable, accord. to the dial. of Temeem,] meaning Wert thou of us, then thou hadst taken to, or wouldst take to, our manners, or dispositions, and fashion, (S, L,) and garb, and way of life. (L.) The words of the poet, falawo kunotumo mun~aA A^axa*onaA biA_ixo*ikumo IAar explains as meaning And were ye of us, we had caught and restored to you your camels: but no other says so. (L.) ― -b3- nujuwmu AlA^axo*i The Mansions of the Moon; (S, L, K;) also called nujuwmu AlA^anowaA='N ; (L; [see art. nw' ;]) called by the former appellation because the moon every night enters ( yaA^oxu*u fiY ) one of those mansions: (S, L:) or the stars which are cast at those [ devils ] who listen by stealth [ to the conversations of the angels ]: (L, K:) but the former explanation is the more correct. (L.) ― -b4- See also A_ixaA*o .

sourceDefinition: and ↓ A_ixaA*apN A pool of water left by a torrent: pl. A^uxu*N : (AO, K:) both signify the same: (L:) or ↓ A_ixaA*apN signifies a thing like a pool of water left by a torrent; and A_ixaA*N is its pl. [or a coll. gen. n.]; and the pl. of this latter is A^uxu*N , like as kutubN is pl. of kitaAbN , and sometimes it is contracted into A^uxo*N : (S, L:) the like of this is said by Aboo-'Adnán: (L:) and A_ixaA*aAtN is also a pl. of A_ixA*apN , occurring in a trad., and signifying pools which receive the rain-water, and retain it for drinkers: (IAth, L:) or the correct word is A_ixaA*N , without p , and it signifies a place where beasts assemble at a pool of water left by a torrent; and its pl. is A^uxu*N (AA, A'Obeyd, L) and A=xaA*N , which latter is extr.: (L:) but as to ↓ A_ixaA*apN , it has a different signification, which will be found below; i. e. land of which a man takes possession for himself, &c.: (AA, L:) or A_ixaA*N is a coll. gen. n., and ↓ A_ixaA*apN is its n. un., and signifies a receptacle made for water to collect therein: and ↓ A^axo*N signifies a thing that one digs for himself, in the form of a watering-trough, which retains water for some days; and its pl. is A^uxo*aAnN : (L:) and ↓ A_ixo*N and ↓ A_ixo*apN also signify a thing that one digs in the form of a wateringtrough; and the pl. is A^uxo*N and A_ixaA*N . (L.) In a trad. of Mesrook Ibn-El-Ajda', A_ixaA* are likened to the Companions of Mohammad; and it is added, that one ↓ A_ixaA*ap suffices for a rider; and one, for two riders; and one, for a company of men: (S, L:) meaning that among them were the young and the old, and the possessor of knowledge and the possessor of more knowledge. (L.) ― -b2- See also A_ixaA*apN .

definition: [ Rush, or rushes: so called in the present day:] a kind of trees: (S:) or [rather] a kind of plant, (M, Mgh, TA,) having shoots (M, Mgh) which are slender, (Mgh,) without leaves;
sourceDefinition: [ Rush, or rushes: so called in the present day:] a kind of trees: (S:) or [rather] a kind of plant, (M, Mgh, TA,) having shoots (M, Mgh) which are slender, (Mgh,) without leaves; (M, Mgh;) or of which the shoot is slender, and of which sieves are made; as is said in the A; and Sgh adds, [ growing ] in El-' Irák: (TA:) AHn says, (TA,) accord. to Aboo-Ziyád, it is of the kind called A^agolaAv , and comes forth in slender shoots, not having branches growing out from them, nor wood, (M, TA,) and sometimes men beat them, and make of them well-ropes and other cords, (TA,) and it seldom or never grows but in a place wherein is water, or near to water: (M, TA:) AHn says [also], it signifies shoots, or twigs, growing (M, K) long and slender and straight, (M,) without leaves; of which mats are made: (M, K:) or A^asalapN , (K,) which is the n. un. of A^asalN applied to the plant mentioned above, (M, K,) signifies any shoot, or twig, in which is no crookedness. (K.) ― -b2- Hence, (M,) (tropical:) Spears; (S, M, K;) as being likened to the plant mentioned above, in respect of its evenness and length and straightness and the slenderness of its extremities: n. un. as above: (M:) and (assumed tropical:) arrows, or Arabian arrows; syn. nabolN ; (M, K:) applied to both of these in a trad. of 'Omar, which refutes an assertion that it is peculiarly applied to spears, or long spears, and not to nbl : (A'Obeyd, TA:) Sh says that it is applied to spears because of the points of the heads fixed upon them. (TA.) ― -b3- (assumed tropical:) Any thin thing of iron, such as a spear-head, and a sword, and a knife. (TA.) ― -b4- (tropical:) The prickles of palm-trees: (M, K:) n. un. as above: (M:) by way of comparison [to the plant mentioned above]: (TA:) or any long thorns, or prickles, of a tree. (S.) ― -b5- [See also what next follows.]

sourceDefinition: , [aor. ,] inf. n. A^akolN and maA^okalN , [ He ate it, ] (S, K,) namely, food. (S.) Er-Rummánee says that A^akolN properly signifies The swallowing food after chewing it; so that the swallowing of pebbles is not properly thus termed: (Msb:) or, accord. to Ibn-El-Kemál, the conveying, or transmitting, to the belly what may be chewed, whether [ the thing be ] chewed or not; so that it does not apply to milk, nor to sawiyq : and as to the saying of the poet, mina AlA=kiliyna AlmaA='a ZulomFA famaA A^araY yanaAluwna xayorFA baEoda A^akolihimu AlmaA='a (assumed tropical:) [ Of the eaters of what they purchase with the price of water, wrongfully, I do not see any attain good after their eating of what they have purchased with the price of the water, ] he means a people who used to sell water and purchase with the price thereof what they would eat: (TA:) [for you say, A^akala ka*aA as meaning (assumed tropical:) He ate the price of such a thing: see another ex. voce A_ikaAfN ; and another voce vadoYN .] ― -b2- The saying, in the Kur [v. 70], laA^akaluwA mino fawoqihimo wamino taHoti A^arojulihimo [ They should eat things above them and things beneath their feet ] means, their means of subsistence should be made ample; (Bd, TA;) by the pouring of the blessings of the heaven and the earth upon them; or by the abundance of the fruit of the trees, and the produce of the grains sown; or by their being blessed with gardens of ripe fruits, so that they should gather them from the upper part of each tree, and pick up what should have fallen upon the ground. (Bd.) ― -b3- AinoqaTaEa A^akoluhu [lit. His eating became cut off, or stopped, ] means (tropical:) he died; [see also A^ukulN ;] and so AisotawofaY A^akolahu [lit. he completed his eating ]. (TA.) ― -b4- A^akala raw^oqahu [lit. He ate his life, ] means (tropical:) he became extremely aged, and his teeth fell out, one after another. (TA.) ― -b5- huwa yaA^okulu Aln~aAsa , and yaA^okulu luHuwma Aln~aAsi [ He eats men, and eats the flesh of men, ] means (tropical:) he defames men; or does so in their absence: (TA:) and the action thus signified may be [ with words, or by making signs ] with the side of the mouth, and with the eye, and with the head. (TA in art. hmz .) It is said in the Kur [xlix. 12], A^ayuHib~u A^aHadukumo A^ano yaA^okla laHoma A^axiyhi mayotFA [lit. Would any one of you like to eat the flesh of his brother when dead? ]; defamation, or defamation of the absent, being meant thereby. (S, * Ibn-' Arafeh, Bd, Jel.) ― -b6- A^akala ganamiY wa $aribahaA (tropical:) [ He ate the flesh of my sheep, and drank the milk of them, means, like A^akala maAliY , he ate, fed upon, devoured, or consumed, my wealth, or property: see 2]. (TA.) ― -b7- A^akalati Aln~aAru AlHaTaba (tropical:) The fire devoured, or consumed, the firewood. (S, Mgh.) ― -b8- A^akalato A^aZofaArahu AlHijaArapu (tropical:) [ The stones wore away his nails ]. (TA.) ― -b9- AlwaAwu fiY maroy^Y~K A^akalatohaA AlyaA='u (assumed tropical:) [ The w in maroy^iY~ , the Y has swallowed it up ]; because it is originally marow^uwYN : a phrase occurring in the 'Eyn. (TA.) ― -b10- A^akala Eumurahu (tropical:) He consumed his life. (Mgh.) ― -b11- It is said in a trad., (TA,) A^umirotu biqaroyapK taA^okulu AlquraY (tropical:) [ I have been commanded to have given unto me a town which shall devour the other towns ]; (K, TA;) said to be Yethrib [afterwards called El-Medeeneh]; (TA;) i. e., the people of which shall conquer the [other] towns and make spoil of their possessions: or it denotes the superior excellence of that town; and is like the saying, h`*aA HadiyvN yaA^okulu AlA^aHaAdiyva [ This is a tradition which does away with, or overrules, the other traditions ]. (Sgh. K, TA.) ― -b12- A^akolu Als~ik~iyni All~aHoma means (tropical:) The knife's cutting the flesh. (TA.) ― -b13- A^akalaniy raA^osiY , inf. n. A_ikolapN and A^ukaAlN and A^akaAlN , (tropical:) My head itched. (K, TA.) An Arab was heard to say, [as is often said in the present day,] jilodiY yaA^okuluniY (tropical:) My skin itches. (TA.) -A2- A^akila , aor. , (K,) inf. n. A^akalN , (TA,) (tropical:) It (a limb, or member, [and a sore,] and a piece of stick, or wood,) became corroded or cankered, or decayed, by the mutual eating away of its several parts; as also ↓ Ay^tkl [written with the disjunctive alif Aiytakala ], and ↓ tA^k~l . (K, TA.) ― -b2- A^akilati AlA^asonaAnu , (S, Msb, K,) aor. and inf. n. as in the next preceding sentence, (Msb,) (tropical:) The teeth rubbed together and wasted away; by reason of age; (S;) or fell out, one after another: (Msb:) or broke in pieces, or became much broken: (K:) and ↓ tA^k~lt signifies the same; (S, Msb;) and so ↓ Ay^tklt . (S.) ― -b3- A^akilati Aln~aAqapu , aor. , inf. n. A^akaAlN , (assumed tropical:) The she-camel experienced an itching and annoyance in her belly, (S, O, K,) from the growth of the hair, (S, O,) or from the growth of the fur, (K,) of her fœtus. (S, O, K.)

sourceDefinition: [ A^k~lhu , inf. n. taA^okiylN , He made him to eat a thing.] ― -b2- A^ak~ala maAliY wa $r~abahu , (S, K,) inf. n. as above, (K,) [lit. definition: A morsel, or small mouthful, of food.
sourceDefinition: A morsel, or small mouthful, of food. (S, Mgh, Msb, K.) [For the pl., see below.] You say, A^akalotu A^ukolapF waAHidapF I ate one morsel. (S.) And A^akla biA^axiyhi A^ukolapF (assumed tropical:) [ He ate a morsel by means of defaming his brother ] is said, in a trad., of a man who is on terms of brotherhood with another, and then goes to his enemy, and speaks of him in a manner not good, in order that he may give him a present for doing so. (TA.) ― -b2- A small round cake of bread; syn. quroSapN ; (S, K;) a single quroS : (Mgh:) pl. A^ukalN , as below. (TA.) ― -b3- See also A^ukulN . ― -b4- Also (assumed tropical:) i. q. TuEomapN ; (S, K;) which is also syn. with ↓ maA^okalapN ; (S, Msb, K, in art. TEm ;) i. e. (S.) ― -b2- See also A^ukolapN , last two sentences. ― -b3- (tropical:) The itch: or an itching: (S, K:) as also ↓ A^ukaAlN , (As, S, K,) [see A^akalaniY raA^osiY , of which both are said to be inf. ns.,] and ↓ A^akilapN : (K:) so the last is written accord. to the correct copies of the K: accord. to Esh-Shiháb, in the Shifá el-Ghaleel, it would seem to be A^ukolapN ; but this is at variance with the authority of the leading lexicologists: the same word, A^akilapN , is also explained in the K as signifying a disease in a limb, or member, in consequence of which one part is [as it were] eaten by another; [a meaning which I believe to be correct, (see A^ukaAlN ,) although SM says,] but this is identical with the itch, or an itching: and ↓ A^akalaAnN is a vulgar term for the same; and so is ↓ A=kilapN , with medd, given as correct by Eth-Tha'álibee, in [his book entitled] the Mudáf and Mensoob, but disallowed by ElKhafájee. (TA.) One says, A_in~iY laA^ajidu fiY jasadiY A_ikolapF (tropical:) [ Verily I experience in my body an itching. ] (S.)

definition: A sheep, or goat, which is set apart (S, Msb, K) to be eaten, (S, Mgh, K,) [i.
sourceDefinition: A sheep, or goat, which is set apart (S, Msb, K) to be eaten, (S, Mgh, K,) [i. e.] to be slaughtered, (Msb,) and which is fattened, (S, Mgh,) and the taking of which by the collector of the poor-rate is disapproved; (S;) not left to pasture by itself, being of the best of the beasts: (Msb:) and ↓ A^akiylapN occurs in the same sense, applied to a sheep, or goat, fattened to be eaten. (Mgh.) Hence the prov., maroEFY walaA A^akuwlapF [lit. Pasturage, and no Akwlp ]; meaning (assumed tropical:) wealth collected together, and none expended. (TA.) ― -b2- Also Barren; applied to a sheep or goat [app. because such is generally eaten]. (K.)

sourceDefinition: , (T, S, M, &c.,) aor. , (Mgh, K,) inf. n. bado'N , (T, S, M, Msb,) i. q. bh ↓ AbtdA^ ; (S, Msb, K;) [ He began with it; ] he made it to have precedence, or to be first; gave precedence to it; syn. qad~amahu : (Mgh, Msb:) in the dial. of the Ansár, badiy^a bh is used in this sense of qd~mh ; (M;) or badiYa bh [without ' ]; (IKtt, TA; [see badp'N ;]) [and badaY bh ; see art. bdY ;] and bh ↓ AbdA^ signifies the same. (Msb.) [So in the Kur xii. 76, fabadaA^a biA^awoEiyatihimo qabola wiEaA='i A^axiyhi And he began with their bags, before the bags of his brother. And badaA^ahu is sometimes used in the sense of badaA^a bihi ; whence, in the Kur ix. 13, wahumo badaw^uwkumo A^aw~ala mar~apK And they, it was, began with you the first time; i. e., as Bd says, by acting with hostility, and fighting.] You say also, bad~aA vum~a EaAda He began, or did a first time, or the first time: then repeated, or did a second time. (Az, TA in art. Ewd .) And badaA^a fiYi AlA^amori [ He began, or made a beginning, in the affair. ] (M.) ― -b2- badaA^a also signifies It (a thing) began; began to be; originated; or came into existence. (Msb.) [See also 5.] -A2- badaA^a Al$~ayo'a , (S, M, K,) aor. and inf. n. as above, (M,) [ He began the thing; commenced it; set about it; as also ↓ AbtdA^hu : accord. to the Mgh, the latter has this meaning, or, agreeably with the authority of the M and K, the meaning which here next follows:] he did the thing first, for the first time, by way of beginning, or originally; (S, M, K;) as also ↓ AbdA^hu and ↓ AbtdA^hu ; (M, K;) i. e., not after the example of anything preceding. (TA. [But this addition seems rather to belong to another explanation to be mentioned below.]) One does not say, zayodFA ↓ AbtdA^ nor badaA^ahu , because these two verbs [signifying as last explained above] do not have for their objects corporeal things. (Mgh.) [El-Mutanakhkhil El-Hudhalee uses the phrase saA^aboduw^uhumo bima$omaEipK I will begin with them (meaning his guests) by sporting and jesting; like the phrase in the Kur ix. 13 cited above: but different from these is the saying in the Kur xxxii. 6, wabadaA^a xaloqi A@loA_inosaAni mino TiynK And He began the creation of man from clay. ] The saying, ↓ faA_ino kaAna Als~abuEu A@botadaA^ahu means AbtdA^ A^axo*ahu A^awo EaD~ahu [ But if the beast, or bird, of prey has begun the seizing of him, or the biting of him ]; the noun that is prefixed [to the pronoun] being suppressed. (Mgh.) You say also, kaAna *`lika fiY AlA^amori ↓ A@botidaA='i That was in the beginning, or first, of the affair. (Msb.) [See also bado'N , below.] ― -b2- He originated the thing; brought it into being or existence; made it, or produced it, for the first time, it not having been before; (Mgh;) [and] so ↓ AbdA^hu , said [of God, and] of a man, as the agent; (Msb;) and ↓ AbtdA^hu . (Mgh in art. bdE .) [Hence,] badaA^a A@ll~`hu Alxaloqa , and ↓ A^abodaA^ahumo , God created, or brought into existence, mankind, or the created beings: (M, Msb, K:) both signify the same. (S.) sourceDefinition: inf.n. of 1; (T, S, M, Msb;) [The act of beginning; ] or the doing a thing first. (M.) You say, laka Albado'u , (M, K,) and ↓ Albudo'u , (As, TA,) and ↓ AlbadoA^apu , (S, M, Msb, K,) and ↓ AlbudoA^apu , (S, M, K,) and ↓ AlbidoA^apu , (L,) and ↓ AlbadaA='apu , (M, K,) and ↓ AlbudaA='apu , (S, M, K,) and AlbudaAhapu , with h substituted for ' , (M, Mtr,) and ↓ AlbidaA='apu , (Mtr, TA,) and, accord. to IKtt, AlbidaAyapu , but see what follows, (TA,) and ↓ Albadiy^apu , (M, K,) and ↓ Albud~aA='apu , (AZ, TA,) It is for thee to begin, (S, M, Msb, K,) before any other, in shooting or casting, &c.: (S:) as to AlbidaAyapu , mentioned above, accord. to Mtr [and Fei], (TA,) it is a vulgar word, (Mgh, Msb, TA,) as IB and several others have stated, (Msb, TA, *) a corruption of ↓ AlbidaA='apu , (Mgh, Msb,) signifying the first; as also ↓ AlbudaA='apu ; and ↓ AlbadoA^apu : (Msb:) but IKtt says that it is a word of the dial. of the Ansár; badaA^otu biAl$~aYo'i and badiytu bihi signifying qad~amotuhu : [see 1:] and he cites the following verse of Ibn-Rawáhah: walawo EabadonaA gayorahu $aqiynaA biA@somi A@loA_ilaAhi wa bihi badiynaA [ In the name of God, and with it we begin; and if we worshipped any other than Him, we should be miserable ]: see art. bdY . (TA. [This verse is also cited in the S in art. bdw , where, in one copy I find it as above; in another, with badayonaA instead of badiyonaA .]) And you say, faEalahu Eawo*aA wabado'FA , (T, S,) and Eawodahu Ealay badoy^ihi , (M,) and fiY Eawodihi wabadoy^ihi , and ↓ fiY Eawodatihi wabadoA^atihi , (S, M,) [ He did it returning and beginning again; or returning to his beginning; i. e. he did it again from the beginning; he recommenced it: or you say this] meaning like as is meant by the saying next following. (TA.) rajaEa Eawodahu EalaY badoy^ihi , (S, K,) and EawodFA EalaY bado'K , in both of which [and in the last following] the verb may be trans., and the noun following therefore in the accus. case, (TA,) and fiY Eawodihi wabadoy^ihi , and ↓ fiY Eawodatihi wabadoA^atihi , [in both of which, if correct, the verb must be intrans.,] and EawodFA wabado'FA , [as though meaning EaAy^idFA wabaAdiy^FA , used as a phrase denotative of state,] (K,) [but in this last, and the two next preceding, accord. to the TA, the verb should be faEalahu , as in the next preceding sentence, instead of rajaEa , and this is confirmed by what is said in the K in art. Ewd ,] He returned in the way whence he had come: (S, K:) [accord. to the TA, the literal meaning of the first and second may be he made his returning to revert to his beginning, and he made a returning to revert to a beginning: ] or the meaning of the first, (Sb, TA in art. Ewd , and K in that art.,) and of the second, (K in that art.,) is, he returned without stopping after he had gone away: (Sb, K:) and sometimes it signifies the stopping in one's coming and then returning: (Sb:) [and it returned to its first state; it recommenced: ] and you say, rajaEotu EawodiY EalaY badoy^iY , meaning I returned like as I had come. (Sb ubi suprà.) ― -b2- Also First, or former; preceding all others, or preceding another; as also ↓ Albado'u badiYo'N ; and AlbadiY'u being syn. with AlA^aw~alu . (S, K.) Hence the saying, AifoEalohu baAdiY bado'K , and ↓ baAdiY badiYo'K , meaning Do thou it the first thing, or the first of everything; [accord. to different copies of the S;] the Y in bAdY being quiescent, in the place of the accus. case, accord. to usage; and sometimes they omit the [altogether], on account of frequent use [of the phrase], as will be stated in art. bdw , (S in the present art.,) saying baAdiY badK , and baAdiYbadiY (S in art. bdw .) You say also, AifoEalohu bado'FA , and A^aw~ala bado'K , (Th, M, K,) and bado'a bado'K , (CK,) and badaA bado'K , (M, K,) and bado'K ↓ baAdiy^a , (A'Obeyd, T, S, M, K,) and baAdiYa badK , (K,) and baAdiYo badFA , (M, K, [in the CK baAdiYo badK ,]) and baAdiYo badFA , (M,) and badiYo'K ↓ baAday^a , (K,) and baAdiYo badaA , (M, K,) and ↓ badiYo'K ↓ baAdiy^a , (A'Obeyd, T, S, M, CK,) and badiY~K ↓ baAdiy^a , which is anomalous, (M,) or baAdiYa bad~iYi , (K,) and baAdiYo badiy~K , (Fr, A'Obeyd, T, S, M,) and ↓ badiy^K ↓ baAdiy^a , (S, CK,) or ↓ baAdiYa badiy^K , (K, TA,) and baAdiYo ↓ badoA^apa , (M, K, TA,) the former word being the act. part. n. of badiYa , which is of the dial. of the Ansár, as mentioned above, and the latter being indecl., with fet-h for its termination, (TA, [in the CK the latter word is written bado'ap ,]) and bado'K ↓ badoA^apa , (CK,) and ↓ badoA^apa badoA^apa , (M, K,) and ↓ badiYo'K ↓ badoA^apa , (S,) and bado'K ↓ badiYo'a , (S, CK,) and bado'a *iY bado'K , (Fr, T,) and *iY bado'K ↓ badoA^apa , (Fr, T, S, K,) and ↓ badoA^apa *iY badoA^apK , and ↓ *iY badiYo'K ↓ badoA^apa , (S, K,) and ↓ *iy badaA='apa ↓ badaA^apa , (K, TA,) not bdA'p [as in the CK], (TA,) and ↓ badiYo'a *iY badiYo'K , (S, K, TA, [in the CK the last word is written bado'K ,]) and ↓ *iY badiYo'K ↓ badaA='api , (K,) meaning Do thou it the first thing; (Fr, T, K;) so in a correct copy [of the K, and so I find in a MS. copy of the K and in the CK]: accord. to another copy, the first of everything: (TA:) or the first of first; (S;) thus in the L: (TA:) the words here put in the accus. case [literally or virtually] are so put [in some instances] as adverbial nouns; or, accord. to MF, they may be [in some instances] denotatives of state, with respect to the agent; the meaning being AifoEalohu HaAlapa kawonika baAdiy^FA , i. e. mubotadiy^aA bihi [lit. do thou it in the state of thy being beginning it ]. (TA.) [In like manner,] you also say, bado'a Alr~aA^oYi , and [more commonly] Alr~aA^oYi ↓ baAdiy^a , At first thought; or on the first opinion: (Lh, M:) [ bado'u Alr~aA^oYi and] Alr~aA^oYi ↓ baAdiy^u signifying the first, and beginning, of the idea, thought, opinion, or judgment; or what is perceived before considering well or thoroughly: (M:) [and bado'N alone signifying a first idea, thought, opinion, or judgment; as is implied in the A, voce Say~uwrN , q. v.:] hence, Alr~aA^oyi ↓ faEalahu fiY baAdiy^i [ He did it at first thought, &c.]: (M:) and Alr~aA^oYi turiydu ↓ A^anota baAdiy^a ZulomanaA , and AlrA^Y ↓ mubotadaA^a , i.e. Thou at first thought, &c., desirest to wrong us: and one says also, baAdiYa AlrA^Y , without; meaning on the occasion of what appeared of opinion; i. e. at the first of what appeared thereof; [or at the first opinion's presenting itself; ;] in which case, the phrase does not belong to this art. [but to art. bdw ]: it occurs in the Kur xi. 29: (M:) AA alone there read baAdiy^a , with; all the other readers pronounced it without ' (TA.) ― -b3- Also A chief, or lord, (S, M, Msb, K,) who occupies the first place in chieftainship or lordship: (S:) or, as some say, a youth, or young man, whose judgment, or opinion, is deemed good, and who is consulted: (M:) or it signifies also an intelligent youth or young man: (K:) pl. buduwo'N . (M.) A poet (namely, Ows Ibn-Maghrà Es-Saadee, TA) says, vunoyaAnunaA A_ino A^ataAhumo kaAna badoA^ahumu wabadow^uhumo A_ino A^ataAnaA kiAna vunoyaAnaA [ Our second chief, if he came to them, would be their first chief; and their first chief, if he came to us, would be a second chief ]. (S.) ― -b4- Also, and ↓ badoA^apN , A share, or portion, of a slaughtered camel: (S, K:) or the best share or portion thereof: (T:) or the former word has the latter signification; and the latter word, the former signification: and the former signifies also a bone with the meat, or flesh, that is on it: (M:) and a joint; syn. mafoSilN ; (AA, T, M;) and so badFA q.v.: (AA, T:) the pl. [of pauc.] of bado'N is A^abodaA='N (S, M, K) and [of mult.] buduwo'N ; (S, K;) the former of which is the more common: (TA:) or this is pl. of badFA . (AA, T.) The shares abovementioned [as commonly divided for the game called Almayosir q. v.] are ten; namely, the two haunches, the two thighs properly so called, the two thighs commonly so called (i. e. the tibiæ), the two shoulders, and the two arms; which last are the worst, because of the many veins [therein]. (TA.) ― -b5- See also badiYo'N .

definition: ― -b2- Also The beginning, or outward course, of a military expedition;
sourceDefinition: : see bado'N , in thirteen places. ― -b2- Also The beginning, or outward course, of a military expedition; opposed to rajoEapN , meaning the returning, or homeward course, thereof: occurring in a trad., in which it is said that the Prophet gave, in the case of the former, a fourth [of the spoil], and in the case of the latter, a third; i.e., when a troop went forth from the main body of the army and attacked a party of the enemy, they were to have a fourth of the spoil that they took, and the rest of the army was to share with them the remaining three fourths; and if a troop did so in returning, they were to have a third of all the spoil that they took, because of the greater difficulty and danger attending this case. definition: , aor. , inf. n. baTarN , He exulted; or exulted greatly, or excessively; and behaved insolently and unthankfully, or ungratefully: or he exulted by reason of wealth, and behaved with pride and...
sourceDefinition: , aor. , inf. n. baTarN , He exulted; or exulted greatly, or excessively; and behaved insolently and unthankfully, or ungratefully: or he exulted by reason of wealth, and behaved with pride and self-conceitedness, and boastfulness, and want of thankfulness: or he behaved with the utmost exultation, &c.: or he rejoiced, and rested his mind upon things agreeable with natural desire: syn. of the inf. n. A^a$arN , (S, A, L, Msb, TA,) and maraHN ; (L, TA;) the former of which signifies $id~apN AlmaraHi , (S, A,) and mujaAwazapu AlHad~i fiY maraHK : (A:) he was, or became, stupified, deprived of his reason, confounded, or amazed, (S, K, Er-Rághib,) bearing wealth ill, or in an evil manner, performing little of the duty imposed on him by it, and turning it to a wrong purpose: (Er-Rághib, TA, * TK:) this is said to be the primary signification: (TA:) he was, or became, stupified, or confounded, and knew not what to prefer nor what to postpone: (TA:) he was, or became, confounded, perplexed, or amazed, by reason of fright: (As, S voce baHira :) he behaved exorbitantly, or insolently, with wealth, (K, TA,) or on the occasion of having wealth: and this, also, is said to be the primary signification: (TA:) he had, or exercised, little of the quality of bearing wealth [ in a becoming, or proper, manner ]: (K:) he behaved proudly: (TA:) he regarded a thing with hatred, or dislike, without its deserving to be so regarded: he was, or became, brisk, lively, or sprightly: (K:) accord. to some, he walked with an elegant and a proud and self-conceited gait, with an affected inclining of the body from side to side. (TA.) It is said in a trad., laA yanoZuru A@ll~`hu yawoma AlqiyaAmapi mano jar~a A_izaArahu baTarFA [ God will not look, on the day of resurrection, upon him who drags along his wrapper of the lower part of the body in exultation and insolence, or pride: meaning one who wears too long a wrapper of the lower part of the body]. (TA.) ― -b2- baTirota Eayo$aka (tropical:) [ Thou exultedst, or exultedst greatly, or excessively, and behavedst insolently and unthankfully, or ungratefully, &c., in thy manner of life, ] is a phrase similar to ra$idota A^amoraka ; (S, TA;) and in like manner baTirato maEiy$atahaA , in the Kur [xxviii. 58]; in which the verb is not trans., but the subst. is put in the accus. case because of fiY understood before it. (Aboo-Is-hák.) ― -b3- laA A^aboTaru AlginaY (assumed tropical:) I do not, or will not, domineer, or assume superiority, over others when I am rich. (Ham p. 517.) ― -b4- baTira Aln~iEomapa (tropical:) He held wealth, or the favour, or benefit, in light estimation, and was unthankful, or ungrateful, for it. (A.) ― -b5- baTira hidaAyapa A^amorihi (assumed tropical:) He refused the right direction as to the management of his affair, and was ignorant of it. (TA.) ― -b6- It is said in a trad., that pride is baTaru AlHaq~i , which means (tropical:) The considering as false, or vain, what God has pronounced to be the truth, or our duty; namely, the confession of his unity, and the obligation of rendering Him religious service: or the being confounded at considering truth, or duty, and not seeing it to be true, or incumbent: (TA:) or the disdaining the truth, or right, and not accepting it or not admitting it. (K.) -A2- baTarahu , aor. (S, K) and , (K,) inf. n. baTorN , (S, Msb,) He cut it, or divided it, lengthwise; slit it; split it. (S, Msb, K.) Hence the appellation bayoTaArN . (S, Msb.)

definition: It rendered him such as is termed baTir ;
sourceDefinition: It rendered him such as is termed baTir ; it (wealth) caused him to exult, or to exult greatly, or excessively, and to behave insolently and unthankfully, or ungratefully: &c.: [see baTira :] (S, A:) it stupified him, deprived him of his reason, confounded him, or amazed him. (S, K.) You say, maA A^amoTarato Hat~aY A^aboTarato It (the sky) rained not until it caused [men] to exult, or to exult greatly, &c. (A.) ― -b2- AbTr Hilomahu (tropical:) It (the ignorance of a person) caused his (another's) clemency, moderation, or gravity, to become converted into inordinate exultation, and insolence, or the like, and levity. (A.) ― -b3- AbTrhu Hilomahu (tropical:) It stupified, confounded, or amazed, him, so as to turn him from his clemency, moderation, or gravity. (TA.) ― -b4- AbTrhu *aroEahu (tropical:) He imposed upon him more than he was able to do; (S;) what was above his power: (K:) *rEh is here a substitute for its antecedent to indicate an implication therein: (A:) you say this when a slow-paced camel has endeavoured in vain to keep pace with another camel; and when any man has imposed upon another a difficulty beyond his power: (TA:) or the meaning is, he cut off his means of subsistence, and wasted his body: (IAar, K:) *rE signifying the “ body. ” (IAar.)

sourceDefinition: Clamorous; long-tongued: and one who perseveres in error: fem. with p : (K:) but it [the former] is mostly used in relation to women, (TA,) and as signifying a woman who exults, or exults greatly, or excessively, and behaves insolently and unthankfully, or ungratefully, ( taboTaru ,) and perseveres in error: (ADk:) [it is said in the TA that some say biZoriyrN , and that this is the more approved; but Az says,] Lth cites, from ADk, the phrase AimoraA^apN biToriyrN as meaning a clamorous, long-tongued woman; liA^an~ahaA qado baTirato wA^a$iratN [because of her insolent behaviour]: and says that, accord. to Aboo-Kheyreh, it is AmrAp biZoriyrN ; her tongue being likened to the baZor : but Lth adds, the saying of ADk is preferable in my opinion, and more correct. (T in art. bZr .)

sourceDefinition: , (S, K, &c.,) aor. , (Msb, K,) inf. n. bugaA='N , (S, Mgh, K, &c.,) or this is a simple subst., and the inf. n. is bagoYN , (Msb,) [but, if this be correct, the former is generally used for the latter,] and bugFY , (Lh, K,) but the first is better known, and is the chaste form, and some say, bigFY , (TA,) and bugoyapN and bigoyapN , (K,) accord. to Th, but others hold these two to be simple substs., and some mention also bagoyapN , with fet-h, (TA,) and bugaAyapN , (As, S, TA,) He sought; sought for, or after; sought, desired, or endeavoured, to find, and take, or get; (S, Mgh, Msb, K, &c.;) a stray-beast, (As, S, TA,) or any other thing, (S, Mgh, * Msb, * K, * TA,) good or evil; (Lh, TA;) as also ↓ AbtgY and ↓ tbg~Y (S, Msb, K) and ↓ AstbgY : (K:) or ↓ AbtgY signifies he sought, &c., diligently, studiously, sedulously, or earnestly: (Er-Rághib, TA:) and bagaY signifies also he loved, or affected, a thing: (MF, TA:) or, accord. to Er-Rághib, the inf. n. signifies the seeking to exceed the just bounds in respect of that which one aims at, or endeavours after, whether one actually exceed or do not; and sometimes it is considered in relation to quantity; and sometimes, in relation to quality. (TA.) You say, bagaAhu bi$ar~K [ He sought him with an evil purpose; or sought to do him evil ]. (S and K in art. Eqb .) ― -b2- And bagaAhu He sought, &c., a thing for him; like bagaY lahu . (Lh, Mgh, * K. *) You say, bagaAhu Al$~aYo'a He sought, &c., the thing for him; (S, K;) as also Al$~aYo'a ↓ AbgAhu : (K:) thus you say, AiboginiY ka*aA or k*A ↓ A^aboginiY and Aiboga liY k*A Seek thou for me such a thing; (TA;) and DaAl~atiY ↓ A^aboginiY Seek thou for me my stray-beast: (Mgh:) or Al$~aY'a ↓ AbgAhu signifies He aided, or assisted, him to seek the thing: (Ks, K:) or ka*aA ↓ A^aboginiY signifies Seek thou for me such a thing; and also Aid thou me to seek such a thing. (JK.) definition: is said in the S to be quasi-pass.
sourceDefinition: is said in the S to be quasi-pass. of bagayotuhu , like as Ainokasara is of kasarotuhu ; and Esh-Shiháb says of the aor. that it is quasi-pass. of bagaAhu , aor. yabogiyhi , in the sense of Talabahu : (TA:) [Fei says,] it has been asserted that AnbgY is quasi-pass. of bagaY ; but a verb of the measure AnfEl is not used as a quasi-pass. unless it implies effort, and the consequence of an action, as in the case of kasarotuhu , of which the quasi-pass. is Ainokasara ; which AnbgY does not: some, however, allow its being thus used: (Msb:) accord. to Zj, it is as though it were syn. with AinoTalaba , as quasi-pass. of Talaba , and means It was, or became, suitable, fit, meet, or proper; (Zj, TA;) [or right, and allowable; and good: or very requisite: (see explanations of exs. following:) or it behooved: and] it was, or became, facilitated, or easy; (Er-Rághib, K;) and practicable, or manageable. (Er-Rághib, TA.) Accord. to some, this verb is not used in the pret. tense, but only in the aor.: it is reckoned among verbs imperfectly inflected: (Msb, TA:) but the pret. is mentioned by AZ and Sb and Zj, and by ElKhattábee on the authority of Ks; and was often used by Esh-Sháfi'ee: it is, however, very rare. (TA.) You say, yanobagiY laka A^ano tafoEala ka*aA [ It is suitable to thee, or is fit, meet, or proper, &c., for thee, or it behooveth thee, that thou shouldst do such a thing ]. (S, TA.) And, accord. to Zj, AinobagaY lifulaAnK A^ano yafoEala , as meaning It was, or became, suitable to such a one, or fit, meet, or proper, for him, that he should do, or to do, such a thing. (TA.) And maA yanobagiY laka A^ano tafoEala h`*aA , (Lh, K,) and ↓ mA yubotagaY , (K, TA,) with fet-h to the g , (TA,) and mA A@nobagaY , and ↓ mA A@botugiYa ; (Lh, K;) of which four phrases, the first is given by Lh as explanatory of the third and fourth, and means, accord. to Esh-Shiháb, It is not right, proper, fit, or meet, nor allowable, for thee that thou shouldst do this, or to do this; and it is not good for thee &c.; but he adds that only the aor. has been heard from the Arabs in this sense. (TA.) And yanobagiY A^ano yakuwna ka*aA It is very requisite that it should be so, or that such a thing ought be; [or it ought to be so, or such a thing ought to be; it behooves that it should be so, or such a thing behooves; ] it is not well that such a thing should be neglected, or left undone. (Msb.) And Ks is related to have heard, from the Arabs, the phrase, maA yanobagiY A^ano yakuwna ka*aA , meaning It is not right that it should be so, or that such a thing should be: or it is not good &c. (Msb.) It is said in the Kur [xxxvi. 69], wamaA Eal~amonaAhu Al$~iEora wamaA yanobagiY lahu , i. e. [ And we have not taught him poetry, or versification ], nor is it right, proper, fit, or meet, for him: (Bd:) or nor is it easy to him, (Bd, Jel, Er-Rághib,) or practicable to him. (Bd, Er-Rághib.)

(Er-Rághib, TA.) Accord. to some, this verb is not used in the pret. tense, but only in the aor.: it is reckoned among verbs imperfectly inflected: (Msb, TA:) but the pret. is mentioned by AZ and Sb and Zj, and by ElKhattábee on the authority of Ks; and was often used by Esh-Sháfi'ee: it is, however, very rare. (TA.) You say, yanobagiY laka A^ano tafoEala ka*aA [ It is suitable to thee, or is fit, meet, or proper, &c., for thee, or it behooveth thee, that thou shouldst do such a thing ]. (S, TA.) And, accord. to Zj, AinobagaY lifulaAnK A^ano yafoEala , as meaning It was, or became, suitable to such a one, or fit, meet, or proper, for him, that he should do, or to do, such a thing. (TA.) And maA yanobagiY laka A^ano tafoEala h`*aA , (Lh, K,) and ↓ mA yubotagaY , (K, TA,) with fet-h to the g , (TA,) and mA A@nobagaY , and ↓ mA A@botugiYa ; (Lh, K;) of which four phrases, the first is given by Lh as explanatory of the third and fourth, and means, accord. to Esh-Shiháb, It is not right, proper, fit, or meet, nor allowable, for thee that thou shouldst do this, or to do this; and it is not good for thee &c.; but he adds that only the aor. has been heard from the Arabs in this sense. (TA.) And yanobagiY A^ano yakuwna ka*aA It is very requisite that it should be so, or that such a thing ought be; [or it ought to be so, or such a thing ought to be; it behooves that it should be so, or such a thing behooves; ] it is not well that such a thing should be neglected, or left undone. (Msb.) And Ks is related to have heard, from the Arabs, the phrase, maA yanobagiY A^ano yakuwna ka*aA , meaning It is not right that it should be so, or that such a thing should be: or it is not good &c. (Msb.) It is said in the Kur [xxxvi. 69], wamaA Eal~amonaAhu Al$~iEora wamaA yanobagiY lahu , i. e. [ And we have not taught him poetry, or versification ], nor is it right, proper, fit, or meet, for him: (Bd:) or nor is it easy to him, (Bd, Jel, Er-Rághib,) or practicable to him. (Bd, Er-Rághib.)

(S, Mgh, Msb.) [See an ex. voce mahorN .] ― -b2- Also A female slave, (JK, S, K,) whether she be a fornicatress or an adulteress or a prostitute or not; (TA;) not meant to imply revilement, though originally applied to female slaves because of their prostitution of themselves: (S:) or a free woman who is a fornicatress or an adulteress or a prostitute: so in the K: but correctly, or a fornicatress or an adulteress or a prostitute, whether free or a slave: (TA:) and a female singer, though chaste; because of fornication's being originally attributable to such a person: (Msb:) pl. as above. (S.) ― -b3- bagaAyaA also signifies The scouts, or companies of scouts, that precede an army: (S, K, TA:) but the sing. of this is ↓ bagiy~apN . (TA.)

definition: Seeking; seeking for, or after; seeking, desiring, or endeavouring, to find, and take, or get: pl. bugaApN and bugoyaAnN (K) and bug~aA='N . (TA: [there mentioned as a pl., but not said to be of...
sourceDefinition: Seeking; seeking for, or after; seeking, desiring, or endeavouring, to find, and take, or get: pl. bugaApN and bugoyaAnN (K) and bug~aA='N . (TA: [there mentioned as a pl., but not said to be of baAgK , nor explained.]) baAgK wahaAdK , lit. A seeker of [stray] camels and a guide of the way, mentioned in a trad. respecting the Hijreh (as said by A booBekr to a man who asked him “ Who are ye? ”), alludes to the seeking of religion and the guiding from error. (TA.) One says, far~iquwA lih`*ihi AlA_ibili bugoyaAnFA yuDib~uwna lahaA , i. e. [ Disperse ye, for these camels, seekers ] to scatter themselves in search thereof. (S.) ― -b2- Acting wrongfully, injuriously, or tyrannically, [&c.,] towards others: pl. bugaApN . (Msb. [See 1.]) gayora baAgK , in the Kur ii. 168, [&c.,] means Not being a revolter from the Muslims, (Jel,) or, against the Imám: (TA:) or it means not desiring to eat for the sake of enjoyment: or not seeking to exceed the limit of his want: (Az, TA:) or not seeking what he should not seek. (Er-Rághib, TA.) fiy^apN baAgiyahN A company of men revolting from the just Imám. (K.) firoqapN baAgiyapN A party occupying itself with corrupt, wrong, or unjust, conduct. (Msb.) ― -b3- A camel that does not impregnate, or get with young. (Kr, K.) ― -b4- A horse that is proud, or self-conceited, with exceeding briskness or liveliness or sprightliness: (JK, Ham p. 210:) [but] Kh disallows its being thus used. (S.) -A2- [The pl.] bugoyaAnN also signifies What the sportsman, or hunter, seeks, of game, or objects of the chase. (JK.) mabogFY [ A place where a thing is sought: and hence, a way, or manner, in which a thing is, or should be, sought ]: this is meant in the saying, ↓ bagayotu AlmaAla mino mabogaAtihi [ I sought wealth by the way, or manner, whereby it should be sought ]; like as maA^otFY is meant in the saying, A^atayotu AlA^amora mino maA^otaAtihi . (S.)

sourceDefinition: , aor. , (AZ, S, Msb, &c.,) inf. n. bahaAjapN (AZ, S, L, K) and bahojapN (AZ, L, [but some seem to regard this as a simple subst.,]) and bahajaAnN , (L,) He, or it, was, or became, beautiful, or goodly: (AZ, S, L, Msb, K:) or beautiful in colour: or beautiful and bright or splendid: or it (a plant) was, or became, beautiful and bright; and he (a man) was, or became, characterized by a laughing, or happy, appearance of the beautiful parts of the face, as the cheeks, and the lines of the forehead: or by the appearance of joy, gladness, or happiness; or by a joyful, glad, or happy, aspect, or appearance.
