sourceDefinition: [a coll. gen. n., The ben-tree; a species of moringa; so in the present day;] a kind of tree, (S, Mgh, Msb, K,) well known: (Msb:) n. un. with p : (S, Mgh, Msb:) its seed, or grain, [ called Hab~u AlbaAni and jawozu AlbaAni and fusotuqu AlbaAni , the glans unguentaria, or nux unguentaria, or ben-nut, ] has a good, or pleasant, [ fragrant ] oil, (K,) called duhonu AlbaAni [ oil of ben ], (S, Mgh, Msb,) and simply baAnN , the prefixed noun being suppressed: (Mgh:) [Az says,] it is the pl. of baAnapN . which is a certain tree having a fruit, or produce, which is perfumed with aromatics, after which its oil is expressed, of a good [or fragrant ] quality: (T in art. bnY : its seed, or grain, is good for [ removing ] the [ affections of the skin termed ] bara$ and nama$ and kalaf and HaSaf and bahaq and saEafap and the mange, or scab, and for the peeling of the skin, applied in the form of a liniment with vinegar; and for hardness of the liver and the spleen, made into a beverage with vinegar; and a mivoqaAl thereof, drunk, is an emetic, which loosens crude phlegm: (K:) AHn says, (TA,) it is a kind of tree that grows tall, in a straight, or an erect, manner, like as grows the [ species of tamarisk called ] A^avol , and its leaves are [ of the kind termed ] hadab , like those of the Avl , but its wood has no hardness: the n. un. is with P : Aboo-Ziyád says, it is of the [ trees called ] EiDaAh , and has long hdb , intensely green; it grows upon [ hills, or what are termed ] haDob ; and its fruit resembles the pods of the [ species of kidney-bean called ] luwbiyaA=' , except that its greenness is intense; and in it is a seed, or grain, from which is extracted the oil of the bAn : on account of the straightness of its growth and of the growth of its braches, and their length and tenderness, the poets liken thereto the tender girl of tall and beautiful, or just, stature; saying kaA^an~ahaA baAnapN [ As though she were a ben-tree ], and kaA^an~ahaA guSonu baAnK [ As though she were a branch of the ben-tree ], &c.: thus does Keys Ibn-El-Kha- teem: (M in art. byn :) and so does Imra-el- Keys. (TA.) [See an ex. voce barahorahapN .] ― -b2- [It is also applied in the present day to A species of willow, the salix Aegyptia of Linnæus, properly called in Arabic xilaAf : and this is said to be meant by modern Arab poets when they liken an elegant girl to a twig of the bAn ; but probably from their erroneously supposing this tree to be meant in the same case by the older poets.]

definition: The mouth of a streamlet or rivulet;
sourceDefinition: The mouth of a streamlet or rivulet; (IB, Msb, K;) i. e. a place hollowed out by the water in the side of a river, whence it flows forth: (Msb:) pl. turaEN (IB, Msb) and turoEaAtN and turaEaAtN and turuEaAtN : (Msb:) in the S it is said to signify the mouths of streamlets or rivulets; but correctly the sentence should be, turaEN is pl. of turoEapN , and has this signification. (IB.) ― -b2- A canal, or channel of water, to a meadow or garden or the like: (L, TA:) this is the meaning commonly known [in the present day: the general name in Egypt for a canal cut for the purpose of irrigation, conveying the water of the Nile through the adjacent fields]. (TA.) ― -b3- The opening, or gap, of a wateringtrough or tank, by which the water enters, and where the people draw it: (Az, Mgh, * K, * TA:) and, (K,) accord. to AA, (TA,) the station of the drinkers at the watering-trough or tank; as in the O and K; or, as in the L, the part of the watering-trough or tank which is the station of the drinkers. (TA.) ― -b4- A meadow, or garden, or the like, (S, K,) in an elevated place: (K:) if in low land, it is called rawoDapN . (TA.) ― -b5- A stair; or a flight of steps by which one ascends; syn. darajapN : (S, K:) so accord. to some in a trad., which see in what follows: (S, * TA:) and particularly the flight of steps of a pulpit. (AA, Sgh, K.) ― -b6- (tropical:) A door, or gate: (S, Sgh, Msb, K:) pl. turaEN . (K.) You say, fataHa turoEapa Ald~aAri (tropical:) He opened the door of the house. (TA.) And it is said in a trad., A_in~a minobariy h`*aA EalaY turoEapK mino turaEi Aljan~api , (S, TA,) as though meaning, (tropical:) Verily this my pulpit is at a gate of the gates of Paradise: thus explained by Sahl Ibn-Saad Es-Sá'idee, the relater of the trad.; and A'Obeyd says, wahuwa Alwajohu [“ and it is the proper, ” or “ the valid and obvious, way, ” of explaining it], meaning that it is the preferable explanation: but the author of the K, mistaking his meaning, makes wajohN to be another signification of turoEapN : or the meaning of this trad. is, he who acts according to the exhortations recited upon the steps of my pulpit will enter Paradise: or, accord. to Kt, prayer and praise in this place are means of attaining to Paradise; so that it is as though it were a portion of Paradise. (TA.) In the same manner Sahl explained his other trad,, A_in~a qadamiY EalaY turoEapK mino turaEi AlHawoDi (tropical:) [ Verily my foot is at a gate of the gates of the pool of Paradise]. (TA.)

definition: A torrent filling the valley;

definition: Remaining, staying, dwelling, or abiding, (T, Msb,) in a country, or town [&c.
sourceDefinition: Remaining, staying, dwelling, or abiding, (T, Msb,) in a country, or town [&c.]; settling therein: also pronounced taAnK , by suppression of the ' : (Msb:) one who remains, stays, or abides, in his country, or town; (Th, TA;) i. q. dihoqaAnN [app. as meaning a man having a fixed abode in a district of cultivated land, or in a village or town of such a district: but see below]: (Th, K, TA:) pl. tun~aA='N . (T, S, Msb, K.) It is said in a trad., layosa lilt~aAniy^api $aYo'N , meaning For those who remain in their abodes, and go not forth with the soldiers on expeditions against the enemy, there shall be nothing; i. e., no share of the spoil. (TA.) ― -b2- Rich; wealthy; possessing much property. (Msb.) [Or A man possessing much land or other immoveable property: for this is a signification assigned to dihoqaAnN .]

definition: , (T, A,) or tAb A_ilaY A@ll~`hi , (S, M, K,) aor.
sourceDefinition: , (T, A,) or tAb A_ilaY A@ll~`hi , (S, M, K,) aor. yatuwbu , (Msb,) inf. n. tawobapN and tawobN , (T, S, M, Msb, K,) both of these signifying the same, (T, S, M, Msb,) the p in the former being added to denote the fem. gender, or, as some say, the former is a n. un. like DarobapN , (Msb,) or, as Akh says, tawobN is pl. [or a quasi-pl. n.] of tawobapN , like as EawomN is of EawomapN , (S,) or like as lawozN is of lawozapN , and this is the opinion of Mbr, (M,) and taAbapN , (M, K,) which is for tawobapN , (M,) and mataAbN (S, M, A, K) and tatowibapN , (S, * M, * K,) of the measure tafoEilapN , (S, M,) an anomalous form, (TA,) syn. with tawobapN , mentioned in the Book of Sb; (S;) [ He repented; or repented toward God; as will be shown by what follows:] originally, he returned unto God, (T, TA,) mino ka*aA and Eano ka*aA [ from such a thing ]: (TA:) or he returned, [or returned unto God, ] (S, M, A, K,) from sin, (S,) or from his sin, (A,) or from disobedience (M, K) to obedience: (M:) or taAba mino *anobihi signifies he desisted from his sin: (Msb:) tawobapN signifies the repenting of sin; i. e. the grieving for it, or regretting it, with the confession of having no excuse for the commission thereof. (Kull.) It is said in a trad., Aln~adamu tawobapN [ Repentance is ] a returning from sin. (S.) The time of El-Islám is termed zamanu Alt~awobapi as being The time of returning from [or repenting of ] the belief in a plurality of gods. (A.) A poet says, tubotu A_ilayoka fataqab~alo taAbatiY waSumotu rab~iY fatafab~alo SaAmatiY [ I have repented toward Thee, and accept Thou my repentance; and I have fasted, O my Lord, and accept Thou my fast ]; meaning tawobatiY and SawomatiY . (M.) ― -b2- taAba A@ll~`hu Ealayohi God returned to forgiveness towards him; became again forgiving to him: (T:) or disposed, or adapted, him to repentance, or returning from sin or disobedience: (S, K:) or reverted from severity to mildness towards him: or returned to him with his favour, or grace, and his acceptance, or approbation; became again propitious to him: (A, K:) all these meanings are correct: (TA:) or God forgave him, and saved him from acts of disobedience: (Msb:) or accepted his repentance: (Jel in ii. 35 &c.:) or returned towards him with mercy, and acceptance of repentance. (Bd ibid.)

definition: , originally tawabuwtN , the t not being the characteristic of the fem.
sourceDefinition: , originally tawabuwtN , the t not being the characteristic of the fem. gender, (Z, MF, TA,) of the measure faEaluwtN , and meaning A chest, or box, from Alt~awobu , because what is taken out from it continually returns to it: (AAF, IJ, Z, MF, TA:) or originally taAbuwapN ; (S, K; [in the CK taA^obuwapN ;]) the w being made quiescent, and the p changed into t : (S, K:) [in Chald. ? : in Hebr. ? :] it signifies also the ribs, with what they contain, as the heart and the liver &c.; as being likened to a chest, or box; (IAth, TA in art. tbt ;) the chest, breast, or bosom: (A in that art.:) or [primarily] the ribs, with what they contain, as the heart &c.: and [hence] applied to a chest, or box: (Towsheeh, MF, TA:) also written tabuwtN . (K in art. tbt .) [It is generally applied in the present day to a bier: a coffin: and an oblong case that is placed over a grave: the pl. is tawaAbiytu .] El-Kásim Ibn-Maan says that it is the only word in the Kur-án in respect of which the dialects of Kureysh and the Ansár differ; the former pronouncing it taAbuwtN ; (S;) and the latter, taAbuwhN . (S, K.) But IB denies that its last letter is originally p , the fem. termination; asserting the final t to be a radical letter, the measure of the word to be faAEuwlN , and its proper place in art. tbt : he says that the final t is changed in a case of pause, but not generally, into h , as is that of AlfuraAt [the Euphrates], in which the t is not the fem. termination. (L, TA.) You say, maA A^awodaEotu taAbuwtiY $ayoy^FA faqadotuhu , meaning I have not deposited in my bosom anything of knowledge, or science, that I have lost. (A in art. tbt .)

definition: , (T, S, Msb,) and vaA^ara bihi , (T, S, M, Msb, K) aor.
sourceDefinition: , (T, S, Msb,) and vaA^ara bihi , (T, S, M, Msb, K) aor. , (Msb, K,) inf. n. vaA^orN and vuw^orapN , (S,) or the latter is a simple subst., as is also vuw^uwrapN , (Lh, M, K,) He revenged, or avenged, his blood, by retaliating his slaughter; he slew his slayer. (T, S, M, Msb, K.) [Hence, vuy^ira maqotuwluhu and bimaqotuwlihi The blood of his slain relation was revenged, or avenged, by retaliation of his slaughter: see 10.] ― -b2- [Hence also,] laA vaA^arato fulaAnFA yadaAhu , (K,) or EalaY fulaAnK , (A,) (tropical:) May his arms, or hands, not profit such a one. (A, K.) ― -b3- Also vaA^arahu , and vaA^ara bihi , (M, K,) and vaA^ara Alqawoma , inf. n. vaA^orN , (T,) He sought to revenge, or avenge, or retaliate, (T, M, K,) his blood, (M, K,) and the blood of the people, or party. (T.) It is said in a prov., laA yanaAmu mano vaA^ara [ He will not sleep who seeks to revenge, or avenge, or retaliate, blood ]: in the Kámil of Mbr, [and in some copies of Meyd,] ↓ mani A@v~aA^ari [which seems to signify the same]. (S, K.)

sourceDefinition: , (S, M, A, Mgh, Msb, K,) which may be also pronounced vaArN , i. e., with the ' suppressed, (Msb,) and ↓ vaA^orapN , (A,) and ↓ vuw^orapN , (S,) which last is a subst. [from vaA^ara ], as also ↓ vuw^uwrapN , (Lh, M, K,) Blood-revenge; or retaliation of murder or homicide: or a seeking to revenge, or avenge, or retaliate, blood: [see 1, of which vaA^orN is an inf. n. :] or a desire, or seeking, for retaliation of a crime or of enmity: or retention of enmity in the heart, with watchfulness for an opportunity to indulge it: syn. *aHolN : (S, A, Msb:) or Talaba biAld~ami : (M, K:) or HiqodN : (Mgh:) or (so accord. to the M; but accord. to the K, “ and ”) blood (M, K) itself: (M:) pl. A^avoA=rN and A=vaArN ; the latter formed by transposition. (Yaakoob, M.) You say, A^adoraka vaA^orahu (S, Mgh, K) and ↓ vuw^oratahu (As, T, S) [ He obtained, or attained, or took, his bloodrevenge, or retaliation: or] he attained the object of his pursuit [for blood-revenge, or retaliation ]; from vaA^arahu : (As, T:) or he slew the slayer of his relation. (Mgh.) And Talaba bivaA^orihi He sought to obtain his blood-revenge, or retaliation; syn. Talaba bi*aHolihi . (S and Msb in art. *Hl .) And A^anaA A^aTolubu vaA^oriY Einodahu I seek my blood-revenge of him; syn. *aHoliY . (A.) And vaA^oriY Einoda fulaAnK My blood-revenge is a debt owed to me by such a one; syn. *aHoliY : meaning such a one is the slayer of my relation. (A.) -A2- vaA^orN also signifies, (A,) or ↓ vaAy^irN , (T,) One who seeks blood-revenge, or retaliation of the slaughter of his relation: and one of whom is sought blood-revenge, or retaliation of the slaughter of a relation: (T, A:) the latter primarily signifies a slayer; and hence, a slayer of a person's relation in vengeance, or retribution: (Ham p. 637:) and the former, one who is sought, or pursued, for blood-revenge; an inf. n. used as a subst.: (Ham p. 87:) the slayer of a person's relation; (S, M, A, K;) as also ↓ vaAy^irN : (A:) pl. of the former A^avoA=rN and A=vaArN [as above] (K) and vaA^oraAtN : (S, A, K:) the first of which three is [also] pl. of vaAy^irN . (T.) You say, huwa vaA^oruhu He is the slayer of his relation. (S.) And yaA vaA^oraAti fulaAnK O slayers of such a one. (T, S, K.) yaA vaA^oraAti EuvomaAna , occurring in a trad., which is also related with the substitution of taAraAt for vA^rAt , may be explained in the same manner; or it may mean O ye seekers of the blood-revenge of 'Othmán, aid me to obtain it; the prefixed noun TaAlibiY , or A^ahol , being understood. (Nh, TA. (A.) In a trad. of Mohammad Ibn-Selemeh, relating to the day of Kheyber, occur the words, A^anaA lahu yaA ↓ rasuwlu A@ll~`hi Almawotuwru lilv~aAy^iri , meaning [ I am for him, i. e. [The explanation there given is clearly shown to relate to Almwtwr .]) ― -b2- vaA^orN signifies also An enemy: pl. (TA.)

sourceDefinition: , (S, M, * K,) aor. , (S, M,) inf. n. vam~N , (T, S, M,) He repaired it; or put it into a good, sound, or right, state; (T, S, M, K;) [ by filling up its interstices, &c., ] with vumaAm [q. v.]. (S.) Hence the saying, vamamotu A^umuwriY (assumed tropical:) I put my affairs into a good, sound, right, or proper, state; restored them to such a state; or set them right, or in order. (S.) And hence also the saying, kun~aA A^ahola vam~ihi waram~ihi (assumed tropical:) [ We were the fit persons to put it into a good, sound, right, or proper, state; &c.]; (S;) occurring in a trad.; accord. to the relaters thereof, warum~ihi ↓ vum~ihi ; but A 'Obeyd holds the former reading to be the right. (T.) ― -b2- He spread vumaAm for it, namely, a skin of milk, and put it [ vmAm ] above it, in order that the sun might not strike it, and its milk become consequently decomposed, or curdled. (T.) ― -b3- [ He stuffed it, either with vumaAm or absolutely: for] vum~a signifies it was stuffed. (T.) ― -b4- He collected it together; (S, M, K;) namely, a thing; (S, M;) mostly used in relation to dry herbage. (M, K.) You say, vum~a lahaA , i. e. Collect thou [ for them; namely, the cattle &c.; like vimo lahaA from wavama ]. (TA.) And huwa yavum~uhu wayaqum~uhu He sweeps it, and collects the good and the bad. (S.) ― -b5- vam~a AlT~aEaAma , (M, K,) [aor. and] inf. n. as above, (M,) He ate the good of the food and the bad thereof; (M, K;) as also qam~ahu . (TA.) ― -b7- vam~a yadahu biAlHa$iy$i , (M, K,) or biAlA^aroDi , (S, M,) [aor. and] inf. n. as above, (TA,) He wiped his hand (S, M, K) with the dry herbage, (M, K,) or upon the ground. (S, M.)

sourceDefinition: There; syn. hunaAka ; (Zj, S, M, K;) a noun of indication, (Zj, T, M, Msb, Mughnee, K,) denoting a place that is remote (Zj, T, S, M, Mughnee, K) from the speaker, (Zj, T, M,) like as hunaA denotes that which is near; (Zj, T, S;) or denoting a place other than that of the speaker: (Msb:) it is an adverbial noun, not to be used otherwise than as such; (Mughnee, K;) indecl. because of its vagueness, and with fet-h for its termination to avoid the concurrence of two quiescent letters. (Zj, T, M.) Thus in the saying [in the Kur xxvi. 64], waA^azolafonaA vam~a AlA=xariyna [ And we brought near, there, the others ]. (Mughnee.) He who makes it decl. as an objective complement (Mughnee, K) in this ex., (Mughnee,) and in the saying in the Kur [lxxvi. 20], waA_i*aA raA^ayota vam~a raA^ayota naEiymFA , is in error: (Mughnee, K: *) Zj says that the meaning is, And when thou castest thine eyes, or thy sight, there, thou shalt behold [scenes of] enjoyment: that Fr asserted the meaning to be, A_i*aA raA^ayota maA vam~a [ when thou seest what is there ]; but that this is an error; for mA , accord. to this interpretation, is a conjunct noun, and it is not allowable to suppress a conjunct noun and leave its complement. (T.) ― -b2- [ mino vam~a is used by postclassical writers as meaning Therefore; for that reason; on that account. ]

sourceDefinition: , (T, S, M, &c.,) for which one also says fum~a , (M, Mughnee,) substituting f for the v , (M,) and vum~ata (T, S, M) and vum~ato , (M, TA,) but vum~ata is the more common, (Mughnee and K on the letter t ,) and fum~ata and fum~ato , (M, TA,) [meaning Then, i. e., afterward, or afterwards, ] a particle, (M, K,) or conjunction, (Zj, T, S, Msb, Mughnee,) denoting order (Zj, T, S, M, Msb, Mughnee) and a delay, (S, Msb,) or having three properties, namely, that of virtually associating in the same case [the latter of the two members which it conjoins with the former of them], and denoting order, and denoting a delay; but respecting all of these there is a difference of opinions. (Mughnee, K. *) As to the associating in the same case, Akh and the Koofees assert that it sometimes fails to have this property, by its occurring redundantly, so as not to be a conjunction at all; and they hold to accord with this assertion the saying in the Kur [ix. 119], Hat~aY A_i*aA DaAqato Ealayohimu A@loA^aroDu bimaA raHubato waDaAqato Ealayohimo A^anofusuhumo waZan~uwA A^ano laA malojaA^a mina A@ll~`hi A_il~aA A_ilayohi vum~a taAba Ealayohimo [ Until, when the earth became strait to them, notwithstanding its amplitude, and their minds became straitened to them, and they knew that there was no repairing for refuge from God save unto Him, then He returned to forgiveness towards them ]: (Mughnee, K: *) but this has been resolved by the subaudition of the complement [of what precedes vum~a , as though the meaning were, then ( they betook themselves unto Him, begging forgiveness, and ) He returned &c.]. (Mughnee.) And as to its denoting order, some hold that there are exs. of its not necessarily implying this; (Mughnee, K; *) one of which is the saying in the Kur [xxxix. 8], xalaqakumo mino nafosK waAHidapK vum~a jaEala minohaA zawojahaA : (Mughnee: [in which are added other similar exs., one of which is given in the K:]) but to this there are five replies: 1st, that this passage is elliptical; the meaning being, He created you from one person ( which He originated ); then He made therefrom its mate: 2nd, that the meaning is, He created you from a person that was alone; then &c.: 3rd, that the progeny of Adam were made to come forth from his back like little ants; then Eve was created from his [rib called the] quSayoraY : 4th, that the creation of Eve from Adam being unusual, vm~ is used to notify its order and posteriority in respect of wonderfulness and of the manifestation of power; not to denote order and posteriority of time: 5th, that vm~ is here used to denote the order of enunciation; not the virtual order: the replies preceding this last are better than it, inasmuch as they verify the order and the delay; whereas the last verifies the order only, as there is no delay between the two enunciations; but the last reply is of more common application, applying to the ex. given above and to others: (Mughnee:) Fr says that the meaning of the ex. given above is, He created you from a person ( which He created ) single; then &c.; and in like manner says Zj. (T.) And as to its denoting a delay, Fr asserts that sometimes this is not the case, as is shown by the saying, A^aEojabaniY maA SanaEota Alyawoma vum~a maA SanaEota A^amosi A^aEojabu [ What thou didst to-day excited my wonder, or admiration, or pleasure; then ( I tell thee ) what thou didst yesterday was more wonderful, or admirable, or pleasing ]; for vm~ is here used to denote the order of the enunciation; not a delay between the two enunciations. (Mughnee, K. *) ― -b2- [It is said that] it denotes order and a delay when it conjoins single words: but Akh says that it has the meaning of wa [ And ], because it is used in cases in which there is no order; as in waA@ll~`hi vum~a waA@ll~`hi laA^afoEalan~a [ By God, and ( I say again, ) By God, I will assuredly do such a thing]: and when it conjoins propositions, it does not necessarily denote order, but has the meaning of wa : (Msb:) it has the meaning of wa , (S, Msb,) the conjunction, (S,) in the saying in the Kur [x. 47], vum~a A@ll~`hu $ahiydN EalaY maA yafoEaluwna [ And God is witness of what they do ]. (S, Msb.) ― -b3- The Koofees allow its being used in the manner of fa and wa so as that the aor. immediately following it after a conditional verb may be man- soob: and Ibn-Málik allows its being thus used so as that the aor. immediately following it after the expression of a desire that the thing shall not be done may be marfooa and mejzoom and man- soob. (Mughnee.)

definition: -A2- In the saying maA lahu vum~N walaA rum~u [ He has not vum~ nor rum~ ], the former of these two nouns signifies water-skins, or milk-skins, and vessels;
sourceDefinition: : see vumaAmN . -A2- In the saying maA lahu vum~N walaA rum~u [ He has not vum~ nor rum~ ], the former of these two nouns signifies water-skins, or milk-skins, and vessels; (M;) or what is bad, or the worst, of those things, (S, K,) accord. to ISk; (S;) or men's household-goods, or furniture and utensils, and their water-skins, or milk-skins, and vessels; (T, TA;) which last is the right meaning: (TA:) and the latter noun signifies maram~apu Albayoti [app. meaning, accord. to analogy, (for I find no suitable explanation of it in any of the lexicons,) the means by which a house, or tent, is put into a good state; and therefore, good furniture and utensils ]. (ISk, S, M, K.) You say also, maA yamoliku vum~FA walaA rum~FA , meaning the same: (S, TA:) or he possesses not little nor much: it is not used save with a negation. (M, TA.) An Arab of the desert said, jaEojaEa biYa Ald~ahoru Eano vum~ihi warum~ihi , [thus in some copies of the S, and in the TA, in which latter the last two nouns are expressly said to be with damm, but in two copies of the S, in this instance, erroneously written, vam~ihi waram~ihi ,] i. e. [ Fortune has debarred me ] from its little and its much. (S, TA.) And hence the saying of the vulgar, jaA='a biAlv~um~i waAlr~um~i , except that they pronounce both these nouns with kesr, meaning He brought little and much. (TA.) ― -b2- See also 1.

definition: [ Panicum, or panic grass;
sourceDefinition: [ Panicum, or panic grass; applied to several species thereof; but restricted by Forskål (Flor. Aeg. Ar., descr. plant., p. 20, where its Arabic name is written “ tummâm, ” ) to panicum dichotomum; called by Delile (Flor. Aeg., no. 58, where its Arabic name is written “ temâm, ” ) pennisetum dichotomum; and described by him in the “ explication des planches ” accompanying his Flora, plate 8: the Arabs use it for making thatch for their huts: ] a kind of plant, (T, S, Msb, K, [in the M termed $ajarN ,]) well known in the desert, not desired, or not much eaten, by the camels, or cattle, except in a case of scarcity, or drought; (T;) weak, or frail; having what are termed xuwS [q. v.], or what resemble xwS , sometimes used for stuffing, (S, TA,) and for stopping up the interstices of houses; (S, Msb, TA;) and sometimes used for removing whiteness from the eye: (K:) accord. to Az, it is of several species, one of which is the DaEap , and another is the jaliylap , and another is the garaf , which resembles rushes ( A^usal ), and brooms are made of it, and water-bags are covered with it to protect them from the sun, causing the water to become cool: (TA:) [see also A^umoSuwxapN :] it is also called ↓ vayomuwmN , (K,) and ↓, [but see what follows,] (T, M,) which is sometimes contracted into vumapN ; (T;) or it is also called ↓ vum~N , of which ↓ vum~apN is the n. un.: (AHn, TA:) the n. un. of vumaAmN is [likewise] with p . (S, M, Msb, K.) You say of a thing that may be reached, or taken with the hand, without difficulty, (T, Z, K,) huwa EalaY Tarafi Alv~umaAmi , (IAar, T, M, Z, K, *,) i. e. (assumed tropical:) It is easy to thee, or within thy reach, no obstacle intervening between thee and it: (IAar, M:) because the vmAm is not tall, (T, K,) so that the reaching it should be difficult. (T.) And ↓ huwa laka EalaY raA^osi Alv~um~api [meaning the same]. (M.) And ↓ huwa EalaY raA^osi Alv~um~api , (TA,) or laka *`lika ↓ EalaY raA^osi Alv~um~api , (assumed tropical:) [ That is easy of attainment to thee ], (M,) is a prov. used in relation to the attainment of a thing that one wants. (M, TA.) The Arabs also say, ↓ huwa A^abuwhu EalaY Tarafi Alv~um~api , meaning (assumed tropical:) He is like his father: and some of them say ↓ Alv~am~ap , with fet-h. (TA.) And it is said in a trad. of 'Omar, AugozuwA waAlgazowu HulowN xaDirN qabola A^ano yaSiyra vumaAmFA vum~a rumaAmFA vum~a HuTaAmFA (assumed tropical:) [ Engage ye in predatory warfare while it is sweet and fresh ], meaning, while ye see, and make abundant, your spoils, before it become feeble like the vmAm ; [ then, decayed; then, broken up. ] (TA.) ― -b2- It also signifies What has become dry, or dried up, of the branches that are placed beneath the naDad [q. v.]. (M.)

sourceDefinition: (like misan~N , K [in the CK, erroneously, muvim~ , like musin~ ,]) One who pastures for him who has no pastor, (T, K,) or no pasturage, (TA,) and lends a beast or camel for riding or carrying, to him who has no beast or camel for riding or carrying ( yufoqiru mano laA Zahora lahu , [in the CK, erroneously, yafoqiru ,]) and sets right ( yavum~u [in the CK, erroneously, yavim~u ]) what the tribe are unable to manage, of their affair: (T, K:) so explained by ISh. (T.) And A man who is strong; who comes after, and aids, those who have recourse to him in need; and bears, or carries, what is redundant, or in excess; and repels the riders. (T.) And rajulN miEam~N mivam~N milam~N A man who sets right an affair, and manages it, or acts vigorously in it. (IAar, T.) ― -b2- rajulN mivam~N wamiqam~N and ↓ mivam~apN wamiqam~apN , (S, K,) in which latter phrase the p is added to give intensiveness to the signification, (S,) A man who sweeps and collects the good and the bad of a thing: (S:) or who eats the good of the food and the bad thereof. (K.) [See also mixam~apN , in art. xm .]

sourceDefinition: A grave; a sepulchre; pl. A^ajodaAvN (S, Msb, K) and A^ajoduvN ; (S, K;) of which latter, J cites an ex., but in this instance it is the proper name of a place. (TA.) It is of the dial. of Tihámeh: the people of Nejd say jadafN : (Msb:) or [as some say] the f in the latter is a substitute for the v in the former; for AjdAv is used as a pl. by common consent, and AjdAf is not used: (TA:) but Suh affirms, in the R, that the latter pl. is used by Ru-beh. (TA in art. jdf .)

definition: , (S, * Msb, K, *) aor.
sourceDefinition: , (S, * Msb, K, *) aor. , (Msb,) inf. n. jadoEN , (S, Msb, K,) He cut off the nose; and in like manner, the ear; and the hand, or arm; and the lip; (S, Msb, K;) and a similar part: (TA:) and A^anofahu ↓ A^ajodaEotu signifies the same as jadaEotu [ I cut off his nose ]: or jadoEN signifies [absolutely] the cutting off; or cutting so as to separate. (TA.) In the following saying of a poet, the verb is used metaphorically, waA^aSobaHa Ald~ahoru *uw AlEironiyni qado judiEaA [lit. And nosed fortune became mutilated in the nose; meaning, (assumed tropical:) became marred ]. (TA.) And in the following phrase, occurring in a verse, kaA^an~a A@ll~`ha yajodaEu A^anofahu waEayonayohi , the poet means, [ As though God cut off his nose ] and put out his eyes: see a similar saying in art. qld , voce taqal~ada . (TA.) ― -b2- jadaEahu , (S, K,) aor. and inf. n. as above, (TA,) He mutilated him, or maimed him, by cutting off his nose, or his ear, or his hand or arm, or his lip, (S, K, TA,) or the like; (TA;) as also ↓ jd~Ehu (S, TA.) [Hence the phrase,] lahu ↓ jadoEFA (S, K) [( May God decree ) to him mutilation, or maining, by the cutting off of his nose, or the like; or cause it to befall him: or] meaning A^alozamahu A@ll~`hu AljadoEa [(assumed tropical:) may God make injury, or diminution of what is good, to cleave to him ]: (K:) said in imprecating a curse upon a man: similar to EaqorFA lahu , q. v.: the first word being governed in the accus. case by a verb understood. (TA.) One says also, AijodaEohumo biAlA^amori Hat~aY ya*il~uwA , a phrase mentioned by IAar, but not explained by him; thought by ISd to mean, (tropical:) Act thou, in commanding, as though thou mutilatedst them by cutting off their noses [ until they become submissive ]. (TA.) In the phrase ↓ Sawotu AlHimaAri Alyujad~aEu [ The voice of the ass that has his ear, or ears, cut off, (see mujad~aEN , below,)], occurring in a verse of Dhu-l-Khirak Et-Tuhawee, (S,) accord. to J, but not found by Sgh in the verses of that poet, and said to be in the Book [of Sb], though IB denies this, asserting it to be in the Nawádir of AZ, (TA,) Akh says, the poet means Al~a*iY yujad~aEu , like as you say, huwaA@loyaDoribuka , meaning Al~a*iY yaDoribuka : Aboo-Bekr Ibn-es-Sarráj says, the poet, requiring refa for the rhyme, has changed the noun into a verb; and this is one of the worst of poetic licences. (S.) ― -b3- [Hence,] Als~anapu tajodaEu Aln~abaAta (tropical:) [ The year of drought cuts off, or destroys, the herbage ]: (A, TA:) and tajodaEu biAlmaAli destroys the camels or the like. (S, O, K.) And AlqaHoTu Alnab~aAti ↓ jad~aEa (tropical:) The drought prevented the growth, or increase, of the herbage. (K, TA.) ― -b4- [Hence also,] jadaEa EiyaAlahu , inf. n. jad~aEN , (assumed tropical:) He withheld good things from his family, or household. (TA.) And jadaEatohu A^um~uhu , aor. , inf. n. as above, (tropical:) His mother fed him with bad food; (Zj, K;) as also ↓ A^ajodaEatohu , (S, K,) inf. n. A_ijodaAEN ; (TA;) and ↓ jad~aEatohu , (K,) inf. n. tajodiyEN : (TA:) and ↓ jd~Ehu and ↓ AjdEhu (tropical:) He (a pastor) confined him [a beast] to bad pasture. (TA.) jadaEotuhu , (S,) inf. n. as above, (K,) also signifies (assumed tropical:) I confined him, restricted him, or the like; syn. Habasotuhu : and (assumed tropical:) I imprisoned him: (S, K: *) and so with * : (S:) or jadoEN and ja*oEN both signify (assumed tropical:) the confining, or restricting, a person with evil management, and with contemptuous treatment, and want of good care. (A Heyth.) -A2- jadiEa , aor. , (Msb,) inf. n. jadaEN , (S, Msb, K,) He (a man) was, or became, mutilated, or maimed, by the cutting off of his nose, or his ear, (S, * Msb, K, *) or his hand or arm, or his lip, (S, K,) or the like: (TA:) or, accord. to some, you do not say jadiEa , but judiEa : (TA:) and jadiEati Al$~aApu The sheep, or goat, was, or became, mutilated by having its ears entirely cut off. (Msb.) ― -b2- [Hence,] also, (S, K,) aor. as above, (K,) and so the inf. n., (S,) [as though meaning (assumed tropical:) He was, or became, injured; ] (tropical:) he (a child) had bad food: (S, K, TA:) and he (a young weaned camel) had bad food: or was ridden while [ too ] young, and in consequence became weak. (TA.)

[of mult.] juluwfN (S, M, Msb) and [of pauc.] A^ajolaAfN and A^ajolufN , which last is rare. (Msb.) ― -b2- Also A [ skin of the kind called ] ziq~ without head and without legs. (IAar, K.) ― -b3- And A skinned animal, (AO, S,) or a skinned sheep or goat, (K,) of which the belly has been taken forth, (AO, S, K,) and the head and legs of which have been cut off; (K;) the body of a skinned sheep or goat, without head and without belly and without legs: or, as some say, a body of any kind without a head upon it: (L:) or a beast without fat, and without back [ to bear ], and without belly to conceive: (IAth, TA:) or the skin of a sheep or goat, and of a camel: (As, Msb:) pl. definition: [a coll. gen. n.] An army; a military force; a legion; a body of troops or soldiers; (L, K;) a collected body of men prepared for war: (Mgh:) auxiliaries: (S, L, Msb, K:) n. un. ↓ junodiY~N...
sourceDefinition: [a coll. gen. n.] An army; a military force; a legion; a body of troops or soldiers; (L, K;) a collected body of men prepared for war: (Mgh:) auxiliaries: (S, L, Msb, K:) n. un. ↓ junodiY~N [signifying a trooper; a soldier; an auxiliary ]; like as ruwmiY~N is n. un. of ruwmN : (Msb:) pl. of the former, junuwdN (S, A, Mgh, Msb) and [pl. of pauc.] A^ajonaAdN . (Mgh, Msb.) It is said in a trad., ↓ AlA^arowaAHu junuwdN mujan~adapN (S, A, L) Souls are troops collected together: meaning that they are created of two parties, each party agreeing together, and disagreeing with the other party, like two armies opposed, each to the other. (L.) ― -b2- Also Any kind, or species, of creatures, or created things, regarded as alone, by itself, or apart from others. (K, * TA.) It is said in a prov., A_in~a lil~hi junuwdFA minohaA AlEasalu Verily to God belong kinds, or species, of created things [ by means of which He effects his purposes as by armies or auxiliaries ], of which is honey: (Z, K:) first said by Mo'áwiyeh, when he heard that El-Ashtar had been given to drink some honey containing poison, in consequence of which he died: and used on the occasion of rejoicing at a misfortune that has befallen an enemy: it occurs in the history of El-Mes'oodee thus; A_in~a lil~hi junodFA fiY AlEasali . definition: (S, M, Msb, K) and minojaniyqN (Msb, K) and ↓ manojanuwqN (Lth, IAar, Msb, K) [ A kind of balista;
sourceDefinition: (S, M, Msb, K) and minojaniyqN (Msb, K) and ↓ manojanuwqN (Lth, IAar, Msb, K) [ A kind of balista; ] an instrument [or engine of war ] with which stones are cast (S, M, K, TA) at the enemy; made by binding [ in some manner ] very tall wooden poles, whereon is placed what is to be cast, which is then struck with a long pole, and so cast to a very distant place: [this imperfect description (the only one that I have found of this engine) seems to show that it was of a very simple and rude construction:] it is an ancient instrument, anterior to the invention [or use] of gunpowder and cannons by the Christians; and was used by Mohammad in the siege of Et-Táïf; but the first [of the Arabs] who used it in the time of paganism is said to have been Jedheemeh El-Abrash, of the Mulook et-Tawáïf: (TA:) pl. manojaniyqaAtN (S, Msb, K) and manojanuwqaAtN (Lth, TA) and majaAniyqu (Sb, S, Msb, K) and majaAniqu : (K:) dim. ↓ mujayoniyqN : (Sb, S:) it is fem., (Lth, S, Msb, K, *) preferably, (Lth, TA,) and in most instances; (Msb;) and hence it is also called AlA^unovaY ; (M in art. Anv ;) but sometimes it is masc.: (Msb, K:) and is arabicized, (S, Msb, K,) from the Persian (S, K) mano JiY niyko , i. e. “ How excellent am I! ” (S,) or mano Jiho niyko , i. e. “ I, how excellent am I! ” (K;) [Golius asserts it to be from the Greek μάγγανον but this is the original of manojanuwnN , which has a different meaning: its derivation, however, seems to have been unknown to the Arabs in general; for] some say that manojaniyqN is of the measure mafoEaliylN , [so in copies of the S, but correctly manofaEiylN , as in the Msb and TA,] because of the phrase nujonaqu mar~apF [see 1]: (S, Msb: *) or, (Msb,) accord. to Sb, (S,) it is of the measure fanoEaliylN ; (S, Msb;) because majaAniyqu is its pl. and the dim. is mujayniyqN ; and because, if the m were augmentative as well as the n , there would be two augmentative letters at the beginning of the noun, and this may not be in substs. nor in epithets that are not conformable to augmented verbs; and if the n were made an essential part of the word, the noun would be a quadriliteral-radical, and augmentative letters are not prefixed to words of this class except nouns conformable to their verbs, like mudaHorajN : (S, TA:) but MF says that these disquisitions are unprofitable; for in his opinion, all the letters of the word are radical, since it is a foreign word. (TA.) manojaniyiqY~N [app. A maker of the kind of engine called mnjnyq ; being mentioned as a surname:] a rel. n. from mnjnyq . (K.)

definition: , a subst., (Msb, TA,) signifying Hunger; or emptiness of the belly; (TA;) contr. of $ibaEN ; (S, K, TA;) as also ↓ majaAEapN , [properly an inf. n.,] and ↓ majowaEapN , (K, TA,) and ↓ majuwEapN ....
sourceDefinition: , a subst., (Msb, TA,) signifying Hunger; or emptiness of the belly; (TA;) contr. of $ibaEN ; (S, K, TA;) as also ↓ majaAEapN , [properly an inf. n.,] and ↓ majowaEapN , (K, TA,) and ↓ majuwEapN . (TA.) You say, juwEFA lahu wanuwEFA [May God decree hunger to him ]: accord. to Sb, an instance of inf. ns. in the accus. case by reason of a verb understood: it is a form of imprecation: and the latter noun may not be put before the former, because it is a corroborative to it: (TA:) or, accord. to some, nuwEN means “ thirst. ” (S, &c., in art. nwE .) And ↓ EaAmu majaAEapK and ↓ majowaEapK (S, K) and ↓ majuwEapK (TA) A year in which is hunger, or emptiness of the belly: (K, TA:) and ↓ EaAmu AlmajaAEapi and ↓ AlmajuwEapi [ the year of hunger, &c.]: (Msb:) pl. majaAy^iEu (K) and majaAwihu : as in the phrases A^aSaAbatohumu AlmajaAwiEu [ Cases of hunger, &c., befell them ] and waqaEuwAfiY AlmajaAwiEi [ They fell into cases of hunger, &c.]. (TA.) And ↓ Alr~aDaAEapu mina AlmajaAEapi , meaning The sucking which occasions interdiction [of marriage with the woman whose milk is sucked and certain of her relations] is that consequent upon hunger which is stopped by the milk in the time of infancy of the child; not when the child's hunger is only to be stopped by solid food. (Mgh.) [See also 1 in art. rDE .] And it is said in a prov., samanu kalobK bijuwEi A^aholihi , i. e. [ The dog's becoming fat is ] by reason of [ the hunger of his owners occasioned by] murrain befalling the camels; (K, * TA;) his owners falling into hunger and distress and leanness: (TA:) or klb was the name of a certain man, who was an object of fear, wherefore he was asked for a pledge, and he pledged his family: then obtaining possession of the camels, or cattle, of the people to whom he had pledged his family, he drove them away, and left his family: (K, TA:) some relate this prov. differently, saying [ samina kalobN “ a dog, ” or “ Kelb, ” “ became fat, ” and] bibuw^osi A^aholihi [“ by reason of the distress of his owners, ” or “ his family ”]. (TA.) [See Freytag's Arab. Prov. i. 615.]

definition: A certain small beast or reptile, (S, K,) well known;
sourceDefinition: A certain small beast or reptile, (S, K,) well known; (K;) the EiZaAyap : (Mgh:) or a species of the [ kind of lizards termed ] EiZaA=' ; of stinking odour: (Msb:) so called because of the largeness of its belly; from A^aHobanu [q. v.]: also called ↓ Hubayonapu ; (S, Msb, K;) and sometimes the article Al is prefixed to it, (S, Msb, K,) so that it is called A^um~u AlHubayoni , (S, Msb,) by poetic license: (TA:) it is of the form of the HirobaA=' [or chameleon ], broad in the breast, and large in the belly: (TA:) or, accord. to some, (TA,) it is the female of the HirobaA=' : (S and Msb and K in art. Hrb , and TA in the present art.:) accord. to Az, it is a small reptile resembling the [ kind of lizard called ] Dab~ : (Msb:) or, as some say, a certain reptile of the size of a man's hand: or, accord. to Ibn-Ziyád, a dust-coloured reptile, with four legs, and of the size of a frog that is not large; and when the children hunt it, they say to it, An~a AlA^amiyra naAZirN A_ilayoki A^um~a AlHubayoni Auno$uriY burodayoki [ Umm-el-Hobeyn, spread forth thy two wings: verily the commander is looking at thee ]: they hunt it until fatigue overcomes it, when it stops, standing upright upon its two kind legs, and spreads forth two wings that it has, of the same dust-colour; and when they hunt it further, it spreads forth wings that were beneath those two wings, than which nothing more beautiful in colour has been seen, yellow and red and green and white, in streaks, one above another, very many; and when it has done this, they leave it: no offspring of it is found; nor any genital organ: (TA:) the appellation A^um~u HubayonK is determinate, like Aibonu EirosK and Aibonu A=waY ; (S, Msb;) and [so is ↓ Hubayonapu ,] like A^usaAmapu ; (S;) but determinate as a generic appellation: (S, Msb:) the suppression of the article does not render it indeterminate; which is contr. to rule: (S, K:) the pl. is A^um~u HubayonaAtK , [which is strange,] and A^um~aAtu HubayonK . (Msb.) ― -b2- The Arabs say, in one of their imprecations, Sab~a A@ll~`hu Ealayoka A^um~a HubayonK maAxiDFA meaning (assumed tropical:) [ May God pour upon thee ] the night. (Ibn-Buzurj, TA in art. mxS .)

definition: Having the dropsy;
sourceDefinition: Having the dropsy; (S, Mgh, Msb;) as also ↓ maHobuwnN (KL) [and ↓ HabiynN ; so in the Lex. of Golius; and so in the present day]: having a disease in the belly, whereby it becomes large and swollen: (K:) fem. HabonaA='u , (S, K,) applied to a woman: (S:) pl. HubonN . (TA.) ― -b2- Hence, (TA,) the fem., (tropical:) Big-bellied; (K, TA;) applied to a woman. (TA.) And (assumed tropical:) A foot ( qadamN ) having much flesh in the baxaSapN [app. here meaning the pulpy portion of the sole ]; (K;) as though it were swollen. (TA.) And (assumed tropical:) A pigeon ( HamaAmN ) that does not lay eggs: pl. HubonN . (K.)

definition: It (the breast of a woman or girl) was, or became, swelling, prominent, or protuberant;
sourceDefinition: It (the breast of a woman or girl) was, or became, swelling, prominent, or protuberant; (Mgh, K;) as also ↓ Hajama , inf. n. HajomN : (K:) or was, or became, round, and swelling, prominent, or protuberant; as also ↓ Hj~m : (A, TA:) properly, became such as to have what is termed HajomN , (Mgh, TA,) meaning projection, protrusion, prominence, or protuberance, and elevation: (Mgh:) or, as some say, became such that the suckling might suck it. (TA.) ― -b2- A^aHojamato lilomawoluwdi (tropical:) She (a woman) suckled the new-born child for the first time. (K, TA.) -A2- AHjm Eanohu He refrained, forbore, abstained, or desisted, from it; (S, K;) quasi-pass. of Hjamotuhu , like as A^akab~a is of kababotuhu ; which are extr. of their kind; (S;) and AjHm Enh signifies the same; (S in art. jHm ;) but is a rare dial. var.: (Har p. 95:) or he drew back from it, or him, in awe, or fear: (K, TA:) or he receded, or drew back, form it; namely, a thing, or an affair: (Msb:) and A^aHojamotu Eani Alqawomi I dreaded, or feared, the people, or party, and returned, and left them, after I had desired to go to them. (AZ, Msb.) ― -b2- AHjm also signifies He (a man) advanced, or went forward; and so AjHm : both of these verbs thus having two contr. meanings. (MF.) -A3- See also 1, last sentence.

definition: A rising, protuberant, or prominent, part of a thing: (S:) a projection, protrusion, prominence, or protuberance;
sourceDefinition: A rising, protuberant, or prominent, part of a thing: (S:) a projection, protrusion, prominence, or protuberance; (S, Mgh;) and a rising, or an elevation: (Mgh:) or the part of a thing that one feels beneath his hand: (ElGhooree, Mgh:) or the part of a thing that one feels projecting, protruding, prominent, or protuberant, beneath his hand: pl. HujuwmN . (K.) One says, layosa limirofaqihi HajomN There is no projection, protrusion, prominence, or protuberance, to his elbow. (S.) Lh says that Hajomu AlEaZomi means One's perceiving the feel of the bones [or bone ] behind the skin: thus explaining it after the manner of explaining inf. ns.: and ISd says, I known not whether it be in his opinion an inf. n. or a simple subst. (TA.) And Lth says that AlHajomu means One's perceiving the feel of a thing beneath a garment: [and that] one says, masasotu baTona AlHubolaY fawajadotu Hajoma AlS~abiY~i fiY baTonihaA [which plainly means, I felt the belly of the pregnant woman, and perceived the bulging of the child in her belly ]. (Mgh, TA.) It is said [of a woman's garment] in a trad., laA yaSifu Hajoma EiZaAmihaA [lit. (tropical:) It does not describe the projecting of her bones ]: meaning, the garment does not stick to her body so as to tell what projects of her bones: it is made to be a describer by way of comparison. (IAth, TA.) ― -b2- [In post-classical works it is often used as signifying Bulk, bigness, or magnitude. ]

sourceDefinition: A cupper; syn. maS~aASN [lit. one who is in the habit of sucking ]; (K;) one who performs the operation termed HajomN ; (S, Mgh;) one who scarifies [ and draws blood with the miHojamap ]; (Msb;) as also ↓ HaAjimN ; (S, Msb, K;) but the former is an intensive epithet [denoting frequency or habit]: (Msb:) so called because he sucks the mouth of the miHojamap . (Az, TA.) Hence the prov. A^aforagu mino Haj~aAmi saAbaATa [ More unoccupied than the cupper of Sábát (the name of a place)]: for military forces used to pass by the man to whom it relates, and he used to cup them on credit, in consequence of want of employment, waiting for payment until they should return. (S: more fully explained in the K in art. sbT .)

sourceDefinition: , aor. , inf. n. HarajN , It (a number of things) became collected together: and, necessarily, became close, strait, or narrow: (so accord. to an explanation of the inf. n. by Er-Rághib, in the TA:) said of anything, it was, or became, close, strait, or narrow. (KL.) One says of dust, Harija A_ilaY HaAy^iTK , or sanadK , It rose, (Lth, Az, TA,) in a narrow place, (TA,) and became collected [ against a wall, or an acclivity or the like ]. (Lth, Az, TA.) ― -b2- Harija Sadoruhu , aor. and inf. n. as above, (assumed tropical:) His bosom became strait, or contracted; (S, A, Mgh, Msb, TA;) not expanded, or dilated, by reason of what was good. (TA.) And Harija alone, aor. and inf. n. as above, (assumed tropical:) He became disquieted, and contracted in bosom: and (assumed tropical:) he became in doubt; he doubted; because doubt disquiets the mind. (So accord. to explanations of the inf. n. by Er-Rághib, in the TA.) ― -b3- Also Harija , aor. and inf. n. as above, [(assumed tropical:) He became straitened, or in difficulty: and particularly, by the commission of a sin, or crime: (see HarajN , below:) and hence, simply,] (assumed tropical:) he committed a sin, a crime, or an act of disobedience for which he deserved punishment. (Msb.) ― -b4- Also He looked, and was unable to move from his place by reason of fear and rage. (T, TA.) And Harijati AlEayonu , (S, A, K,) aor. , (K,) inf. n. as above, (TA,) (tropical:) The eye became dazzled, ( HaArat , S, K, TA,) or sank in its socket, ( gaArat ,) and its vision became straitened: (A, TA:) or it did not turn about, nor wink, by reason of intent gazing. (TA.) ― -b5- Also, (S, A, K,) aor. as above, (K,) and so the inf. n., (S, K,) (tropical:) It was, or became, forbidden, or prohibited, (S, A, K,) and attended with straitness, or difficulty. (A.) So in the saying, Harija EalaY~a Zulomuka (tropical:) The wronging of thee is forbidden, or prohibited, to me. (S, TA.) And Harija Ealayohi Als~aHuwru (tropical:) The meal termed sHwr became forbidden, or prohibited, to him, (A, TA,) namely, a man fasting, and attended with difficulty, (A,) by reason of the straitness of the time thereof. (TA.) And Harijati AlS~alaApu (tropical:) Prayer became forbidden, or prohibited, (A, and TA as from the K, [but not found by me in the copies of the K,]) EalayohaA to her [by reason of legal impurity, as is shown in the A]. (A, TA.) ― -b6- Harija A_ilayohi (tropical:) He betook himself, or had recourse, to him, or it, for protection from a strait, or difficulty. (TA.) And Harija A_ilaY ka*aA wa ka*aA (assumed tropical:) He betook himself to such and such things. (TA.)

definition: He made him to betake himself to a narrow, or confined, place;
sourceDefinition: He made him to betake himself to a narrow, or confined, place; and so A^aHojarahu and A^aHoradahu . (TA.) And He made him (a dog or a beast of prey) to betake himself to a narrow, or confined, place, and then attacked him. (TA.) definition: (tropical:) A wood, or collection of trees;
sourceDefinition: (tropical:) A wood, or collection of trees; (S, K, TA;) so called because of their closeness: or dense and tangled trees: (TA:) or a thicket, or collection of dense and tangled trees, of the kind called salam , into which no one can penetrate; (AHeyth, Az, TA;) or of the samur and TaloH and Eawosaj and salam and sidor ; or of the sidor and olive and other trees: or a place in a wood where trees are dense and tangled, extending as far as a stone's throw: and also a tree which the pasturing animals cannot reach: (TA:) pl. ↓ HarajN (S, K) [or rather this is a coll. gen. n., of which HarajapN is the n. un.,] and HarajaAtN (S, A) and HiraAjN (S) and [of pauc.] A^aHoraAjN : (A, TA:) or ↓ HarajN signifies a place in which is a collection of trees, and where they are close together. definition: [ A petition for the putting down of a heavy burden from one: or, (tropical:) of the heavy burden of sin: or merely a putting down thereof: ] a subst.
sourceDefinition: [ A petition for the putting down of a heavy burden from one: or, (tropical:) of the heavy burden of sin: or merely a putting down thereof: ] a subst. from AstHT~hu wizorahu , explained above; as also ↓ HiT~iyTaY . (K.) It is said in the Kur [ii. 55, and vii. 161], wa quwluwA HiT~apN ; i. e. they were told to say HiT~apN for the purpose of asking thereby for the putting down of their heavy burdens from them, and they should be put down from them: (Ibn-Isráeel, TA:) the meaning is, And say ye, Put Thou down from us our heavy burdens, (S, TA,) or (tropical:) our sins: (Ibn-' Arafeh, K:) or [ and say ye, ] Our petition is HiT~apN ; i. e. that Thou wouldest put down from us our sins: (Aboo-Is- hák, K:) or, accord. to some, HiT~ap is a word which the children of Israel were commanded to say; and if they said it, their heavy burdens, or sins, were put down: (S, TA:) accord. to IAar, it is the saying laA A_il`ha A_il~aA A@ll~`hu : (TA:) or it means forgiveness: (I' Ab:) or our affair is an alighting and abiding in this town: (Bd in ii. 55:) and there is another reading, wa quwluwA HiT~apF , which is explained in two ways; either by making the verb to govern the noun, as though he had said, and say ye a saying which shall put down from you your heavy burdens, or (tropical:) sins; or by making the noun to be in the accus. case as an inf. n. meaning supplicating and petitioning [ that God may put down from you your heavy burdens, or (tropical:) sins ]; i. e. AuHoTuTi A@ll~ahum~a A^awozaAranaA HiT~apF : (TA:) but they changed this saying, (Fr, Sgh, K,) using for it a Nabathean expression; (Fr, TA;) saying hiT~iY sumohaAvFA , i. e. ” red wheat, “ (Sgh, K,) accord. to Es-Suddee and Mujáhid; or, accord. to IAar, HinoTapF $umoqaAyaA , i. e. ” good wheat. “ (Sgh, TA.) You say also, ↓ saA^alahu AlHiT~iyTaY , i. e. AlHiT~apa [ He asked of him the putting down of his heavy burden from him: or (tropical:) his sin ]. (TA.) And it is said in a trad., that when God tries a person with a trial in his body, huwa lahu HiT~apN , i. e. It is to him a mode of putting down from him his sins. (TA.) AlHiT~apu is also A name of the month of Ramadán, in the Gospel, or some other book: (Az, K, * TA:) because it puts down somewhat of the sin of him who observes the fast thereof. (Az, TA.) ― -b2- Also (tropical:) A decrease, or state of diminution, in respect of rank, or station: (TA:) [or low, or the lowest, rank, or station: for] ↓ AlHuTuTu , (K, TA,) which is its pl., (TA,) is explained as signifying, (K, TA,) on the authority of IAar, (TA,) maraAkibu Als~ifali , or correctly maraAtibu Als~ifali : (K, TA:) the latter [meaning (tropical:) the ranks, or stations, of the lowest, or meanest, of mankind, ] is the right reading, as verified by Az. (TA.)

(TA.) ― -b3- As a conventional term in grammar, [meaning Imitation, or conforming, in language,] it is of two kinds: HikaAyapu jumolapK [ The imitation of a proposition, or phrase ], and HikaAyapu muforadK [ The imitation of a single word ]: the former is of two sorts; one of which is termed HikaAyapu malofuwZK [ The imitation of a thing uttered ], whereof qaAluwA AlHamodu ll~`hi [They said, “ Praise be to God, ” (Kur vii. 41,)] is an ex.; and the other, HikaAyapu makotuwbK [ The imitation of a thing written ], whereof qaraA^otu EalaY faS~ihi muHam~adN rasuwlu A@ll~`hi [I read upon his ring-stone, “ Mohammad is the Apostle of God, ”] is an ex.: and the latter kind, also, (that of a single word,) is of two sorts; one of which is with the interrogative A^aY~N or mano , as when, to one who says, raA^ayotu rajulFA [pronounced rajulaA , I saw a man], you say, A^ay~aA [What (man)?], or manaA [Whom?], and the like, which sort is agreeable with a common rule; the other sort being without an interrogative, as the saying of one of the Arabs, to one who said, haAtaAni tamorataAni [These are two dates], daEonaA mino tamorataAni [Abstain thou from troubling us about two dates], which sort is anomalous. (El-Ashmoonee's Expos. of the Alfeeyeh of Ibn-Málik.) [ HikaAyapu SawotK signifies A word imitative of a sound; an onomatopœia: see Aisomu SawotK in art. smw .]

definition: Blackness: (S:) or intense blackness;
sourceDefinition: Blackness: (S:) or intense blackness; as also ↓ HulokapN ; (K;) like the colour of the crow, or raven: (TA:) [for] Halaku AlguraAbi signifies the blackness of the crow, or raven; as in the saying, A^asowadu mivolu Halaki AlguraAbi [ black like the blackness of the crow, or raven ]: (S:) or it means its Hanak [q. v.] : (K:) or if you say mvl Hanaki AlgrAb , you mean its beak; (S;) or the blackness of its feathers: (Er-Rághib, TA in art. Hnk :) or they said A^asowadu mino Halaki AlguraAbi [ blacker than the Hlk of the crow, or raven ]: or mn Hanaki AlgrAb : an Arab of the desert, being asked by Fr whether he said the latter or the former, answered that he never said the former: Umm-El-Heythem, being asked by AHát the same, answered that she said the former, and never the latter; (TA;) and she explained the former as meaning its two jaws and the part around them; adding that [the saying that it means] its beak is nought: and IDrd is related to have disallowed the saying mn Hnk AlgrAb : (TA in art. Hnk :) accord. to AZ, AlHalak means the colour; and AlHanak , the beak: some say that the n in the latter is a substitute for the l in the former; but others deny this. (TA.) In the saying of a poet, AlguraAbi ↓ midaAdN mivolu HaAlikapi [ Ink like the HAlkp of the crow, or raven ], cited by Th, HAlkp may be a dial. var. of Halak : or it may mean its feathers; its xaAfiyap or its qaAdimap or other feathers. (TA.)

definition: , (S, Msb, K,) aor.
sourceDefinition: , (S, Msb, K,) aor. and , inf. n. HanokN ; (Msb;) and ↓ Hn~khu , (S, Msb, K,) inf. n. taHoniykN ; (Mgh, Msb;) He chewed some dates, or some other thing (S, Mgh, Msb, K) of a similar kind, (Msb,) and rubbed therewith the Hanak [i. e. palate, or soft palate, ] of the child. (S, Mgh, Msb, K.) ― -b2- And Hanaka Alfarasa , aor. as above, (S, K,) and so the inf. n., (S,) He put a rope in the mouth of the horse; (S, K;) held by ISd to be derived from AlHanaku , though it is said that this is not the case; (TA;) as also ↓ AHtnkhu ; (S, K;) which signifies accord. to Yoo he put a rope in his mouth and led him: and thus Ibn- 'Arafeh explains the saying of Iblees, in the Kur [xvii. 64], *ur~iy~atahu A_il~aA qaliylFA ↓ laA^aHotanikan~a , i. e. (assumed tropical:) I will assuredly lead to obey me his progeny, except a few. (TA. [But see 8.]) ― -b3- And [hence,] Hanakatohu Als~in~u , inf. n. HanokN and HanakN , (K,) (tropical:) Age rendered him firm, or sound, in judgment, by means of experience: (TK:) or experiences rendered him firm, or sound, in judgment; (K, TA;) as also ↓ Hn~kthu , (Zj, S, K,) inf. n. taHoniykN ; (TA;) and ↓ AHnkthu , (Zj, S, K,) and ↓ AHtnkthu : (K:) this is said to be the case when the wisdom-tooth ( sin~u AlEaqoli ) grows forth: and accord. to Lth, Hanakatohu AlEaqoli signifies his teeth called A^asonaAnu AlEaqoli [ the wisdom-teeth ] grew forth. (TA.) And Hanakatohu AlA^umuwri (tropical:) Affairs did to him what is done to the horse by putting the rope in his mouth; i. e., rendered him experienced and submissive: or trained, or disciplined, and reformed, or improved, him; as also ↓ Hn~kth . (TA.) And Hanakahu Ald~ahoru (tropical:) Time, or fortune, tried, or proved, him, and taught him, and rendered him expert, or experienced, and well informed, or firm, or sound, in judgment. (IAar, TA.) ― -b4- And Hanaka Al$~aYo'a , (S, K,) inf. n. HanokN , (TA,) (tropical:) He understood the thing, and knew it soundly, thoroughly, or well; syn. fahimahu waA^aHokamahu ; (S, K, TA;) like laqifahu , inf. n. laqofN . (TA.)

definition: (tropical:) The locusts ate what was upon the land;
sourceDefinition: (tropical:) The locusts ate what was upon the land; (S, K, TA;) and consumed, or made an end of, its herbage: (S:) or gained the mastery over the land with the Hanak [here meaning the mouth ], and ate [ the produce of ] it, and extirpated it: (Er-Rághib, TA:) derived from AlHanaku , by which is sometimes meant “ the mouth, ” and “ the beak. ” ('Ináyeh, MF.) And AHtnk AlbaEiyru AlS~il~iyaAnapa (assumed tropical:) The camel pulled up by the roots the [ plant called ] Sl~yAnp . (Az, TA.) And AHtnk [for AHtnk Aln~abotu (assumed tropical:) He cropped the herbage ] is said of a young gazelle. (K voce $aSarN , q. v.) And AHtnkhu (assumed tropical:) He took his (a man's) property; (ISd, K;) as though he ate it with the Hanak . (ISd, TA.) And (assumed tropical:) He took it entirely; took the whole of it; namely, what another possessed. (ISd, TA.) And (tropical:) He gained the mastery over him, or it; got him, or it, in his power. (K, TA.) Accord. to Akh, laA^aHotinakan~a *ur~iy~atahu , in the Kur [xvii. 64, cited, and explained on the authority of Ibn-' Arafeh, above], means (tropical:) I will assuredly extirpate his progeny; and I will assuredly incline them [ to obey me ]: (TA:) or, accord. to Fr, (tropical:) I will assuredly gain the mastery over his progeny. (S, TA. *) ― -b2- See also 1, in three places. -A2- Also AHtnk [and ↓ tHn~k , the latter found by Reiske in this sense, as mentioned in Freytag's Lex.,] (tropical:) He (a man) was, or became, firm, or sound, in judgment, [ by means of experience: ] (S, TA:) or experienced and submissive, like the horse in whose mouth the rope has been put. (TA.)

definition: The part beneath the chin [ and lower jaw ], (S, Mgh,) of a man &c.
sourceDefinition: The part beneath the chin [ and lower jaw ], (S, Mgh,) of a man &c.: (S:) or [the palate, or soft palate; ] the interior of the upper part of the inside of the mouth, (K, TA,) of a man and of a beast: (TA:) and the lower part, from the extremity of the fore part of the two jaws, (K,) below these: (TA:) or the roof of the upper part of the mouth, (Zj in his “ Khalk el-Insán, ” El-Ghooree, Mgh, TA,) from which depends the lahaAp [or uvula ]: (Zj ubi suprà:) and also applied to the two jaws : (TA:) or, accord. to IAar, the Hanak is the lower part of the mouth, [ beneath the lower jaw, ] and the fqm is the upper part: and the HanakaAni are the upper and the lower: (Th, Az, Mgh, TA:) but HanakN is scarcely ever applied to the upper alone: [this art., however, shows instances in which it is thus applied:] (Az, TA:) it is masc.: (Msb:) pl. A^aHonaAkN , (Msb, K,) which is its only pl. form. (TA.) Sometimes, [as is often the case in modern Arabic,] The mouth is meant thereby. ('Ináyeh. MF.) And The beak: (S, 'Ináyeh:) Hanaku AlguraAba signifying the beak of the crow, or raven: or the blackness thereof: (K:) or the blackness of its feathers: (Er-Rághib, TA:) [whence the saying,] A^asowadu mivolu Hanaki AlguraAbi , (S,) or mino Hanaki AlguraAbi ; respecting which see HalakN . (TA.) ― -b2- And (tropical:) A party of men seeking after herbage in a district, or country, to pasture [ their animals ] upon it: (K, TA:) pl. A^aHonaAkN . (TA.) You say, maA taraka AlA^aHonaAku fiY A^aroDinaA $ayoy^FA , meaning (tropical:) The parties of men passing [ in search of herbage left not in our land anything ]. (TA.)

(TA.) HayoSN also signifies The retiring, or going back, from a thing. (S, TA.) [See also maHiySN , below.]

(S.) (Nh.) And A_in~aka lataHosibu EalaY~a AlA^aroDa HayoSFA bayoSFA , or, as some say, HySi bySi , [i. e., HayoSi bayoSi or HiySi biySi , meaning, Verily thou thinkest the earth to be straitened to me, so that I may not act as I please therein: &c.] (S.) ― -b2- HayoSa bayoSa also signifies The hole of the rat or mouse. (TA in art. byS .)

sourceDefinition: [ A kind of whirling plaything; ] a thing which a boy turns round by means of a thread, or string, in his hands, causing it to make a sound such as is termed dawiY~ : (S, K:) or a small piece of wood, or a slit, or split, reed or cane, in the middle of which is cut a notch, and which is then tied with a thread, or string, which being pulled, it turns round, and is heard to make a sound such as is termed Hafiyf : boys play with it; and it is also called xar~aArapN : (Lth, TA: [in the latter of which, in art. xr , the xr~Arp is said to be a piece of wood like the half of a sandal, tied with a thread or string, which, being put in motion, draws along the piece of wood and causes it to make a sound: ]) or a small, round, piece of skin, attached to which are two connected threads or strings, which being pulled by a boy, with his fingers, it turns round, causing a sound to be heard such as is termed dawiY~ : (EM p. 43:) pl. xa*aAriyfu . (S.) Imra-el-Keys likens to it a swift horse: (S:) and it is applied as an epithet to a horse; (Lth;) meaning Swift in his running, (Lth, K, TA,) or in going. (TA.) And one says, tarakati Als~uyuwfu raA^osahu xa*aAriyfa , meaning (assumed tropical:) The swords made his head to be pieces, each piece like the x*rwf . (S, K.) ― -b2- Clay kneaded, and made like sugar, ( yuEomalu $abiyhFA biAls~uk~ari , in the CK yuEomalu mnhu $abiyhFA biAls~uk~uri , [the latter reading evidently wrong, and the former I think doubtful,]) with which boys play. (K.) ― -b3- The piece of wood that is put [app. as a handle ] in the hole of the upper millstone. (TA.) ― -b4- A herd of camels: and one separate therefrom. (K.) ― -b5- Lightning gleaming, or shining brightly, in the clouds, and separate therefrom. (K.) ― -b6- Anything scattered from, or of, a thing. (L, O, K.) ― -b7- The xa*aAriyf of the hawodaj are The pieces of wood ( saqaAy^if ) with which the hwdj is made of a square form. (K.) [See also daAmigapN .]

(Msb.)

A property, quality, nature, or disposition: and a habit, or custom: (KL, PS, TK:) [and a practice, or an action: it is used in these various senses in different trads.: in one trad., avarice is termed a xaSolap ; and so is evilness of nature: in another, fasting, and praying: in another, the inflicting of castigation, and the executing of retaliation, in a mosque:] it signifies an excellent quality or the like; and a low, base, or mean, quality or the like; (K, TA;) in a man: (TA:) or its predominant application is to an excellent quality or the like: (K:) so in the M: (TA:) [it is said that] it is used only in commendation; whereas xal~apN is used in relation to good and evil: (Ham p. 525:) [but this is a mistake, as I have shown above:] accord. to Az, it signifies the states, or conditions, of things or affairs: (TA:) [or this is a signification of the pl.:] the pl. is xiSaAlN (K) and xaSalaAtN ; (TA;) [and ↓ xaSaAy^ilu is a pl. pl., i. e. pl. of xiSaAlN , with which it is explained in the KL as syn.: see an ex. in a verse cited voce dafiy^N .] -A2- A hitting of the target; (K;) in shooting: (TA:) or, (K,) as also ↓ xaSolN , (JK, K,) in a shooting-match, (JK,) it is [ a shot ] in the case in which the arrow goes close by the target: (JK, K: *) thus accord. to Lth, who says that the former explanation is erroneous; (TA;) [as appears also from the assertion that] what are termed xaSolataAni , in a shooting-match, are reckoned as equivalent to a shot that goes right to the target. (T, K, TA.) ― -b2- And accord. to Sgh, A single act of overcoming in a shooting-match. (TA.) -A3- Also, and ↓ xuSolapN , A raceme, or bunch, of grapes or the like; syn. EunoquwdN . (K.) ― -b2- And (both words) A stick, branch, or twig, ( EuwdN ,) in which are thorns. (K.) ― -b3- And xaSolapN and ↓ xaSalapN , or this latter only, The extremity of a fresh, pliant, soft, or tender, twig, or rod: (K, * TA:) and (some say, TA) a soft and tender twig or rod, of the [ species of mimosa called ] EurofuT : (K, TA:) and ↓ xaSolN [of which xaSolapN is the n. un.] signifies the slender extremities and branches of the EurofuT : (JK:) and ↓ xuSolapN , a soft and tender branch of any tree: (T, TA:) and [its pl.] xuSalN , the pendent extremities of trees. (S, TA.)

(TA.) ― -b2- See also xuSolapN . -A2- And for the pl. xaSaAy^ilu see also xaSolapN .

sourceDefinition: , [aor. ,] inf. n. xafoDN , He lowered it; depressed it; namely, a thing; contr. of rafaEahu . (A.) ― -b2- He (God) abased him; (S, Msb;) namely, an unbeliever. (Msb.) You say, Aall~`hu yaxofiDu mano ya$aA='u wayorfaEu (assumed tropical:) God abaseth whom He will, and exalteth.. (S.) ― -b3- xafaDa janaAHahu He (a bird) [ lowered or] relaxed his wing, and contracted it to his side, in order that he might rest, or cease, from his flying. (TA.) ― -b4- And the same phrase, (tropical:) He made himself gentle, easy to deal with, compliant, or obsequious. (TA.) It is said in the Kur [xv. 88], waA@xofiDo xanaA=Haka lilomuw^ominiyna (tropical:) And make thyself gentle, &c., to the believers: (Jel, TA:) or be thou condescending to the believers, and treat them with gentleness. (Bd.) And again, in the same [xvii. 25], (TA,) waA@xofiDo lahumaA janaAHa Al*~ul~i mina Alr~aHomapi (tropical:) And humble, or abase, thou thyself to them both, from compassion: (Bd, K, TA:) or make thyself submissively gentle to them both, from compassion: (Bd, * Jel:) or there is a transposition in the sentence, and the meaning is wAxfD lhmA jnAH AlrHmp mn Al*l~ [ and make thyself compassionately gentle to them both, from submissiveness ]. (O, K.) ― -b5- A_in~a A@ll~`ha yaxofiDu AlqisoTa wayarofaEuhu , in a trad., means Verily God, at one time, bringeth down to the ground the just, or equitable; and, at another time, exalteth him: (ISh:) or maketh ample [ the means of subsistence &c.] to whom He will, and maketh scanty to whom He will: (Sgh, K:) or maketh little the portion of the means of subsistence which is the share of any created being, and maketh it much. (TA in art. qsT , q. v.). xafoDu AlEadoli warafoEuhu is also explained as signifying The just's being overcome by the unjust, when men act corruptly, and the just's overcoming the unjust, when they repent, and act righteously. (TA.) [See also art. rfE .] ― -b6- maAzaAlato taxofiDuniY A^aroDN watarofaEuniY A^uxoraY Hat~aY waSalotu A_ilayokumo (tropical:) [app. means One land ceased not to make me go a gentle pace, and another to make me go a vehement pace, until I came unto you: for xafaDa as relating to pace is probably not only intrans., as it will be seen to be below, but also trans., like its contr. rafaEa : or it may mean one land ceased not to make me go down, and another to make me go up, &c.; though its being tropical if having this meaning may be doubted]. (A, TA.) ― -b7- xafaDa Sawotahu , (A, Msb,) aor. , (Msb,) inf. n. xafoDN , (S, Msb, K,) (tropical:) He (a man, Msb) lowered his voice; (S, K;) did not raise his voice; (Msb;) [ contr. of rafaEahu , as is indicated in the A.] ― -b8- [In most of the above-mentioned senses, ↓ xaf~aDa is nearly; if not exactly, syn. with xafaDa .] ― -b9- xafaDa AlHarofa fiY AlA_iEoraAbi (assumed tropical:) He made the [final] letter to have kesreh, in inflection. (Msb.) xafoDN is syn. with jar~N [q. v.] (S, K) in the inflection of words: (K:) these two terms, in the inflection of words, are like kasorN in the non-inflection, in the conventional language of the grammarians. (S.) -A2- xafuDa Eayo$uhu , aor. , [inf. n., app., xafoDN , q. v. infrà,] (assumed tropical:) His life was, or became, easy; free from trouble or inconvenience, and toil or fatigue; tranquil; and plentiful. (JK, K. *) ― -b2- xafuDa SawotuhaA (assumed tropical:) Her (a woman's) voice was, or became, [ low, soft, ] gentle and easy. (TA.) ― -b3- xafaDato (assumed tropical:) She (a woman) was, or became, low, soft, or gentle, in voice. (TA.) ― -b4- xafaDati AlA_ibilu , [inf. n. xafoDN and maxofuwDN , like the contr. rafoEN and marofuwEN , (see xafoDN below,)] (tropical:) The camels went a gentle pace; (A, TA;) contr. of rafaEat . (A.) ― -b5- xafaDa biAlmakaAni , aor. , (assumed tropical:) He remained, stayed, or abode, in the place. (K.) [See also xaAfiDN .] A poet says, [app. using the verb in this sense,] A_in~a $akoliY waA_in~a $akolaki $at~aY faA@lozamiY AlxuS~a waA@xofiDiY taboyaDiD~iY [ Verily the like of me, and verily the like of thee, are different: therefore keep thou to the booth which is our home, and remain at rest: thou wilt become fair ]: the last word is for taboyaD~iY ; a D being added. (S.) ― -b6- xafaDa , inf. n. xufuwDN , also signifies (assumed tropical:) He died; said of a man. (TA.) -A3- xafaDati AljaAriyapa , [aor. and inf. n. as below,] She circumcised the girl: [see baZorN :] (Msb:) xafaDotu AljaAriyapa , (S,) or xufiDati AljaAriyapu , (A, K,) is like xatanotu AlgulaAma , (S,) or, xutina AlgulaAmu : (A, K:) the former verb applies only to a girl: (Msb, K:) or you say sometimes, xfaDa AlS~abiY~a , aor. , inf. n. xafoDN , meaning he circumcised the boy. (TA.)

sourceDefinition: : [see xafaDa , (of which it is the inf. n.,) throughout. ― -b2- ] A state of abatement, or remissness, or the like: (A, TA:) (assumed tropical:) ease; repose; freedom from trouble or inconvenience, and toil or fatigue; tranquillity; quietness; quietude; stillness; syn. daEapN ; (S, A, K;) and raAHapN ; (Msb;) and sukuwnN ; (TA;) of life: (Msb:) or ampleness of the circumstances of life; (El-Marzookee, Msb;) plentifulness and pleasantness thereof: (El-Marzookee:) softness, delicateness, or easiness: (A, TA:) pleasant life: (L:) and [in like manner] ↓ xafiyDapN , softness, delicateness, or easiness, of life; and ampleness of the circumstances thereof: (TA:) and the former, (assumed tropical:) gentleness and easiness of voice. (TA.) You say, humo fiY xafoDK mina AlEayo$i (assumed tropical:) They are in an easy, or a tranquil, [or a plentiful and pleasant, or a soft or delicate, ] state of life. (S.) [This phrase is said in the A to be tropical; but why, I do not see; since xafoDN in the sense of daEapN is proper accord. to the same authority.] And huwa fiY xafoDi AlEayo$i (assumed tropical:) He is in an ample, and an easy, or a tranquil, state of life. (Msb.) And a poet says, laA yamonaEan~aka xafoDa AlEayo$i fiYdaEapK nuzuwEu nafosK A_ilaY A^aholK waA^awoTaAni taloqaY bikul~i bilaAdK A_ino Halalota bihaA A^aholFA biA^aholK wajiyraAnFA bijiyraAni (Ham p. 137, and Sgh;) i. e. (assumed tropical:) [ Let not yearning of soul for family and homes prevent thee from enjoying ] ampleness of the circumstances of life, or plentifulness and pleasantness thereof, in ease and tranquillity: [ thou wilt find in every country, if thou take up thine abode in it, a family for a family, and neighbours for neighbours: ] (ElMarzookee, MF:) another reading, which is preferable, though each is allowable, is nizaAEu in the place of nuzuwEu . (Ham ubi suprà.) ― -b3- [It is also used as an epithet; app. for *uw xfoDK .] You say, Eayo$N xafoDN , (JK, TA,) and ↓ xaAfiDN , (S, A, K,) and ↓ xafiyDN , and ↓ maxofuwDN , (TA,) (assumed tropical:) An easy, or a tranquil, (JK, S, K, TA,) and plentiful, (JK, TA,) and soft, or delicate, (TA,) life: (JK, S, &c.:) and ↓ maxofiDN signifies the same as xafoDN . (TA: there mentioned in the same place as here.) [It is said in the A, that Ey$ ↓ xAfD is like Eiy$apN raADiyapN , (meaning that it is for Eayo$N maxofuwDN ,) and that it is tropical.] ― -b4- Also (tropical:) A gentle pace; contr. of rafoEN ; (S, A, * K;) and so ↓ maxofuwDN ; (S, * A;) contr. of marofuwEN . (A, TA.) [See xafaDati AlA_ibilu .] ― -b5- Also Low, or depressed, land: (TA:) and [in like manner] ↓ xaAfiDapN a low, or depressed, tract ( taloEapN muTomay^in~apN ) of land: (ISh, K:) raAfiEapN signifying [the contr., i. e.] a hard and elevated tract of land. (ISh.)

sourceDefinition: , aor. , (TA,) inf. n. xamorN , (K,) He veiled, covered, or concealed, a thing; (K, * TA;) as also ↓ xm~r , inf. n. taxomiyrN , (Mgh, Msb,) which also signifies he covered over a thing; (S, Msb, K;) and ↓ Axmr , (TA,) inf. n. A_ixomaArN . (K.) [Hence,] xamarahaA [and app. ↓ xm~rhA also, for the quasi-pass. is txm~rt as well as Axtmrt , He veiled her with a muffler; ] he put on her a ximaAr . (A.) And A_inaA='ahu ↓ xm~r , and wajohahu , He covered over his vessel, and his face. (S.) And bayotahu ↓ xm~r He concealed his house, or chamber, or tent, [meaning its interior,] and ordered it aright. (TA, from a trad.) And AlA^aroDu Ean~iY ↓ A^axomaratohu and min~iY and EalaY~a The land, or ground, concealed him, or it, from me. (K.) And ↓ Axmrhu (assumed tropical:) He concealed it, or conceived it, in him mind. (S, K.) And fulaAnN EalaY~a Zin~apF ↓ Axmr (assumed tropical:) Such a one concealed, or conceived, in his mind a suspicion, or an evil opinion, of me. (T, TA.) And xamara $ahaAdatahu , (S, Msb,) and ↓ xm~rhA , (A, Mgh,) and ↓ AxmrhA , (TA,) (tropical:) He concealed his testimony. (S, A, Mgh, Msb, TA.) And Alxamoru taxomuru AlEaqola (assumed tropical:) Wine veils [or obscures ] the intellect; (K;) and so ↓ tuxaAmiruhu , lit. covers it: (Msb:) or the latter signifies (assumed tropical:) Infects it; [as though acting like leaven; and if so, from xamara AlEajiyna , which see in what follows; nearly the same as “ intoxicates, ” which properly signifies “ empoisons, ” or “ infects with poison; ”] syn. tuxaAliTuhu . (S, * K. [See xamorN .] -A2- xamira , aor. , (S, K,) inf. n. xamarN , (S,) He became concealed, or hidden; or he concealed, or hid, himself; (S, K;) Ean~iY from me; (S;) as also ↓ xAmr , (S, K,) inf. n. muxaAmarapN ; (K;) and ↓ Axmr : (K:) or this last signifies he concealed, or hid, himself in a xamar [or covert of trees or the like ]. (TA.) One says also, xamira Ean~iY Alxabaru (assumed tropical:) The news, or story, became concealed from me. (S.) And one says to the hyena, A^um~a EaAmirK ↓ xaAmiriY Hide thyself, O Umm-'Ámir: (S, K:) which is a prov.: (TA:) and is said to be also a phrase used as a surname of the hyena, in the manner of taA^ab~aTa $ar~FA . (Ham p. 242.) And HaDaAjiro A^ataAki maA tuHaA*iro ↓ xaAmiriY [ Hide thyself, O hyena: what thou fearest has come to thee ]: thus we have found it: (K:) and this is the reading commonly obtaining accord. to the authors on proverbs: (TA:) but it should properly be xaAmirN [and A^ataAka ] or tuHaA*iryna . (K.) ― -b2- xamarN also signifies The becoming changed, or altered, from a former state or condition. (K.) You say, xamira Al$~aYo'u The thing became changed, &c. (TK.) -A3- xamara AlEajiyna , (Ks, S, A, Msb, K,) aor. (S, Msb, K) and , (S, K,) inf. n. xamorN , (S, Msb, K,) [ He leavened the dough; ] he put xumorap , (Ks, A,) or xamiyr , (S, A, Msb,) into the dough; (Ks, S, A, Msb, TA;) as also ↓ xm~rhu : (TA:) or he left the dough until it became good [or mature ]; (K;) and in like manner, accord. to the K, AlT~iyna [ the clay, or mud : see faTara ]: or, as in other lexicons, AlT~iyba [ the perfume ]; (TA;) and the like; as also ↓ xm~rhu , inf. n. taxomiyrN , in relation to any of these things; and ↓ Axmrhu in relation to the first [and probably to the others also]: (K:) and xamara Aln~abiy*a [ he fermented the beverage called nby* ;] he put xumorap into the nby* . (A.) [Mtr says, in the Mgh, AlEaSiyra ↓ xam~ara I have not found, nor ↓ txm~r as its quasi-pass.] ― -b2- xamarahu , aor. , (TA,) inf. n. xamorN ; (K;) and ↓ Axmrhu ; (Mgh;) He gave him (namely, a man, and a beast, such as a horse and the like, TA) wine ( xamor ) to drink. (K, * Mgh, TA.) ― -b3- xumira , (Mgh, TA,) inf. n. xamorN , (TA,) He suffered, or was affected with, xumaAr [i. e. the remains of intoxication ]. (Mgh, TA.) [See also 5.] -A4- xamarahu , aor. , (AA, S,) inf. n. xamorN , (K,) He was ashamed for himself, or of himself, or was bashful, or shy, with respect to him; was abashed at him, or shy of him. (AA, S, K. *)

[See 3.] So in the trad. of Mo'ádh, mano A@sotaxomara qawomFA A^aw~aluhumo A^aHoraArN wajiyraAnN musotaDoEafuwna falahu maA qaSara fiY bayotihi [ Whosoever hath made slaves, or taken as slaves, persons the first state of whomhath been that of freemen and neighbours, regarded as weak, to him shall belong what he hath held in possession in his house or tent ]: (S, * L:) i. e., hath taken them by force, and obtained possession of them: (S:) meaning, whosoever hath made slaves, or taken as slaves, persons in the Time of Ignorance, and then El-Islám hath come, to him shall belong those whom he hath held in possession in his house or tent: they shall not go from his hand. (Az, TA.) Mohammad Ibn-Ketheer says, This is a phrase known to us in ElYemen, where any other is scarcely ever used [in its stead]. (S.)
