definition: [ Wine: or grape-wine :] what intoxicates, of the expressed juice of grapes: (ISd, K:) or the juice of grapes when it has effervesced, and thrown up froth, and become freed therefrom, and still:...
sourceDefinition: [ Wine: or grape-wine :] what intoxicates, of the expressed juice of grapes: (ISd, K:) or the juice of grapes when it has effervesced, and thrown up froth, and become freed therefrom, and still: (Mgh:) or it has a common application to intoxicating expressed juice of anything: (K, TA:) or any intoxicating thing, that clouds, or obscures, (lit. covers, ) the intellect; as some say: (Mgh, * Msb: [but see what follows:]) and the general application is the more correct, because xamor was forbidden when there was not in El-Medeeneh any xamor of grapes; the beverage of its inhabitants being prepared only from dates in their green and small state, or full-grown but unripe, or fresh and ripe, or dried: (K, * TA:) or the arguing thus, from this fact alone, requires consideration: (MF:) AHn says, it is (assumed tropical:) sometimes prepared from grains: but ISd holds this to be an improper signification: (TA:) it is also sometimes applied to the (assumed tropical:) beverage called nabiy* , like as nby* is sometimes applied to wine expressed from grapes: (L in art. nb* :) applied to (tropical:) expressed juice from which xamor [ properly so called ] is made, [i. e., to must, or unfermented nabiy* ,] it is tropical: it is so used in a trad. in which xamor is said to have been sold by [a companion of Mohammad named] Samurah: xamor [in its proper acceptation] is so called because it veils ( taxomuru , i. e. tasoturu ,) the intellect: (K:) or because it infects ( tuxaAmiru , i. e. tuxaAliTu ,) the intellect: (S, K:) [as though acting like leaven: (see 1:)] so said 'Omar: (TA:) or because it is left until it has become mature [and fermented]; (K;) or until its odour has changed: (IAar, S:) [see 8:] the proper application of the root is to denote “ covering, ” and “ commingling in a hidden manner: ” (Sgh, Er-Rághib, TA:) it is of the fem. gender, and sometimes masc.: (Msb, K:) you say huwa Alxamoru as well as hiYa Alxamoru : but As does not allow it to be masc.: (Msb:) and ↓ xamorapN signifies the same: (K:) [or a kind of wine: ] or xamorN and xamorapN are like tamorN and tamorapN ; [the former a coll. gen. n., and the latter its n. un.;] (S;) and xamorapN [thus] signifies some wine; lit., a portion of xamor : (Msb:) the pl. of xamorN is xumuwrN . (S, Msb.) You say [also] SirofN ↓ xamorapN [ Some pure, or unmixed, wine; using a masc. epithet, contr. to rule]. (S.) ― -b2- [Hence the saying,] maA Einoda fulaAnK xal~N walaA xamorN , (S,) or maA huwa bixal~K walaA xamorK , (K,) (tropical:) Such a one, (S,) or he, (K,) possesses neither good nor evil: (S, K:) [or neither evil nor good: for] AA says that some of the Arabs make Alxamoru to be good, and Alxal~u to be evil; and some of them make Alxmr to be evil, and Alxl~ to be good. (Har p. 153.) ― -b3- xamorN also signifies (assumed tropical:) Grapes; (AHn, M, K;) in the dial. of ElYemen:) (M:) like as EinabN signifies “ wine ” in that dial. (AHn, TA in art. Enb .) It is said in the Kur [xii. 36], A_in~iY A^araAniY A^aEoSiru xamorFA Verily I thought myself pressing grapes: (ISd:) or the meaning is, pressing out wine from grapes. (Ibn- 'Arafeh.)

definition: A covert of trees &c.
sourceDefinition: A covert of trees &c. : (ISk, S, Mgh, K:) or a place where the ground is eaten away by a torrent, or an oblong tract of sand collected together and elevated, forming a place for concealment: (ISk, S:) and a hollow, or cavity, in which a wolf conceals himself: and tangled trees. (TA.) You say, tawaAraY AlS~ayodu min~iY fiY xamari AlwaAdiY [ The game, or wild animal or animals, concealed itself, or themselves, from me in the covert, &c., of the valley ]. (S.) And huwa yadib~u lahu AlD~araA='a wa yamo$iY lahu Alxamara (assumed tropical:) [ He creeps to him in the thicket, or place overgrown with trees; and he walks to him in the covert of trees, &c.: see Freytag's Arab. Prov. 913]: speaking of a man when he deceives, or circumvents, his companion. (S.) And jaA='anaA EalaY xamorK and ↓ ElY ximorapK (assumed tropical:) He came to us secretly; unexpectedly; clandestinely. (K.) ― -b2- Hence, (S,) xamarN and ↓ xumaArN and ↓ xamaArN (S, K) and ↓ xamorapN (K) (assumed tropical:) A crowding, (S,) or congregation, (K,) and multitude, of men or people. (S, K.) You say, Aln~aAsi ↓ daxala fiY xamaAri and ↓ xamaArihimo , dial. vars. of gumaAr and gamaAr , i. e. (tropical:) He entered among the crowding and multitude of the men or people; (S;) and in like manner, fY ↓ xamarotihimo and gamarotihimo ; (TA;) as also fY xamarihimo and gamarihimo : (TA in art. gmr :) or among such [ a crowd ] of the people as hid him. (ISk, S.)

definition: ― -b2- Also a dial.
sourceDefinition: : see xamiyrN , in two places. ― -b2- Also a dial. var. of gumorapN [q. v.], A thing [or composition ] which is used as a liniment for beautifying the complexion; (S;) [the plant called ] waros and certain perfumes which a woman uses as a liniment (so in the K, or applies as a liniment to her face, as in other lexicons, TA) to beautify her face. (K.) -A2- Pain, and headache, and annoyance, occasioned by wine ( xamor , for which in some copies of the K we find Hum~aY erroneously put, TA); as also ↓ xumaArN : or the intoxication thereof, which has infected ( xaAlaTa ) [ a person ]; (K;) and so ↓ xumaArN : (TA:) or this latter signifies the remains of intoxication: (S:) pl. of the former xumarN . (TA.) ― -b2- See also xamorapN . -A3- A small pot or jar: and a vessel for leaven. (KL.) -A4- A small mat, (S, A, * Mgh, Msb, K,) [ of an oblong shape, ] large enough for a man to prostrate himself upon it, (Mgh, Msb,) used for that purpose [ in prayer ], (S, A,) made of palm-leaves (S, K) woven ( turomalu ) with threads or strings: (S:) so called because it veils the ground from the face of the person praying [upon it]: (Zj, * Mgh:) or because its threads or strings are hidden by its palm-leaves. (TA.)

sourceDefinition: A hiding, or concealing, oneself: (IAar, TA:) [or, accord. to analogy, a mode, or manner, of doing so. ] ― -b2- See also xamarN . ― -b3- A mode, manner, or way, of wearing the ximaAr . (K, * TA.) You say, A_in~ahaA laHasanapu Alximorapi [ Verily she has a beautiful mode of wearing the xmAr ]. (S.) And hence the saying of 'Omar to Mo'áwiyeh, maA A^a$obaha Eayonaka biximorapi hinodK [ How like is thine eye to Hind's (when she practises her) mode of wearing the xmAr !]. (TA.) Hence also, (TA,) A_in~a AlEawaAna laA tuEal~amu Alximorapa [ Verily she who has had a husband will not require to be taught the mode of wearing the xmAr ]: (S, K, * TA:) a prov., (S, TA,) applied to him who is experienced and knowing: (K:) i. e. the experienced woman is not to be taught how she should act. (TA.) -A2- See also xamorapN .

sourceDefinition: [ A woman's muffler, or veil, with which she covers her head and the lower part of her face, leaving exposed only the eyes and part or the whole of the nose : such is the xmAr worn in the present day: a kind of veil which is called in Turkish ya$omaqo ; as in the TK:) a woman's headcovering; (Mgh, TA;) a piece of cloth with which a woman covers her head; (Msb;) i. q. naSiyfN , (K,) pertaining to a woman; (S) as also ↓ ximir~N : (Th, K:) and any covering of a thing; anything by which a thing is veiled, or covered: (K:) pl. [of pauc.] A^axomirapN (K) and [of mult.] xumurN (Msb, K) and xumorN . (K.) ― -b2- Also A man's turban; because a man covers his head with it in like manner as a woman covers her head with her xmAr : when he disposes it in the Arab manner, he turns [a part of] it under the jaws [nearly in the same manner in which a woman disposes her xmAr ]. (TA.) [Hence,] maA $am~a ximaAraka , a prov., (TA,) [meaning] (assumed tropical:) What hath changed thee from the state in which thou wast? What hath befallen thee? (K.)

sourceDefinition: , aor. , inf. n. daA^olN (S, M, K) and daA^alN (K [perhaps a mistake for the next, which is well known but not mentioned in the K, but see *aA^ala ,]) and daA^alaAnN (S, M) and daA^alaY , (M, K,) He walked, or went, in a weak manner, (M, K,) and with haste: (M:) or he ran with short steps: (M, K:) or he walked, or went, in a brisk, or sprightly, manner: (K:) or he walked, or went, as though labouring in his gait, by reason of briskness, or sprightliness: (M:) [or he went along by little and little, stealthily, lest he should make a sound to be heard: for] daA^olN is syn. with xatolN : or, accord. to AZ, it signifies the walking, or going, in a manner resembling that which is termed xatolN ; and in the manner of him who is heavily burdened, or overburdened: and As, in describing the manner in which horses go, explains daA^alaAnN as signifying the walking, or going, with short steps, and in an unusual manner, as though heavily burdened, or overburdened. (S.) definition: A hollow, or cavity, or a deep hollow or cavity, in the ground, and in the lower parts of valleys, narrow, and then widening: (As, T, S, O:) or a [ hollow such as is termed ] qaEor , in the ground,...
sourceDefinition: A hollow, or cavity, or a deep hollow or cavity, in the ground, and in the lower parts of valleys, narrow, and then widening: (As, T, S, O:) or a [ hollow such as is termed ] qaEor , in the ground, curving, or winding, or uneven, resembling a well, narrow at the mouth, and then widening; or it may be not widening: (Ham p. 477:) or, as also ↓ duHolN , a hole ( naqobN ) narrow in the mouth and wide in the lower part, so that one may walk therein, (K, TA,) having a bending or the like, (TA,) and sometimes producing sidor [or lote-trees ]: or a place into which one may enter beneath a jurof [or water-worn bank ]; or in the width of the side of a well, in its lower part; (K;) and the like in a watering-place: all these explanations in the K are found in the M: (TA:) or each, (accord. to the K,) or daHolN , (accord. to the TA,) signifies [or rather signifies also] (assumed tropical:) a hole in [ any of ] the tents of the Arabs of the desert, made for the purpose of a woman's entering into it when a man enters [ the tent ]; (M, K;) so called as being likened to the daHol [commonly thus termed]: (TA:) and a kind of reservoir ( maSonaEN ) that collects water: (K:) Az describes, as seen by him, at El-Khalsà, in the district of Ed-Dahnà, many a daHol , being a natural subterranean cavity extending in an even manner, and then becoming hollowed out on the right and left, sometimes narrow and sometimes wide, in smooth rock, and leading to an abyss ( jaw~ ) of water, of extent and abundance unknown because of the darkness of the dHl beneath the earth, sweet and clear and cold and pleasant to drink because of rain-water that had flowed thither from above, and collected therein: (TA:) and daHolN also signifies a lateral hollow ( laHodN ) of a grave: (TA in art. tw : [in this sense, perhaps formed by transposition:]) ↓ daHiylapN , also, signifies a hollow, or cavity, in the ground; like daHolN ; or like the daHol : (Ibn-'Abbád, TA:) the pl. [of pauc.] of dHl is A^adoHaAlN (S, K) and A^adoHulN (K) and [of mult.] duHuwlN and diHaAlN and duHolaAnN . (S, K.)

definition: , (S, Mgh, Msb, K,) of the measure fiEolalN , (Msb, MF,) of which it has been said that there are only three other instances, but there are many more;
sourceDefinition: , (S, Mgh, Msb, K,) of the measure fiEolalN , (Msb, MF,) of which it has been said that there are only three other instances, but there are many more; (MF;) an arabicized word, (S, Msb,) from the Pers. [ diramo ]; (S;) also pronounced ↓ dirohimN , (S, Msb, K,) but this is of rare occurrence; (TA;) and ↓ dirohaAmN , (S, K,) which is more rare; (TA;) A certain silver coin; (Mgh, Msb;) like as diynaArN signifies a certain gold coin: (Mgh:) [and the weight thereof; i. e. a drachm, or dram: ] its weight is six dawaAniyq [or dániks ]; (Msb, and K in art. mk ;) i. e., the weight of the diroham A_isolaAmiY~ : but in the Time of Ignorance, some dirhems were light, being four dwAnyq ; and these were called Tabariy~apN : and some were heavy, being eight dwAnyq ; and these were called Eabodiy~apN , or bagoliy~apN : and of these two they made two that were equal; so that each drhm was six dwAnyq : this is said to have been done by 'Omar: or, accord. to another account, some dirhems were of the weight of twenty carats, and were called the weight of ten [i. e. of ten dániks ]; and some were of the weight of ten [ carats ], and were called the weight of five; and some were of the weight of twelve [ carats ], and were called the weight of six; and they put the three weights together, and called the third part thereof the weight of seven: and one of the weights of the drhm before El-Islám was twelve carats, which is six dwAnyq : but the drhm AslAmY~ is sixteen carats; the dAnq of this being a carat and two thirds: (Msb:) or dirhems should be fourteen carats [i. e. seven dániks ]; ten being of the weight of seven mavaAqiyl [or mithkáls]: in the Time of Ignorance, some were heavy, [equal to] mvAqyl ; and some were light, [called] Tabariy~apN ; and when they were coined in the age of El-Islám, they made of the heavy and the light two dirhems, so that ten became equal to seven mvAqyl : A 'Obeyd says that this was done in the time [of the dynasty] of the sons of Umeiyeh: (El-Karkhee, cited in the Mgh:) [see also De Sacy's “ Chrest. Arabe, ” sec. ed., vol. ii. p. 110 of the Arabic text, and p. 282 of the transl.; where it is further stated, on the authority of Ibn-Khaldoon, that the diroham magoribiY~ was three dwAnyq ; and the yamaniY~ , one dAnq ; and, as is said in the Msb, that 'Omar adopted the mean between the bglY~ and the TbrY~ , making the drhm to be six: ] the pl. (of drhm , S) is daraAhimu and (of drhAm , S) daraAhiymu . (S, K.) [The former of these pls. is often used as signifying Money, cash, or coin, in an absolute sense.] The dim. is ↓ durayohimN and ↓ durayohiymN : the latter held by Sb to be anomalous; for he says that it is as though it were formed from dirohaAmN , though this was not used by them. (TA.) ― -b2- Hence, as being likened thereto, [i. e., to the coin thus called,] (TA,) dirohamN signifies also (assumed tropical:) A Hadiyqap [app. as meaning a round piece of land surrounded by a fence or the like, or by elevated land; for this is one of the significations of HadiyqapN ]. (K.) [It is said that] this is taken from the saying of 'Antarah, [describing shower of copious rain,] fatarakona kul~a HadiyqapK kaAld~irohami [ So that they left every ridged-round spot of ground like the drhm ]. (TA.) [But accord. to one reading, he said, kul~a qaraArapK ; meaning, as is said in the EM, p. 227, “ every round hollow; ” and likening such a hollow to the drhm because of its roundness, and the clearness and whiteness of its water.]

Aimotad~a : (TK:) and [ it continued, lasted, endured, or remained, long; ] its time was, or became, long: (TA:) and i. q. baqiYa [as syn. with vabata (explained above) and as meaning it continued, lasted, or existed, incessantly, always, endlessly, or for ever; it was, or became, permanent, perpetual, or everlasting ]: (Msb in art. bqY :) and ↓ AstdAm signifies the same as dAm [in all of these senses]: (TA:) [but Mtr says,] AstdAm Als~afaru [ The journey continued, or continued long, ] is not of established authority. (IAar, M.) Dhu-r-Rummeh says, (de scribing a wild bull, T, TA,) Hat~aY A_i*aA daw~amato fiY AlA^aroDi raAjaEahu kiborN wa lawo $aA='a naj~aY nafosahu Alharabu [ Until, when they went far in the land, pride returned to him: but, had he pleased, flight had saved his blood: J, however, assigns to the verb in this instance another signification, as will be seen below]. (M, TA.) ― -b3- dw~m said of a bird, (T, M, K,) inf. n. tadowiymN , (T, S,) (tropical:) It circled (Lth, T, S, M, K, TA) in the sky, (Lth, T, M, K,) as also ↓ tdAwm , (KL,) [or ↓ tadw~m , (see mutadaw~imaAtN ,)] to rise high towards the sky; (S;) as also ↓ AstdAm : (M, K:) or circled in the sky, (M,) or flew, (T, * K,) without moving its wings; (T, M, K;) like the kite and the aquiline vulture: (T, TA:) or put itself into a state of commotion in its flying. (TA. [See also 1, near the end of the paragraph.]) Dhu-r-Rummeh makes Alt~adowiym to be on the earth, or ground, in the verse cited above in this paragraph; [as though the meaning were, (assumed tropical:) Until, when they went round &c.;] As disallows this, and asserts that one says only daw~aY fiYAlA^aroDi , and daw~ama fiY Als~amaA='i ; but some affirm that Alt~adowiymu fiYAlA^aroDi is correct; and say that hence is de rived ↓ Ald~uw~aAmapu , meaning “ the round thing [or top] which the boy throws, and makes to revolve, or spin, upon the ground, by means of a string; ” though others say that this is so called from the phrase daw~amotu Alqidora [explained below], because, by reason of the quickness of its revolving, or spinning, it seems as though it were at rest: and tadowaAmN is like tadowiymN : some, however, say that tadowiymu Alkalobi signifies the dog's going far in flight: (S:) AHeyth says that, accord. to As, Alt~adowiymu is only the act of a bird in the sky: (T, TA:) AAF says that, accord. to some, Alt~adowiymu is in the sky, and Alt~adowiyapu is on the earth, or ground; but accord. to others, the reverse is the case; and this, he says, is the truth in his opinion. (M, TA. [See also daw~aYa in art. dwY .]) ― -b4- You say also, daw~amati , Al$~amosu , (M, K,) or dw~mt Al$ms fY Als~amaA'i , (T,) or fiYkabidi Als~amaA='i , (S,) i. e. daArato fiY Als~amaA='i [or dArt fY kbd AlsmA' , lit. (tropical:) The sun spun in the sky, or in the middle of the sky; meaning, was as though it were spinning ]; (T, M, K;) or was as though it were motionless [&c.]: (T, S:) and hence is [said to be] derived the word ↓ duw~aAmapN applied to the boy's revolving, or spinning, thing. (T.) Dhu-r-Rummeh says, (describing the [insect called] junodab , [generally said to be a species of locust,] TA in art. rmD ) maEoraworiyFA ramaDa Alr~aDoraADi yarokuDuhu waAl$~amosu HayoraY lahaA fiY Aljaw~i tadowiymu (T, * S, TA) i. e. Venturing upon the [vehement] heat of the pebbles, [meaning the vehemently-hot pebbles,] striking them with its foot, for so the jndb does, (TA,) (assumed tropical:) when the sun is [apparently] stationary in the summer midday, [as though perplexed in its course,] as though having a spinning [in the region between heaven and earth ]: (T, TA:) or as though it were motionless. (S.) ― -b5- And one says, daw~amato Eayonuhu (assumed tropical:) [ His eye rolled; i. e.] the black of his eye revolved as though it were in the whirl of a spindle. (IAar, M, K.) -A2- [ dw~m is also trans.] You say, dw~m Ald~uw~aAmapa , (M, K,) inf. n. tadowiymN , (TA,) (assumed tropical:) He made the dw~Amp [ or top ] to revolve, or spin [so as to seem to be at rest, as has been shown above]: (M, K:) or he played with the dw~Amp . (TA.) ― -b2- And dw~mt Alxamoru $aAribahaA (tropical:) The wine intoxicated its drinker so as to make him turn round about. (As, S, TA.) ― -b3- And daw~amuwA AlEamaAy^ima (assumed tropical:) They wound the turbans around their heads. (TA.) ― -b4- And dw~m Almaraqapa (assumed tropical:) He put much grease into the broth so that it swam round upon it. (M, K.) ― -b5- Alt~adowiymu [or app. tadowiymu All~isaAni ] also signifies (assumed tropical:) The mumbling the tongue, and rolling it about in the mouth, in order that the saliva may not dry up: so says Fr. (S, TA.) ― -b6- [Hence, app., as the context seems to indicate,] Dhu-r-Rummeh says, describing a camel braying in his $iqo$iqap [or faucial bag], daw~ama fiyhaA riz~ahu wa A^aroEadaA [as though meaning (assumed tropical:) He made his braying to roll, or rumble, in it, and threatened ]. (Fr, S, TA.) ― -b7- And dw~m signifies (tropical:) He moistened a thing. (S, M, K.) Ibn-Ahmar says, waqado yudaw~imu riyqa AlT~aAmiEi AlA^amalu (S, M;) i. e. (assumed tropical:) [ And hope sometimes, or often, ] moistens the saliva [ of the eager ]: (S:) he is praising En-Noamán Ibn-Besheer, and means that his hope moistens his saliva in his mouth by making his eulogy to continue. (IB.) ― -b8- (tropical:) He mixed, or moistened, or steeped, ( daAfa ,) saffron, (Lth, T, S, M, K, TA,) and stirred it round in doing so: (Lth, T, TA:) he dissolved saffron in water, and stirred it round therein. (A, TA.) ― -b9- dw~m Alqidora , and ↓ AdAmhA , (S, M, K,) He stilled the boiling of the cooking-pot by means of some [ cold ] water: (S:) or he sprinkled cold water upon [ the contents of ] the cooking-pot to still its boiling: (M, K:) or the former, (K,) or both, (M,) he allayed the boiling of the cooking-pot by means of something, (M, K,) and stilled it: (M:) and the latter signifies he left the cooking-pot upon the A^avaAfiY [or three stones that supported it ], after it had been emptied, (Lh, M, K,) not putting it down nor kindling a fire beneath it. (Lh, M.)

[When no objective complement is expressed, it seems to mean (assumed tropical:) He paused, and acted with deliberation, or in a patient or leisurely manner, or he waited in expectation; app. from the same verb as syn. with daw~ama ; and thus, like one who hovers about a thing: see Haw~ama ; and see also AinotaZara .] And AstdAmhu (tropical:) He acted with moderation, gently, deliberately, or leisurely, in it; (S, M, K, TA;) namely, an affair, or a case: (S:) or he sought, desired, asked, or demanded, its continuance, or long continuance, or endless continuance: and so ↓ dAwmhu (M, K, TA) in both of these senses: (K, TA:) or he asked him to render a thing continual &c.: (Mgh, Msb, TA:) and also (assumed tropical:) he acted gently and deliberately in it; namely, an affair, or a case: (Msb:) and (assumed tropical:) he acted gently with him; (Fr, T in art. dym , M, Msb, Kt;) i. e., another person, (Msb,) or his creditor; as also AisotadomaAhu , (Fr, T, M, K,) which we judge to be formed from the former by transposition, because we do not find it [in this sense] to have any inf. n. (M.) A poet says, (T, S, Msb,) namely, Keys Ibn-Zuheyr, (S,) falaA taEojalo biA^amorika waA@sotadimohu ↓ famaA Sal~aY EaSaAka kamusotadiymi (T, S, Msb,) i. e. (assumed tropical:) [ Therefore haste not in thine affair, but act with moderation, gently, deliberately, or leisurely, therein ]; for no one has straightened thy staff by turning it round over the fire, (T,) meaning, no one has managed thine affair soundly, like one who acts with moderation, &c. (T, Msb.) And another says, (S,) namely, Mejnoon, (TA,) waA_in~aY EalaY layolaY lazaArK waA_in~aniY EalaY*aAka fiymaA bayonanaA A^asotadiymuhaA meaning (assumed tropical:) [ And verily I am blaming Leylà; and verily, notwithstanding that, ] I look for her aiding me by good conduct [ in the matter that is between us ]. (S.) You say also, A^asotadiymu A@ll~`ha niEomataka I seek, or desire, or ask, of God the continuance, or long continuance, or endless continuance, of thy favour, or the like. (Mgh, TA. *) And A^asotadiymu A@ll~`ha Eiz~aka I ask God to continue, or continue long, &c., thy might, or power, &c. (Msb.) The phrase AstdAm lubosa Alv~awobi , meaning [ He continued long the wearing of the garment, or] he did not hasten to pull off the garment, may be from the saying Aisotadamotu EaAqibapa AlA^amori , meaning I looked, or watched, or waited, for the end, or issue, or result, of the affair, or case. (Msb.) -A3- Also He (a man) stooped his head, blood dropping from it: formed by transposition from AisotadomaY (Kr, TA.)

sourceDefinition: A lasting, or continuous, and still rain: (As, M, and TA voce DarobN , q. v.:) or rain in which is neither thunder nor lightning; the least of which is the third of a day or the third of a night; and the most thereof, of any period: (AZ, S in art. dym :) or rain that continues some days: (Msb:) or rain that continues long and is still, without thunder and lightning: (K, * TA:) or rain that continues five days, or six, (M, K,) or seven, (K,) or a day and a night, (T in art. dym , M, K,) or more; (T, TA;) or the least whereof is a third of a day or of a night; and the most thereof, of any period: (K, TA:) pl. diyamN , (S, M, K,) the w being changed [into Y ] in the pl. because it is changed in the sing., (M,) and duyuwmN , (Abu-l-'Omeythil, T, K,) and [coll. gen. n.] ↓ diyomN (Sh, T, TA.) [See also mudaAmN .] ― -b2- Hence other things are thus termed by way of comparison. (S.) It is said in a trad. (S, M) of 'Áïsheh, (M,) kaAna Eamaluhu diymapF (S, M, Msb) (assumed tropical:) His work was incessant [ but moderate, or not excessive ]; (Msb;) referring to Mohammad; (T, S, M, Msb;) on her being asked if he preferred some days to others: (T:) she likened it to the rain termed dymp in respect of continuance and moderation. (T, M.) And it is related of Hudheyfeh that he said, mentioning fitan [i. e. trials, or probations, or conflicts and factions, &c.], A_in~ahaA laA=tiyatukumo diymFA diymFA , meaning (assumed tropical:) [ Verily they are coming to you ] filling the earth, or land, [ and ] with continuance. (T.)

(S, M) of 'Áïsheh, (M,) kaAna Eamaluhu diymapF (S, M, Msb) (assumed tropical:) His work was incessant [ but moderate, or not excessive ]; (Msb;) referring to Mohammad; (T, S, M, Msb;) on her being asked if he preferred some days to others: (T:) she likened it to the rain termed dymp in respect of continuance and moderation. (T, M.) And it is related of Hudheyfeh that he said, mentioning fitan [i. e. trials, or probations, or conflicts and factions, &c.], A_in~ahaA laA=tiyatukumo diymFA diymFA , meaning (assumed tropical:) [ Verily they are coming to you ] filling the earth, or land, [ and ] with continuance. (T.)

(TA.)

(T, K.)

definition: , aor. , inf. n. rutuwEN (S, Msb, K) and ratoEN (Msb, K) and ritaAEN , (IAar, K,) He (a beast) pastured at pleasure; (Msb;) he (a beast, S, TA) ate (S, K) and drank (K) what he pleased, (S, K,) and...
sourceDefinition: , aor. , inf. n. rutuwEN (S, Msb, K) and ratoEN (Msb, K) and ritaAEN , (IAar, K,) He (a beast) pastured at pleasure; (Msb;) he (a beast, S, TA) ate (S, K) and drank (K) what he pleased, (S, K,) and came and went in the pasturage, by day, (TA,) amid abundance of herbage, and plenty: (K:) or (tropical:) he ate and drank plentifully and pleasantly, in land of seed-produce and fruitfulness, of green herbs or leguminous plants and of waters: (Lth, K, TA:) or (tropical:) he ate (IAar, K) and drank (K) with great greediness. (IAar, K.) In its primary acceptation, it is said of a beast. (TA.) ― -b2- It is metaphorically said of a man, as meaning (tropical:) He ate much; accord. to El-Isbahánee in the Mufradát, and the A and the B. (TA.) ― -b3- You say, rataEa fulaAnN fiY maAli fulaAnK (tropical:) Such a one acted as he pleased in eating and drinking the property of such a one. (TA.) ― -b4- And xarajonaA naloEabu wanarotaEu (tropical:) We went forth [ playing, or sporting, and enjoying ourselves; or] enjoying ourselves; and playing, or sporting. (S, TA. *) It is said in the Kur [xii. 12], (TA,) accord. to different readings, (K, TA,) A^arosilohu maEanaA gadFA yarotaEo wayaloEabo (tropical:) [ Send thou him with us to-morrow ] that he may play, or sport, and enjoy himself: or the meaning is, that he may walk [ abroad at his pleasure ] and become cheerful in countenance, or dilated in heart: (TA:) and wayaloEabu ↓ nurotiEo that we may put our beasts to eat and drink what they please, amid abundance of herbage, and plenty, [or to pasture at pleasure, ] and he shall play: (K, TA:) and the reverse, (K,) yurotiEo wanaloEabu , (TA,) i. e. that he may put our beasts to eat and drink &c., and we will play together: (K, TA:) and with n in each case. (K.) ― -b5- And it is said in a trad., mano yarotaEo Hawola AlHimaY yuw$iko A^ano yaxaAliTahu , i. e. (assumed tropical:) He who goes round about [ the prohibited place of pasturage will soon enter into it ]. (TA.) ― -b6- And in another trad., A_i*aA mararotumo biriyaADi Aljan~api faA@rotaEuwA , meaning (tropical:) [ When ye pass by a scene of ] the commemoration of the praises of God, enter ye thereinto; the entering thereinto being thus likened to the eating and drinking what one pleases, amid abundance of herbage. (TA.)

definition: He put his camels [ to pasture at pleasure;
sourceDefinition: He put his camels [ to pasture at pleasure; (see 1;) or] to eat (S, K) and drink (K) what they pleased, (S, K,) amid abundance of herbage, and plenty: (K: [in which it is implied that the verb may have this signification or others agreeable with explanations in the first sentence of this art.:]) or he pastured his camels, or put them to pasture, by themselves. (TA.) See the ex. in the Kur-án cited above. ― -b2- Hence, (tropical:) He ruled, or governed, his subjects well; [as though] leaving them to satiate themselves in the pasturage. (TA.) ― -b3- It (a party of men) lighted upon abundance of herbage, and pastured. (TA.) ― -b4- It (rain) produced, or gave growth to, herbage in which the camels might pasture at pleasure, or eat and drink what they pleased, amid abundance thereof and plenty. (S, Msb, K.) ― -b5- ArtEt AlA^aroDu The land became abundant in herbage. (TA.)

definition: Abundance of herbage;
sourceDefinition: Abundance of herbage; or of the goods, conveniences, and comforts, of life; fruitfulness; plenty: and a state of ampleness in respect thereof: (K:) a subst. from 1. (TA.) Hence the prov., Alqayodu waAlr~atoEapu , and ↓ Alr~ataEapu ; (K;) the former on the authority of Fr, and the latter from some other, accord. to the O; but in the L, the latter is ascribed to Fr; (TA;) [ Bonds and plenty; the latter word] meaning AlxaSobu : said by 'Amr Ibn-Es-Saak: he had been taken prisoner by Shákir Ibn-Rabee'ah, a tribe of Hemdán, who treated him well; and when he left his people, he was slender; then he fled from Shákir; and when he came to his people, they said, “ O 'Amr, thou wentest forth from us slender, and now thon art corpulent; ” and he replied in the words above. (K.)

definition: One who leaves his travelling-camels to pasture at their pleasure, or to eat and drink what they please, coming and going in the pasturage, by day, amid abundance of herbage, and plenty.
sourceDefinition: One who leaves his travelling-camels to pasture at their pleasure, or to eat and drink what they please, coming and going in the pasturage, by day, amid abundance of herbage, and plenty. (TA.) ― -b2- (tropical:) A man having abundance of herbage, or of the goods or conveniences and comforts of life, not lacking anything that he may desire. (K, TA.) You say also qawomN murotiEuwna ↓ raAtiEuwna , meaning (assumed tropical:) A people, or company of men, who are scarcely ever without abundance of herbage, or of the goods or conveniences and comforts of life; syn. maxaASiybu ; and ↓ qawomN ratiEuwna , after the manner of a rel. n., like TaEimN : and in like manner ↓ ratiEN is applied to herbage [as meaning scarcely ever other than abundant, or generally abundant ]. (TA.) ― -b3- Rain that produces, or gives growth to , herbage in which the camels may pasture at pleasure, or eat and drink what they please, amid abundance thereof and plenty. (S, Msb.) ― -b4- A^aroDN murotiEapN Land in which the beasts eagerly desire to satiate themselves. (Sh.)

See 5.

definition: , (T, S, O, Msb, K &c.
sourceDefinition: , (T, S, O, Msb, K &c.,) aor. , (K,) inf. n. radofN , (MA, KL,) He rode behind him [ on the same beast ]; (AZ, Sh, Zj, T, MA, Msb;) [and] so radafahu , [aor. ;] (M;) and ↓ Ardfhu ; (AZ, Sh, T, M;) said by IAar to signify the same as radifahu : (T:) [or, in other words,] radifahu signifies he became to him a ridof [meaning a radiyf ]; and so radifa lahu ; for the Arabs often add the l with a trans. v. that governs an accus. noun; so that they say, samiEa lahu and $akara lahu and naSaHa lahu , meaning samiEahu and $akarahu and naSaHahu : (Fr, T:) [and also] he, or it, followed, or came after, him, or it; (S, O, K, and Ham p. 148;) and so radifa lahu ; (Ham ibid.;) and radafahu , aor. ; (K;) and ↓ Ardfhu ; (S, K, and Ham ubi suprà;) and ↓ Artdfhu also signifies the same as radifahu ; (K;) radifahu and ↓ Ardfhu being like tabiEahu and A^atobaEahu in [form and] meaning: (S:) [↓ rad~afahu , likewise, appears to be syn. with radifahu ; or, probably, rud~ifahu , which seems to signify lit. he was made to ride behind him; &c.; for it is said that] the inf. n. tarodiyfN signifies the coming, or going, behind; as also tarodaAfN : (KL:) and radifotuhu also signifies I overtook him and outwent him. (Msb: [explained in my copy by lHqth wsbqth : but I think that sbqth is a mistranscription for tabiEotuhu ; and that the meaning therefore is, I overtook him and followed him. ]) One says, kaAna nazala bihimo A^amorN faradifa lahumo A=xaru A^aEoZamu minohu [ An event had befallen them, and another, of greater magnitude than it, happened afterwards to them ]. (Lth, * T, * S, O.) And A^amorN ↓ Ardfhu is a dial. var. of radifahu , meaning An event happened to him afterwards: (S, O:) or radifahumu AlA^amoru and ↓ A^arodafahum signify the event came upon them suddenly, or unexpectedly; or came upon them so as to overwhelm them. (M.) It is said in the Kur [xxvii. 74], EasaY A^ano yakuwna radifa lakumo baEoDu A@l~a*iY tasotaEojiluwna , meaning [ Perhaps a portion of that which ye desire to hasten ] may have drawn near to you; (Yoo, Fr, T, O,) as though the l were introduced because the meaning is danaA lakumo : or it may mean yakuwna radifakumo [may have become close behind you ]; (Fr, T, O;) the l being introduced for a reason mentioned above, as in samiEa lahu &c. for samiEahu &c.: (Fr, T:) El-Aaraj read radafa lkm . (O.) And Khuzeymeh Ibn-Málik Ibn-Nahd says, Alv~uray~aA ↓ A_i*aA AljawozaA='u A^arodafati Zananotu biA=li faATimapa AlZ~unuwnaA [ When Orion, or Gemini, shall ride behind, or closely follow, the Pleiades, (an event which will never occur,) I will form in my mind, respecting the family (meaning the father ) of Fátimeh, opinions ]: (S, O:) cited by Fr [and by J] as an ex. of Ardft in the sense of radifat : (T:) he means Fátimeh the daughter of Yedhkur Ibn-'Anazeh, who [i. e. Yedhkur] was one of the qaAriZaAn . (S, O. [Respecting the qArZAn , see art. qarZ .])

definition: The beast allowed a radiyf [ to ride it ], and was strong enough to bear him;
sourceDefinition: The beast allowed a radiyf [ to ride it ], and was strong enough to bear him; as also ↓ Ardft [accord. to some]. (Msb.) You say, ha*ihi daAb~apN laA turaAdifu (T, S, M, O, K) and ↓ laA turodifu , (Lth, M, O, K,) but the latter is rare, (K,) or post-classical, of the language of the people of towns and villages, (T, O,) and not allowable, (T,) This beast will not allow a radiyf (Lth, T, M) to ride it; (Lth, T;) will not bear a rdyf . (S, O, K.) ― -b2- muraAdafapu AljaraAdi signifies The mounting of [ locusts one behind, or upon, another; ] the male locust upon the female, and the third upon those two. (S, O, K.) ― -b3- And muraAdafapu Almuluwki is [a phrase meaning The acting as a ridof , or as A^arodaAf , to the kings, ] from Alr~idaAfapu [q. v.]. (O, K.) Jereer, who was of the Benoo-Yarbooa, to whom pertained the ridaAfap in the Time of Ignorance, says, rabaEonaA waraAdafonaA Almuluwka faZal~iluwA wTaAba AlA^aHaAliybi Alv~umaAma Almunaz~aEaA [ We have taken the fourth part of the spoils, and we have acted as A^arodaAf to the kings; therefore shade ye the skins of the camel-loads of milk collected from the camels in the pasture with panic grass plucked up, and so make it cool for us ]: (S, * O:) wiTaAb is the pl. of the waTob of milk. (S.) ― -b4- [In the conventional language of lexicology, rAdfhu , inf. n. muraAdafapN , signifies It was synonymous with it; i. e. a word with another word: as though the former supplied the place of the latter, like as the ridof supplied the place of the king. See also 6.]

definition: One who rides behind another (S, M, O, Msb, K) on the back of the [ same ] beast;
sourceDefinition: One who rides behind another (S, M, O, Msb, K) on the back of the [ same ] beast; (Msb;) as also ↓ ridofN (S, M, O, Msb, K) and ↓ murotadifN : (S, K:) the pl. (M, K) of the first (M) is rudaAfaY , (M, K, [in my copy of the Msb rdfY , which is app. a mistranscription, and there said to be irreg.,]) or the pl. of radiyfN is ridaAfN , (S, [so in both of my copies,]) and rudafaA='u : (M:) and ↓ rudaAfaY is used as a sing., syn. with radiyfN , (T, K,) accord. to some, (T,) as well as pl. [thereof]: (K:) or it is pl. of ridofN [q. v.]. (T.) [Hence,] one says, jaAw^uwA rudaAfaY They came following one another. (K.) [Hence,] also, A Haqiybap , and the like, that is [ conveyed ] behind a man; [i. e. a bag, or receptacle, in which a man puts his travellingprovisions; and any other thing that is conveyed behind a man on his beast; ] and so ↓ ridofN . (M.) ― -b2- See also ridofN , in two places. ― -b3- Also A star rising in the east, when its opposite star is setting in the west. (S, O, K.) And (K) A star facing a rising star: (Lth, M, O, * K:) used in this sense by Ru-beh; who terms the rising star raAkibu AlmiqodaAri . (Lth, M.) ― -b4- Also One who brings his arrow after the winning of one of the players at the game called Almayosir , or of two of them, and asks them to insert his arrow among theirs: (O, K:) or ↓ ridaAfN [so in the M accord. to the TT, but app. a mistranscription,] signifies one who brings his arrow after they have divided among themselves the slaughtered camel, and who is not turned back by them disappointed, but is assigned by them a portion of what has become their shares. (M.)

definition: The function of the ridof of a king, (S, O, K,) in the Time of Ignorance: (S: [see ridofN :]) a term similar to AlxilaAfapu : (K:) it pertained to the Benoo-Yarbooa, in that time;
sourceDefinition: The function of the ridof of a king, (S, O, K,) in the Time of Ignorance: (S: [see ridofN :]) a term similar to AlxilaAfapu : (K:) it pertained to the Benoo-Yarbooa, in that time; because there were not among the Arabs any who waged war more than they did against the kings of El- Heereh, who therefore made peace with them on the condition that the rdAfp should be assigned to them and that they should abstain from waging war against the people of El-'Irák: (S, O:) it was of two kinds; one being the riding behind the king upon his horse; and the other, what has been explained above, as from the S, voce ridofN . (Har p. 321.)

definition: , as a conventional term in lexicology, Synonymous: you say A^alofaAZN mutaraAdifapN synonymous words or expressions.
sourceDefinition: , as a conventional term in lexicology, Synonymous: you say A^alofaAZN mutaraAdifapN synonymous words or expressions. (Mz, 27th nwE .) [Loosely explained in the K by the words A^ano yakuwna A@somFA li$~Yo'K waAHidK , meaning significant of one thing; which is the contr. of mu$otarakN , i. e. “ homonymous: ” and in like manner, AlmutaraAdifapu is expl. in the O, An tkwn A^asomaA='F l$Y'K wAHdK ; and is said to be post-classical.] mutaraAdifaAtN [its pl. when used as a subst.] signifies Synonyms; i. e. single, or simple, words denoting the same thing considered in one and the same respect or light: thus the mutaraAdifaAni differ from the noun and the definition [thereof], because these [generally] are not both single words; and from the mutabaAyinaAni [or “ two disparates ”] such as Als~ayofu and AlS~aArimu , because these denote the same thing considered in two different respects, the one in respect of the substance, and the other in respect of the quality: (Fakhred-Deen [Er-Rázee] in the Mz, 27th nwE :) or they may be two simple words, as All~ayovu and AlA^asadu ; and two compound expressions, as, juluwsu All~ayovi and quEuwdu AlA^asadi ; and a single word and a compound expression, as Almuz~u and AlHulowu AlHaAmiDu . (Kull p. 130.) [See also muraAdifu lafoZK .] [This art. is wanting in the copies of the L and TA to which I have had access.]

sourceDefinition: , aor. ; and raDaEa , aor. ; (S, Msb, * K;) the former of the dial. of Tihámeh; (O, L;) the latter of the dial. of Nejd; (S, O, L;) or the former of the dial. of Nejd; and the latter of the dial. of Tihámeh, and used by the people of Mekkeh; (Msb;) and raDaEa , (Msb,) i. e. raDaEa vadoYa A^um~ihi , (IKtt, TA,) aor. ; (IKtt, Msb;) inf. n. raDaAEN , (S, Msb, K,) of the first, (S, TA,) or of the third, (Msb,) and riDaAEN , (K,) [which is also an inf. n. of 3,] and raDaEN , (Msb, K,) of the first, (Msb, TA,) and raDoEN , (S, Msb, K,) of the second, (S, Msb,) and raDiEN , (Msb, K,) said by some to be the original form of the inf. n. of the second, (Msb,) and raDaAEapN , (Msb, K,) of the third, (Msb,) and riDaAEapN ; (K;) or the last two are simple substs. form raDaAEN ; (IAth;) said of a child; (S, Msb;) He sucked the breast of his mother; (K;) and ↓ ArtDE signifies the same. (Msb, TA.) You say, h`*aA A^axiY mina Alr~aDaAEapi [ This is my foster-brother ]; and h`*aA raDiyEiY . (S, K. *) The saying, in a trad., Alr~aDaAEapu mina AlmajaAEapi , and Alr~iDaAEapu , means The sucking which occasions interdiction of marriage [with the woman whose milk is sucked and certain of her relations] is that of an infant when hungry; not of a child that is grown up: (IAth:) or that consequent upon hunger which is stopped by the milk in the time of infancy of the child; not when the child's hunger is only to be stopped by solid food. (Mgh in art. jwE .) You also say, of a man, yaroDaEu A_ibilahu (S, K) and ganamahu (S) [ He sucks the teats of his camels and of his ewes or she-goats, by reason of his sordidness: see raADiEN ]. ― -b2- raDiEa All~uw^oma mino vadoYi A^um~ihi (tropical:) [ He sucked meanness, sordidness, or ignobleness, from the breast of his mother ]; (K;) i. e. he was born in meanness, sordidness, or ignobleness. (TA.) ― -b3- yaroDaEu Aln~aAsa (assumed tropical:) He begs of men; (K, TA;) asks gifts of them. (TA.) So, accord. to IAar, in the saying of Jereer, wayaroDaEu mano laA qaY waA_ino yara muqoEadFA yaquwdu biA^aEomaY faA@lofarazodaqu saAy^luho [ And he begs of him whom he meets; and if he see a cripple leading a blind person, El-Farezdak asks of him ]: but [properly speaking] the muqEad is one who cannot stand, so as to lead the blind. (TA.) ― -b4- huwa yaroDaEu Ald~unoyaA waya*um~uhaA (tropical:) [ He sucks the sweets of the present world, and dispraises it ]. (TA.) -A2- raDuEa , (S, Z, K,) with damm, as though what the verb denotes were natural to the person of whom it is said, (S, TA,) or the verb has this form because it is changed in meaning so as to be intensive, (Z, TA,) aor. ; and raDaEa , aor. ; (Ibn- 'Abbád, K;) inf. n., (Z, K,) of the former verb, (Z, TA,) raDaAEapF , (Z, K,) with fet- h only; (IAth, TA;) (tropical:) He (a man, S) was, or became, mean, sordid, or ignoble: (S, * K, TA:) or he was, or became, very mean, &c.: (Z, TA:) [see raADaEN :] or one says, law^uma waraDuEa , for the sake of mutual resemblance; and the meaning is, [ he was, or became, mean, sordid, or ignoble, and ] he sucked from the teat of the she-camel, fearing lest, if he milked, any one should know of his doing so, and demand of him somewhat. (Msb.) -A3- raDaEato A^alobaAnuhaA (tropical:) Their milk became little in quantity; said in reference to milch-camels abounding with milk. (TA. [But the context in the TA suggests that this is a mistake; that the phrase is said of the wind called raDaAEapN ; and that the right reading is raDaEato A^alobaAnahaA ; and the meaning, (assumed tropical:) It rendered their milk little in quantity. ])

(S, K. *) The saying, in a trad., Alr~aDaAEapu mina AlmajaAEapi , and Alr~iDaAEapu , means The sucking which occasions interdiction of marriage [with the woman whose milk is sucked and certain of her relations] is that of an infant when hungry; not of a child that is grown up: (IAth:) or that consequent upon hunger which is stopped by the milk in the time of infancy of the child; not when the child's hunger is only to be stopped by solid food. (Mgh in art. jwE .) You also say, of a man, yaroDaEu A_ibilahu (S, K) and ganamahu (S) [ He sucks the teats of his camels and of his ewes or she-goats, by reason of his sordidness: see raADiEN ]. ― -b2- raDiEa All~uw^oma mino vadoYi A^um~ihi (tropical:) [ He sucked meanness, sordidness, or ignobleness, from the breast of his mother ]; (K;) i. e. he was born in meanness, sordidness, or ignobleness. (TA.) ― -b3- yaroDaEu Aln~aAsa (assumed tropical:) He begs of men; (K, TA;) asks gifts of them. (TA.) So, accord. to IAar, in the saying of Jereer, wayaroDaEu mano laA qaY waA_ino yara muqoEadFA yaquwdu biA^aEomaY faA@lofarazodaqu saAy^luho [ And he begs of him whom he meets; and if he see a cripple leading a blind person, El-Farezdak asks of him ]: but [properly speaking] the muqEad is one who cannot stand, so as to lead the blind. (TA.) ― -b4- huwa yaroDaEu Ald~unoyaA waya*um~uhaA (tropical:) [ He sucks the sweets of the present world, and dispraises it ]. (TA.) -A2- raDuEa , (S, Z, K,) with damm, as though what the verb denotes were natural to the person of whom it is said, (S, TA,) or the verb has this form because it is changed in meaning so as to be intensive, (Z, TA,) aor. ; and raDaEa , aor. ; (Ibn- 'Abbád, K;) inf. n., (Z, K,) of the former verb, (Z, TA,) raDaAEapF , (Z, K,) with fet- h only; (IAth, TA;) (tropical:) He (a man, S) was, or became, mean, sordid, or ignoble: (S, * K, TA:) or he was, or became, very mean, &c.: (Z, TA:) [see raADaEN :] or one says, law^uma waraDuEa , for the sake of mutual resemblance; and the meaning is, [ he was, or became, mean, sordid, or ignoble, and ] he sucked from the teat of the she-camel, fearing lest, if he milked, any one should know of his doing so, and demand of him somewhat. (Msb.) -A3- raDaEato A^alobaAnuhaA (tropical:) Their milk became little in quantity; said in reference to milch-camels abounding with milk. (TA. [But the context in the TA suggests that this is a mistake; that the phrase is said of the wind called raDaAEapN ; and that the right reading is raDaEato A^alobaAnahaA ; and the meaning, (assumed tropical:) It rendered their milk little in quantity. ])

definition: He sought, or demanded, a wetnurse.
sourceDefinition: He sought, or demanded, a wetnurse. (K.) It is said in the Kur [ii. 233], waA_ino A^aradotumo A^ano tasotaroDiEuwA A^awolaAdakumo And if ye desire to seek, or demand, wet-nurses for your children; i. e., An tstrDEwA AwlAdkm maraADiEa ; the second objective complement [accord. to this order of the words], but the first in reality because the wetnurse is the agent with respect to the child, being suppressed; for you say, AisotaroDaEotu AlmaroA^apa waladiY , meaning I sought, or demanded, of the woman that she should suckle my child: (IB:) accord. to some, the verb is doubly trans.: accord. to others, the prep. li is suppressed in the Kur; the meaning being liA^awolaAdikumo . (El-Howfee, in the “ Burhán fee tefseer-el-Kur-án. ”)

definition: Sucking the breast of his mother;
sourceDefinition: Sucking the breast of his mother; a suckling; as also ↓ raDiEN : pl. of the former ruD~aEN ; and of the latter; ruDuEN . (K. [See also raDiyEN , which signifies the same; as is shown below, voce muroDiEN ; and by Bd in xxii. 2; &c.]) ― -b2- One who sucks from the teat of the she-camel, fearing lest, if he milked, any one should know of his doing so, and demand of him somewhat: (Msb:) or a pastor who does not take with him a milkingvessel, and, when he is asked for milk, excuses himself on that ground, (K, TA,) and, when he desires to drink, sucks the teat of his milchbeast: (TA:) pl. ruD~aEN . (Msb.) The phrase lay^iymN raADiEN [i. e. Mean, sordid, or ignoble; who sucks the teats of his she-camels, &c.,] originated, (S, K,) as they assert, (S,) from a certain man's sucking the teats of his she-camels (S, K) or ewes or she-goats, and not milking them, (S,) lest the sound of his milking should be heard and somewhat should be demanded of him: (S, K:) or the origin was the coming of a guest by night to a certain man of the Amalekites, whereupon the latter sucked the udder of his ewe, lest the guest should hear the sound of the streaming of the milk from the teat. (IDrd.) But when a single epithet is used, one says ↓ raDiyEN . (Msb. [See, however, what follows.]) ― -b3- [Hence,] (tropical:) Mean, sordid, or ignoble; (K, TA;) as also ↓ raDiyEN and ↓ raD~aAEN : pl. ruD~aEN and ruD~aAEN : (K:) and raDiEuwna , as a pl., [i. e. pl. of ↓ raDiEN ,] has the same signification, of mean, &c. (TA.) It is said in a trad. of Selemeh Ibn-El-Akwa', Alyuwoma yuwomu Alr~uD~aEi , meaning (tropical:) To-day is the day of the destruction of the mean, &c. (TA.) ― -b4- Also (tropical:) Mean, sordid, or ignoble, who has sucked meanness, sordidness, or ignobleness, from the breast of his mother; (ElYemámee, K, TA;) i. e. born in meanness, sordidness, or ignobleness. (TA.) ― -b5- (tropical:) A beggar: (TA:) one who begs of men: (K:) thus Ibn-'Abbád explains lay^iymN raADiEN . (TA.) ― -b6- (assumed tropical:) One who eats the particles of food remaining between his teeth, lest anything [ thereof ] should escape him: (K:) or such is termed lay^iymN raADiEN . (TA.) -A2- A possessor of milk: after the usual manner of a possessive epithet [like laAbinN ]. (TA.)

definition: and muroDaEapN A mother [or other woman] suckling: (Msb:) or one having with her a child which she suckles: the former epithet may with reason be applied to the mother because suckling is performed...
sourceDefinition: and muroDaEapN A mother [or other woman] suckling: (Msb:) or one having with her a child which she suckles: the former epithet may with reason be applied to the mother because suckling is performed only by females, like as the epithets HaAy^iDN and TaAmivN are applied to a woman; and if muroDaEapN were applied to her who has with her a child, it would be correct: (Fr, TA:) [but see another saying ascribed to Fr in what follows:] or the former, a woman having a child which she suckles; (Kh, S, IB, K;) after the manner of a possessive epithet; (IB;) i. e. having a raDiyE ; (Kh, IB;) like AimoraA^apN muTofilN “ a woman having a Tifol ; ” (Kh;) or ZaboyapN mu$odinN “ a doe-gazelle having a $aAdin ; ” though muroDiEN has a verb bearing a signification agreeing with this; and it sometimes occurs as meaning having milk, though not having a child that is suckled: (IB:) but the latter is used in describing a woman as performing an action; (Kh;) signifying suckling a child: (S, K:) the former is used when the [abstract] quality is meant: the latter, when the action is meant: but God knows: (Akh:) or the former signifies one who is near to suckling, but has not yet suckled: and one having with her the child that is suckled [ by her ] ( AlS~abiY~u Alr~aDiyEu ): and the latter, [in the TA the former, but this is a mistranscription, as is shown by what follows,] one who is suckling, her teat being in the mouth of her child; and in this sense it is used in the Kur, in a passage which see below: (AZ in the TA:) Th says, the latter signifies one who suckles, though she have not a child, or if she have a child: and the former, one who has not a child with her, and sometimes having with her a child: and in one place he says, when the action is meant, the latter is used, and it is made an epithet: and when the p is not added, it is meant as a subst: (TA:) Fr and some others say that it is without p when the proper signification of suckling is meant: and with p when the tropical signification of a subject of the attribute of suckling in time past or future is meant: (Msb:) the pl. [of both, though said in the Mgh and TA to be that of the former,] is maraADiEu (Mgh, Msb, TA) and maraADiyEu . (Msb, TA.) The saying in the Kur [xxii. 2], yawoma tarawonahaA ta*ohalu kul~u muroDiEapK Eam~aA A^aroDaEato means [ On the day when ye shall see it, ] every woman that is suckling;, (AZ, Kh,) in the act of doing so, (Kh,) with her teat in the mouth of her child; (AZ,) [ shall neglect, or become heedless of or diverted from, that which she shall have been suckling: ] or mrDEp here has the last signification explained in the preceding sentence [so that the meaning is every woman who shall have been suckling or shall be going to suckle ]. (Msb.) ― -b2- It is said in a trad., niEomati AlmuroDiEapu wabiy^osati AlfaATimapu , meaning (assumed tropical:) Excellent in the office of commander, or governor, and the profit, or advantage, which it brings to its possessor; and very evil is death, which destroys his delights, or pleasures, and stops the profits, or advantages, of that office. (TA.) ― -b3- The pl. maraADiyEu is metaphorically applied as an epithet to bees ( jawaAris , i. e. naHol ). (TA.)

definition: , (S, O, Mgh, Msb, K,) aor.
sourceDefinition: , (S, O, Mgh, Msb, K,) aor. , (S, Msb,) inf. n. rifoqN (S, * O, Mgh, * Msb, * K) and marofiqN and mirofaqN (AZ, O, K,) and marofaqN ; (O, K;) and rafiqa , (JK, O, K,) [aor. ,] inf. n. rafaqN ; (JK;) and rafuqa ; (JK, O, K;) He was, or became, gentle, soft, tender, gracious, courteous, or civil; or he be haved, or acted, gently, softly, &c. (JK, S, O, Mgh, Msb, K.) You say, rafaqa bihi , (AZ, S, O, Mgh, Msb, K,) and Ealayohi , (AZ, O, K,) inf. ns. as above; (O, K;) and rafiqa , and rafuqa ; (K;) He was, or became, gentle, &c., or he behaved, or acted, gently, &c., with him, (AZ, S, O, Mgh, Msb, K,) and to him; (AZ, O, K;) and in like manner, bihi ↓ trf~q , (S, O, Mgh, K,) and ↓ Arfqhu . (AZ, O, K.) Hence the saying of the Prophet, mano rafaqa biA^um~atiY rafaqa A@ll~`hu bihi [ He who is gentle, &c., with my people, God will be gentle, &c., with him ]. (O.) [Hence, also,] one says, ↓ trf~q fiY A^amorihi [and rafaqa fiyhi as is indicated in the O] He used gentleness, or acted gently, in his affair; syn. taA^at~aY . (Msb in art. AtY .) And liHaAjatihi ↓ trf~q He applied himself with gentleness to his needful affair or business; syn. taA^at~aY . (T in art. AtY .) And liloA^amori ↓ trf~q He applied himself with gentle ness to the affair; syn. talaT~afa . (S in art. lTf .) ― -b2- Hence, rafuqa , in form like faruba , He was, or became, gentle, delicate, nice, neat, or skilful, in work or operation; the contr. of such as is termed A^axoraq . (Msb.) ― -b3- And rafaqotu AlEamala , with fet-h to the f , aor. , I did, or made, the deed, or work, soundly, thoroughly, skilfully, judiciously, or well. (Msb.) ― -b4- And rafaqotu fiY Als~ayori I pro ceeded in a right, or a moderate, manner in journeying, or in pace. (Msb.) -A2- See also 4. -A3- rafaAqapN is an inf. n. signifying The being a rafayq . (O, K.) Fr says, I heard a man at 'Arafát saying [to the pilgrims there assembled], jaEalakumu A@ll~`hN fiY rafaAqapi muHam~adK Sal~aY A@ll~`hu Ealayohi wasal~ama [ May God make you to be in the companionship of Mohammad: may God bless and save him ]. (O.) [And accord. to the TK, one says, rafuqa bihi , inf. n. rafaAqapN , meaning He became a rafiyq with him: but what is commonly said in this sense is raAfqahu , q. v.] -A4- rafaqa fulaAnFA , He struck the mirofaq [or elbow ] of such a one. (K.) ― -b2- And rafaqa Aln~aAqapa , (S, O, K,) aor. , inf. n. rafoqN , (S, O,) He bound the she-camel's arm [app. together with the shank (for such is the common practice)], (S, O, K,) to prevent her going quickly, (S, O,) when fearing her yearning towards, or longing for, her home, or accustomed place: (S, O, K:) [or] rafaqa AlbaEiyra , aor. , inf. n. rafoqN , he bound the camel's neck ( Eunuq [probably, I think, a mistranscription for EaDud i. e. arm, ]) to his pastern, because of a slight lameness therein. (JK.) -A5- rafiqa said of a camel, aor. , inf. n. rafaqN , He had his elbow dis torted from his side. (TA and TK. [See rafaqN below, and A^arofaqu : and see also dafiqa .]) ― -b2- [And rafiqato , inf. n. rafaqN , is probably said of a she-camel, as meaning She had, in her teat, or teats, what is termed rafaqN : see, again, this word below.]

[of mult.] rifaAqN , (S, O, Mgh, Msb, K,) which is pl. of rufoqapN , (Mgh, Msb,) and rufaqN , [which is also pl. of rufoqapN ,] and [of pauc.] A^arofaAqN ; (O, K;) and the pl. of rifoqapN is rifaqN : (Msb:) or rufoqapN is a quasi-pl. n. of ↓ rafiyqN , or syn. with this last used in a pl. sense; and its pl. is rifaqN and rufaqN and [quasi-pl. n.] ↓ rafaqN . (K.) (TA voce raTaAnapN .)

definition: The cord that is used for the purpose described in the explanation of rafaqa Aln~aAqapa , (S, O, K,) or in the explanation of rafaqa AlbaEiyra .
sourceDefinition: The cord that is used for the purpose described in the explanation of rafaqa Aln~aAqapa , (S, O, K,) or in the explanation of rafaqa AlbaEiyra . (JK.) [See 1, in the latter part of the paragraph.] So in the saying of Bishr, (S,) i. e. of Bishr Ibn-Abee- Házim, (O,) faA_in~iY waAl$~akaApa mina Ali laA^oYK ka*aAti AlDigoni tamo$iY fiY Alr~ifaAqi (O,) or waA=la laAmK , (S, O,) accord. to different readings: (O:) [i. e. And verily I, with respect to the fault, or the complaint, of the family of Läy, or and the family of Lám, am like her that yearns towards, or longs for, her home, or accustomed place, going along with her arm and shank in the rfAq ]: he says, I am withheld from satirizing them, like as this she-camel that yearns towards, or longs for, her home, or accustomed place, is bound and withheld; but if they do not what I approve, I will let loose my tongue with satirizing them. (O.) ― -b2- Also A thing in form like a finger, made for the teat of a she-camel when she is affected with the [ disorder termed ] rafaq : it is stuffed with dates, and then the SiraAr [q. v.] is bound over it, in order that it [ the teat ] may be cured. (JK.)

(T, S.) [Or] ramala Als~ariyra , and [so in the M, but in the K “ or ”] AlHaSiyra , aor. , inf. n. ramolN , He ornamented the couch, and the mat, with jawohar [i. e. jewels, precious stones, gems, &c.], and the like. And ramala Als~ariyra , (S, K,) [aor. and] inf. n. as above; (TA;) and ↓ Armlhu ; He wove ( ramala ) $ariyT [or palm leaves split and then plaited together ], (S, O, K,) or some other thing, (S, O,) and made the same a back ( jaEalahu ZahorFA ) to the couch. (S, O, K. [What is here called the “ back ” of the couch is app. so called as being likened to the back of a beast on which one rides: see rumaAlN .]) Accord. to IKt, ramalotu Alsyr [app. a mistranscription for Als~ariyra ] and ↓ A^aromalotuhu signify I wove the syr [or the sryr ] with a $ariyT of leaves, or fibres, of the palm-tree. (TA.) ― -b2- [Hence,] ramalotu Alqawola and AlwaSofa [(assumed tropical:) I wove, i. e. composed, the saying and the description ]. (S, TA.) [It is also said of a camel: see rataka .] -A4- ramalN as an inf. n. [app. of ramila AlEaAmu or ramilati Als~anapu ] signifies The year's having little rain. (TA.) Hence, in a trad. respecting [the eating of the flesh of] domestic asses, A^amara A^ano tukofaA^a Alquduwru waA^ano yuram~ala All~aHomu biAlt~uraAbi , meaning [ He ordered that the cooking-pots should be turned upside-down, and ] that the flesh should be stirred about and mixed with dust, in order that no use might be made of it. (TA.) ― -b2- And He defiled, or smeared, him, or it, with blood; (S, M, TA;) namely, a man, (S,) or a garment, and the like; (M, TA;) and (TA) so ↓ ramalahu ; (K TA;) but in this sense also the former verb is the more chaste. (TA.) And rum~ila fulaAnN biAld~ami Such a one was defiled, or smeared, with blood. (T, TA. [See also 4 and 5.]) ― -b3- In relation to speech, or language, (TA,) Alt~aromiylu signifies (tropical:) i. q. Alt~azoyiyfu ; (K, TA; [in the CK, erroneously, Alt~aroniyfu ;]) i. e., [as inf. n. of ram~ala , The adulterating it, corrupting it, or rendering it unsound, or untrue; and as inf. n. of rum~ila ,] its being [ adulterated, corrupted, or] unsound, or untrue. (TA. [See the pass. part. n., below.]) ― -b4- See also 1. -A2- And see 4.

definition: Weak rain: (IAar, T:) or little rain: (Har p.
sourceDefinition: Weak rain: (IAar, T:) or little rain: (Har p. 55:) or a small quantity of rain: (ElUmawee, T, S, M, K:) one says, A^aSaAbahumo ramalN mino maTarK A small quantity of rain fell upon them: (El-Umawee, T, M:) but Sh says, “ I have not heard ramalN in this sense except on the authority of El-Umawee: ” (TA:) the pl. is A^aromaAlN . (T, S, M.) ― -b2- [Hence, perhaps,] A^aromaAlN mino A_ibilK A number of camels in a state of dispersion. (TA.) ― -b3- Also, the sing., [as a coll. gen. n.,] Lines, or streaks, upon the legs of the wild cow, (S, M, K,) upon her fore legs and kind legs, (M,) differing from the rest of her colour: (S, M, K:) n. un. ↓ ramalapN . (TA. [See also rumolapN .]) ― -b4- And A redundance, or an excess, ( ziyaAdapN ,) in a thing. (K.) -A2- Alr~amalu is also the name of A certain kind of metre of verse; (T, S, M, K;) [ the eighth kind; ] the measure of which is [ originally ] composed of faAEilaAtuno (T, TA) six times; (TA;) so called from Alr~amalu signifying “ a certain kind of walk or pace, ” inf. n. of ramala [q. v.]: (M, K: *) and Kh says that it is also applied to any meagre verse or poetry, incongruous in structure; such being so named by the Arabs without their defining anything respecting it; as, for instance, the saying [of 'Abeed Ibn-El-Abras (TA in arts. *nb and qTb )], faAlquTabiy~aAtu faAl*~anuwbu A^aqofara mino A^aholihi maloHwbu [ Melhoob (the name of a place, K in art. lHb ) has become destitute of its inhabitants, and El- Kutabeeyát, (by which is meant a certain water, called AlquTabiy~apu , with its environs, K* and TA in art. qTb ,) and Edh-Dhanoob (the name of a place, TA in art. *nb )]: he says also that, generally, the majozuwo' [i. e. what is curtailed of two of the original feet, or what consists of two feet only, ] is thus called by them: accord. to IJ, it is applied by them to verse, or poetry, that is incongruous, unsound, or faulty, in structure, and such as falls short of the original [ standard so as not to answer completely to any regular kind or species ]: (M, TA:) thus it signifies as first explained above, and also any verse, or poetry, that is not such as is termed qaSiyd [ as meaning that of which the hemistichs are complete ] nor such as is termed rajaz [which some hold to be not verse, or poetry, but a kind of rhyming prose]. (IJ, M, K. *) [See also zamalN .]

A^araAmilu : (Msb:) or A^aromalu is applied to a man, and ↓ A^aromalapN to a woman, (M, K,) and the latter also to a pl. number, (M,) as meaning needy, needing, or in want: (M, K:) or as meaning [ misokiynN and] misokiynapN [and masaAkiynu , i. e. destitute, or indigent, &c.]: (K:) and the pl. is A^araAmilu and A^araAmilapN ; (M, K;) after the manner of substs., because the quality of a subst. is predominant therein: (M:) ↓ A^aromalapN is applied to any collective number of men and women, or men without women, or women without men, after they have become in need or want: (M:) [and] it is applied [also] to a man and to a woman as meaning poor so as to be unable to obtain anything: (T, and Mgh as from the T:) accord. to ISk, A^araAmilu is applied to a number of men and women, as meaning masaAkiynu [expl. above]; (T, S, Mgh;) or so to a number of persons whether men or women; (Msb;) and to men though there be not among them women; (T, S, Mgh;) and so ↓ A^aromalapN : (T, Mgh:) or this last, to a number of men and women needy, needing, or in want; (S;) and to men needy, needing, or in want, and weak, (S, K,) though there be not among them women. (S.) Ibn-Buzurj mentions the saying, A_in~ bayota fulaAnK laDaxomN maA yuHom~iluwnahu A_il~aA maA A@sotafoqaruwA lahu ↓ waA_in~ahumo laA^aromalapu , meaning [ Verily the household of such a one is large, and verily they are destitute of what camels they may load therewith except ] what they borrow [ for that purpose ]; (T, * TA;) i. e., they are a party not possessing camels, and unable to make a journey except upon camels that they borrow; [ AstfqrwA being] from A^ufoqira Zahora baEiyriY signifying “ he was lent the back of my camel. ” (TA.) See also A^uromuwlapN . ― -b2- ↓ A^aromalapN is also applied to a woman as meaning Having no husband: (T, S, M, Msb, K:) or a widow; one whose husband has died: (IAmb, Mgh:) or not if she possesses competence, or wealth: (Ibn-Buzurj, T, Mgh, Msb, K:) it is applied to her who has no husband because she is in need of him who would expend upon her; (Msb;) or to her whose husband has died because her provision has gone and she has lost him who earned for her (IAmb, Mgh) and by means of whom her state of life had been good: (IAmb:) in like manner, also, A^aromalu is applied to a man as meaning having no wife, (T, S, M, Mgh, Msb, K,) accord. to Kt (T, Mgh) and Sh; (Mgh;) like as A^ay~imN is applied to a man [as well as to a woman], and A^ay~imapN to a woman: (T:) or a widower; one whose wife has died: (TA:) or A^aromalu is not applied in this sense except in cases of deviation from the usual course of speech, (IAmb, Mgh, Msb, [and the like is said in the Mgh also as on the authority of Lth, and in the M as on the authority of IJ,]) because the man's provision does not go in consequence of the death of his wife, since she is not his maintainer, (IAmb, Mgh, Msb,) whereas he is her maintainer: (IAmb:) Jereer says, kul~u AlA^araAmili qado qaDayota HaAjatahaA famano liHaAjapi h`*aA AlA^aramali Al*~akari (M, TA,) or h`*iY AlA^araAmilu Alx ; (S, Mgh; [in the former ascribed in one of my copies to an unnamed poet, and in the other, to El-Hotei-ah; but in the Mgh, to Jereer, as in the M;]) [i. e. All the widows, or these widows, thou hast accomplished their want; but who is there for the want of this male widowed person ]; meaning thereby himself. (M, TA.) It is said that, if one bequeath his property to the A^araAmil , some of it is to the men whose wives have died: (Mgh:) IB says, on the authority of IKt, that when a man says, “ This property is for the A^araAmil , ” it is for the men and the women, because AlA^araAmilu applies to the males and the women; but he adds, IAmb says that it is to be given to the women exclusively of the men, because AlArAml generally applied to the women. (TA. [This is cited in the TA as though relating to ArAml as meaning masaAkiyn : but IAmb evidently uses it here as applying to women whose husbands have died; and this is its predominant meaning.]) ― -b3- It is also applied to a [lizard of the kind called] Dab~ , in the following saying of a rájiz, A^uHb~u A^ano A^aSoTaAda Dab~FA saHobalaA raEaY Alr~abiyEa waAl$~itaA='a A^aromalaA (T, TA,) meaning [ I love to hunt out, or catch, a large Db~ , that has pastured during the autumn and the winter, ] having no female, so that he may be fat. (TA.) ― -b4- And one says also EaAmN A^aromalu (ISk, T, S, M, K) and sanapN ramolaA='u (ISk, T, S, M) meaning (tropical:) A year of little rain (ISk, T, S, M, K, TA) and of little good or benefit. (T, M, K, TA.) -A2- Also i. q. A^abolaqu [i. e. Black and white: or white in the kind legs as high as the thighs ]: (AA, T:) or a sheep or goat of which all the legs are black: fem. ramolaA='u : (A 'Obeyd, S:) or the latter is applied to a ewe as meaning of which the legs are black, the rest of her being white. (AZ, T, M, K.)

definition: , (S, A, Mgh, Msb, K,) aor.
sourceDefinition: , (S, A, Mgh, Msb, K,) aor. , (Msb, TA,) inf. n. zajorN , (S, A, Msb,) He chid him, by a cry, by his voice, or by reproof: (S, * K, * TA:) he checked him, restrained him, or forbade him, with rough speech: (TA:) or prevented, hindered, restrained, or withheld, him: or forbade, or prohibited, him: [ by any kind of cry or speech: ] as also ↓ Azdjrhu ; (S, A, Mgh, Msb, K;) the latter originally Aztjrhu : (Msb, TA:) Eano ka*aA from [ doing ] such a thing: (A, * Mgh, TA:) and Eani Als~uwo'i from evil. (TA.) ― -b2- zajara Alkaloba , (K,) and Als~abuEa , (TA,) and zajara bihi (K,) (assumed tropical:) He cried out to, or at, the dog, (K,) and the beast of prey, (TA,) in order that he might forbear, refrain, or abstain. (K, TA.) [See a tropical ex. voce HinowN .] ― -b3- zajara AlbaEiyra (tropical:) He incited the camel to quickness: (TA:) he drove, or urged, the camel, (S, K, TA,) and incited him with a peculiar cry, so that he became excited, and went on: (TA:) he said to the camel Hawobi : and zajara Aln~aAqapa (assumed tropical:) He said to the she-camel Halo : (AZ, TA:) and zajara Alganama (tropical:) He (a pastor) cried out to, or at, the sheep or goats: (A, Mgh, TA:) and in like manner, to or at, a horse or the like, and a camel, and a beast of prey, with a high, or loud, voice, and vehemently: (TA:) and Alr~iyHu tazojuru Als~aHaAba (tropical:) [ The wind drives the clouds ]. (A.) ― -b4- zajorN signifies The driving away with crying or a cry: and by subsequent applications, sometimes, (assumed tropical:) the driving away: and sometimes (assumed tropical:) the crying, or crying out, or a cry. (B, TA.) ― -b5- zajara AlT~aAy^ira , (K,) aor. , inf. n. zajorN ; (TA;) and ↓ Azdjrhu ; (K;) (tropical:) He chid the bird, auguring evil from it. (K, TA.) ― -b6- And zajara AlT~ayora (tropical:) He threw a pebble at the birds, and cried out; and if, in flying, they turned their right sides towards him, he augured well from them; but if their left sides, evil. (A.) ― -b7- Hence, (A,) zajorN also signifies (tropical:) The auguring from the flight, alightingplaces, cries, kinds, or names, of birds: (S, A, K:) you say, huwa yazojuru AlT~ayora He augurs from the flight, &c., of birds: (A:) or zajorN signifies the auguring well from a bird's or some other thing's sunuwH [or turning the right side towards one, or the contrary ], and evil from its buruwH [or turning the left side towards one, or the contrary ]. (Zj.) And zajara guraAba Albayoni means (assumed tropical:) He went away, departed, or journeyed. (Har p. 308.) ― -b8- [Hence,] it also signifies (tropical:) The practising of divination: (K:) or a species thereof: you say, zajarotu A^an~ahu yakuwnu ka*aA waka*aA I have divined that it is so and so. (S, L.) [See also zaAjirN ] ― -b9- zajarato bimaA fiY baTonihaA (assumed tropical:) She (a camel) cast forth what was in her belly. (K, TA.)

definition: He drew water by means of the zuronuwq , (Mgh, K, TA,) or the zuronuwqaAni , (TA,) for hire.
sourceDefinition: He drew water by means of the zuronuwq , (Mgh, K, TA,) or the zuronuwqaAni , (TA,) for hire. (Mgh, K, TA.) Hence the saying of 'Alee, laA A^adaEu AlHaj~a walawo tazaronaqotu , meaning I will not omit, or neglect, the pilgrimage, though I should draw water by means of the zrnwq , or zrnwqAn , and perform it with the hire obtained thereby: thus it is explained: another explanation will be found in what follows. (Mgh, TA.) -A2- tzrnq fiY Alv~iyAbi He clad, and covered, himself in the clothes. (K.) ― -b2- And hence, [it is said,] because implying concealment of the excess [of the price] in the sale, (TA,) tzrnq also signifies taEay~ana , (Mgh, K, TA, [in the CK, erroneously, tagay~ara ,]) from Alz~aronaqapu meaning AlEiynapu ; (Mgh;) i. e. He bought on credit, for an excess [ in the amount of the price ]. (TK.) And accord. to some, walawo tazaronaqotu , in the saying of 'Alee mentioned above, means walawo taEay~anotu , (Mgh,) i. e. walawo taEay~anotu Eiynapa Alz~aAdi waAlr~aAHilapi [ though I should buy on credit, for more than the current price, the travelling-provision and the camel to be ridden ]: (TA:) but the former explanation is the more likely. (Mgh.)

sourceDefinition: , as some pronounce it, is by others pronounced zaronuwqN , which is of a strange form, [said to be] of the measure faEonuwlN , (IJ, TA,) mentioned by Kr on the authority of Lh: (TA:) [the dual] zuronuwqaAni , (S, Mgh, K,) mentioned by J in art. zrq , the n being regarded by him as augmentative, but by the author of the K as radical, (TA,) also pronounced zaronuwqaAni , (K,) signifies Two pillarlike structures ( manaArataAni ) constructed by the head of a well, (S, Mgh, K,) on the two sides thereof; (K;) or two walls; or two posts; (Mgh;) across which is placed a piece of wood, (S, Mgh,) called the naEaAmap ; (S;) and to this is suspended the pulley by means of which the water is drawn: (S, Mgh:) or two structures like the signs set up to show the way, by the brink of a well, of clay or of stones: (TA:) accord. to the S, (TA,) if of wood, they are called diEaAmataAn : or, as El-Kilábee says, if of wood, they are called naEaAmataAni , and the crosspiece is called the Eajalap , and to this the large bucket is suspended: (S, TA:) pl. zaraAniyqu . (TA.) ― -b2- zuronuwqN also signifies A rivulet; (Sh, Mgh, K;) app. a rivulet in which runs the water that is drawn by means of the zrnwq . (Sh, Mgh,* TA.)

definition: , aor. , inf. n. zamaEN , He became confounded, or perplexed, and unable to see his right course; or he became bereft of his reason or intellect; in consequence of fear: (S, Msb, * K: *) he feared,...
sourceDefinition: , aor. , inf. n. zamaEN , He became confounded, or perplexed, and unable to see his right course; or he became bereft of his reason or intellect; in consequence of fear: (S, Msb, * K: *) he feared, or was afraid: (K:) he was impatient; or had not sufficient strength to bear what befell him, and found not patience: (L:) he became disquieted, disturbed, agitated, flurried, or in a state of commotion. (Lh.) -A2- zamaEati AlA^aronabu , aor. , (TA,) inf. n. zamaEaAnN , (Lth, K, TA,) The hare was light, or active, and quick, or swift: (Lth, K, TA:) and ↓ AzmEt it ran, (S, TA,) and was light, or active. (TA.) And zamaEa , aor. , inf. n. zamaEaAnN , He went slowly. (ISk, S, K.) Thus the verb has two contr. significations. (K.) And He went with short steps; as also ↓ tzm~E . (TA.)

sourceDefinition: , and zahiqato , (S, Mgh, Msb, K,) the latter preferred by IKoot and Hr, but the former by A'Obeyd, (TA,) aor. , (S, Msb, K, *) inf. n. zuhuwqN , (S, Mgh,) which is of both verbs, (S,) or this is of the former verb, and the inf. n. of the latter is zahaqN , (Msb,) [but in the K it seems to be indicated, by its being said of the latter verb that it is of the class of samiEa , that the inf. n. of this verb is zahoqN ,] His soul went forth, passed forth, or departed: (S, Mgh, Msb, K, TA:) it perished: it died: (TA:) nafosuhu ↓ Ainozahaqato and AinozihaAqu Alr~uwHi are not of the [classical] language of the Arabs. (Mgh.) It is said in the Kur [ix. 55 and 86] watazohaqa A^anofusuhumo wahumo kaAfiruwna [ And that their souls may depart while they are unbelievers ]. (S.) The primary meaning of zuhuwqN is The going forth, passing forth, or departing, with difficulty. (Bd in ix. 55.) ― -b2- [Hence,] zahaqa Al$~aYo'u (tropical:) The thing perished, passed away, or came to nought; (Msb, K, TA;) became null, void, or of no effect. (K, TA.) And zahaqa AlbaATilu (tropical:) What was false, or vain, passed away, or came to nought, (S, Msb, K, TA,) being overcome by the truth, or reality, or fact: or, accord. to Katádeh, by AlbATl is here meant the devil. (TA.) ― -b3- And zahaqa Als~ahomu (S, Msb, K, TA) and zahiqa (Msb) (tropical:) The arrow passed beyond the butt, (S, Msb, K, TA,) and fell behind it: (TA:) or went swiftly: (Ham p. 23:) or the former has this meaning: and the latter is syn. with zaliqa [app. meaning it slid along the ground ]. (JK.) ― -b4- And zahaqa Alfarasu , aor. , inf. n. zuhuwqN , (assumed tropical:) The horse preceded, went before, got before, outwent, or outstripped. (S, * Msb.) And zahaqati Alr~aAHilapu , inf. n. zuhuwqN (ISk, S, K) and zahoqN , (TA as from the K, [but not in the CK nor in my MS. copy of the K,]) (tropical:) The saddle-camel preceded, went before, got before, outwent, or outstripped, the horses, or horsemen; (ISk, JK, * S, K, TA;) and ↓ Anzhqt signifies the same. (JK.) And zahaqa fulaAnN , inf. n. zahoqN and zuhuwqN , (tropical:) Such a one preceded, went before, &c.; (K, TA;) or zahaqa bayona A^ayodiynaA (tropical:) preceded us, went before us, &c., and preceded, &c., the horses, or horsemen; (TA;) and ↓ Anzhq signifies the same. (K.) -A2- zahaqa said of a bone, (S, K,) aor. , (K,) inf. n. zuhuwqN , Its marrow became compact and full; (S, K;) as also ↓ Azhq . (L, K.) And zahaqati Ald~aAb~apu , with the same aor. and inf. n., The beast was, or became, marrowy in the utmost degree, its marrow-bones being compacted and full. (TA.) ― -b2- Also, said of marrow, It was, or became, compact and full. (S, K.)

definition: He (God) caused his soul to go forth, pass forth, or depart.
sourceDefinition: He (God) caused his soul to go forth, pass forth, or depart. (Mgh, Msb.) The phrase Alqatolu A_izohaAqN means (assumed tropical:) Slaughter is a cause of making the soul to come to nought, and to depart. (Mgh.) ― -b2- [Hence,] Azhq AlbaATila (tropical:) He (God) caused what was false, or vain, to pass away, or come to nought. (S, K, TA.) See also 3. ― -b3- And Azhq Als~ahoma (S, K) mina Alhadafi (K) (tropical:) He made the arrow to pass beyond the butt. (S, K, TA.) ― -b4- And Azhqt Ald~aAb~apu Als~aroja (assumed tropical:) The beast shifted forward the saddle, and threw it upon its neck: (S, K:) and, or but, it is said to be with raA=' : [i. e. one says also, or correctly, accord. to some, A^arohaqatohu :] a rájiz says, A^axaAfu A^ano tuzohiqahu A^awo yanozariqo [(assumed tropical:) I fear that she may shift it forward, and throw it upon her neck, or it may shift backwards ]: [thus, says J,] cited to me by Abu-lGhowth, with zaAY . (S.) [Accord. to my copy of the KL, ↓ tazohiyqN , inf. n. of zh~q , signifies (assumed tropical:) The shifting backwards of a camel's saddle from his back: see 2 in art. zrq .] ― -b5- And Azhq fiY Als~ayori (assumed tropical:) He was quick [ as though urging himself forward ] in pace, or journeying. (K.) -A2- Azhqhu also signifies He filled it; (S, O, K;) namely, a vessel: (S, O:) but accord. to the L, he overturned it; i. e. a vessel. (TA.) -A3- See also 1, near the end.

definition: (tropical:) A thing passing away, or coming to nought;
sourceDefinition: (tropical:) A thing passing away, or coming to nought; or that passes away, or comes to nought; as also ↓ zaAhiqN . (K, TA.) Hence, in the Kur [xvii. 83], A_in~a AlbaATila kaAna zahuwqFA , i. e. (tropical:) [ Verily what is false, or vain, ] is a thing that passes away, or comes to nought. (TA.) ― -b2- (tropical:) A deep well; (JK, S, K;) as also ↓ zaAhiqapN ; [in the TA zaAhiqN ;] and in like manner both are applied to a place of destruction ( matolafapN ); (JK;) and to a matolafap [app. meaning a desert in which people perish] as meaning far-extending. (Ham p. 23.) And in like manner, (S,) the former is also applied [app. as an epithet] to a faj~ [or road, or depressed road,] of an overpeering, or overhanging, mountain. (S, K.) ― -b3- Also (tropical:) Light, or active; syn. xafiyfN . (JK.)
