definition: Perishing, or dying.
sourceDefinition: Perishing, or dying. (Az, TA.) ― -b2- See also zahuwqN , in two places. ― -b3- (tropical:) An arrow passing beyond the butt, and falling behind it: (Mgh, TA:) whence the saying, in a trad., A_in~a HaAbiyFA xayorN mino zaAhiqK [expl. in art. Hbw ]. (TA.) ― -b4- [(assumed tropical:) Preceding, or outgoing. ] You say, jaA='a zaAhiqFA (assumed tropical:) He came before, or in advance of, the horses, or horsemen. (JK.) And raAHilapN zaAhiqapN (assumed tropical:) A saddlecamel preceding, going before, getting before, outgoing, or outstripping, the horses, or horsemen. (S.) ― -b5- (assumed tropical:) A man put to flight: (S, O, K:) pl. zuhaqN , (so in my copies of the S,) or zuh~aqN , (so in the O,) or zuhoqN and zuhuqN , with damm and with two dammehs. (K.) ― -b6- (tropical:) Water running vehemently: (JK, K, TA:) and (assumed tropical:) a canal ( xaliyjN ) running swiftly. (TA.) -A2- Applied to a beast ( daAb~ap ), Fat, (JK, Az, S, K,) and marrowy: (S, K:) or marrowy, but not fat in the utmost degree: or having thin, or little, marrow: (TA:) and dry, or tough, (K, TA,) by reason of leanness; so says As: (TA:) and, (K,) or as some say, (JK,) very lean; (JK, K, TA;) Such that a foul odour is perceived arising from the meagreness of its flesh: (TA:) thus it bears two contr. meanings. (K.) ― -b2- And, applied to marrow, Compact and full: (S, TA:) or, so applied, good in respect of fatness: and some say, i. q. raArN [i. e. in a melting state, or corrupt, by reason of emaciation; or thin; &c.]: so that [thus applied also] it bears two contr. meanings. (JK.) In the saying of a rájiz, (S, TA,) namely, 'Omárah Ibn-Tárik, (TA,) wamasadK A^umir~a mino A^ayaAniqi lasona biA^anoyaAbK walaA HaqaAy^iqi walaA DiEaAfK mux~uhun~a zaAhiqu accord. to Fr, it is in the nom. case, the poetry being what is termed mukofaA^ , [by which is here meant having one rhyme made to end with kesreh (which is substituted for fet-hah by poetic license) and another with dammeh,] the poet meaning [ And a rope, or many a rope, tightly twisted, of the fur of she-camels, that were not aged ones, nor such as had their teeth fallen out by reason of extreme age, nor weak, ] but whose marrow was compact and full: [or, agreeably with an explanation given above from the JK, zAhq may mean in a melting state, &c.:] another explanation is, that zAhq here means *aAhib [ going away ]: (S, TA:) but, as Sgh says, the [right] reading is EiysK EitaAqK *aAti mux~K zaAhiqi [meaning but of a reddish, or yellowish, or dingy, white hue, of generous race, having compact and full marrow ]. (TA.)

definition: One who reviles, vilifies, upbraids, reproaches, or defames, much, being reviled, &c.
sourceDefinition: One who reviles, vilifies, upbraids, reproaches, or defames, much, being reviled, &c.; (A'Obeyd, S, M, Msb, * K;) as also ↓ misab~N . (S, K.) And [simply] One's mutual reviler or vilifier &c.; (A'Obeyd, S, M, K;) as also ↓ sabiybN (M, K.) A poet, (S,) namely, 'Abd-Er-Rahmán Ibn-Hassán, satirizing Miskeen Ed-Dárimee, (TA,) says, laA tasub~an~aniY falasota bisib~iY A_in~a sib~iY mina Alr~ijaAli Alkariymu [ Thou shalt by no means revile me; for thou art not my mutual reviler: verily he, of men, who is my mutual reviler is the generous ]. (S, TA.) [See also musotab~N : and sab~aAbN .] -A2- A veil, or the like; syn. sitorN . (M.) ― -b2- A woman's muffler, or head-covering; syn. ximaArN . (S, M, Msb, K.) ― -b3- A turban. (S, M, Mgh, Msb, K.) El-Mukhabbal Es-Saadee says, (S, M, Mgh,) using it in this sense, (M, Mgh,) waA^a$ohadu mino EawofK HuluwlFA kaviyrapF yaHuj~uwna sib~a Alz~iboriqaAni AlmuzaEofaraA [ And I witness many persons of 'Owf, alighting during their journeys, going repeatedly to and fro to see Ez-Zibrikán's turban dyed with saffron ]: (S, M, Mgh:) for it was a custom of the chiefs of the Arabs to dye their turbans with saffron: or, as some say, the meaning is his Aisot ; [but this is correctly, or more commonly, termed sab~ap ;] and Ktr asserts that he was suspected: (M:) he says that Ez-Zibrikán used to tinge his Ast yellow; but this is a strange saying. (TA in art. zbrq .) ― -b4- Also, and ↓ sabiybapN , An oblong piece (S, M, K) of cloth, (M,) or of thin cloth, (K,) or of thin linen cloth, (S,) or of white cloth: (M:) or a thin garment: (Aboo-'Omar, TA:) or so the latter word: (M:) or this signifies a linen stuff that is brought from the region of the Nile, of a kind commonly known among the merchants by [ the name of ] krx , some of which are made in Misr, and their length is eight by six [ cubits: cubits being meant because the ns. of number here are fem., and *iraAE is fem.]: (Sh, TA:) or this same word signifies an oblong piece of cloth of any kind, or, as some say, of linen: (TA:) the pl. of the former is subuwbN ; (S, K, TA;) and of the latter, sabaAy^ibN : (S, M, K, TA:) in a verse of 'Alkameh Ibn-'Abadeh, the phrase bisabaA Alkat~aAni is used for bisabaAy^ibi Alkt~An . (M.) ― -b5- See also sababa , first signification.

definition: A rope, or cord;
sourceDefinition: A rope, or cord; (S, M, A, Msb, K;) as also ↓ sib~N ; (S, M, K;) the latter of the dial. of Hudheyl, (S,) and occurring in this sense in a verse of Aboo-Dhu-eyb cited voce xayoTapN ; (S, M;) accord. to some, as there meaning a wooden peg, [a meaning assigned to it in the K,] but the former is the correct meaning: (M:) the pl. of both words is A^asobaAbN , (M, TA, *) [and] the pl. of the latter word is subuwbN (S, TA) also: (TA:) or sababN signifies any rope let down, or made to descend, from above: (AO, TA:) or a strong and long rope, but no rope is so called except one by means of which one ascends and descends: (Khálid Ibn-Jembeh, TA:) or this appellation is only given to a rope of which one end is attached to a roof or ceiling or the like: (TA:) or one by means of which one ascends palm-trees: (Er-Rághib, TA:) [and] a rope by means of which one reaches, or gains access to, water. (TA.) faloyamodudo bisababK A_ilaY A@ls~amaA='i vum~a liyaqoTaEo , in the Kur [xxii. 15], means Let him stretch a rope to the roof, or ceiling, of his dwelling; then let him die strangled: i. e. let him die of rage: (M, TA:) or, as some say, let him stretch a rope to the lowest heaven; then let him traverse the intervening space until he reach the highest part thereof. (Bd.) The saying jab~ato nisaA='a AlEaAlamiyna biAls~ababo has been expl. in art. jb : in this instance, a rope or cord, may be meant; or a string, or thread. (M, TA.) ― -b2- Hence, (Msb,) (tropical:) A thing (S, M, Msb, K) of any kind (S, Msb, K) by means of which one attains, reaches, or gains access to another thing: (S, M, Msb, K:) pl. as above. (M.) One says, jaEalotu fulaAnFA liY sababFA A_ilaY fulaAnN fiY HaAjatiY , i. e. (assumed tropical:) [ I made such a one ] a means of access [ to such a one in the case of my want ]. (TA.) Hence, (M,) A^asobaAbu Als~amaA='i (assumed tropical:) The places of ascent of the heaven, or sky: (M, K:) or the tracts, or regions, thereof: (S, K:) or the gates thereof. (Ibn-Es-Seed, K. [See an ex. in a verse cited voce vamaAnuwna .]) And the saying, AirotaqaY fiY AlA^asobaAbi , meaning (assumed tropical:) He excelled [or attained to excellence ] in religion. (M.) ― -b3- (assumed tropical:) A road, or way. (A. [There mentioned among proper, not tropical, significations.]) So in the saying, in the Kur xviii. 88 and 91, vum~a A@t~abaEa sababFA (assumed tropical:) [ Then he followed a road, or way ]. (Bd.) definition: [The matter contained in the secundines;
sourceDefinition: [The matter contained in the secundines; ] a yellow, thick water [or fluid ], that comes forth with the fœtus; (S, M, K;) as also suxotN : (M, TA:) hence, in a trad., the appearance upon the face produced by excitement from remaining awake during the night is termed, by way of comparison, suxod upon the face: (S, * L:) or blood and water in the membrane that envelops the fœtus of a beast: or what comes forth with the membrane that envelops the fœtus: said to be peculiar to the human species: or common to the human species and beasts: (L:) or the water [or fluid ] in that membrane; as also suxotN and nuxoTN and faqo'N : (IAar, TA in art. fqA^ :) or [the placenta; i. e.] a thing like the liver, or like the spleen, compact, which is in the membrane that envelops the fœtus of a beast: sometimes children play with it: or that membrane itself: and i. q. rahalN [which is expl. as meaning yellow water in the suxodK , and it is also the inf. n. of rahila , q. v.]: and SuxodN is a dial. var. thereof in all its senses, those above mentioned and those following. (L.) ― -b2- Also The urine of a camel's fœtus ( faSiyl ) in its mother's belly. (L.) ― -b3- And (assumed tropical:) Yellowness in the face [as in the trad. above mentioned]. (L.)

sourceDefinition: , (S, Mgh, O, Msb,) or Al$~aYo'a , (K,) and saraqahu maAlFA , (S, Mgh, O, Msb,) thus also they sometimes said, (S, O,) the prep. being suppressed for the sake of alleviation, but meant to be understood, (Ham p. 155,) aor. inf. n. saraqN (S, Mgh, O, Msb, K) and sariqN and saraqapN (Mgh, K) and sariqapN and saroqN , (K,) He stole from him property, [or the thing, ] i. e. he took it [ from him ] secretly, and by artifice; (Mgh;) or he came clandestinely to a place of custody, and took what belonged to him, namely, another person; (O, K;) as also ↓ Astrqhu [followed by minohu ]. (IAar, K.) And saraqahumo [alone, He stole from them; or robbed them ]. (JK and K in art. bwq .) It is said in a prov., suriqa Als~aAriqu faA@notaHara (S, O) The thief was robbed, and in consequence slew himself: applied to him who has a thing not belonging to him taken from him, and whose impatience consequently becomes excessive. (Meyd, * O.) And ↓ sr~qhu , inf. n. tasoriyqN signifies the same as saraqahu : El-Farezdak says, laA taHosiban~a daraAhimFA sar~aqotahaA tamoHuw maxaAziyka Al~atiY biEumaAni [ By no means reckon thou that dirhems which thou stolest will efface thy disgraceful practices that were committed in 'Omán ]. definition: Lower, and lowest;
sourceDefinition: Lower, and lowest; contr. of A^aEolaY (M, Msb, K:) fem. sufolaY : (TA:) and pl. A^asaAfilu . (M, TA.) One says, SaAraA^asofala mino gayorihi [ He, or it, became lower than another ]. (Msb.) And it is said in the Kur [viii. 43], wA@lr~akobu A^asofala minokumo The caravan being in a place lower than ye; Asfl being here an adv. n.: or, as some read, A^asofalu minokumo , i. e. being lower than ye. (M.) ― -b2- ↓ vum~a radadonaAhu A^asofala saAfiliyna , in the Kur [xcv. 5], means (assumed tropical:) [ Then we rendered him the lowest of low: or] we reduced him to extreme old age, or decrepitude: or to a state of perishing, or passing away: or to a state of error; relating to him who has disbelieved; (M, K;) for every infant is born of the natural constitution with which he is created in his mother's womb, and he who disbelieves and errs is reduced to this state: (M:) or the meaning is, we have made him to be of the people of the fire [ of Hell ]: or [ we have made him to go down ] to the fire [ of Hell ]. (Bd.) ― -b3- sufolay muDara [ The lower of Mudar ] is said to denote those of Mudar with the exception of Kureysh and Keys: opposed to EuloyaAmuDara . (TA in art. Elw .) ― -b4- See also sufolN . ― -b5- The pl. A^asaAfilu means The lower, or lowest, parts of valleys [&c.]. (TA.) The phrase kilaAbu AlA^asaAfili occurs in a verse of Aboo-Dhu-eyb as meaning [ The dogs ] of the lower, or lowest, parts of the valleys. (M.) ― -b6- And (assumed tropical:) The young ones of camels. (As, S, * TA.)

sourceDefinition: , aor. , inf. n. salajaAnN (S, O, Msb, K) and salojN , (S, O, K,) He swallowed (S, O, Msb, K) a morsel, or mouthful, or gobbet, (S, O, K,) and food, (TA,) or a thing; (Msb;) as also salaja , aor. ; (Msb;) and ↓ tsl~j : (O, K: *) or salajaAnN signifies the eating quickly. (TA.) Hence the saying, AlA^akolu salajaAnN waAlqaDaA='u lay~aAnN [ Eating is a swallowing, and paying is a putting off ], (S, Meyd, O,) or AlA^axo*u salajaAnN Alx [ Taking, or receiving, is a swallowing, &c.]: (Meyd, TA:) i. e., when a man receives a loan, or the like, he devours it [greedily]; but when he from whom he has received it demands his due, he puts him off by promising to pay it: (S, O:) a prov., (Meyd, O, TA,) applied to him who takes the property of others and to whom it is easy to do so; but when he is sued for payment, puts off, and it is difficult to him: (Meyd:) meaning that one loves to take, and hates to return, or restore. sourceDefinition: A certain plant, (S, K,) upon which the camels pasture, (S,) soft, flaccid, or fragile, of the shrub-kind; (TA;) also called ↓ sul~ujaAnN , (K, TA,) or ↓ sul~ajaAnN , (CK,) like qm~HAn ; (K;) and ↓ saliyjapN : (TA:) or the ↓ sl~jAn , (O, TA,) i. e. sul~ajaAn , with damm to the s , and teshdeed and fet-h to the l , (O,) is a species of the sul~aj ; (O, TA;) and this last is one of the largest of the kind of trees called HamoD : (O:) accord. to AHn, (TA,) or as is said by some one or more of the Arabs of the desert, (O,) the sul~aj is a large kind of trees, like the tails of the [ lizards called ] DibaAb [pl. of Dab~N ], green, and having thorns, and [ of the kind termed ] HamoD : (O, TA:) in the T it is said to be a sort of HamoD that ceases not to be green in the summer, or hot season, and in the rabiyE [app. here meaning autumn ], and is weak, or weak and soft: Az also says that it grows in the plains, or level tracts, has a fruit, or produce, with a sharpness in the extremities thereof, and is green in the [ season called ] rabiyE , and then dries up, and becomes yellow: and he adds, [contr. to what has been said above, from his work, the T,] it is not reckoned among the trees called HamoD . (L, TA.)

sourceDefinition: [accord. to those who make the alif to be a sign of the fem. gender] or salowFY [accord. to those who make that letter to be one of quasicoordination] A certain bird, (S, M, Msb, K,) [in the present day applied to the quail, ] i. q. sumaAnaY [which is also applied in the present day to the quail], (Ksh and Bd and Jel in ii. 54,) [or] white [?], resembling the sumaAnaY , (M,) or like the pigeon, but longer in the shank and neck than the latter, and of a colour resembling that of the sumaAnaY , quick in motion: accord. to Akh, the word is used as sing. and pl.: (Msb:) [or] Akh says, I have not heard any sing. thereof, and it seems that the single one is thus called like the pl. number, in like manner as dfolaY is [said to be] applied to one and to the pl. number: (S:) or the n. un. is salowaApN ; (M, K;) of which Lth cites as an ex. this saying, [in which bal~alahu should be bal~alahaA ,] kamaA A@notafaDa Als~alowaApu bal~alahu AlqaToru [ Like as shakes the selwáh which the rain has much wetted ]. (M.)

definition: A water which is drunk and which renders one forgetful, or content, or happy, in a case of privation;
sourceDefinition: A water which is drunk and which renders one forgetful, or content, or happy, in a case of privation; or comforts, or consoles, for a loss or want: (Lh, M, K:) or a thing that is given to drink to the passionate lover in order that he may be forgetful, or content, or happy, without the woman: (Lh, M:) or it consists in one's taking some of the dust, or earth, of a grave, and sprinkling it upon water, and giving it to drink to the passionate lover, (M, K, *) whereupon his love dies: (K:) or rain-water poured upon a certain bead ( xarazapN ) called ↓ sulowaAnapN , of which they used to say that when the passionate lover drank this water he became forgetful, or content, or happy, in his privation: (S:) or a certain medicine which is given to drink to him who is in grief and in consequence of which he becomes happy; (S, K;) called by the physicians mufar~iHN : (S:) or a certain bead ( xarazapN ) for captivating, or fascinating, also called ↓ sulowaAnapN , (Lh, M, K,) and ↓ salowaAnapN , (Sgh, K,) with which women captivate, or fascinate, men, restraining them from other women: (Lh, M:) or ↓ sulowaAnapN signifies [or, accord. to the K, signifies also] a certain bead ( xarazapN , M, K,) transparent, (M,) which, when one has buried it in the sand and then scraped the sand up from over it, is seen to be black, and is given [ in water ] to drink to a man, and renders him forgetful, or content, or happy, in a case of privation: (M, K: *) or a pebble upon which water is poured and given to drink to a man, who thereupon becomes forgetful, or content, or happy, in a case of privation: (M:) Ru-beh says, lawo A^a$orabu Als~ulowaAna maA saliytu maAbiY ginFY Eanoki waA_ino ganiytu (S, M, *) and Nuseyr Ibn-Abee-Nuseyr, in answer to a question of As respecting the meaning of AlslwAn , said that it is a bead ( xarazapN ) which is bruised, or pulverized, [ and upon which water is then poured, ] the water of which occasions in the drinker thereof forgetfulness, or content, or happiness, in a case of privation: but As disallowed this, and said that it is an inf. n. of salawotu , and that the meaning is lawo A^a$orabu Als~uluw~a [i. e. (assumed tropical:) Were I made to drink forgetfulness, &c., I should not become forgetful, &c.: there is not in me freedom from want of thee, though I be free from want of others]. (TA.) See also salowapN .

definition: a word of which the final radical letter is rejected, (S, Msb,) and of which there are two dial.
sourceDefinition: a word of which the final radical letter is rejected, (S, Msb,) and of which there are two dial. vars., (Msb,) being, accord. to some, originally sanohapN , (S, Msb,) like jabohapN (S) or sajodapN , (Msb,) and accord to others, sanowpN , (S, * Msb,) like $ahowapN , and upon each of these originals are founded modifications of the word, (Msb,) therefore it is mentioned in the K [and S and other lexicons] in the present art. and again in art. snw , (TA,) A year; syn. HawolN ; (Msb;) or EaAmN : (M, K:) or, as Suh says, in the R, the sanap is longer than the EaAm ; the latter word being applied to the [twelve] Arabian months [collectively], and thus differing from the former word: (TA:) with the Arabs it consists of four seasons, mentioned before [in art. zmn , voce zamanN ]: but sometimes it is tropically applied to (tropical:) a single faSol [or quarter ]; as in the saying, daAma AlmaTaru Als~anapa kul~ahaA , meaning [ The rain continued ] during the faSol [or quarter, all of it ]: (Msb:) [see more in art. snw and snY :] the dim. is ↓ sunayohapu (S, Msb) accord. to those who make the original of sanapN to be sanohapN , (Msb,) and ↓ sunay~apN (S, Msb) accord. to those who make the original of sanapN to be sanowapN ; (Msb;) and some say sunayonapN , but this is rare: (TA:) the pl. is sanahaAtN (Msb, K) accord. to those who make the original of sanapN to be sanohpN , (Msb,) and sanawaAtN (Msb, K) accord. to those who make the original of sanapN to be sanowapN ; (Msb;) and sinuwna also, (S, Msb, K,) like the masc. perfect pl., (Msb,) [agreeably with a rule applying to other cases of this kind,] with kesr, to the s , (S, TA,) and siniyna [in the accus. and gen. cases], (Msb, TA,) so that one says, h`*ihi sinuwna [ These are years ], and raA^ayotu siniyna [ I saw years ], (TA,) and the n is elided when it is prefixed to another noun, governing the latter in the gen. case, (Msb,) and some say sunuwna , with damm to the s ; (S, TA;) and in one dial., the Y is retained in all the cases, and the n is made a letter of declinability, with tenween when the word is indeterminate, [so that one says siniynN ,] and is not elided when the word is prefixed to another noun, governing the latter in the gen. case, because it is [regarded as] one of the radical letters of the word; and of this dial. is the saying of the Prophet, Aall~`hum~a A@joEalohaA Ealayohimo siniynFA kasiniyni yuwsufa [ O God, make them to be to them years like the years of Joseph ]; (Msb; [but in my copy of the Mgh, I find kasiniY yuwsufa ;]) or with respect to siniynN , like miy^iynN , with refa [and tenween], there are two opinions; one is, that it is of the measure fiEoliynN , like gisoliynN , with a rejection [of one letter], though this is an anomalous pl., for there sometimes occurs among pls. that which has no parallel, as EidFY , and this is the opinion of Akh; the other is, that it is of the measure faEiylN , changed to fiEiylN because of the kesreh of the second letter; the pl. being in some instances of the measure faEiylN , like kaliybN and EabiydN ; but he who holds this opinion makes its final n to be a substitute for w , and that of miAy^apN a substitute for Y : (S:) you may also suppress the tenween in siniynN ; [in which case it seems that one says siniyna in the nom. case (assimilating it to sinuwna ) as well as in the accus. and the gen.; like as one does in the instances of buriyn and biriyn , pls. of burapN , accord. to the K, though, as I have shown in art. brw , there is some doubt on this point;] but the suppression of the tenween in siniynN is more rare than its pronunciation: (I' Ak p. 18:) and another pl. is suniY~N , [originally sunuw~N ,] of the measure fuEuwlN . (Er-Rághib, TA in art. snw .) The phrase val`va miAy^apK siniyna , in the Kur [xviii. 24], is said by Akh to be for val`vamiAy^apK mina Als~iniyna [ Three hundred of years ]: and he says that if the sinuwn be an explicative of the miAy^ap , it is in the gen. case [to agree with miAy^apK ]; and if an explicative of the val`v , it is in the accus. case [to agree with val`va ]. (S. [See also Bd on this phrase; and see De Sacy's Ar. Gr., 2nd ed., i. 423.]) [ lisanapK , relating to an animal or a plant or the like, means To the completion of a year: and lisanatihi , to the completion of his, or its, year; i. e. in his, or its, first year. ] And one says, ↓ laqiytuhu muno*u sunay~aAtK [ I met him some years ago; three or more, to ten, years ago ]: a phrase like laqiytuhu *aAta AlEuwayomi . (Az, TA in art. Ewm .) And ↓ sunay~apN is a dim. of enhancement, of sanapN : one says sunay~apN HamoraA='u A severe year of drought or barrenness or dearth: (TA:) and AlbiyDi ↓ waqaEuwA fiY Als~unay~aAti [ They lapsed into the severe years of scantiness of herbage ]: these were years that pressed hard upon the people of ElMedeeneh. (K, TA.) ― -b2- sanapN [alone] also signifies (tropical:) Drought, or barrenness: (Msb, K, TA:) or vehement, or intense, drought: (TA in art. snw :) an instance of a noun used especially in one of its senses, like daAb~apN applied to “ a horse, ” and maAlN applied to “ camels: ” pl., in this, as in the former, sense, sanahaAtN [and sanawaAtN ] and sinuwna and siniynN . A seeker of herbage and of a place in which to alight was sent to a tract, and found it dried up by want of rain, and when he returned, being asked respecting it, he said, Als~anapu , meaning (tropical:) Drought, &c. (TA.)

Ar., sec. ed., iii. 473:)] a certain species of tree, (S, A, Mgh, O, Msb, K,) of great size, (Msb,) growing to a very great size, (Mgh,) that grows only in India, and is conveyed thence to other countries; (Mgh, Msb;) so they say: (Mgh:) Z says, (Msb,) it is a black, heavy, wood, which is brought from India, (A, Msb,) in pieces made of an oblong form, and squared, (A,) and which the woodfretter can hardly, or not at all, wear, or waste; (A, Msb;) and he says that its pl. is siyjaAnN : (Msb: [but this is said in the A only to be pl. of sAj meaning “ a rounded, wide, TayolasaAn : ”]) some say that it resembles ebony, but is less black: (Msb:) accord to the A, Noah's ark was made of it: but several authors say that it is related in the Book of the Law revealed to Moses that it was made of the Sanawobar [or pine-tree]; and some say that the Snwbr is a species of the sAj : (TA:) AHn describes it, (O, TA,) on the authority of one who had seen it in its places of growth, (O,) as a species of tree that grows to a great size, tall and wide, having leaves like the shields of the Deylem ( Ald~ayolam , q. v.), with one of which leaves a man may cover himself, and it will protect him from the rain, and it has a sweet odour, like the odour of the leaves of the walnut, and is fine and soft, or smooth; (O, TA,) the elephants [he says] are fond of it, and of the leaves of the banana, both of which they eat: it is not of the trees that grow in the land of the Arabs, nor does it grow in any country except those of India and the Zenj; nor does any tree grow so tall, nor any so big: (O:) ↓ saAjapN is the n. un.; and its pl. is saAjaAtN : (Msb:) and it signifies a piece of wood of the tree called sAj , made of an oblong form, and squared, as brought from India; (A, * Mgh, TA;) such as is cut and prepared for a foundation and the like: (Mgh:) one says, fiY A^asaAsi binaAy^ihi saAjapN [ In the foundation of his building is a piece of wood of the sAj cut in an oblong form, and squared ]: (A:) a sAjp from which a door is cloven, or divided off lengthwise, is called saliyjapN : (TA:) and the term saAjapN is also applied to the board, or tablet, [ of wood of the sAj ,] upon which stand [ or rest ] the two scales of the balance when one weighs with it. (Ham. p. 818.) -A2- Also A [ garment of the kind called ] TayolasaAn of the colour termed xuDorap [here meaning a dark, or an ashy, dust-colour ]: (S, A, O, K:) or a black TylsAn : (IAar, O, K:) or a large, thick, or coarse, TylsAn : (TA:) or a TylsAn made of a round form, (A, TA,) and wide: (A:) or a TylsAn hollowed out in the middle ( muqaw~arN ); so woven: (Az, O, Msb:) this last is said to be meant in a trad. in which it is said that the Prophet used to wear in war such qalaAnis [pl. of qalanosuwapN , q. v.,] as were [made] of siyjaAn : (TA:) siyjaAnN is the pl.: (T, S, A, O, Msb:) the dim. is ↓ suwayojN . (TA.) It is tropically applied to signify (tropical:) A [ garment of the kind called ] kisaA=' made of a square form, or four-sided; and is described as a sort of miloHafap , woven. (TA.) As meaning a TylsAn , it is said by some, that its A is originally Y . (L, TA.) ― -b2- It is also used, by a poet, in the manner of an epithet, as meaning Of the colour termed xuDorap [expl. above]. (TA.)

sourceDefinition: , inf. n. of saAma , primarily signifies The going, or going away, engaged, or occupied, in seeking, or in seeking for or after, or in seeking to find and take or to get, a thing: and sometimes it is used as meaning the going, or going away; as when it is said of camels [or the like]: and sometimes, as meaning the seeking, or seeking for or after, or seeking to find and take or to get; as when it relates to selling or buying. (Er-Rághib, TA.) ― -b2- You say, saAmati AlmaA$iyapu (S, Mgh, Msb, TA) or Aln~aEamu (M) or AlmaAlu , (K,) aor. tasuwmu , (S, M, Msb,) inf. n. sawomN , (S, M, Mgh, Msb,) The cattle pastured (S, M, Mgh, Msb, K, TA) by themselves (Msb) where they pleased; and in like manner, Alganamu [ the sheep or goats ]: or went away at random, or roved, pasturing where they pleased. (TA.) ― -b3- [Hence, sAm , inf n as above, He did as he pleased. ] You say, xal~ayotuhu wasawomahu I left him to do as he pleased. (S, M, K * [In the CK, xal~Ahu wasaw~amahu limaAyuriyduhu is put for xal~aAhu wasawomahu limaA yuriyduhu ; and the like is done in one of my copies of the S. See also 2.]) ― -b4- And saAma , (S,) or saAmati AlA_ibilu , and Alr~iyHu , (M, K,) or Alr~iyaAHu , (S,) inf. n. as above, (S, M,) He, or it, (S,) or the camels, and the wind, (M, K,) or the winds, (S,) passed, went, or went on or along: (S, M, K:) or sawomN signifies the passing, &c., quickly; one says of a she camel, saAmat , aor. and inf. n. as above, she passed, &c., quickly; (As, TA;) and hence the saying of Dhu-l-Bijádeyn cited in art. ErD , voce taEar~aDa : or the passing, &c., quickly, with the desire of making a sound in going along. (TA.) ― -b5- And saAmati AlT~ayoru EalaY Al$~aYo'i , (M, K,) aor. and inf. n. as above, (M,) The birds went, [or hovered, ] or circled, round about the thing: (M, K:) or, as some say, sawomN signifies any going, [or hovering, ] or circling, round about. (M.) -A2- [As mentioned in the first sentence of this art.,] sawomN is also in selling and buying. (S.) You say, sAm Als~iloEapa , (Mgh, Msb,) aor. and inf. n. as above, (Msb,) He (the seller) offered the commodity, or article of merchandise, (Mgh, Msb:) and it is also said of the purchaser, like ↓ AisotaAmahaA , (Mgh, Msb,) meaning he sought to obtain the sale of the commodity, or article of merchandise: and one says also of the seller, and of the purchaser, sAm biAls~iloEapi , meaning he mentioned the price of the commodity [ in offering it for sale, and in offering to purchase it ]: (Msb:) and in like manner, sumotu fulaAnFA siloEatiY , inf. n. as above, I said to such a one, “ Wilt thou take [or purchase ] my commodity for such a price? ” (TA:) and saAmaniY bisiloEatihi he (the seller, Msb) mentioned to me the price of his commodity [ in offering it for sale ]: (Msb, TA:) [and, agreeably with these explanations,] Kr says that Als~awomu signifies AlEaroDu [i. e. the act of offering, &c.]: (M, TA:) or sumotu biAls~iloEapi , inf. n. sawomN (M, K) and suwaAmN , with damm; (K, TK; [in the former only said to be syn. with sawomN in selling and buying;]) and ↓ saAwamotu , (M, K,) inf. n. siwaAmN ; (TA;) and bihaA ↓ Aisotamotu and EalayohaA ; signify gaAlayotu [which means I offered the commodity for sale, mentioning its price, and was exorbitant in my demand: and also I purchased the commodity for a dear, or an excessive, price: and both these meanings are app. here intended]: (M, K, TA:) and in like manner, Als~iloEapa ↓ Aisotamotuhu [ I offered to him the commodity for sale, &c.: and I purchased of him the commodity, &c.]: (TA:) or, as some say, (so in the TA, but in the M and K “ and, ”) this last, as also EalaY Als~iloEapi , ↓ Aisotamotuhu , means ↓ saA^alotuhu sawomahaA [i. e. I asked him the price at which the commodity was to be sold ]: (M, K, TA:) and saAmaniyhaA , (M,) or ↓ saAwamaniyhaA , (TA, [but the former is app. the right,]) means ↓ *akara liY sawomahaA [i. e. he mentioned to me the price at which it was to be sold ]: (M, TA:) you say also, Ealayohi ↓ Aisotamotu bisiloEatiY when you mention the price of the commodity [i. e. it means I mentioned to him the price at which I would sell my commodity ]: and you say, min~iY siloEatiY ↓ AisotaAma when he is the person who offers to thee the price [i. e. it means he offered to me a price for my commodity; or he sought to obtain from me the sale of my commodity by offering a price for it ]: (TA:) and EalaY~a ↓ AisotaAma he contended [ by bidding ] against me in a sale: (S, * PS:) or EalaY~a Als~iloEapa ↓ AisotaAma , which means AstAm EalaY sawomiY [i. e. he sought to obtain the sale of the commodity in opposition to me, or to my seeking it ]. (Msb. [See also 3.]) Hence, [Mo- hammad is related to have said,] laA yasuwmu Alr~ajulu EalaY sawomi A^axiyhi , (Mgh,) or lAyswm A^aHadukumo ElY swm Axyh , (Msb,) i. e. [ The man, or any one of you, ] shall not purchase [ in opposition to his brother ]: (Mgh, Msb:) and it may mean shall not sell; the case being that of a man's offering to the purchaser his commodity for a certain price, and another's then saying, “ I have the like thereof for less than this price: ” so that the prohibition relates in common to the seller and the buyer: (M:) and the saying is also related otherwise, i. e. ↓ laAyasotaAmu , meaning shall not purchase. (Mgh.) And it is said in a trad., nahaY Eani Als~awomi qabola TuluwEi Al$~amosi , meaning, accord. to Aboo-Is-hák, A^ano bisiloEatihi ↓ yusaAwima [i. e. He (Mohammad) forbade the offering a commodity for sale before the rising of the sun ]; because that is a time in which God is to be praised, and one should not be diverted by other occupation: or, he says, it may mean the pasturing of camels; because, before sunrise, when the pasturage is moist with dew, it occasions a fatal disease. (TA.) You say also, sumotuka HasanapF ↓ baEiyraka siymapF [ I have mentioned to thee a good price for thy camel ]. (S.) And fiyhi ↓ AisotaAma gaAliyapF ↓ siymapF [ He demanded for it a dear price ]. (TA in art. Hvr .) And saAmahu biEamalK [ He made to him an offer of working, mentioning the rate of payment; or bargained, or contracted, with him for work ]. (K in art. Eml . [See also 3.]) ― -b2- The Arabs also say, EaraDa EalaY~a sawoma EaAl~apK [ He offered to me in the manner of offering water to camels taking a second draught ]; meaning like the saying of the vulgar, EaroDa saAbiriY~K : (Ks, TA: [see art. sbr :]) a prov. applied to him who offers to thee that of which thou hast no need. (Sh, TA. [See also art. El ; and see Freytag's Arab. Prov. ii. 84.]) ― -b3- And you say, saAmahu AlA^mora , (M, K,) aor. as above, (TA,) inf. n. sawomN , (M, TA,) He imposed upon him, or made him to undertake, the affair, as a task, or in spite of difficulty or trouble or inconvenience; or he ordered, required, or constrained, him to do the thing, it being difficult or troublesome or inconvenient: (M, K, TA:) or he brought upon him the affair, or event; (Zj, M, K, TA;) as also ↓ saw~amahu , (K,) inf. n. tasowiymN : (TA:) or he endeavoured to induce him, or incited him, or made him, to do, or to incur, the affair, or event: (Sh, TA:) it is mostly used in relation to punishment, and evil, (Zj, M, K, TA,) and wrong-doing: and hence the saying in the Kur [ii. 46 and vii. 137 and xiv. 6], yasuwmuwnakumo suwo'a A@loEa*aAbi They bringing upon you evil punish- ment or torment: (Zj, M, TA:) or seeking, or desiring, for you evil punishment: (Ksh and Bd in ii. 46:) or endeavouring to induce you to incur it: (Ksh ibid.:) from saAmahu xasofFA [expl. by what here follows]. (Ksh and Bd ibid.) You say, sumotuhu xasofFA I brought upon him xasof [i. e. wrong, or wrong treatment, as expl. in the Ksh and by Bd ubi suprà]: or I endeavoured to induce him to incur it ( A^aradotuhu Ealayohi ): (S:) [see also xasofN : and sumotuhu xuT~apa xasofK ; expl. in art. xT :] and siyma Alxasofa He was constrained to incur, or to do, what is termed Alxasof [meaning abasement or ignominy, or that which was difficult ]: (TA:) and sumotuhu *ul~FA I abased him. (Msb.) -A3- saAmahu , aor. as above, also signifies He kept, or clave, to it, not quitting it. (M, * TA.) -A4- See also 4.

(Er-Rághib, TA.) ― -b2- You say, saAmati AlmaA$iyapu (S, Mgh, Msb, TA) or Aln~aEamu (M) or AlmaAlu , (K,) aor. tasuwmu , (S, M, Msb,) inf. n. sawomN , (S, M, Mgh, Msb,) The cattle pastured (S, M, Mgh, Msb, K, TA) by themselves (Msb) where they pleased; and in like manner, Alganamu [ the sheep or goats ]: or went away at random, or roved, pasturing where they pleased. (TA.) ― -b3- [Hence, sAm , inf n as above, He did as he pleased. ] You say, xal~ayotuhu wasawomahu I left him to do as he pleased. (S, M, K * [In the CK, xal~Ahu wasaw~amahu limaAyuriyduhu is put for xal~aAhu wasawomahu limaA yuriyduhu ; and the like is done in one of my copies of the S. See also 2.]) ― -b4- And saAma , (S,) or saAmati AlA_ibilu , and Alr~iyHu , (M, K,) or Alr~iyaAHu , (S,) inf. n. as above, (S, M,) He, or it, (S,) or the camels, and the wind, (M, K,) or the winds, (S,) passed, went, or went on or along: (S, M, K:) or sawomN signifies the passing, &c., quickly; one says of a she camel, saAmat , aor. and inf. n. as above, she passed, &c., quickly; (As, TA;) and hence the saying of Dhu-l-Bijádeyn cited in art. ErD , voce taEar~aDa : or the passing, &c., quickly, with the desire of making a sound in going along. (TA.) ― -b5- And saAmati AlT~ayoru EalaY Al$~aYo'i , (M, K,) aor. and inf. n. as above, (M,) The birds went, [or hovered, ] or circled, round about the thing: (M, K:) or, as some say, sawomN signifies any going, [or hovering, ] or circling, round about. (M.) -A2- [As mentioned in the first sentence of this art.,] sawomN is also in selling and buying. (S.) You say, sAm Als~iloEapa , (Mgh, Msb,) aor. and inf. n. as above, (Msb,) He (the seller) offered the commodity, or article of merchandise, (Mgh, Msb:) and it is also said of the purchaser, like ↓ AisotaAmahaA , (Mgh, Msb,) meaning he sought to obtain the sale of the commodity, or article of merchandise: and one says also of the seller, and of the purchaser, sAm biAls~iloEapi , meaning he mentioned the price of the commodity [ in offering it for sale, and in offering to purchase it ]: (Msb:) and in like manner, sumotu fulaAnFA siloEatiY , inf. n. as above, I said to such a one, “ Wilt thou take [or purchase ] my commodity for such a price? ” (TA:) and saAmaniY bisiloEatihi he (the seller, Msb) mentioned to me the price of his commodity [ in offering it for sale ]: (Msb, TA:) [and, agreeably with these explanations,] Kr says that Als~awomu signifies AlEaroDu [i. e. the act of offering, &c.]: (M, TA:) or sumotu biAls~iloEapi , inf. n. sawomN (M, K) and suwaAmN , with damm; (K, TK; [in the former only said to be syn. with sawomN in selling and buying;]) and ↓ saAwamotu , (M, K,) inf. n. siwaAmN ; (TA;) and bihaA ↓ Aisotamotu and EalayohaA ; signify gaAlayotu [which means I offered the commodity for sale, mentioning its price, and was exorbitant in my demand: and also I purchased the commodity for a dear, or an excessive, price: and both these meanings are app. here intended]: (M, K, TA:) and in like manner, Als~iloEapa ↓ Aisotamotuhu [ I offered to him the commodity for sale, &c.: and I purchased of him the commodity, &c.]: (TA:) or, as some say, (so in the TA, but in the M and K “ and, ”) this last, as also EalaY Als~iloEapi , ↓ Aisotamotuhu , means ↓ saA^alotuhu sawomahaA [i. e. I asked him the price at which the commodity was to be sold ]: (M, K, TA:) and saAmaniyhaA , (M,) or ↓ saAwamaniyhaA , (TA, [but the former is app. the right,]) means ↓ *akara liY sawomahaA [i. e. he mentioned to me the price at which it was to be sold ]: (M, TA:) you say also, Ealayohi ↓ Aisotamotu bisiloEatiY when you mention the price of the commodity [i. e. it means I mentioned to him the price at which I would sell my commodity ]: and you say, min~iY siloEatiY ↓ AisotaAma when he is the person who offers to thee the price [i. e. it means he offered to me a price for my commodity; or he sought to obtain from me the sale of my commodity by offering a price for it ]: (TA:) and EalaY~a ↓ AisotaAma he contended [ by bidding ] against me in a sale: (S, * PS:) or EalaY~a Als~iloEapa ↓ AisotaAma , which means AstAm EalaY sawomiY [i. e. he sought to obtain the sale of the commodity in opposition to me, or to my seeking it ]. (Msb. [See also 3.]) Hence, [Mo- hammad is related to have said,] laA yasuwmu Alr~ajulu EalaY sawomi A^axiyhi , (Mgh,) or lAyswm A^aHadukumo ElY swm Axyh , (Msb,) i. e. [ The man, or any one of you, ] shall not purchase [ in opposition to his brother ]: (Mgh, Msb:) and it may mean shall not sell; the case being that of a man's offering to the purchaser his commodity for a certain price, and another's then saying, “ I have the like thereof for less than this price: ” so that the prohibition relates in common to the seller and the buyer: (M:) and the saying is also related otherwise, i. e. ↓ laAyasotaAmu , meaning shall not purchase. (Mgh.) And it is said in a trad., nahaY Eani Als~awomi qabola TuluwEi Al$~amosi , meaning, accord. to Aboo-Is-hák, A^ano bisiloEatihi ↓ yusaAwima [i. e. He (Mohammad) forbade the offering a commodity for sale before the rising of the sun ]; because that is a time in which God is to be praised, and one should not be diverted by other occupation: or, he says, it may mean the pasturing of camels; because, before sunrise, when the pasturage is moist with dew, it occasions a fatal disease. (TA.) You say also, sumotuka HasanapF ↓ baEiyraka siymapF [ I have mentioned to thee a good price for thy camel ]. (S.) And fiyhi ↓ AisotaAma gaAliyapF ↓ siymapF [ He demanded for it a dear price ]. (TA in art. Hvr .) And saAmahu biEamalK [ He made to him an offer of working, mentioning the rate of payment; or bargained, or contracted, with him for work ]. (K in art. Eml . [See also 3.]) ― -b2- The Arabs also say, EaraDa EalaY~a sawoma EaAl~apK [ He offered to me in the manner of offering water to camels taking a second draught ]; meaning like the saying of the vulgar, EaroDa saAbiriY~K : (Ks, TA: [see art. sbr :]) a prov. applied to him who offers to thee that of which thou hast no need. (Sh, TA. [See also art. El ; and see Freytag's Arab. Prov. ii. 84.]) ― -b3- And you say, saAmahu AlA^mora , (M, K,) aor. as above, (TA,) inf. n. sawomN , (M, TA,) He imposed upon him, or made him to undertake, the affair, as a task, or in spite of difficulty or trouble or inconvenience; or he ordered, required, or constrained, him to do the thing, it being difficult or troublesome or inconvenient: (M, K, TA:) or he brought upon him the affair, or event; (Zj, M, K, TA;) as also ↓ saw~amahu , (K,) inf. n. tasowiymN : (TA:) or he endeavoured to induce him, or incited him, or made him, to do, or to incur, the affair, or event: (Sh, TA:) it is mostly used in relation to punishment, and evil, (Zj, M, K, TA,) and wrong-doing: and hence the saying in the Kur [ii. 46 and vii. 137 and xiv. 6], yasuwmuwnakumo suwo'a A@loEa*aAbi They bringing upon you evil punish- ment or torment: (Zj, M, TA:) or seeking, or desiring, for you evil punishment: (Ksh and Bd in ii. 46:) or endeavouring to induce you to incur it: (Ksh ibid.:) from saAmahu xasofFA [expl. by what here follows]. (Ksh and Bd ibid.) You say, sumotuhu xasofFA I brought upon him xasof [i. e. wrong, or wrong treatment, as expl. in the Ksh and by Bd ubi suprà]: or I endeavoured to induce him to incur it ( A^aradotuhu Ealayohi ): (S:) [see also xasofN : and sumotuhu xuT~apa xasofK ; expl. in art. xT :] and siyma Alxasofa He was constrained to incur, or to do, what is termed Alxasof [meaning abasement or ignominy, or that which was difficult ]: (TA:) and sumotuhu *ul~FA I abased him. (Msb.) -A3- saAmahu , aor. as above, also signifies He kept, or clave, to it, not quitting it. (M, * TA.) -A4- See also 4.

definition: , (S, K,) or AlA_ibila , (M,) [inf n.
sourceDefinition: , (S, K,) or AlA_ibila , (M,) [inf n. tasowiymN ,] He sent forth (S, M, K) the horses, (S, K,) or the camels, (M,) [sometimes meaning] to the pasturage, to pasture where they would. (TA. [See also 4.]) ― -b2- [Hence,] sw~mhu means xal~aAhu wasawomahu , (AZ, S, M, K,) i. e. [ He left him ] to do as he pleased; namely, a man. (AZ, S, K. [In the CK is a mistranscription in this place, before mentioned: see 1, fourth sentence.]) Whence the prov., EabodN wasuw~ima A slave, and he has been left to do as he pleases. (TA.) ― -b3- And saw~amotu fulaAnFA fiY maAliY I gave such a one authority to judge, give judgment, pass sentence, or decide judicially, respecting my property. (AO, S: and in like manner saw~mhu fiY maAlihi is expl. in the M and K.) And saw~amotuhu A^amoriY I made him to have the ordering and deciding of my affair, or case, to do what he would; like saw~afotuhu A^amoriY . (TA in art. swf .) ― -b4- And sw~m EalaY Alqawomi He urged his horses [ xayolahu being understood] against the people, or party, and made havoc among them. (S, K.) ― -b5- And tasowiymN signifies also The making a horse to sweat well. (KL.) ― -b6- See also 1, in the last quarter of the paragraph. -A2- And sw~m Alfarasa , (M, K,) inf. n. tasowiymN , (K,) He put a mark upon the horse: (M, K:) he marked the horse with a piece of silk ( bHryrp [perhaps a mistranscription for biHadiydapK i. e. with an iron such as is used for branding]), or with something whereby he should be known. (Lth, TA.) See also 5. [And see 4.]

definition: Death: (IAar, S, M, Mgh:) and saAmapN [as its n.
sourceDefinition: Death: (IAar, S, M, Mgh:) and saAmapN [as its n. un.] a death: (IAar, TA:) but the former [signifies the same in Pers., and] is said to be not Arabic. (TA.) It is related in a trad., respecting the salutation of the Jews, that they used to say, Als~aAmu Ealayokumo [ Death come upon you, instead of Als~alaAmu Ealayokumo ]; and that he [i. e. Mo- hammad] used to reply, Ealayokumo ; accord. to the generality of the relaters, waEalayokumo , but correctly without the w , because the w implies participation: and it is related of 'Áïsheh that she used to say to them, Ealayokumu Als~aA^omu waAl*~aA^omu waAll~aEonapu , as mentioned in art. sA^m : (TA:) the Jews are also related to have said [to the Muslims], Ealayokumu Als~aAmu Ald~aAmu meaning Almawotu Ald~aAy^imu . (TA in art. dwm : see daAy^imN in that art.) -A2- Also A kind of tree, of which are made the masts ( A^adoqaAl [pl. of daqalN ]) of ships: (Kr, M, TA:) accord. to Sh, (TA,) the [ tree called ] xayozuraAn . (K, TA. [And accord. to some copies of the K, saAmapN also has this signification, and the signification expl. in the sentence here next following: but accord. to the text of the K as given in the TA, waAls~aAmapu has been erroneously substistituted in the copies above referred to for waAls~aAqapu , which, by reason of what precedes it, means that saAmapN also signifies the same as saAqapN ; and if the former reading were right, the context in the K would imply that AlsAmp is also the name of a son of Noah, which is incorrect; the name of that son being only saAmN .]) -A3- Also A [ hollow, or cavity, in the ground, such as is called ] nuqorap , in which water remains, or stagnates, and collects. (K. [For the verb in this explanation, which is written yunoqaEu in the CK and in my MS. copy of the K, I read yanoqaEu .]) -A4- Also a pl. [or rather coll. gen. n.] of which the sing. [or n. un.] is saAmapN : (M, K:) the former signifies Veins of gold: and the latter, a single vein thereof: (S:) or the latter, a vein in a mountain, differing from its [ general ] nature; (M, K;) if running from east to west, not failing of its promise to yield silver: (M:) or the former, (M,) or latter, (K, TA,) gold, and silver; (M, K, TA;) accord. to As and IAar: (M, TA:) or, as some say, an ingot of gold, and of silver: (TA:) or veins of gold, and of silver, in the stone [or rock ]: (M, K:) En-Nábighah El-Jaadee, (M,) or Edh-Dhubyánee, (TA,) uses AlsAm as meaning silver; for he likens thereto a woman's front teeth in respect of their whiteness: (M, TA:) and Aboo-Sa'eed says that silver is called in Pers. siymo , and in Ar. saAmN : (TA:) but the meaning most commonly known is gold. (M, TA.) A poet says, (M,) namely, Keys Ibn-El-Khateem, (S,) lawa A@n~aka tuloqiY HanoZalFA fawoqa bayoDinaA tadaHoraja Eano *iY saAmihi AlmutaqaAribi (S, M,) [i. e. sourceDefinition: , (Msb,) sec. pers. $aHaHota , aor. ya$uH~u and ya$iH~u , (S, O, Msb, K,) the latter of these aors. agreeable with analogy as the verb is intrans., and the former deviating therefrom; (MF;) and sec. pers. $aHiHota , aor. ya$aH~u ; (S, O, Msb, K;) [the first of which, having for its aor. ya$uH~u , is the most common;] inf. n. $uH~N (S, A, O, Msb, K) and $iH~N and $aH~N , (ISk, O, K,) of which three inf. ns. the first is the most approved; (TA;) He was, or became, niggardly, tenacious, stingy, penurious, or avaricious; syn. yaxila : (Msb:) or bxl relates to single things, or particulars; and $H~ , to things in general: or bxl relates to wealth, or property; and $H~ , to wealth, or property, and to kindness, or beneficence: or $H~ , signifies he was, or became, niggardly, &c., as above, in the utmost degree: (TA:) or he was, or became, niggardly, &c., as above, (S, A, O, K,) and covetous, or vehemently or greedily or excessively or culpably desirous, (K,) or with covetousness, or vehement or greedy or excessive or culpable desire. (S, A, O.) You say, $aH~a bihi and $aH~a Ealayohi ; (T, M, K;) by the former meaning He was, or became, niggardly, &c., of it, i. e., of his property, or the like; and by the latter, he was, or became, niggardly, &c., to him, i. e., to an asker, or a beggar, or a seeker, or the like: (MF:) or [in some cases, as will be seen from phrases mentioned below, (see $aHiyHN ,)] meaning by the latter the same as by the former. (L.) [Thus] one says, huwa ya$uH~u bimaAlihi [ He is niggardly, &c., of his property; and sometimes, in the same sense, ya$uH~u EalaY maAlihi ]. (A.) And $aH~a baEoDuhumo EalaY baEoDK [ Some of them were niggardly, &c., to some; meaning they were niggardly, &c., one to another ]. (Msb, K.)

A^a$iH~apF EalaY Alxayori , in the Kur [xxxiii. 19], means [ They being niggardly, or vehemently desirous, of the good things, i. e.] of the wealth and spoils: (TA:) and A^a$iH~apN Ealayokumo , in the same verse, means [ They being niggardly ] of aid [ to you ]. And ↓ zanodN $aHaAHN (tropical:) A piece of stick, or wood, for producing fire, that does not yield fire. (S, A, K.) And maA='N ↓ $aHaAHN (assumed tropical:) Water little in quantity; not copious. (K.) And ↓ A^aroDN $aHaAHN (assumed tropical:) Land that will not flow with water unless in consequence of much rain; (S, O, K;) as also ↓ $aHo$aHN : (O, K:) and also, (ISk, L, TA,) or ↓ the latter word, (so accord. to the K,) (assumed tropical:) Land that flows in consequence of the least rain; (ISk, K, TA;) as though it were niggardly of itself to the water: (TA;) like Ha$aAdN [in this, or in the former, sense]: (ISk, L:) thus having two contr. meanings. (K.) And accord. to AHn, $iHaAHN signifies (assumed tropical:) [Small water-courses such as are termed] $iEaAb any one of which is made to flow if a skinful of water is poured into it. (TA.)

definition: a word of well-known meaning [i.
sourceDefinition: a word of well-known meaning [i. e. A devil; and with the article Al , the devil, Satan ]: (S, K:) any that is excessively, or inordinately, proud or corrupt or unbelieving or rebellious, or that is insolent and audacious in pride and in acts of rebellion, of mankind, and of the jinn, or genii, and of beasts; (A'Obeyd, S, Msb, K;) as is shown in relation to the first and second of these by what is said in the Kur vi. 112, and ii. 13 and 96: (TA:) the n is radical, (S, Msb, TA,) the word being of the measure fayoEaAlN , from $aTana , (Msb, TA,) signifying “ he was, or became, distant, or remote, ” (TA,) or signifying “ he was, or became, remote, or far, from the truth, and from the mercy of God; ” (Msb;) as is indicated by the pl. $ayaATiynu ; [for] the reading of El-Hasan in the Kur xxvi. 210, Al$~ayaATuwna , is anomalous, [like basaAtuwna for basaAtiynu ,] and is said by Th to be a mistake: (TA:) or, as some say, the n is augmentative, (S, Msb, TA, *) and the Y is radical, so that the word is of the measure faEolaAn , (Msb,) from $aATa , aor. ya$iyTu , (Msb, TA,) signifying “ it was, or became, null, void, of no account, ” and the like, and “ it burned, ” or “ became burnt, ” (Msb,) or signifying “ he burned with anger: ” but the former opinion is the more common: (TA:) [in the Kur, the word is always perfectly decl.; and so it is said to be by SM, in art. $yT of the TA; unless used as a proper name: but J says,] if you make it to be of the measure fayoEaAl from ta$ayoTana said of a man, [or rather because they say of a man t$yTn ,] you make it perfectly decl.; but if you make it to be from $ay~aTa [“ he burned ” a thing], you make it imperfectly decl., because it is of the measure faEolaAn . (S.) ― -b2- Also The serpent: (S, K:) or a certain species of serpents; (Fr, S, TA;) having a mane, of foul aspect: or, as some say, a slender, light, or active, serpent. (TA.) ― -b3- Respecting the saying in the Kur [xxxvii. 63], TaloEuhaA kaA^an~ahu ruw^uwsu Al$~ayaATiyni [ Its fruit is as though it were the heads of the $yATyn ], Fr says that there are three ways in which it may be explained: one is, that the TlE is likened to the heads of the $yATyn [meaning devils ] in respect of foulness, or ugliness, because these are described as foul, or ugly: (S:) or it is likened to the evil in disposition of the jinn, because these are imagined as foul, or ugly: Zj says, in explaining it, that one says of a thing deemed foul, or ugly, kaA^an~ahu wajohu $ayoTaAnK [ as though it were the face of a devil ], and kaA^an~ahu raA^osu $ayoTaAnK [ as though it were the head of a devil ]; for though the $yTAn is not seen, he is conceived in the mind as the foulest, or ugliest, of things: (TA:) the second is, that [the meaning is foul, or ugly, serpents; for] the Arabs apply the name $yTAn to a sort of serpents, having a mane, foul, or ugly, in the head and face: (S, TA: *) the third is, that a certain foul, or ugly, plat is named ruw^uwsu Al$~ayaATiyni ; (S, TA;) which is expl. in the K only as meaning a certain plant. (TA.) ― -b4- $ayoTaAnu AlfalaA [lit. The devil of the waterless deserts ] means (assumed tropical:) thirst. (K.) ― -b5- $ayoTaAnN signifies also (assumed tropical:) Any blamable faculty, or power, [or propensity, ] of a man. (Er-Rághib, TA.) One says, rakibahu $ayoTaAnuhu i. e. (assumed tropical:) [ His anger got the ascendency over him; or] he was, or became, angry. (TA.) And nazaEa $ayoTaAnahu (assumed tropical:) He plucked out his pride. (TA.) ― -b6- Also, [probably as being likened to a serpent,] (assumed tropical:) A mark made with a hot iron in the upper part of the haunch of a camel, perpendicularly, upon the thigh, extending to the hock; (K, TA;) from the “ Tedhkireh ” of Aboo-'Alee; (TA;) likewise called ↓ mu$ayoTanapN . (AZ, K, TA.)

sourceDefinition: , aor. , inf. n. $agFA , [signifies accord. to some] He (a man) had a tooth, or teeth, exceeding the other teeth: and [accord. to others, agreeably with what is said to be the right meaning of $aAgiyap below,] he had a tooth, or teeth, differing in the manner of growth from the other teeth. (S.) [And] $agiyati Als~in~u , aor. ; (Msb, K;) and $agat , aor. ; (K;) inf. n. (of the former, Msb, TA) $agFA (Msb, K, TA) and [of the latter] $uguw~N , (K, TA, [in the CK $agow , but]) like Euluw~N ; (TA;) [accord. to some] The tooth exceeded the other teeth: (Msb:) and [accord. to others] (Msb) the tooth differed from the other teeth (Msb, K, TA) in an absolute sense, (TA,) or in respect of its place of growth, (Msb,) or in its manner of growth, in length, and shortness, and receding, and projecting: (K, TA:) or, accord. to the A, $agFA signifies the differing in respect of the manner of growth and of collocation: or the upper teeth's not falling upon the lower: (TA:) or, as IF says, the advancing of the upper teeth beyond the lower. (Msb.) The epithet applied to a man is ↓ A^a$ogaY ; and to a woman, $agowaA='u ; and the pl. is $ugowN : (S, Msb:) [and] the epithet applied to a tooth is $agowaA='u and $agiyaA='u ; (K;) or ↓ $aAgiyapN ; (S, Msb;) which last is said by Az to have two meanings; one whereof is exceeding [ the other teeth ]; and the other, being longer and larger, and differing in respect of the place [or more probably the manner ] of its growth from those next to it: (Msb:) or, accord. to a marginal note in the S, in the handwriting of Aboo-Zekereeyà, this signifies differing in the manner of its growth from the manner of growth of the others, whether exceeding or not exceeding: or, accord. to a marginal note in the copy of Aboo-Sahl El-Harawee, crooked; not exceeding. (TA.)

sourceDefinition: A certain northern constellation, [namely, Lyra, ] consisting of ten stars, the bright star [alpha] of which is called Aln~asoru AlwaAqiEu : the Arabs liken it to a vulture ( nasor ) which has contracted its wings to itself, as though it had alighted upon a thing: the vulgar call [ the three chief stars in ] it AlA^avaAfiY : and before the bright star is a dim star which the Arabs call AlA^aZofaAr [i. e. the talons ]. (Kzw. [Not in any of my Lexicons.])

definition: He made him to smell it, or perceive it by the nose.
sourceDefinition: He made him to smell it, or perceive it by the nose. (K.) You say, A^a$omamotuhu AlTiyba [ I made him to smell the perfume ]. (S, Msb.) ― -b2- And [hence] one says to the prefect, or governor, or prince, or commander, A^a$omimoniY yadaka A^uqab~ilohaA (assumed tropical:) [ Suffer me to approach thy hand that I may kiss it ]; (S, * TA;) a phrase like naAwiloniY yadaka , (TA,) but better than the latter phrase: so says Kh. (S.) ― -b3- And A$m~ AlxitaAna , and A$m~t AlbaZora , (tropical:) He, and she, i. e. the operator, took, (K, TA,) or cut off, (TA,) a small portion of the prepuce, and of the baZor [q. v.]: (K, TA:) or the latter signifies she cut off a portion of the nawaAp [q. v.], not extirpating it. (TA.) ― -b4- And A$m~ AlHarofa , (S, * K,) inf. n. A_i$omaAmN , (S,) (assumed tropical:) He made the consonant to have a smack of the dammeh or the kesreh, (lit., made it to smell, S, or to taste, K, the dammeh or the kesreh, ) in such a manner (S, K) that the A_i$omaAm , (S,) or that the dammeh or kesreh, (K,) was not heard, (S, K,) what is termed A_i$omaAmu AlHarofi being less than what is termed rawomu AlHarakapi , the former being apparent only by the motion of the lip, (S,) or of the upper lip, (so in one of my copies of the S,) no account being taken of it, (S, K,) i. e. of the dammeh or kesreh, (K,) it not being reckoned as a Harakap because of its feebleness, the consonant in this case being quiescent or like that which is quiescent, (S,) and the prosodical measure not being broken thereby: (K:) for ex., in the following verse, mataY A^anaAmu laA yuw^ar~iqoniY AlkariY layolFA walaA A^asomaEu A^ajoraAsa AlmaTiY [meaning AlkariY~ and AlmaTiY~ , (as is said in one of my copies of the S,) i. e. When I sleep, he who lets beasts on hire will not render me wakeful by night, nor do I hear the bells of the camels on which people ride ], the Arabs [or, as is said in the TA, some of the Arabs] make the q [in yw^r~qnY ] to have a smack of the dammeh; but if you took account of the Harakap of the A_i$omaAm [in this case,] the measure of the verse would be broken, [the foot] rqnY AlkrY becoming, in the scanning, mutafaAEiluno , which may be only in the kaAmil ; whereas this verse is of the rajaz : (Sb, S:) another case of A_i$omaAm is that of the Y in duwayob~apN , [in which that letter is quiescent, but made to have a smack of kesreh,] as is the same letter in every similar case, in a dim. noun, when followed by a doubled letter. (Zj, T in art. db .) Also He pronounced the consonant with a Harakap [or vowel-sound ] between damm and kesr, apparent only in utterance, not in writing; as in qiyla and giyDa in the Kur xi. 46. (I 'Ak pp. 130 and 131.) [See also rawomu AlHarakapi , voce raAma .] ― -b5- [Golius explains A$m~ as signifying also “ Reduxit, fecit ut converteret se ab aliqua re; ” as on the authority of the KL; in my copy of which, however, I do not find this meaning.] -A2- A$m~ , (S, K,) inf. n. A_i$omaAmN , [as an intrans. verb,] said of a man, (S,) also signifies He passed by, or along, raising his head; (S, K, TA;) and magnified, or exalted, himself; behaved proudly, or disdainfully; or elevated his nose, from pride. (TA. [See also 1, near the end.]) ― -b2- And He turned away from a thing. (K.) One says bayonaA humo fiY wajohK A_i*o A^a$am~uwA , i. e. [ While they were in a certain direction, lo, ] they turned away; (S, TA, as from AA;) or ↓ $am~uwA . (Thus in one of my copies of the S [but I think it to be a mistranscription].) And A$m~ Alqawomu The people, or party, deviated in their directions to the right and left: a phrase heard in this sense by AA. (S.)

sourceDefinition: inf. n. of the intrans. verb $am~a [q. v.]. (Msb, TA.) ― -b2- [Used as a simple subst.,] Highness of the nose: (Msb:) or highness of the bone of the nose, (S, K,) and beauty thereof, (K,) with evenness, or straightness, of its upper part, (S, K, when there is in it a gibbousness it is termed qanFA , S,) and uprightness of the end, or lowest part: (K:) or, as some say, this last quality [ alone ]: (TA:) or length of the end, or lower part, of the nose, so that it extends over the middle of the mustache, ( wuruwdu AlA^aronabapi ,) with beautiful evenness, or straightness, of the bone, and highness thereof greater than the highness that is termed *alafN : or length and slenderness of the nose, and a downward extending of its rawovap [i. e. end or tip, or part where the blood that flows from the nostrils drops or drips ]: (K:) or [ simply ] length. in the nose. (Ham p. 789.) ― -b3- And, in a man, The quality of having what is termed $amamN of the nose. (S.) ― -b4- [And hence, (tropical:) Self-magnification, or pride, or haughtiness: see 1, near the end.] ― -b5- And (tropical:) Generosity. (Ham p. 728.) ― -b6- Also Highness, (K,) or tallness of the head, (S,) of a mountain. (S, K.) ― -b7- And (tropical:) Nearness: and (tropical:) remoteness: thus having two contr. meanings. (K, TA.) It has both of such meanings in the phrase daAruhu $amamN (tropical:) [ His house, or abode, is near: and, remote ]: (K, TA:) and in the phrase raA^ayotuhu mino $amamK (tropical:) [ I saw him, or it, from within a short distance: and, from afar ]. (TA.)

definition: A sort of melon resembling a small colocynth, [or rather a small melon resembling a colocynth, ] streaked with redness and greenness and yellowness: called in Pers.
sourceDefinition: A sort of melon resembling a small colocynth, [or rather a small melon resembling a colocynth, ] streaked with redness and greenness and yellowness: called in Pers. dasotanobuwyah [i. e. “ perfume ”]; (K;) originally dasoto buwY [or dasoto buwyaho ]: (TA:) its odour is cool, pleasant, lenitive, and narcotic; and the eating of it is laxative to the bowels: (K:) [The cucumis dudaïm of Linn.; called by Forskål cucumis schemmam: the latter thus describes it (Flora Aegypt. Arab. p. 169): “ Caules 5-sulcati, setis rigidis, scandentes, cirrhosi: folia cordato-oblonga, acuta, subsinuata, dentato-repanda, hispida: calyces villosi, molles: flores flavi, conferti in alis: fructus globosoovatus, glaberrimus, magnitudine citri, flavus, maculis inæqualibus, fulvo-ferrugineis, versus polos in lineas confluentibus; pulpa aquosa, seminibus tota plena: fructus juvenis villosus; maturus glaber: odor, fortis nec ingratus; eamque ob caussam cultus; non edulis: ” in the present day, the same appellation is applied in Egypt to several species of melon, of pleasant odour and taste; but this application I believe to be of very late origin: see also luf~aAHN : and see De Sacy's “ Rel. de l'Égypte par Abd-allatif, ” pp. 126-7.]

(K, TA.) [Hence] $Ar nafosahu He displayed his agility, to show his power. (TA, from a trad.) ― -b3- And $urotuhu I ornamented, or decorated, it. (TA.) -A3- $Ar He (a man) became goodly in countenance. (Fr, TA.) ― -b2- He (a horse) became fat and goodly: (S:) and so $Art said of a she-camel: (TA:) [and ↓ t$w~rt said of a woman: (Freytag, from the Deewán of the Hudhalees:)] or $Art said of a she-camel, she became fat; (K;) and in like manner ↓ A$tAr and ↓ Ast$Ar said of a he-camel: (S:) and ↓ A$tArt AlA_ibilu the camels became somewhat fat: (S:) and ↓ Ast$Art they became fat and goodly: (K:) or this last signifies (tropical:) they became fat; because their owner points to such with his fingers; as though they desired to be pointed to. (A.)

sourceDefinition: and ↓ ma$uwrapN and ↓ $uwraY signify the same: (S:) the first and second are substs. from $aAwarahu , and the third is a subst. from ta$aAwaruwA : (Msb:) or the first (Lth) and second [which is written in the CK ma$owarapN ] (Lth, K) and third (K) are from AlA_i$aArapu (Lth) or A^a$aAra Ealayohi : (K:) [they signify Consultation; or mutual debate in order that one may see another's opinion; or counsel, or advice: or a command, an order, or an injunction: or] the extracting, or drawing forth, opinion: (Bd, as mentioned above: see 6:) ↓ ma$uwrapN [in the CK ma$owarapN ] is of the measure mafoEulapN , [originally ma$owurapN , in the CK mafoEalapN ,] not mafoEuwlapN , (K, TA,) because it is an inf. n., [or rather a quasi-inf. n.,] and such a noun has not this last measure: (TA:) it is like maEuwnapN ; (Msb;) and is a contraction of ma$owurapN : (Fr, TA:) and it is said also to be from $aAra Ald~aAb~apa ; or, accord. to some, from $aAra AlEasala ; good counsel or advice being likened to honey. (Mgh.) And one says also, ↓ Aln~aAsu fiyhi $uwraY [ The people are to determine by consultation respecting it ]. (A.)

sourceDefinition: inf. n. of Sadifa [q. v.]. (M, Msb.) -A2- Also Anything high, or lofty, (As, S, M, O, K,) such as a wall and a mountain, (M,) or such as a wall and the like; (K;) like what is termed hadafN : (As, S, O:) and the side of a mountain: (M:) or SadafN and hadafN both signify any building or structure, that is high, or lofty, and great; (A'Obeyd, TA;) accord. to Az, likened to the Sadaf of a mountain, which is the side that faces one, thereof: (TA:) and SadafN and ↓ SudufN (S, M, O, K) and ↓ SudafN and ↓ SadufN , (O, K,) accord. to different readings of a passage in the Kur, (S, M, O, K,) [xviii. 95,] in which the dual occurs, (S, M, O,) signify the place of ending, or breaking off, (S, O, K,) of a mountain, (K,) or of a lofty mountain: (S, O:) or the side of a mountain: (K:) or the part between two mountains: (M:) or, as used in this instance, (K, TA,) in the verse of the Kur, (TA,) AlS~adafaAni , (M, K,) as also ↓ AlS~udufaAni , (M,) means two mountains (M, L, K) meeting together, (M, L, TA,) in the copies of the K, mutalaAziqaAni [i. e. cleaving together ], but the correct reading is mutalaAqiyaAni , as in the L [and M], (TA,) between Ya-jooj and Ma-jooj: (M, L, K, TA:) and ↓ AlS~udufaAni , (M, K,) with damm to the d (M,) i. e. with two dammehs, especially, (K,) or this as well as AlS~adafaAni , (TA,) means the two sides of the $iEob [app. here meaning ravine, or gap, between two mountains ], or of the valley: (M, K, TA:) so says IDrd: (M, TA:) both signify the two sides of the mountain when they [ meet together, and ] face each other, so called litaSaAdufihimaA , i. e. because of their meeting together, and facing each other, having between them a [ road such as is termed ] faj~ , or a $iEob [expl. above], or a valley. (TA.) -A3- Also [The mother-of-pearl shell; or oyster-shell; and any shell of a mollusk: and, by an extension of its primary application, the oyster itself; and any shell-fish, or testaceous mollusk of the water, and likewise of the land: ] the cover of the pearl; (K;) or this is called Sadafu Ald~ur~api , (S, O,) or Sadafu Ald~ur~i ; (Msb;) a kind of cover created in the sea, composed of [ what are termed ] SadafataAni [i. e. a pair of shell-valves ], which are opened from [i. e. so as to disclose ] a kind of flesh in which is life, called the maHaArap [i. e. oyster ], and in the like thereof are found pearls; (Lth, TA;) i. q. maHaArN [which means oyster-shells, and also oysters themselves, and both of these may be here meant, as both are correct meanings of SadafN ]: (M:) n. un. with p : (S, M, O, Msb, K:) [in the Msb it is also said that AlS~adafapu signifies the maHaArap , which is the maHomil of the pilgrims; but I think that this is a mistake, caused by understanding maHaArap here in a wrong sense; for I find no other authority for assigning this meaning to AlS~adafapu :] pl. A^aSodaAfN . (O, K.) [See an ex. of the pl. voce HalazuwnN .] ― -b2- [Hence,] AlS~adafapu signifies also, (M, TA,) or Sadafapu AlA^u*uni , (O,) The maHaArap [or concha, i. e. the external, deep, and wide, cavity, around the hole, ] of the ear. (M, O, TA.) ― -b3- [And hence, also,] AlS~adafataAni signifies The two small hollows, or sockets, in each of which is set the head of one of the two thing-bones, and in each of which is a ligament ( EaSabapN [app. that called ligamentum teres, forming a tie ]) to that head. (M, TA.) [And in like manner, The two sockets in the scapula, in each of which turns the head of one of the two upper arm-bones: (see HaAriqapN :) or these, it seems, are called by some AlS~adafaAni ; for it is said that] AlS~adafu signifies the part of the scapula which is the place of the waAbilap . (O, K.) ― -b4- And SadafN also signifies (tropical:) Flesh, (O,) or a piece of flesh, (K, TA,) growing in a wound of the head, next the skull, resembling the cartilages. (O, K.) -A4- And in the Tekmileh it is said that [the pl.] A^aSodaAfN signifies Waves of the sea. (TA.) -A5- See also SudafN .

definition: [ A thunderbolt;
sourceDefinition: [ A thunderbolt; i. e.] a thing descending from the thunder, that smites not anything but it alters it and burns it: (Msb:) or fire that falls from the sky, (AZ, S, O, K,) in vehement thunder: (AZ, S, O:) or fire that God sends with vehement thunder: (TA:) or the scourge ( mixoraAq ) that is in the hand of [ the angel who is ] the driver of the clouds, and that comes not upon anything but it burns it: (O, K:) or a vehement sound from a thundering with which falls a piece of fire: or the sound of thunder: (TA:) Wahb Ibn-Munebbih, being asked respecting it, whether it were a tangible thing or fire or what else, answered that he thought no one knew it except God: (O, TA:) accord. to some, (TA,) it signifies also the cry, or vehement cry, or shout, [ that is an efficient ] of punishment: (S, O, K:) and death; (O, K;) so accord. to Katádeh (O, TA) and Mukátil: (TA:) or a cause of death: (Zj, TA:) and any destructive punishment: (O, K:) and ↓ SaEoqapN and SaAqiEapN are dial. vars. thereof: (TA:) the pl. is SawaAEiqu . (O, Msb, TA.)

definition: , aor. , inf. n. SufuwnN , said of a horse, He stood upon three legs and the extremity of the hoof of the fourth leg; (AZ, * S, K, TA;) [thus expl.] without restriction to a fore leg or a hind leg:...
sourceDefinition: , aor. , inf. n. SufuwnN , said of a horse, He stood upon three legs and the extremity of the hoof of the fourth leg; (AZ, * S, K, TA;) [thus expl.] without restriction to a fore leg or a hind leg: (TA:) or he stood upon three legs, and turned back the extremity of the fore part of the fourth hoof, that of his fore leg: (M, TA:) [or he stood upon three legs, and otherwise: (see SaAfinN :)] accord. to Fr, the poems of the Arabs indicate that SufuwnN signifies peculiarly, or specially, [or simply,] the act of standing, or standing still. (TA.) ― -b2- Also, (M, Msb, K,) aor. and inf. n. as above, (M, Msb,) said of a man, (K,) or Safana qadamayohi , (TA, from a trad.,) meaning Saf~a qadamayohi [ He set his feet evenly, side by side ], (M, Msb, K, TA,) standing, (Msb,) and praying. (TA.) [Or, said of a man standing in prayer, it signifies, or in this case it signifies also, He put his feet close together: or he turned one of his feet backward, like as the horse turns one hoof when standing upon three legs: see, again, SaAfinN .] -A2- Safana AlHa$iy$a (M, TA) waAlwaraqa , aor. , (M,) inf. n. SafonN , said of a bird, or flying thing, It compacted the dry herbage (M, TA) and the leaves, [ to make a habitation, ] for its young ones, (M,) or around its place of entrance [ into its habitation ]; (TA;) and ↓ Sf~nhu signifies the same: (M:) ↓ taSofiynN as the act of the hornet and the like is the compacting for itself, or for its young ones, a habitation (K, TA) of dry herbage and of leaves: so says Lth. (TA.) ― -b2- And Safana viyaAbahu He collected together his clothes (JM, TA) fiY sarojihi [ upon his saddle ], (TA,) or fiY Als~aroji wanaHowihi [ upon the saddle and the like thereof ]. (JM.) ― -b3- Safana bihi AlA^aroDa , (K, TA,) aor. , inf. n. SafonN , (TA,) He flung him, or it, upon the ground. (K, TA.) -A3- And Safanahu , aor. , inf. n. SafonN , He rent, or slit, his Safan , i. e. scrotum. (M.)

definition: A horse standing upon three legs and the extremity of the hoof of the fourth leg: (A'Obeyd, * S, TA:) or standing upon three legs, and turning back the extremity of the fore part of the fourth hoof,...
sourceDefinition: A horse standing upon three legs and the extremity of the hoof of the fourth leg: (A'Obeyd, * S, TA:) or standing upon three legs, and turning back the extremity of the fore part of the fourth hoof, that of his fore leg: (M, TA:) or standing upon three legs, and otherwise: thus, says Fr, I have found the Arabs use the word: (TA: [see 1, first sentence:]) pl. SufuwnN (M, TA) and SawaAfinu and [the pl. of SaAfinapN is] SaAfinaAtN . (TA.) SaAfinaAtN occurs in the Kur xxxviii. 30. (M, TA.) And in the same, xxii. 37, I'Ab and Ibn-Mes-'ood used to read SawaAfina [instead of SawaAf~a ]; the former explaining it as meaning Having the shank of one fore leg tied up to the arm; for thus is done with the camel when he is slaughtered: the latter, as meaning standing, or standing still. (TA.) ― -b2- And applied to a man, it means SaAf~N qadamayohi [ setting his feet evenly, side by side ], (A'Obeyd, M, TA, and the like is said in the S and Msb,) standing. (A'Obeyd, Msb, TA.) It is said in a trad., (S, M, Msb, TA,) referring to the Prophet mentioned as praying, (S, M,) qumonaA xalofahu SufuwnFA [app. meaning We stood behind him setting our feet evenly, side by side; for so the context seems to indicate]. (S, M, Msb, K.) [But] in another trad., Sal`wpu AlS~aAfini is said to be forbidden; meaning [ The praying ] of him who puts his feet close together: or, as some say, of him who turns back his foot [i. e. one of his feet ] like as the horse turns his hoof [i. e. one of his hoofs, when standing upon three legs ]. (TA.) -A2- AlS~aAfinu signifies [ The saphena, or crural vein; so in the present day; i. e.] the vein of the saAq : (S: [see A^aboharu , and see also Aln~asaA :]) or a vein lying deep in the arm ( Al*~iraAE ) [ and ] amid the sinews of the [ fore ] shank of a beast: or the SaAfinaAni are two veins penetrating into the interior of the two shanks: or two veins in the legs: or two branches [ of veins ] in the two thighs: and the SAfn is [strangely said to be] a vein in the interior of the back bone, extending lengthwise, uniting with the niyaAT [q. v.] of the heart, also called the A^akoHal . (M.)

definition: He, or it, (a man, S, or a thing, Msb,) had a foul, or fetid, odour, such as is termed SunaAn : (S, Msb, K:) so too said of a he-goat, when excited by lust.
sourceDefinition: He, or it, (a man, S, or a thing, Msb,) had a foul, or fetid, odour, such as is termed SunaAn : (S, Msb, K:) so too said of a he-goat, when excited by lust. (TA.) And said of flesh-meat, [like San~a ,] It stank. (TA.) And ASn~t Albaqolapu The herb, or leguminous plant, when held in the hand, stank. (TA.) And ASn~ said of water, It became altered [ for the worse ]. (K.) -A2- Also He elevated his nose, (S, K,) or his head, (ISk, TA,) from pride. (ISk, S, K.) And hence, (S,) ASn~t said of a she-camel, She, having conceived, behaved disdainfully to the stallion. (S, K.) ― -b2- And He was, or became, angry. (K.) -A3- ASn~t said of a she-camel, (ISh, M,) or of a mare, (A 'Obeyd, K,) when near to bringing forth, (A 'Obeyd,) Her young one struggled, or was in a state of commotion, (A 'Obeyd, M,) in the part bordering upon her tail [so I render fiY SalaAhaA ], (A 'Obeyd,) or its hind leg fell [or happened to come ] into that part; (M;) or her young one stuck fast in her belly, and it pushed with its head, (ISh, K,) or with its shank and its nose, (ISh,) in the region of her anus. (ISh, K.) The epithet applied to her in this case is ↓ muSin~N : (ISh:) and the pl. is muSin~aAtN and maSaAn~u . (Az, TA.) -A4- ASn~t said of a woman, She became old, but having in her some remains [ of vigour ]: and such is termed ↓ muSin~N and muSin~apN . (M.) -A5- ASn~ also signifies He spoke in a low, faint, gentle, or soft, manner. (TA.) -A6- And ASn~ EalaY AlA^amori He persevered, or persisted, in the affair. (K.)
