sourceDefinition: , (M, TA,) inf. n. A_iSaAbapN , (M, K, TA,) He descended, or went down, into a lower land, or country; contr. of A^aSoEada . (M, K, * TA. [See also 1 as syn. with 5; and see 2, last sentence.]) -A2- ASAb AlqiroTaAsa , [inf. n. as above,] said of an arrow, [ It hit, or struck, the butt, or target; or went right thereto; ] (S, TA;) and ↓ SaAbahu , (S, TA,) or SAb Alhadafa , (M,) aor. yaSiybuhu , (S, M,) inf. n. SayobN , (S, TA,) likewise said of an arrow, (S, M, TA,) signifies the same; (S, TA;) or SAb said of an arrow is intrans. (M.) And ASAb alone, [as though used elliptically,] (Msb, TA,) inf. n. as above; (Msb, K;) and ↓ SAb , aor. yaSuwbu , (S, Msb,) inf. n. SayobuwbapN , (S,) or SawobN ; (Msb, K;) and ↓ SAb , aor. yaSiybu , inf. n. SayobN ; (Msb;) likewise said of an arrow, (S, Msb,) It went right; did not deviate from the right course: (S, K, * TA:) or it reached [or hit ] the object of aim. (Msb.) And naHowa Alr~imiy~api ↓ SAb , (M, A, TA,) aor. yaSuwbu , (A, TA,) inf. n. SawobN and SayobuwbapN , (M, TA,) said of an arrow, (M, A, TA,) It went right towards the thing, or animal, shot at; (M, TA;) as also ASAb . (TA.) ― -b2- Also ASAb AlqiroTaAsa , (S, TA,) and ASAb fiY AlqiroTaAsi , (TA,) [said of a man, as is indicated by the context in the S and TA, He hit the butt, or target; ] he did not miss the butt, or target. (TA.) And ASAb alone is said of an archer or the like [as meaning He hit the object of his aim ]: (Msb:) one says, ramaY faA^aSaAba [ He shot, or cast, and hit the object of his aim ]. (A.) ― -b3- [Hence, likening an event, &c., to an arrow,] one says also, ASAbhu A^amorN , inf. n. as above, (assumed tropical:) [ An event smote him, or befell him; ] and ↓ SAbhu , aor. yaSuwbuhu , inf. n. SawobN , signifies the same. (Msb.) And A^aSaAbatohu muSiybapN (assumed tropical:) [ An affliction, or a calamity, &c., smote him, or befell him ]. (S.) And ASAbhu Al$~aYo'u (assumed tropical:) The thing reached him [ so as to take effect upon him ]: (Mgh, * Msb:) whence the saying, A^aSaAbahu mino qawoli Aln~aAsi maA A^aSaAbahu (assumed tropical:) [ There reached him &c., of the sayings of the people, what reached him &c.]. (Msb.) [Thus tropically used, ASAbhu may generally be rendered It hit, struck, smote, wounded, hurt, affected, assailed, or befell, him. One says, ASAbhu maraDN , and wajaEN , and ASAbthu riyHN , &c., (assumed tropical:) A disease, and pain, and wind, &c., smote, affected, or assailed, him. ] And AlmaTaru ↓ SaAbahu , (S, Msb,) aor. yaSuwbuhu , inf. n. SawobN , (Msb,) (assumed tropical:) [ The rain fell, or lighted, upon him, or it; wetted him, or it; ] he, or it, was rained upon. (S.) And Als~amaA='u AlA^aroDa ↓ SaAbati i. e. (assumed tropical:) [ The sky, or clouds, or rain, ] watered the earth, or land, copiously: (Lth, M, TA:) or it means A^aSaAbatohaA biSawobK [ it smote it with rain; or sent rain upon it ]. (M, L, TA.) In the following verse, cited by IAar, fakayofa turaj~iY AlEA*ilaAtu tajal~udiY HamiymuhaA ↓ waSaboriY A_i*aA maA Aln~afosu Siyba he explains Siyba as being like quSida , and says that it may be of the dial. of him who says SaAba Als~ahomu ; but [ISd remarks,] I know not how this is, for SaAba Als~ahomu is not trans.; [though, as shown above, he has mentioned it as being trans.;] and in my opinion, [he says,] Syb here is from the phrase SaAbati Als~amaA='u AlA^aroDa [expl. above; the meaning of the verse being, But how should the censuring women hope for my constraining myself to behave with hardiness, and for my being patient, when the beloved of the soul has been smitten by death, or by the decree of death; for ISd adds,] kaA^an~a Almaniy~apa SaAbati AlHamiyma faA^aSaAbatohu biSawobihaA . (M, TA. *) ― -b4- [ ASAb is also used in many phrases in which its agent is likened to an archer.] One says, ASAb AlS~awaAba (tropical:) [ He hit the right thing or point, or the object, or aim, of his words or of his actions ]: (A:) and ASAb Als~adaAda [which means the same]. (S in art. sd .) And ASAb alone [means thus likewise; or] (assumed tropical:) he said, or did, that which was right. (M, K. *) And ASAb fiY qawolihi wafiEolihi (assumed tropical:) He hit the right thing in his saying and his deed; (Msb;) and so fiY raA^oyihi in his opinion; contr. of A^axoTaA^a . (A.) And ASAb bigoyatahu (assumed tropical:) He attained, or obtained, the thing that he sought, or wanted: whence the saying, ASAb mino zawojatihi [and so app. A^aSaAbahaA (see safaqa )] (assumed tropical:) He obtained his desired enjoyment of his wife: (Msb:) ASAb min~iY occurs in a trad., [as a euphemism,] said by the wife of Handhaleh, meaning (assumed tropical:) He compressed me: (Mgh:) and it is said in a trad., kaAna yuSiybu mino raA^osi baEoDi nisaAy^ihi wahuwa SaAy^imN , meaning (assumed tropical:) He used to kiss [ the head of some one or more of his wives when he was fasting ]. (TA: and the like is said in the Mgh.) And ASAb mina AlmaAli wagayorihi (assumed tropical:) He took, or took with his hand, of the property and other things. (TA.) And ASAb Al$~aYo'a (tropical:) [ He hit upon, or lighted on, the thing; ] he found the thing. (S, M, K, * TA.) And ASAbhu [(assumed tropical:) He found it, met with it, or experienced it; namely, a good or an evil event. And (assumed tropical:) He found it out, or discovered it; namely, an enigma (see 8 in art. Hjw ) or the like. And] (assumed tropical:) He found it to be right: and (assumed tropical:) he saw it, considered it, or held it, to be right. (TA. [See also 10.]) And (assumed tropical:) He aimed at it; (As, TA;) (tropical:) he desired, wished, willed, intended, or meant, it. (As, M, A, Msb, TA.) One says, A^aSaAba fulaAnN AlS~awaAba faA^axoTaA^a AljawaAba (assumed tropical:) Such a one aimed at, and desired, [to say] that which was right, (As, Msb, * TA,) and failed of giving rightly the reply. (As, TA.) And A^ayona tuSiybaAni (assumed tropical:) [ Whither do ye two desire to go? ]; a saying of Ru-beh. (TA.) tajoriY biA^amorihi ruxaA='F Hayovu A^aSaAba , in the Kur [xxxviii. 35, referring to the wind], has been expl. as meaning (assumed tropical:) [ Running by his command softly, or gently, ] whithersoever He desireth. (M, * TA.) And ASAb A@ll~`hu Al~a*iY A^araAda , said in a trad., in reply to a question respecting the interpretation of a text, means (assumed tropical:) God desireth, or meaneth, [thereby,] what He desireth, or meaneth. (TA.) And ASAb A@ll~`hu bika xayorFA means A^araAdahu (tropical:) [i. e. May God intend thee good ]. (A.) And ASAb alone (assumed tropical:) He desired, or intended, or meant, that which was right. (M, K. *) One says also, ASAbhu bixayorK (assumed tropical:) [meaning He did good to him ]. (El-Muärrij, TA in art. Asw .) [But] ASAbhu bika*aA , (M,) inf. n. A_iSaAbapN , (K,) with which are syn. ↓ muSaAbN [in accordance with a usage generally allowable] (S, TA) and ↓ muSaAbapN , (K, TA,) (assumed tropical:) [generally] means He afflicted him with, or by, such a thing; or gave pain to him thereby. (M, K: * in the latter, only the inf. n. of the verb in this sense; and so in other senses.) [Thus one says, ASAbhu bi$ar~K (assumed tropical:) He afflicted him with evil; or did evil to him: and ASAbhu bimakoruwhK (assumed tropical:) He afflicted him with, or did to him, an abominable, or an evil, thing or action: and ASAbhu biqawolK qabiyHK (assumed tropical:) He afflicted him with, or said to him, a foul saying: and ASAbhu bi*aHolK (assumed tropical:) He punished him by blood-revenge: and ASAbhu bimaraDK (assumed tropical:) He, (i. e. God,) or it, (a thing,) affected him with disease; or rendered him diseased: and in many similar cases, the phrase may be well rendered with a verb derived from the noun; like phrases in which “ affecit ” (a Latin equivalent of ASAb ) occurs; as in “ honore affecit, ” meaning “ honoravit. ”] El-Hárith Ibn-Khuld El-Makhzoomee says, rajulFA ↓ A^aZulayomu A_in~a muSaAbakumo A^ahodaY Als~alaAma taHiy~apF Zulomu (assumed tropical:) [ O Dhuleymeh, verily your afflicting a man who has given the salutation of peace, greeting, is tyranny ]: IB says that this verse is not of El- 'Arjee, as El-Hareeree imagined it to be: the correct reading is A^aZulayomu , as above: Zlym is an apocopated from of Zulayomapu ; which is the dim. of Zaluwm : some read A^aZaluwmu : and some, A^asulayomu : [the verse is cited accord. to this last reading in the S:] rajulFA is governed in the accus. case by muSaAb [as an inf. n.]: and Zulomu is the enunciative of A_in~a . (L, TA.) A^aSaAbahumu Ald~ahoru binufuwsihimo waA^amowaAlihimo (assumed tropical:) means Time, or fate, afflicted them by destruction, or extirpation, among themselves and their cattle, or possessions. (M.) [In the K, AlA_iSaAbpu is expl. as signifying AlAiHotiyaAju : but the right reading is evidently AlAijotiyaAHu , as Ibr D has remarked in the margin of my copy of the TA; so that ASAb signifies (assumed tropical:) He destroyed, or extirpated; agreeably with an explanation in the sentence next preceding above, from the M.] mano yuridi A@ll~`hu bihi xayorFA yuSibo minohu , (assumed tropical:) occurring in a trad., means Him whom God intendeth good He trieth with afflictions, that He may recompense him for them. (TA.) And one says, maA kunotu muSaAbFA walaqado A^uSibotu (assumed tropical:) [app. meaning I was not affected with weakness of intellect, or madness, and I have become affected therewith: see muSaAbN , below]. (IAar, TA.)

SawobN and SayobuwbapN , (M, TA,) said of an arrow, (M, A, TA,) It went right towards the thing, or animal, shot at; (M, TA;) as also ASAb . (TA.) ― -b2- Also ASAb AlqiroTaAsa , (S, TA,) and ASAb fiY AlqiroTaAsi , (TA,) [said of a man, as is indicated by the context in the S and TA, He hit the butt, or target; ] he did not miss the butt, or target. (TA.) And ASAb alone is said of an archer or the like [as meaning He hit the object of his aim ]: (Msb:) one says, ramaY faA^aSaAba [ He shot, or cast, and hit the object of his aim ]. (A.) ― -b3- [Hence, likening an event, &c., to an arrow,] one says also, ASAbhu A^amorN , inf. n. as above, (assumed tropical:) [ An event smote him, or befell him; ] and ↓ SAbhu , aor. yaSuwbuhu , inf. n. SawobN , signifies the same. (Msb.) And A^aSaAbatohu muSiybapN (assumed tropical:) [ An affliction, or a calamity, &c., smote him, or befell him ]. (S.) And ASAbhu Al$~aYo'u (assumed tropical:) The thing reached him [ so as to take effect upon him ]: (Mgh, * Msb:) whence the saying, A^aSaAbahu mino qawoli Aln~aAsi maA A^aSaAbahu (assumed tropical:) [ There reached him &c., of the sayings of the people, what reached him &c.]. (Msb.) [Thus tropically used, ASAbhu may generally be rendered It hit, struck, smote, wounded, hurt, affected, assailed, or befell, him. One says, ASAbhu maraDN , and wajaEN , and ASAbthu riyHN , &c., (assumed tropical:) A disease, and pain, and wind, &c., smote, affected, or assailed, him. ] And AlmaTaru ↓ SaAbahu , (S, Msb,) aor. yaSuwbuhu , inf. n. SawobN , (Msb,) (assumed tropical:) [ The rain fell, or lighted, upon him, or it; wetted him, or it; ] he, or it, was rained upon. (S.) And Als~amaA='u AlA^aroDa ↓ SaAbati i. e. (assumed tropical:) [ The sky, or clouds, or rain, ] watered the earth, or land, copiously: (Lth, M, TA:) or it means A^aSaAbatohaA biSawobK [ it smote it with rain; or sent rain upon it ]. (M, L, TA.) In the following verse, cited by IAar, fakayofa turaj~iY AlEA*ilaAtu tajal~udiY HamiymuhaA ↓ waSaboriY A_i*aA maA Aln~afosu Siyba he explains Siyba as being like quSida , and says that it may be of the dial. of him who says SaAba Als~ahomu ; but [ISd remarks,] I know not how this is, for SaAba Als~ahomu is not trans.; [though, as shown above, he has mentioned it as being trans.;] and in my opinion, [he says,] Syb here is from the phrase SaAbati Als~amaA='u AlA^aroDa [expl. above; the meaning of the verse being, But how should the censuring women hope for my constraining myself to behave with hardiness, and for my being patient, when the beloved of the soul has been smitten by death, or by the decree of death; for ISd adds,] kaA^an~a Almaniy~apa SaAbati AlHamiyma faA^aSaAbatohu biSawobihaA . (M, TA. *) ― -b4- [ ASAb is also used in many phrases in which its agent is likened to an archer.] One says, ASAb AlS~awaAba (tropical:) [ He hit the right thing or point, or the object, or aim, of his words or of his actions ]: (A:) and ASAb Als~adaAda [which means the same]. (S in art. sd .) And ASAb alone [means thus likewise; or] (assumed tropical:) he said, or did, that which was right. (M, K. *) And ASAb fiY qawolihi wafiEolihi (assumed tropical:) He hit the right thing in his saying and his deed; (Msb;) and so fiY raA^oyihi in his opinion; contr. of A^axoTaA^a . (A.) (TA: and the like is said in the Mgh.) And ASAb mina AlmaAli wagayorihi (assumed tropical:) He took, or took with his hand, of the property and other things. (TA.) And ASAb Al$~aYo'a (tropical:) [ He hit upon, or lighted on, the thing; ] he found the thing. (S, M, K, * TA.) And ASAbhu [(assumed tropical:) He found it, met with it, or experienced it; namely, a good or an evil event. And (assumed tropical:) He found it out, or discovered it; namely, an enigma (see 8 in art. Hjw ) or the like. And] (assumed tropical:) He found it to be right: and (assumed tropical:) he saw it, considered it, or held it, to be right. (TA. [See also 10.]) And (assumed tropical:) He aimed at it; (As, TA;) (tropical:) he desired, wished, willed, intended, or meant, it. (As, M, A, Msb, TA.) One says, A^aSaAba fulaAnN AlS~awaAba faA^axoTaA^a AljawaAba (assumed tropical:) Such a one aimed at, and desired, [to say] that which was right, (As, Msb, * TA,) and failed of giving rightly the reply. (As, TA.) And A^ayona tuSiybaAni (assumed tropical:) [ Whither do ye two desire to go? ]; a saying of Ru-beh. (TA.) tajoriY biA^amorihi ruxaA='F Hayovu A^aSaAba , in the Kur [xxxviii. 35, referring to the wind], has been expl. as meaning (assumed tropical:) [ Running by his command softly, or gently, ] whithersoever He desireth. (M, * TA.) And ASAb A@ll~`hu Al~a*iY A^araAda , said in a trad., in reply to a question respecting the interpretation of a text, means (assumed tropical:) God desireth, or meaneth, [thereby,] what He desireth, or meaneth. (TA.) And ASAb A@ll~`hu bika xayorFA means A^araAdahu (tropical:) [i. e. May God intend thee good ]. (A.) And ASAb alone (assumed tropical:) He desired, or intended, or meant, that which was right. (M, K. *) One says also, ASAbhu bixayorK (assumed tropical:) [meaning He did good to him ]. (El-Muärrij, TA in art. Asw .) [But] ASAbhu bika*aA , (M,) inf. n. A_iSaAbapN , (K,) with which are syn. ↓ muSaAbN [in accordance with a usage generally allowable] (S, TA) and ↓ muSaAbapN , (K, TA,) (assumed tropical:) [generally] means He afflicted him with, or by, such a thing; or gave pain to him thereby. (M, K: * in the latter, only the inf. n. of the verb in this sense; and so in other senses.) [Thus one says, ASAbhu bi$ar~K (assumed tropical:) He afflicted him with evil; or did evil to him: and ASAbhu bimakoruwhK (assumed tropical:) He afflicted him with, or did to him, an abominable, or an evil, thing or action: and ASAbhu biqawolK qabiyHK (assumed tropical:) He afflicted him with, or said to him, a foul saying: and ASAbhu bi*aHolK (assumed tropical:) He punished him by blood-revenge: and ASAbhu bimaraDK (assumed tropical:) He, (i. e. God,) or it, (a thing,) affected him with disease; or rendered him diseased: and in many similar cases, the phrase may be well rendered with a verb derived from the noun; like phrases in which “ affecit ” (a Latin equivalent of ASAb ) occurs; as in “ honore affecit, ” meaning “ honoravit. ”] El-Hárith Ibn-Khuld El-Makhzoomee says, rajulFA ↓ A^aZulayomu A_in~a muSaAbakumo A^ahodaY Als~alaAma taHiy~apF Zulomu (assumed tropical:) [ O Dhuleymeh, verily your afflicting a man who has given the salutation of peace, greeting, is tyranny ]: IB says that this verse is not of El- 'Arjee, as El-Hareeree imagined it to be: the correct reading is A^aZulayomu , as above: Zlym is an apocopated from of Zulayomapu ; which is the dim. of Zaluwm : some read A^aZaluwmu : and some, A^asulayomu : [the verse is cited accord. to this last reading in the S:] rajulFA is governed in the accus. case by muSaAb [as an inf. n.]: and Zulomu is the enunciative of A_in~a . (L, TA.) A^aSaAbahumu Ald~ahoru binufuwsihimo waA^amowaAlihimo (assumed tropical:) means Time, or fate, afflicted them by destruction, or extirpation, among themselves and their cattle, or possessions. (M.) [In the K, AlA_iSaAbpu is expl. as signifying AlAiHotiyaAju : but the right reading is evidently AlAijotiyaAHu , as Ibr D has remarked in the margin of my copy of the TA; so that ASAb signifies (assumed tropical:) He destroyed, or extirpated; agreeably with an explanation in the sentence next preceding above, from the M.] mano yuridi A@ll~`hu bihi xayorFA yuSibo minohu , (assumed tropical:) occurring in a trad., means Him whom God intendeth good He trieth with afflictions, that He may recompense him for them. (TA.) And one says, maA kunotu muSaAbFA walaqado A^uSibotu (assumed tropical:) [app. meaning I was not affected with weakness of intellect, or madness, and I have become affected therewith: see muSaAbN , below]. (IAar, TA.)

(Msb) meaning Rain; (Lth, Msb;) and so ↓ Say~ibN , which is originally [ SayowibN , i. e.] of the measure fayoEilN from AlS~awobu : (Bd in ii. 18:) or Say~ibN is an epithet applied to clouds ( gayomN , Sh, O, or saHaAbN , S, Msb) meaning having rain, (O,) i. q. *uw SawobK : (S, Msb:) or SawobN and ↓ Say~ibN and ↓ Say~uwbN [the last of which is written in the CK SayuwbN ] all signify the same, (M, K,) as epithets applied to rain, meaning pouring forth: (M:) or ↓ Say~uwbN , which is originally of the measure fayoEuwlN , [being altered from SayowuwbN ,] means rain pouring forth much, or abundantly: (IDrd, O:) [↓ SaAy^ibN , also, is applied as an epithet to rain, like SawobN and Say~ibN ; and] in the phrase SiybaAnu AlmaTari , accord. to Abu-l-'Alà, SiybaAn is pl. of SaAy^ib ; or it may be an inf. n., like HiromaAn : and if one say ↓ SayobaAn , with fet-h, the meaning is, what has poured forth of rain, notwithstanding the Y in it, for similar to this are rayoHaAn from Alr~awoH and EayodaAn (meaning “ tall ” palm-trees) from AlEuwod . (Ham p. 796.) -A2- Also Course, or tendency; syn. qaSodN : so in the saying, to one who is traversing a desert in uncertainty and has declined from the right way, A^aqimo Sawobaka [ Rectify thy course ]: and in the phrase fulaAnN musotaqiymu AlS~awobi [ Such a one is pursuing the right course ], said of a person when he is not declining from his way to the right or left. (TA. [See also another ex. voce A^awobN .]) ― -b2- And A place, or point, of tendency or direction or bearing, syn. jihapN , (Msb, TA,) of a thing; (Msb;) and naAHiyapN [which means the same; and also a side; or a lateral, or an adjacent, part or tract of a thing; and in this sense SawobN is used in the present day]; and jaAnibN [which generally has the latter of these meanings]. (TA.) ― -b3- See also SawaAbN , in three places.

senses.text: signifies The drawing near, or approaching, by little and little, in a deceitful, or guileful, manner, going this way and that, or to the right and left; (Ibn-'Abbád, O, K;) as also ↓ taDar~uEN : (K:) you say Dar~aEa and taDar~aEa . (O, TA.)

And Dar~aEati Al$~amosu , (K,) inf. n. as above, (S, O,) (tropical:) The sun approached the setting; (S, O, K;) [like Dj~Et ;] and ↓ DaraEat signifies the same; [like DajaEat ;] or the sun set; (K;) and Al$~amosu ↓ DaAriEati , inf. n. muDaAraEapN , signifies the same as DaraEat and Dr~Et . (TA.)

And Dar~aEati Alqidoru i. q. HaAna A^ano tudorika [i. e. The cookingpot approached, or attained, to the time of the cooking of its contents; and so, app., ↓ DArEt , accord. to the TA, but the passage in which this is there indicated presents an obvious mistranscription]. (S, O, K, TA. [In the CK, tudoraka is erroneously put for tudorika .])

And Dar~aEa Alr~ub~u [app. means The rob, or inspissated juice, became nearly mature; or] the expressed juice was cooked, but its cooking was not complete. (O, K, * TA. [In the CK, Alr~ub~a is erroneously put for Alr~ub~u , and Tabax for Tubixa , and yutim~a Taboxahu for yatim~a Taboxuhu .])

(TA.) [See also an ex. voce taHal~aja .] ― -b2- Also i. q. muqaArabapN [meaning The approaching a thing]. (TA.) See 2, in two places.

definition: , said of a ewe or she-goat, Her milk descended [ into her udder, i.
sourceDefinition: , said of a ewe or she-goat, Her milk descended [ into her udder, i. e. she secreted milk in her udder, as is shown in the lexicons in many places, (see for instance, A^arad~ato , and rid~apN ,)] a little before her bringing forth: (S, O, K:) and [in like manner] said of a she-camel, her milk descended from ( mino [a mistranscription for fiY i. e. into ]) her udder near the time of bringing forth; and the epithet applied to her is ↓ muDoriEN [without p ]: or, as in the A, said of a she-camel and of a cow, her udder ( DaroEuhaA ) became prominent before bringing forth: (TA:) or, said of a ewe or she-goat, she showed herself to be pregnant, and became large in her udder. (T in art. rmd .) And A^aDoraEato EalaY raA^osi Alwaladi [ She secreted milk, or became large, in the udder, at the time of bringing forth, or when about to produce the young, like as one says kaAna *`lika EalaY raA^osi fulaAnK expl. in art. rA^s ], said of a ewe or goat. (S in arts. rmd and rbq [in both of which the meaning is clearly shown] and in art. dfE [in which last see several sentences].) ― -b2- [Hence, app.,] A^aDoraEotu lahu maAliY (assumed tropical:) I gave him liberally, unsparingly, or freely, my property. (O, K. *) ― -b3- And ADrEhu signifies also He, or it, lowered, humbled, or abased, him. (S, O, K.) Thus, in a trad. of 'Alee, A^aDoraEa A@ll~`hu xuduwdakumo May God lower, or humble, or abase, your cheeks. (TA.) One says also, kaAna mazohuw~FA faA^aDoraEahu Alfaqoru [ He was proud, haughty, or insolent, and poverty lowered, or humbled, or abased, him ]. (TA.) And it is said in a prov., AlHum~aY A^aDoraEatoniY laka , (S, Meyd, A, O,) or liln~awomi , (Meyd, O, K,) accord. to different relations, (Meyd, O,) [meaning The fever abased me to thee, or to sleep; ] asserted by El-Mufaddal to have been first said by a certain man named Mureyr, to a Jinnee by whom he was carried off while sleeping under the influence of fever, after he had been making a fruitless search after his two brothers, Murárah and Murrah, who had also been carried off by Jinn: [his story is related at length in the O and TA, as well as by Meyd.; and is given in Har p. 568, and in Freytag's Arab. Prov. i. pp. 364-5:] the prov. is applied to the case of abasement on the occasion of need. (Meyd, O, TA.) ― -b4- One says also, ADrEhu A_ilayohi He, or it, constrained him to have recourse to him, or it. (TA.) ― -b5- And ADrEhu AlHub~u Love rendered him lean, or emaciated. (TA.)

definition: a word of well-known meaning;
sourceDefinition: a word of well-known meaning; (TA;) [properly and generally, the udder, but sometimes applied to the dug, or teat: ] the DaroE is of every female that has a cloven hoof, or of the she-camel: (S, O:) [i. e.] of each of these: (K:) or [ of the former only; i. e.] of the sheep or goat and of the cow and the like; that of the camel being termed xilofN : (Lth, O, K:) it is, to the clovenhoofed female, like the vadoY to the woman: (Msb:) or, to cattle, like the vadoY to the woman: (Towsheeh, TA:) accord. to the IF, it is of the sheep or goat and of other animals: accord. to IDrd, of the sheep or goat [ only ]: AZ says, it comprises the A^aTobaA=' , which are the A^axolaAf , and in which are the A^aHaAliyl , which are the orifices for the passing forth of the milk: (O:) the pl. is DuruwEN . (O, Msb, K.) maA lahu zaroEN walaA DaroEN [lit. He has not seed-produce nor an udder ] means (tropical:) he has not anything: (TA:) or it means he has not land to sow, nor ewe or she-goat or she-camel or other animal having a DaroE . (O.) -A2- See also the next paragraph, in two places.

definition: Lowly, humble, submissive, or in a state of abasement;
sourceDefinition: Lowly, humble, submissive, or in a state of abasement; [originally an inf. n., and therefore, as an epithet,] applied to a single person and to a pl. number: (O:) and ↓ DaAriEN signifies the same, applied to a single person; (O, Msb;) as also ↓ musotaDoriEN , (K, *TA:) accord. To Lth, one says, ↓ xad~uka DaAriEN , (O,) and ↓ A^aDoraEu , which signifies the same, (Ham p. 344,) and ↓ janobuka DaAriEN , [meaning, as is implied in the O, Thy cheek is lowly &c., and so thy side, and the like is said in the Ham p. 590,] and ↓ A^anota DaAriEN [ Thou art lowly &c.]: (O:) and the pl. of DaAriEN is DaraEapN and DuruwEN : (TA:) or ↓ DaAriEN signifies, and so ↓ DariEN , and [in an intensive sense] ↓ DaruwEN and ↓ DaraEapN , lowering, humbling, or abasing, himself: (K:) or thus, and making petition for a gift: (TA:) and DaraEN signifies weak; (S, Mgh, Msb, K:) as also ↓ DariEN ; (K;) the former (Msb, K) originally an inf. n. (Msb) [and therefore, as an epithet,] applied to a single person and to a pl. number: (K:) and DaraEN and ↓ DaAriEN small; applied to anything: or small in age, weak, (K, TA,) and lean, spare, or light of flesh: (TA:) and Aljisomi ↓ DaAriEu , (S,) and ↓ DariEN , (TA,) lean, spare, or light of flesh, and weak, in the body; (S, TA;) applied to a man: (S:) and DaraEN applied to a colt, not having strength to run, (K, TA,) by reason of the smallness of his age. (TA.) Also (assumed tropical:) Cowardly, or weak-hearted: you say, huwa waraEN DaraEN [both app. meaning the same]. (TA.) And, applied to a man, (tropical:) Inexperienced in affairs; ignorant; or in whom is no profit nor judgment; syn. gumorN . (TA.)

sourceDefinition: and ↓ Duwo'N and ↓ DiyaA='N (S, M, O, K) and ↓ DiwaA='N , (M, K,) the last of which is [erroneously] written in the L DawaA='N , (TA,) signify the same, (S, M, O, K,) i. e. Light, syn. nuwrN , (K, TA,) accord. to the leading lexicologists; but see what follows: (TA:) and Dawo'N is an inf. n. of DaA='a , (S, M, O, Msb, K,) and so is ↓ Duwo'N , (S, O, K,) or this is a simple subst. from DaA='a , and so is ↓ DiyaA='N , which is also, sometimes, written ↓ Diy^aA='N , from A^aDaA='a as syn. with DaA='a : (Msb:) the pl. of Dawo'N (M, TA) and ↓ Duwo'N (M) is A^aDowaA='N ; and ↓ DiyaA='N is sometimes a pl., (M, TA,) as Zj states it to be: (TA:) some say that Dawo'N has a more intensive signification than nuwrN , and that hence God has likened his direction [the Kur-án] to Aln~uwr rather than to AlD~awo' ; because if it were otherwise, no one had erred: and that hence, also, [in the Kur x. 5,] the sun is termed ↓ DiyaA=' ; and the moon, nuwrN : it is also said that Dawo'N signifies the rays that are diffused by what is termed nuwrN : the kádee Zekereeyà affirms that these two words are syn. by their original application, but that Dawo'N is more forcible accord. to usage: and some say that AlD~awo'u signifies that [ light ] which subsists by itself, as [that of] the sun, and fire; and Aln~uwru , to that which subsists by some other thing [as does the light of the moon]. (MF, TA.)

sourceDefinition: (S, Mgh, Msb, K, &c.) and ↓ TiboYN (S, K) [ A teat, or dug, of any of certain animals mentioned in what follows; agreeably with an explanation of its pl. in the O, voce DaroEN , on the authority of AZ; and agreeably with a usage of its pl. in the TA, voce xilofN , on the authority of Lth: this is the most usual, if not the only proper, signification:] the DaroE [which sometimes means the teat, or dug, and is app. here used in this sense]; mostly, of a beast of prey: (Mgh:) or it is to the beast of prey, and to the solid-hoofed animal, (As, T, S,) like the DaroE to others; and sometimes to the camel; (S;) or that of the camel and of the cloven-hoofed animal is termed xilofN : (As, T:) or, to the camel, and to the cloven-hoofed animal, like the vadoY [which some- times means the teat ] to the woman; and in rare instances, to the solid-hoofed animal, and to the beast of prey: (Msb:) or the HalamaAt [meaning teats ], (K, TA,) or, accord. to the M, the HalamataAni [meaning pair of teats ], (TA,) of the DaroE [or udder ], of the camel, and of a cloven-hoofed animal, and of a solid-hoofed animal, and of a beast of prey: (K:) [and ↓ TuboyapN is perhaps a dial. var.: (see xaAtamN , last sentence but two:)] pl. (TA.) ― -b3- A^aTobaA='u Alkalobapi (assumed tropical:) [ Bitch's dugs ] is an appellation of the tree called muxaATap [i. e. the sebesten ]. (TA in art. mxT , q. v.)

definition: , aor. , inf. n. TaEomN and TaEaAmN , He ate it; namely, food: (K, * TA:) and TaEima , aor. as above, inf. n. TuEomN , with damm, he tasted [a thing]: (K:) or TaEima , aor. as above, (S, Mgh, * Msb,)...
sourceDefinition: , aor. , inf. n. TaEomN and TaEaAmN , He ate it; namely, food: (K, * TA:) and TaEima , aor. as above, inf. n. TuEomN , with damm, he tasted [a thing]: (K:) or TaEima , aor. as above, (S, Mgh, * Msb,) inf. n. TuEomN , with damm, (S,) or TaEomN , with fet-h, (Msb,) or both, (Mgh,) and maToEamN also is an inf. n. of the same verb, (TA,) signifies he ate, (S, Mgh, Msb, *) a thing, (Mgh,) and [app. also he swallowed, for it is said that] it applies to anything that is swallowed easily or agreeably, even to water: (Msb:) and he tasted (S, Mgh, Msb) a thing; (Mgh, Msb;) as also ↓ tTE~m ; (S, Mgh, K;) [i. e.] this latter verb signifies he tasted food in order that he might know its flavour; and so ↓ AstTEm : (Msb:) and TaEima as meaning he tasted may be used in relation to that which is eaten and to that which is drunk. (L.) Hence, in the Kur [xxxiii. 53], faA_i*aA TaEimotumo faA@nota$iruwA And when ye shall have eaten [ disperse yourselves ]. (S, * TA.) And you say, fulaAnN qal~a TuEomuhu , meaning [ Such a one, ] his eating [ was, or became, little ]. (S.) The saying in the Kur [ii. 250], wamano lamo yaToEamohu faA_in~ahu min~iY means But whoso does not taste it, (S, Msb, * TA,) he is of my followers, (Bd, Jel,) or is at one, or in union, with me: (Bd:) or, accord. to Zj, the meaning is, bihi ↓ lamo yataTaE~amo [app. meaning does not refresh himself with it as though with food ]: (TA:) or, as some say, the passage in which it occurs denotes a prohibition to take aught save as much as is laded out with the hand; and when water has with it something that is chewed, one says of it yuToEamu . (Er-Rághib, TA.) taToEamo ↓ taTaE~amo i. e. Taste thou, (S, Mgh, K,) then thou wilt have desire, or appetence, (Mgh,) or so that thou mayest have desire, or appetence, and mayest eat; (S, K;) or taste thou the food, for it will induce thee to eat it; (IB, TA;) is a prov., (IB, Mgh, TA,) said to him who refrains from an affair; meaning, commence it, for thy doing so will invite thee to finish it. (IB, TA.) ― -b2- AlT~aEomu signifies also The eating with the central incisors: one says, A_in~ahu layaToEamu TaEomFA HasanFA [ Verily he eats well with the central incisors ]. (TA.) ― -b3- maA yaToEamu A=kilu h`*aA AlT~aEaAmi , (K, * TA,) a phrase mentioned by ISh, (TA,) means (tropical:) The eater of this food does not become satisfied in stomach. (K, * TA.) ― -b4- TaEima said of a branch, or shoot, (tropical:) It received ingraftment. (ISh, K, TA.) ― -b5- And [hence, perhaps,] TaEimato Eayonuhu (assumed tropical:) [ His eye had a mote cast into it: see 4]. (TA.) ― -b6- TaEima Ealayohi , (K, TA,) inf. n. TuEomN , (K, * TA,) which, in the K, is improperly disjoined from its verb, [as though it were a simple subst.,] (TA,) i. q. qadara [i. e. He had power over him, or it; or he had power, or ability, to do it, &c.]. (K, TA.)

TuEuwmN . (K.) One says, TaEomuhu mur~N [ Its taste is bitter ], (S, TA,) and HulowN [ sweet ], (Msb, TA,) and HaAmiDN [ acid ]: and tagay~ara TaEomuhu Its taste became altered from its natural quality. (Msb.)

sourceDefinition: i. q. maA^okalapN , (S, Msb, K, TA,) or rizoqN ; (Mgh;) i. e. (assumed tropical:) An assigned, or appointed, means of subsistence; such as a grant of a tract of land; [ an allodium so granted; ] and a tax, or a portion of a tax or of taxes; and the like: (Mgh, TA:) pl. TuEamN . (Mgh, K.) One says, jaEalotu h`*ihi AlD~ayoEapa TuEomapF lifulaAnK (assumed tropical:) [ I have assigned this estate as a means of subsistence to such a one ]. (S.) [For other exs., see 4.] And it is said in a trad. respecting the inheritance of the grandfather, A_in~a Als~udosa AlA=xara TuEomapN lahu i. e. (assumed tropical:) The other sixth is a surplus for him beyond his [ regular ] due. (TA.) ― -b2- Also An invitation to food. (K.) ― -b3- And (tropical:) A mode, or manner, of gain; (S, K, Ta;) as also ↓ TiEomapN : (TA:) it is like HirofapN . (A, TA.) One says, fulaAnN Eafiyfu AlT~uEomapi (tropical:) [ Such a one is uncorrupt in respect of the mode of gain ]: and xabiyvu AlT~uEomapi i. e. corrupt in respect of the means of gain. (S, TA.)

definition: A way, mode, or manner, of eating: (K, TA:) Lh explains it as meaning a way, mode, or manner, of acting or conduct, without saying in eating or in any other thing.
sourceDefinition: A way, mode, or manner, of eating: (K, TA:) Lh explains it as meaning a way, mode, or manner, of acting or conduct, without saying in eating or in any other thing. (TA.) And fulaAnN Tay~ibu AlT~iEomapi (tropical:) [ Such a one is accustomed to eat nothing but what is lawful ], and xabiyvu AlT~iEomapi accustomed to eat nothing but what is unlawful. (TA.) sourceDefinition: [as an inf. n.: see 1. ― -b2- As a subst.,] Food, (S, Nh, Mgh, Msb, K,) of any kind; (Nh, TA;) like as $araAbN signifies beverage [of any kind]: (Mgh, Msb:) and especially wheat, (S, Nh, Mgh, Msb, K,) to which it is applied by the people of El-Hijáz; (Msb, TA;) and barley; (Nh, TA;) [and corn in general; thus applied to millet in the present day in some parts of Arabia, as, for instance, in El-Yemen; (see miyrapN ;)] and dates, (Nh, Mgh, TA,) when said not to mean wheat; (Mgh, TA;) &c.: (Nh, TA:) and in the Expos. of the “ Shifè, ” it is said to be applied to (tropical:) other than food tropically: (TA:) and ↓ TuEomN signifies the same; (S, Mgh, Msb, K;) as also ↓ maToEamN ; (Ham p. 166, and K; *) of which the pl. is maTaAEimu : (Ham ubi suprà:) one says, huwa yaHotakiru AlmaTaAEima , meaning [ He collects and withholds ] wheat [ waiting for a time of scarcity and dearness ]: (A, TA:) the pl. of TaEaAmN is A^aToEimapN , (Mgh, Msb, K,) and pl. pl. A^aToEimaAtN . (K.) [It often means A meal, or repast. ] TaEaAmu AlbaHori means That from which the water [ of the sea, or of the great river, ] has receded, leaving it, so that it is taken without fishing: or, as some say, anything that is irrigated by the water of the bHr [i. e. great river ], and consequently vegetates: so says Zj. (TA. [See the Kur v. 97.])

sourceDefinition: The Had~ , (T, M, Msb, K,) or Taraf , (S,) [both of which mean the end, or extremity, but the former means also the edge, ] of a sword, (T, S, M, Msb, K,) or of a spear-head and the like, (K,) or also of a spear-head and of an arrowhead and of a dagger and the like; (M;) or the part next to the Taraf [or extremity ] of the sword; also called its *ubaAb : (T:) or the ZubataAni are the parts of the two edges that are on either side of the *ubaAb [by which last word is here app. meant the point ] of the sword: (AZ, T and TA voce *ubaAbN , q. v.:) [for the swords of the Arabs, in the older times, were generally straight, twoedged, and tapering to a point:] or, accord. to Aboo-Riyásh, the Zubap of the sword is the part that is four digits' measure below, or within, ( duwna ,) the *ubaAb thereof; and is the strikingplace thereof: and it is also its Had~ ; and the Zubap of the spear-head is likewise its Had~ : (Ham p. 48:) the p in ZubapN is a substitute for w , which is the final radical, (S, M, Msb, K,) the word being originally ZubawN : (S, TA:) the pl. is A^aZobK , (S, K,) a pl. of pauc., (S,) and ZubaAtN (T, S, M, Msb, K) and ZubaApN [which is originally ZubawapN ] (S, * TA) and Zubuwna (T, S, M, Msb, K) and Zibuwna and ZubFA or ZubFY . (M, K.) In the saying of EsSemow-al Ibn-'Ádiyà, tasiylu EalaY Had~i AlZ~ubaAti nufuwsunaA walayosato EalaY gayori AlZ~ubaAti tasiylu [ Our bloods flow upon the edge of the ZbAt , and upon other than the edge of the ZbAt they flow not ], by the ZbAt may be meant the swords, altogether, or the striking-places of the swords. (Ham p. 52. [See also a similar ex. in p. 48 of the same.]) -A2- Also A kind of mazaAd [or leathern water-bag ]. (M.) -A3- And A place of bending, or turning, of a valley; like ZaboyapN [which belongs to art. ZbY ]: pl. of the former ZubaA='N , a pl. of a rare form. (M in art. ZbY .)

rawSourceText: The Had~ , (T, M, Msb, K,) or Taraf , (S,) [both of which mean the end, or extremity, but the former means also the edge, ] of a sword, (T, S, M, Msb, K,) or of a spear-head and the like, (K,) or also of a spear-head and of an arrowhead and of a dagger and the like; (M;) or the part next to the Taraf [or extremity ] of the sword; also called its *ubaAb : (T:) or the ZubataAni are the parts of the two edges that are on either side of the *ubaAb [by which last word is here app. meant the point ] of the sword: (AZ, T and TA voce *ubaAbN , q. v.:) [for the swords of the Arabs, in the older times, were generally straight, twoedged, and tapering to a point:] or, accord. to Aboo-Riyásh, the Zubap of the sword is the part that is four digits' measure below, or within, ( duwna ,) the *ubaAb thereof; and is the strikingplace thereof: and it is also its Had~ ; and the Zubap of the spear-head is likewise its Had~ : (Ham p. 48:) the p in ZubapN is a substitute for w , which is the final radical, (S, M, Msb, K,) the word being originally ZubawN : (S, TA:) the pl. is A^aZobK , (S, K,) a pl. of pauc., (S,) and ZubaAtN (T, S, M, Msb, K) and ZubaApN [which is originally ZubawapN ] (S, * TA) and Zubuwna (T, S, M, Msb, K) and Zibuwna and ZubFA or ZubFY . definition: A receptacle (Lth, T, S, M, Mgh, O, Msb, K) of anything;
sourceDefinition: A receptacle (Lth, T, S, M, Mgh, O, Msb, K) of anything; (Lth, T, M;) [ a vessel, or vase; ] an A_iboriyq is thus termed as being a Zrf for what is in it: (Lth, T, TA:) and AHn applies it to a seed-vessel, or pericarp, or a cell of a pericarp: (M, TA:) [and it is also applied to a case, or cover, for a book or the like:] the pl. is ZuruwfN : (T, S, * M, Mgh, O, Msb, K:) A^aZoraAfN is a mistake. (Mgh.) [Applying it to a vessel of silver,] Har uses it as meaning “ silver. ” (P. 614 [referring to a phrase in p. 213].) One says, A^axa*otu AlmataAEa biZarofihi [ I took the goods with the receptacle thereof ]. (A, TA.) And hence, (A, TA,) raA^ayotuhu biZarofihi (tropical:) I saw him himself. (A, O, K, TA.) And huwa naqiY~u AlZ~arofi (tropical:) He is faithful, (O, K, TA,) not treacherous. (M, O, K, TA.) ― -b2- And hence (assumed tropical:) [ An adverbial noun of place or of time, implying the meaning of the preposition fY ; and also by some applied to a noun of place or of time together with that preposition; i. e.] what are termed Zarofu AlmakaAni and Alz~amaAni , (O,) pl. Zuruwfu Alz~amaAni and AlmakaAni : (S, M: *) the descriptive terms that denote the places [or times] of things are called ZuruwfN : (Lth, T:) they are thus termed by Kh; and by Ks, maHaAl~u ; and by Fr, SifaAtN . (T.) ― -b3- Also [ Excellence, or elegance, in mind, manners, and address or speech; and in person, countenance, or garb, guise, or external appearance; or all of these qualities combined: ] a term denoting a condition that combines the generality of mental and bodily and extrinsic excellences; likened [by reason of its comprehensiveness] to the receptacle thus called: (Er-Rághib, TA:) or cleverness, ingeniousness, intelligence, or acuteness in intellect; syn. kiyaAsapN , (S, O, K,) or kayosN , (Mgh, Msb,) and *akaA='N : (Mgh:) or i. q. baraAEapN , and *akaA='u qalobK ; [the former meaning excellence in knowledge, or other qualities; or accomplishment, or perfection, in every excellence, and in goodliness; ] ('Eyn, M, O, Msb, K; *) thus accord. to most of the copies of the K [as well as the 'Eyn and M and O and Msb], but correctly bazaAEap , with the letter zAY : (TA:) [if so, these two explanations ( bazaAEapN and *akaA='u qalobK ) add nothing to others here given:] or skilfulness (M, K, TA) in a thing (M, TA) is thus termed by the people of El-Yemen: (TA:) or it is in the tongue, (IAar, T, K,) only; (K;) meaning beauty of expression, (M, L, TA,) and eloquence; (L, TA;) and HalaAwapN is in the eyes, and malaAHapN is in the mouth, and jamaAlN is in the nose: (IAar, T:) or beauty of garb, guise, or external appearance: (M:) or beauty of face, and of garb, guise, or external appearance: (O, K:) or it is in the face and in the tongue: (Ks, O, K:) or goodliness, or beauty; and A^adab [as having the meaning first assigned to ZarofN in this sentence, i. e. excellence, or elegance, in mind, manners, or address or speech; or as meaning good breeding, good manners, politeness, or polite accomplishments ]: (Msb:) or, as an inf. n., the being elegant, graceful, or beautiful: and the being intelligent, sagacious, or acute in intellect: (KL:) accord. to the author of the 'Eyn, (O,) it is only an attribute of young men and young women (M, O, Msb, * K) that are acute in intellect, clever, or skilful; (M, O, K;) not of elders, nor of lords, or chiefs: (M, K:) but as meaning kiyosN , it is common to young persons and elders: (Msb:) some of those who affect distinctness of speech by twisting the sides of the mouth say that the word is ↓ ZurofN , with damm, to distinguish it from ZarofN meaning “ a receptacle; ” but this is a sheer mistake. (MF, TA.)

definition: Possessing the quality, or qualities, termed Zarof ;
sourceDefinition: Possessing the quality, or qualities, termed Zarof ; (T, S, M, O, Msb, K;) as also ↓ ZuraAfN , (Lh, M, O, K,) the two being like TawiylN and TuwaAlN , (O,) [or the latter has an intensive signification, (see TuwaAlN , and see also the “ Durrat el-Ghowwás, ” in De Sacy's Anthol. Gramm. Arabe, p. 48 of the Ar. text,)] and ↓ Zur~aAfN , (M, K,) or this last, which is like Tuw~aAlN , denotes more than ZuraAfN without teshdeed: (O:) accord. to Mbr, it is derived from Zarof signifying “ a receptacle, ” as though meaning a receptacle for excellence, or elegance, in mind, manners, or address or speech: (TA:) [it may be rendered, agreeably with explanations of ZarofN , excellent, or elegant, in mind, manners, and address or speech; and in person, countenance or garb, guise, or external appearance: or clever, ingenious, intelligent, or acute in intellect; well-mannered, well-bred, accomplished, or polite; beautiful in person or countenance; elegant, or graceful; &c.:] and is expl. as meaning eloquent; thus by As and IAar: and possessing knowledge and courage: and goodly, or beautiful, in clothing, and in outer apparel: (TA:) and is used by the people of El-Yemen as meaning skilful: (O:) and, as Ks says, it is applied as an epithet to a tongue, and to a face: (TA:) the pl. of ZariyfN is ZiraAfN (S, M, O, Msb, K) and ZurafaA='u (T, S, O, Msb, K) and Zariyfuwna (O, K) and ZurufN , (S, M, IB, K,) a form sometimes used, (IB, TA,) and ZuruwfN , (T, S, M, O, K,) also a form sometimes used, (S, O,) approvable in poetry, (T,) as though formed from ZarofN , or [anomalous] like ma*aAkiyru (S, O, K) accord. to Kh (S, O) and Sb: (TA:) the pl. of ↓ ZuraAfN is ZurafaA='u : (Lh, M, K:) and the pl. of ↓ Zur~aAfN is Zur~aAfuwna : (M, K:) the fem. of ZariyfN is ZariyfapN ; and the pl. of this is ZiraAfN , (Sb, T, M, Msb, TA,) like a pl. of the masc., (Sb, M, TA,) and ZaraAy^ifu . (T, M, TA.) It is said in a trad. of 'Omar, mentioned by IAar, (Mgh, O, TA,) and by As, (TA,) A_i*aA kaAna All~iS~u ZariyfFA laA yuqoTaEu , (Mgh,) or lamo yuqoTaEo , (O, TA,) meaning When the thief is eloquent (Mgh, O, TA) and intelligent, (Mgh,) he averts from himself the prescribed punishment by his pleading [so that he will not be, or is not, mutilated by amputation of the hand]. (Mgh, O, TA.)

definition: a rel. n. from ↓ EaboqarN , a place which the Arabs assert to be of the lands of the Jinn, or Genii: (S, O, Msb:) or a certain place, (K,) in the desert, (TA,) abounding with Jinn: (K:) AO says, We...
sourceDefinition: a rel. n. from ↓ EaboqarN , a place which the Arabs assert to be of the lands of the Jinn, or Genii: (S, O, Msb:) or a certain place, (K,) in the desert, (TA,) abounding with Jinn: (K:) AO says, We have not found any one who knows where this country is, or when it existed. (TA.) Hence it is applied as an epithet to anything wondered at, or admired, for the skilfulness which it exhibits, or the excellence of its manufacture, and its strength: (S, O:) or to any work great in estimation, and fine, and delicate: (Msb:) it is both sing. and pl.; and the fem. is Eaboqariy~apN : you say, viyaAbN Eaboqariy~apN [ Cloths, or garments, of admirable manufacture ]: (S, O:) [or such are so called in relation to a certain town; for] ↓ EaboqarN is also a town (M, K) in El-Yemen, (M,) or, accord. to the Moajam, in El-Jezeereh, in which cloths or garments, and carpets, are variegated, or figured, (TA,) and of which the cloths or garments are of the utmost beauty. (K.) ― -b2- And A kind of carpets, (S, O, K,) variously dyed and figured: upon such the Prophet used to prostrate himself when he prayed: (S, O:) as also ↓ EabaAqiriY~N : (K:) and some read EabaAqiriY~ in the Kur lv. 76: (S, O:) as pl. of EaboqariY~N : (TA:) but this is a mistake; for a rel. n. has no such pl; (S;) unless it be from a sing. n. of a pl. form, like HaDaAjiriY~N from HaDaAjiru , and so be a rel. n. from EabaAqiru : so say the skilful grammarians, Kh and Sb and Ks: Az mentions the reading ↓ EabaAqariY~ , with fet-h to the q ; as though it were a rel. n. from EabaAqarN : Fr says that EaboqariY~N signifies thick [ carpets of the kind called ] TanaAfisa : and also silk brocade; syn. diybaAjN : Kt, that it signifies what are called zaraAbiY~ : Sa'eed Ibn-Jubeyr, that it signifies excellent zrAbY~ : (TA:) the n. un. is Eaboqariy~apN . (Fr, TA.) ― -b3- Also Good, or excellent; applied to an animal, and to a jewel. (TA.) ― -b4- Perfect, or complete; applied to anything. (K.) ― -b5- A pure, unmixed, lie; (O, K, * TA;) that has no truth mixed with it. (O, TA.) ― -b6- A lord, or chief, (O, K,) of men: (TA:) or (TA, in the K, “ and ”) one who has none above him: and strong. (K.) You say of a strong man, h`*aA EaboqariY~u qawomK : (S, O:) or this means This is a chief, or lord, of a people: (As, on the authority of 'Amr Ibn-El-'Alà:) and in a trad. it is said that the Prophet related a dream, mentioning 'Omar, and said, falamo A^ara Eaboqariy~FA yaforiY fariy~ahu [ And I have not seen a chief of a people do his wonderful deeds ]. (S, * O, TA.) ― -b7- It is also applied as an epithet denoting superlativeness [of any quality]. (TA.) They even said ZulomN EaboqariY~N [ Excessive, or extreme, wrongdoing ]. (S, O.)

definition: The primary signification of EajozN [an inf.
sourceDefinition: The primary signification of EajozN [an inf. n. of Eajaza ] is The being, or becoming, behind, or behindhand, or backward, with respect to a thing; or holding back, hanging back, or abstaining, from it: and its happening at the latter, or last, part, or at the end, of an affair: and hence, in common conventional language, it has the signification shown by the explanation here next following. (Er-Rághib, B, &c., and TA.) ― -b2- Eajaza , aor. , inf. n. EajozN and maEojazapN and maEojizapN (S, Mgh, O, Msb, K) and maEojazN , (S, O, Msb, K,) which is agreeable with rule, (S,) and maEojizN , (S, O, Msb, K,) which is extr., (Sb, TA,) and EajazaAnN and EujuwzN ; (O, K;) and Eajiza , aor. , (O, Msb, K,) inf. n. EajazN , (Msb,) said by IKtt to be mentioned by Fr, as of the dial. of some of the tribe of Keys, but by others [and among them Sgh in the O] said to be a bad form, (TA,) or mentioned by AZ, as of the dial. of some of the tribe of Keys- 'Eylán, but not known to them, and said by IF to be disallowed by IAar in the sense here immediately following; (Msb;) He lacked strength, or power, or ability; he was, or became, powerless, impotent, or unable. (S, * Msb, * K, TA.) You say, Eajaza Eano ka*aA , (S, A, O, Msb, TA,) and accord. to some, as shown above, Eajiza Eanohu , (Msb, TA,) He lacked strength, or power, or ability, for, or to do, effect, accomplish, achieve, attain, or compass, such a thing; he was unable to do it: (S, * O, * Msb, * TA:) or (tropical:) he was too old to do it. (A, TA.) And it is said in a trad., (S, * Mgh,) of 'Omar, (TA,) laA tuliv~uwA bidaAri maEojazapK , meaning Remain ye not in a country, or district, or town, where ye are unable to gain your livelihood. (S, A, Mgh, * TA.) You say also, laA yasaEuniY $aYo'N wayaEojizu Eanoka (tropical:) [app. A thing will not suffice me when it cannot thee ]. (A, TA.) And jaAw^uwA bijayo$K taEojizu AlA^aroDu Eanohu (tropical:) [ They came with an army which the earth had not strength to bear, or scarce sufficed to contain ]. (A, TA.) ― -b3- [And Eajaza Eano ka*aA also signifies He, or it, lacked such a thing: see an ex. voce EarofN .] ― -b4- [Hence,] Eajazato , (S, O, Msb, K,) aor. , (S, O, K,) or , (Msb,) inf. n. EujuwzN (S, O, K) and EajozN , (TA,) She (a woman, S, O, Msb) became aged; (S, O, Msb, K;) [because the aged lacks strength;] as also Eajuzato , aor. ; (O, K;) and ↓ Eaj~azato , inf. n. taEojiyzN . (S, O, K.) -A2- Eajizato , aor. , (S, O, K,) inf. n. EajazN and EujozN , (S, K,) [or the latter is a simple subst.,] or EajozN and EujozaAnN , (O,) She (a woman, S) became large in the hinder parts, or posteriors; (S, O, K;) as also ↓ Euj~izato , inf. n. taEojiyzN : (Yoo, O, K:) and Eajiza , inf. n. EajazN , he (a man) became large therein: (Msb:) accord. to IAar, as related by Th, one does not say thus of a man except in this sense. (S, O.) ― -b2- [Hence,] Eajizati Alr~amolapu (assumed tropical:) The piece of sand became high. (IKtt, TA.) -A3- Eujiza He (a man) was importuned for his property: part. n. ↓ maEojuwzN . (O.) -A4- EaAjazotuhu faEajazotuhu : see 3.

sourceDefinition: , (Msb,) inf. n. taEojiyzN , (S, O, Msb, K,) He attributed, or imputed, to him lack of strength or power or ability; i. e., inability, or impotence: (S, * O, * K, * TA:) he asserted him to be, or called him, or made him, ( jaEalahu ,) unable, or impotent. (Msb.) [Compare 4, in a sense given below from the B.] You say also, Eaj~aza fulaAnN raA^oYa fulaAnK Such a one attributed, or imputed, the opinion of such a one to littleness of good judgment, or of prudence; as though he attributed it to inability. (TA.) ― -b2- Also He withheld him, or kept him back, or diverted him, (S, K,) from ( Eano ) a person or thing: (TA:) [as though he made him unable to attain his object: compare 4.] -A2- Eaj~azato , said of a woman: see 1, latter part. -A3- Euj~izato , said of a woman: see 1, latter part. ― -b2- Ej~z daAb~atahu He put the Haqiybap [q. v.] upon his beast. (Sgh, TA.) ― -b3- Ej~z Al$~aAEiru The poet uttered, or wrote, the Eajuz , or last foot, of the verse. (TA.)

sourceDefinition: (S, A, O, L, Msb, K) and ↓ EajozN (O, L, Msb, K) and ↓ EujuzN (L, Msb) and ↓ EujozN (O, L, Msb, K) and ↓ EajizN (O, L, K) and ↓ EijozN , (K,) but the first form is the most chaste, (Msb,) fem. and masc., (S, O, Msb, K,) in the first of the following senses, i. e., in the general application; and in the second, or restricted application, fem., but made masc. by the Benoo- Temeem, (Msb,) or, accord. to El-Heythemee, fem. only, (TA,) The hinder part of a thing; (S, A, O, L, Msb, K;) i. e., of anything: (Msb:) and particularly the hinder parts, posteriors, buttock, or buttocks, rump, or croup, (S, * O, *) or what is between the two hips, (Mgh, Msb,) or what is after the back, (TA,) of a man, and of a woman; (S, Mgh, O, Msb, TA;) [and of a camel, &c.;] and ↓ EajiyzapN signifies the same, but of a woman only, (S, O, Msb, K,) in its proper application, though sometimes of a man also by way of comparison: (IAth, Mgh, TA:) pl. of EajuzN , (S, Msb, K,) and of its variants, (Msb, K,) A^aEojaAzN , (S, Msb, K,) the only pl. form: (TA:) and of ↓ EajiyzapN , EajiyzaAtN : they do not say EajaAy^izu , [the regular form of pl. of Ejyzp ,] for fear of confusion [as it is pl. of EajuwzN or of EajuwzapN ]. (TA.) One says also, A_in~ahaA laEaZyimapu AlA^aEojaAzi Verily she is large in the hinder parts: as though the term EajuzN were applicable to every portion thereof. (Lh, TA.) And rakiba fiY AlT~alabi A^aEojaAza AlA_ibili He exposed himself, in seeking [a thing], to abasement and difficulty and patient endurance, and exerted unsparingly his power or ability, (K, TA,) not caring for undergoing long night-journeying. (TA.) Thus expl. in a saying of 'Alee: lanaA Haq~N A_ino nuEoTahu naA^oxu*ohu waA_ino numonaEohu narokabo A^aEojaAza AlA_ibili waA_ino TaAla Als~uraY [ There is a right belonging to us: if we be given it, we take it: and if we be refused it, we expose ourselves to abasement, &c., though the night-journeying be long ]: (O, * TA:) or, accord. to Az, he does not mean this, but alludes to others' having precedence in respect of his right, and his being himself kept back from it. (TA.) One also says, banuw fulaAnK yarokabuwna A^aEojaAza AlA_ibili The sons of such a one are in a state of abasement, dependents of others: or experience difficulties; because the rump, or croup, of the camel is a difficult place to ride upon. (A.) And it is said by one of the wise, (Aktham Ibn-Seyfee, T, in TA, art. dbr ,) laA tadab~aruwA A^aEojaAza A^umuwrK qado wal~ato SuduwruhaA , (TA, in this art., and O,) or laA tatadab~aruwA , (T, in TA, art. dbr ,) (tropical:) [ Think ye not upon the ends of things whereof the beginnings have passed: ] meaning, when a thing has passed, make not your minds, or desires, to follow after it, regretting what has passed, but be consoled for it, placing your reliance upon God: (O, TA:) and, as IAth says, it is intended to incite to the consideration of the results, or issues, of affairs before the entering upon them. (TA.) [See also dab~ara .] ― -b2- A^aEojaAzu naxolK The trunks of palm-trees. (S, O, K.) [See Kur liv. 20 and lxix. 7.) And A^aEojaAzu AlS~il~iyaAni [ The stems of the Sil~iyaAn ]. (AHn, M in art. Sl .) ― -b3- EajuzN also signifies The last foot of a verse; contr. of SadorN . (TA.) And The latter hemistich of a verse: the former hemistich is termed SadorN . (O.) [And The last word of a clause of rhyming prose. And the latter part of a word.] -A2- See also EaAjizN . -A3- A^ay~aAmu AlEajuzi : see EajuwzN .

(K.) ― -b2- An old, or aged, woman: (S, O, Msb, K:) a woman extremely old; or old and weak: so called because of her inability to do many things: (TA:) [this is the most common signification of the word:] accord. to ISk, (S, O, Msb,) you should not say ↓ EajuwzapN ; (S, O, Msb, K;) or this is bad; (K;) and is said by the vulgar; (S, O;) but IAar authorizes it; (O;) and IAmb allows it, to demonstrate its being fem.; and Yoo is related to have heard it from the Arabs: (Msb:) pl. EajaAy^izu , (S, O, Msb, K,) or this is pl. of EajuwzapN ; (R, TA;) and EujuzN , (S, O, Msb, K,) and EujozN , a contraction of EujuzN , occurring in traditions. (TA.) ― -b3- A man's wife, whether old or young: (Az, O, K, * TA:) and in like manner, the husband, though young, is called $ayoxN . (Az, O, TA.) ― -b4- An old, or aged, man: (O, TA:) a man extremely old; or old and weak. (TA.) -A2- (tropical:) Wine; (S, O, K;) because of its oldness: (S, O:) or old wine. (A, TA.) -A3- A certain nail in the hilt of a sword, (IAar, O, K,) with which is another nail called Alkalobu . (IAar, O, TA.) Az approves of this explanation. (O.) ― -b2- A sword-blade. (Lth, S, O, K.) ― -b3- A sword. (O, TA.) ― -b4- [It has a great variety of other significations; but these are of very rare occurrence, and are therefore to be mentioned ( An $A=' All~`h ) in Book II.] -A4- A^ay~aAmu AlEajuwzi ; (S, O, K;) also called ↓ A^ay~aAmu AlEajuzi , because they come in the latter part ( Eajuz ) of winter; but the former is the correct appellation; (MF;) accord. to the usage of the Arabs, Five days, the names of which are Sin~N and Sin~aborN and waborN and muTofiy^u Aljamori and mukofiy^u AlZ~aEoni ; said by Ibn-Kunáseh to be of the nawo' of AlS~arofap [by which is meant the auroral setting of the Twelfth Mansion of the Moon, which, in Central Arabia, about the commencement of the era of the Flight, happened on the 9th of March O. S.: in the modern Egyptian Almanacs, the Ay~Am AlEjwz are said to commence now on the 9th of March N. S., which is now the 26th of February O. S.]: (S, O, TA:) or, accord. to Abu-l-Ghowth, (S,) they are seven days, (S, K,) named Sin~N and Sin~aborN and waborN and AlA=miru and Almuw^otamiru and AlmuEal~ilu and muTofiy^u Aljamori , or mukofiy^u AlZ~aEoni : (K:) and some reckon mkfy^ AlZEn an eighth: but most authors hold these names to be post-classical: (MF:) accord. to Esh-Shereeshee, they are seven days; four of the last [ days ] of February, and three of the first [ days ] of March: (Har p. 295:) during these days blew the wind by which the tribe of 'Ád was destroyed: and they are thus called because they are [in] the latter part ( Eajoz ) of winter; or because an old woman ( Eajuwz ) of 'Ád concealed herself in a subterranean excavation, from which the wind dragged her forth on the eighth day, and destroyed her: (Bd in lxix. 7:) or A=mirN and muw^otamirN are the names of the last two days; (K in art. Amr ;) the former being the sixth, and the latter the seventh. (M in that art.) Ibn-Ahmar says, (S,) or, accord. to IB, not Ibn-Ahmar, but Aboo-Shibl 'Ásim Ibn-el-Aarábee, as Th says, on the authority of IAar, (TA,) or Aboo-Shibl 'Osm Ibn-Wahb Et-Temeemee, (O,) kusiEa Al$~itaA='u bisaboEapK gubori A^ay~aAmi $aholatinaA mina Al$~ahori faA_i*aA A@noqaDato A^ay~aAmuhaA wamaDato Sin~N waSin~aborN maEa Alwabori wabiA=mirK waA^uxay~ihi muw^otimaro wamuEal~ilK wabimuTofiy^i Aljamori *ahaba Al$~itaA='u muwal~iyFA EajilFA waA^atatoka waAqidapN mina Aln~aHori [ The winter is driven away, or is closed, by seven dusty ( days ), our old woman's days of the month; and when her days come to an end, and Sinn and Sinnabr, with El-Webr, and with Ámir and his little brother Mu-temir, and Mo'allil, and with Mutfi-el-Jemr, pass, the winter goes away, retiring quickly, and a burning wind ( riyHN being understood) comes to thee from the first day of the ensuing month, or, accord. to a reading which I find in one copy of the S, from the sea, mina AlbaHori ]. (S, O, TA.)

sourceDefinition: [act. part. n. of 4, q. v.]. ― -b2- The words of the Kur [xxix. 21] wamaA A^anotumo bimuEojiziyna fiY A@loA^aroDi walaA fiY A@ls~amaA='i signify, accord. to Fr, And ye shall not escape in the earth, nor shall those in the heaven escape: or, accord. to Aboo-Is-hák, and ye shall not escape in the earth, nor should ye if ye were in the heaven: or, accord. to Akh, and ye shall not escape by fleeing in the earth nor in the heaven: but Az says that the explanation of Fr is the best known. (L.) ― -b3- ↓ muEojizapN [ A miracle performed by a prophet; distinguished from karaAmapN , which signifies one performed by a saint, or righteous man, not claiming to be a prophet;] that by which a prophet disables the opponent in a contest; the p implying intensiveness; (K;) as defined by the Muslim theologians, an event at variance with the usual course [ of nature ], produced by means of one who lays claim to the office of a prophet, in contending with those who disacknowledge [ his claim ], in such a manner as renders them unable to produce the like thereof; (O;) or an event breaking through, or infringing, the usual course [ of nature ] ( A^amorN xaAriqN liloEaAdapi ), inviting to good and happiness, coupled with a claim to the prophetic office, and intended to manifest the veracity of him who claims to be an apostle of God: (KT:) pl. muEojizaAtN . (S, O, TA.)

(TA.) ― -b4- See also 1, last sentence.

sourceDefinition: , [mentioned in the first sentence of this art. as an inf. n.,] (S, Mgh, Msb, K,) when used as [a simple subst.] denoting a quality of a boy, or child, (S, Mgh,) or of a man, (K,) signifies Evilness of disposition, or illnature, and exceeding perverseness or crossness or repugnance; (S, Msb, K;) and vehemence, and strength; (Mgh, * TA;) and sharpness; (Msb;) and annoyance, or molestation: (K:) [and] the quality of quitting the right course, and exorbitance. (Ham p. 277.) ― -b2- Hence, in a trad. of 'Omar, metaphorically used as meaning (assumed tropical:) Sharpness and strength of [the beverage termed] nabiy* made of raisins. (Mgh.) ― -b3- And Numerousness of an army, (S, K,) and sharpness, and vehemence, thereof. (K.) ― -b4- Also Ignorance. (Fr, TA.) -A2- And The EuraAq [app. meaning flesh-meat ] of a bone: and likewise [i. e., app., portions that are cropped by camels] of trees. (S, K. [See EuraAqN , voce EaroqN .]) One says mino ↓ A^aEoramu kalobK EalaY EuraAmK [ More evil in disposition than a dog over a piece of flesh-meat of a bone ]. (TA.) Or, accord. to Az, AlEuraAmu signifies, (TA,) or it signifies also, (K,) What falls of the bark of the [ thorn-tree called ] Eawosaj : (K, TA:) but others explain it in a general manner, saying that EuraAmu Al$~ajarapi signifies the bark of the tree. (TA.) ― -b2- See also EaromN .

(S, A, O, Msb, K, * TA.) You say, Easura Ealayohi , (TA,) and Easira , (S, O,) and ↓ tEs~r , and ↓ tEAsr , and ↓ AstEsr , (K,) It was, or became, difficult, hard, strait, or intricate, to him. (S, * O, * K.) ― -b2- Easura maA fiY AlbaToni , (as in the CK and a MS. copy of the K,) or Easara , (accord. to the TA,) What was in the belly would not come forth. (K.) You say Easara Ealayohi maA fiY AlbaToni What was in his belly would not come forth. (TA.) ― -b3- See also 4. ― -b4- Easura , (Msb,) or Easara , (IKtt, TA,) or Easira , (TK,) inf. n. EusorN and EasaArapN (Msb, IKtt, TA) and EasarN , (IKtt, K,) He (a man) had little gentleness, (Msb, IKtt,) fiY AlA^umuwri [ in the execucution of affairs ]; (Msb;) and was narrow, or niggardly, in disposition: (IKtt:) or he was hard in disposition; or illnatured. (K, * TK.) ― -b5- Easura Ealayohi , (A, and so in the CK and a MS. copy of the K,) or Easara , (as in the TA,) inf. n. (Sb, O, * TA.) ― -b6- Easura Alz~amaAnu , (so in the CK and in a MS. copy of the K,) or Easara , (so in the TA,) Time, or fortune, became severe, rigorous, afflictive, or adverse, (K,) EalayonaA to us. (TA. ― -b7- Easurati Aln~aAqapu and Easirat The she-camel was untrained. (O.) ― -b8- And Easarato , (K, TA,) and Easarato bi*anabihaA , (S, O, TA,) aor. , inf. n. EasaraAnN (S, O, K, TA) and EasorN , (O, K, TA,) She (a camel) raised her tail, after conception, to show the stallion that she was pregnant: (S, * O, TA:) and [as also, app., ↓ Es~rt , or Es~rt danabahaA , inf. n. taEosiyrN , (see nAqp EasiyrN , voce EasirN ,)] she (a camel) raised her tail in her running. (K, TA.) [In the former case, the action denotes repugnance to the stallion: in the latter, a degree of refractoriness: in both, difficulty.] -A2- Easara Algariyma , aor. and , (S, O, Msb, K,) inf. n. (TA.) ― -b2- Easarahu , (As, TA,) and ↓ AEtsrhu , (S, TA,) He forced, or compelled, him, against his wish; [ EalaY AlA^amori to do the thing; ] i. q. qasarahu , (As, TA,) and Aqtsrhu . (S, O, TA.) -A3- Easira , and Easirato , (TK,) or Easarato , (K, TA,) aor. , (TK,) inf. n. EasarN , (S, Mgh, O, Msb, K,) He, (a man, TK,) and she, (a woman, TK,) was left-handed. (S, Mgh, O, Msb, K.) ― -b2- EasaraniY , (O, L, and K, and so in a copy of the S,) aor. , (L,) or , (TA,) inf. n. EasorN ; (L, TA;) and ↓ Eas~araniY , (K,) or EasiraniY , (L and TA, and so in a copy of the S,) aor. ; (TA;) He came on my right side. (S, O, L, K, TA.)

definition: and ↓ EusurN (S, A, O, K) and ↓ EasarN (S, A, K) and ↓ maEosuwrN [respecting which, as well as some other words here mentioned, see below, in this paragraph, and see what is said of its contr.
sourceDefinition: and ↓ EusurN (S, A, O, K) and ↓ EasarN (S, A, K) and ↓ maEosuwrN [respecting which, as well as some other words here mentioned, see below, in this paragraph, and see what is said of its contr. mayosuwrN , voce yusorN ,] and ↓ EusorapN and ↓ maEosarapN and ↓ maEosurapN and ↓ EusoraY [all of which are app. inf. ns., of 1, q. v.,] (K) Difficulty; hardness; straitness; intricacy; contr. of yusorN . (S, A, O, K.) ― -b2- 'Eesà Ibn-'Omar observes that every noun of three letters of which the first is with damm and the second quiescent is pronounced by some of the Arabs with the second movent like the first; as EusorN and EusurN , and ruHomN and ruHumN , and HulomN and HulumN . (S, O.) ― -b3- It is said in the Kur [lxv. 7], sayajoEalu A@ll~`hu baEoda EusorK yusorFA [ God will give, after difficulty, ease ]. (O, TA.) And again, [xciv. 5 and 6,] faA_in~a maEa A@loEusori yusorFA maEa A@loEusori yusorFA [ And verily with difficulty shall be ease: verily with difficulty shall be ease ]: on reciting which, Ibn-Mes'ood said, lano yagoliba EusorN yusorayoni [ A difficulty will not predominate over twofold ease ], which, says Abu-l-'Abbás, is meant as an explanation of the words of the Kur immediately preceding it, agreeably with a rule mentioned by Fr [and applying to most cases, but not to all]: for AlEsr being mentioned, and then repeated with Al , the latter is known to be the same as the former; and ysrA being mentioned, and repeated without Al , the latter is known to be different from the former. (O, * TA.) ― -b4- It is also said, lawo daxala AlEusoru juHorFA ladaxala Alyusoru Ealayohi [ If difficulty were to enter a burrow in the ground, ease would enter upon it ]. (TA.) ― -b5- As to ↓ maEosuwrN , it is the contr. of mayosuwrN , and both are inf. ns.: (S, O:) or they are put in the places of EusorN and yusorN : (TA:) or accord. to Sb, they both are epithets; for he holds that there is no inf. n. of the measure mafoEuwlN ; and the saying daEohu A_ilaY mayosuwrihi waA_ilaY maEosuwrihi is expl. as signifying Leave thou him to a thing in which he experiences ease, and to a thing in which he experiences difficulty: and maEoquwlN is also expl. in like manner. (S, O.) [In like manner also,] fulaAnK ↓ balagotu maEosuwra [may be expl. as signifying I effected a thing in which such a one experienced difficulty; meaning I treated such a one with hardness, harshness, or illnature; being] said when thou hast not treated the person of whom thou speakest with gentleness, graciousness, courtesy, or civility. (O, TA.) You also say, [using mEswr and its contr. myswr as epithets,] ↓ xu*N mayosuwrahu wadaEN maEosuwrahu [ Take thou what is easy thereof, and leave thou what is difficult thereof ]. (A.) ― -b6- EusorN also signifies Poverty: (Msb:) and ↓ EusorapN , [ the same: or] littleness of possessions, of property, of wealth, or of power: (S, TA:) and ↓ maEosarapN and ↓ maEosurapN , [ the same: or] difficulty, and poverty; contr. of mayosarapN : (O, TA:) both inf. ns.: (O:) and ↓ EusoraY , [ the same: or] difficult things, affairs, or circumstances; (TA;) contr. of yusoraY : (S, O, TA:) and fem. of A^aEosaru , applied to a thing, or an affair, or a circumstance. (TA.) ― -b7- ↓ jayo$u AlEusorapi [ The army of difficulty ] is an appellation given to the army of Tabook; because they were summoned to go thither during the intense heat of summer, (O, K,) and in the season of the ripening of the fruit, (O, TA,) so that it was hard to them; (O, K;) and because the Prophet never warred before with so numerous an army, amounting to thirty thousand. (O, TA.) ― -b8- ↓ fasanuyas~iruhu liloEusoraY , in the Kur [xcii. 10], signifies, as some say, [ We will smooth his way ] to punishment, and a difficult case. (O, TA.)

definition: , (S, Mgh, O, Msb, K,) aor.
sourceDefinition: , (S, Mgh, O, Msb, K,) aor. , (O, K,) inf. n. EuTuwfN , (Mgh, Msb,) or EaTofN , (O, TA,) He, or it, (a man, S, O, or a thing, Msb,) inclined; (S, Mgh, O, Msb, K;) or bent: (MF, TA:) and ↓ AnETf also has the former meaning, (Mgh, Msb, * TA,) as in the saying AnETf naHowahu i. e. he, or it, inclined towards him, or it; (TA;) [or the latter meaning;] or it became inclined, (Msb,) or became bent, (S, * O, Msb, K,) or both, (TA,) as quasi-pass. of EaTafahu ; (S, O, Msb, TA;) and ↓ tET~f likewise has both of these meanings, as quasi-pass. of ET~fhu , or [signifies it became much inclined and bent, for] ET~f is with teshdeed to denote muchness. (TA.) ― -b2- Hence, (MF, TA,) EaTafa Ealayohi , (S, Mgh, MA, O, K,) [aor. as above,] inf. n. EaTofN ; (MA, MF, TA;) and Elyh ↓ tET~f ; (S, MA, O, K;) [and ↓ AnETf Elyh ;] (tropical:) He was, or became, favourably inclined towards him; or affectionate, or kind, to him; (MA, PS;) he regarded him, or treated him, with mercy or pity or compassion; (MA, Mgh;) because in mercy, or pity, or compassion, is an inclining towards its object; (Mgh;) i. q. A^a$ofaqa Ealayohi ; (S, O, K;) and waSalahu , and bar~ahu . (TA in explanation of the second.) And EaTafato EalaY waladihaA , aor. as above, inf. n. EaTofN , said of a she camel, (assumed tropical:) She became favourably inclined, or compassionate, towards her young one, and yielded her milk; (Msb;) and Ealayohi ↓ tET~ft [signifies the same, or she was made to incline to him, or to affect him ]. (M in art. rA^m , &c) ― -b3- EaTafa Ealayohi also signifies He turned, or returned, against him: (S:) or he charged, or made an assault or attack, upon him, [in battle,] and turned, or returned, against him: (O, K:) or he returned against him with that which he disliked, or hated: and to him with that which he desired. (L, referring to a verse of Aboo-Wejzeh Es-Saadee cited in art. Hyn , q. v.) ― -b4- And EaTafa , aor. as above, (TA,) inf. n. EaTofN , (K, TA,) signifies also He turned away, or back. (K, * TA.) ― -b5- And [hence,] EaTafa Eanohu signifies (tropical:) the contr. of EaTafa Ealayohi in the first of the senses assigned to this latter above [i. e. it signifies (tropical:) He was, or became, averse from him; or disaffected, or unkind, to him; or unmerciful, unpitying, or uncompassionate, to him ]. (MF, TA.) ― -b6- EuTuwfN and EaTofN [as intrans. inf. ns.] also signify A sheep's, or goat's, bending the neck, not by reason of an ailment. (TA.) ― -b7- And EaTofN [app. likewise as an intrans. inf. n.] also signifies The folding of the extremities of the skirt, of the facing, or outer side, upon, or against, the lining, or inner side. (TA.) -A2- EaTafahu , (Mgh, Msb, TA,) [aor. as above,] inf. n. EaTofN , (Mgh, Msb,) He inclined it; (Mgh, Msb, TA;) namely, a thing; (Msb, TA;) as also ↓ AstETfhu : (Mgh:) or he bent it, or doubled it, or folded it: (Msb:) or it signifies also he bent it: and ↓ ET~fhu likewise, inf. n. taEoTiyfN , has both of these meanings: (TA:) or this latter verb is with teshdeed to denote muchness [of the action], or multiplicity [of the objects]: (S, O, TA:) you say, EaTafotu AlEuwda (S) I bent [or inclined ] the stick, or piece of wood: (MA, PS:) and AlEiydaAna ↓ EaT~afotu [ I bent, or inclined, the sticks, or pieces of wood ]: (S, O:) and zaA^osa Alxa$abapi ↓ EaT~afotu [ I bent, or inclined, much, the head of the piece of wood ]. (TA.) One says of a she-gazelle, taEoTifu jiydahaA A_i*aA rabaDato [ She inclines, or bends, her neck when she lies down on her breast ]. (O, K.) And one says, EaTafa raA^osa baEiyrihi A_ilayohi He inclined, or bent, or turned aside, the head of his camel towards him; inf. n. EaTofN : (TA:) and naAqatahu ↓ AstETf He turned aside his she-camel ( EaTafahaA ) by pulling her nose-rein in order that she should incline her head. (Mgh.) And EaTafa AlwisaAdapa , (S, O, K,) aor. and inf. n. as above; (O;) and ↓ EaT~afahaA ; (K;) He bent, or doubled, or folded, the pillow, or cushion, (S, O, K,) when leaning with his elbow upon it. (O.) ― -b2- And [hence] one says, EaTafa A@ll~`hu biqalobi Als~uloTaAni EalY riEay~athi (assumed tropical:) God made the heart of the Sultán, or ruling power, to be favourably inclined towards his subjects; to regard them, or treat them, with mercy. (TA.) And EaTafatoka Ealayohimu Alr~aHimu (assumed tropical:) [ The feeling of relationship, or consanguinity, or the sympathy of blood, caused, or hath caused, thee to be favourably inclined towards them; &c.]. (Ham p. 765.) And EaTafa Aln~aAqapa EalaY waladihaA (assumed tropical:) [ He made the she-camel to incline to, or affect, her young one ]. (M in art. rA^m ; &c.: see also liqaAHN muEaT~afapN in this art.) And tuEoTafu EalaY Albaw~i (assumed tropical:) [ She (a camel) is made to incline to, or affect, the stuffed skin of a young unweaned camel in order that she may yield her milk, when her young one has died]. (S, O, [See EaTuwfN .]) ― -b3- And EaTafotuhu Eano HaAjatihi (assumed tropical:) I turned him away, or back, from his object of want. (Msb.) ― -b4- And EaTofu Almudomaji i. e. AlqidoHi means The turning round about, or shuffling, of the gaming-arrow. (S voce mudomajN : see a verse there cited.)

sourceDefinition: The side of a human being, from the head to the hip, or to the foot: (Mgh:) and the side of a thing: (Msb:) or the dual signifies the two sides of a man, from the part next the head to the hips: (S, O:) and the two sides of the neck of a man: (TA:) and the two sides of anything: (S, O, K:) as relating to a man, (TA,) or a thing. (Msb,) the pl. is A^aEoTaAfN , [properly a pl. of pane.,] (Msb, TA,) and, as relating to a man, EiTaAfN also, and EuTuwfN . (TA.) Hence the phrase, humo A^aloyanu EiTofFA [ They are more pliant, or pliable; properly as meaning flexible, supple, lithe, or limber; but app. here used tropically, as meaning compliant: compare lay~inu AljaAnibi ]. (Mgh.) And lay~inu AlA^aEoTaAfi [ Pliant, or pliable, &c.], applied to a horse: (En-Nadr, TA voce guwojN : [see also EaAjN , in art. Ewj :]) and ↓ saholu AlmaEoTifi [and ↓ AlmaEaATifi and AlA^aEoTaAfi , which signify the same,] so applied. (S and O and TA voce gawojN .) And [hence, also,] one says, vanaY Ean~iY EiTofahu [lit. He bent from me his side ], meaning he turned away from me. (S, O, K.) And jaA='a vaAniYa EiTofihi He came in an unstraitened, or an easy, or a pleasant and plentiful, state, or condition: (O, K:) or (K) vaAniYa EiTofihi in the Kur [xxii. 9] means (O) twisting, or bending, his neck: (O, K:) or (K) magnifying himself, or behaving proudly, and turning away (O, K) from El-Islám. (O.) And fulaAnN yanoZuru fiY EiTofayohi [lit. Such a one looks at his sides ], meaning, is self-conceited. (IDrd, O, K. *) ― -b2- Also The armpit (Az, O, K, TA) of a man: and his shoulder: pl. EuTuwfN . (Az, TA.) ― -b3- And The curved part of each of the two extremities of the bow; (O, K, TA;) the two being called its EiTofaAni . (TA.) One says, taEaw~aja Alqawosu fiY EiTofayohi , (O, TA,) in the copies of the K, taEar~aja Alfarasu fiY EiTofayohi , but the former is the right, (TA,) meaning [ The bow ] bent to the right and left [ in the two curved parts of its extremities ]. (O, K, TA.) ― -b4- One says also, tanaH~a Eano EiTofi AlT~ariyqi [i. e. Go thou aside from ] the beaten track of the road; as also ↓ EaTofihi : (IAar, O, K:) or ↓ EaTofN signifies a bending (Mgh, Msb) in a street (Mgh) or road, (Msb,) being an inf. n. used as a simple subst.; but the EiTof in a street [or road] is [ a bent part, being] of the measure fiEolN in the sense of the measure mafoEuwlN . (Mgh. [See similar instances voce *iboHN .])

sourceDefinition: A certain plant which twines upon trees and has no leaves nor branches, fed upon by the oxen [app. meaning the wild oxen,] (K, TA,) but injurious to them: (TA:) some of its Euruwq [app. here meaning root-like stalks] are taken, and twisted, and charmed [by some invocation or otherwise], and cast upon the woman that hates her husband, and she consequently loves him: (K, TA:) so they assert: (TA:) accord. to AA, ↓ EaTafN signifies one of the strange kinds of trees of the desert: (O, TA:) EaTafapN is the n. un. thereof. (TA.) See also EaTofapN .

sourceDefinition: The fruit of the [ trees called ] TaloH , which resembles the fresh bean, (S, O, K,) and upon which, when they come forth, the camels pasture: (S, O:) or the pods, or receptacles of the fruit, thereof: (TA:) [i. e.] the fruit of the TlH when it succeeds the baramap ; resembling the [ kidney-bean called ] luwbiyaA=' : (IAar, TA:) the n. un. is Eul~afapN : (S, O, K:) AHn says that this is like the great Syrian carob ( xar~uwabap [n. un. of xar~uwb q. v.]), except that it is bigger, and in it are grains like lupines, of a tawny colour, upon which the cattle pasturing at their pleasure feed, but which men eat not save in case of necessity: and the like thereof in size, of the fruit of the EiDaAh , is also termed Eul~afN : what is smaller than it, like the fruit of the salam and of the samur and of the EurofuT , is [properly] termed Hubolap : the Eul~af are long, and expanded, or extended: (O:) [it is also said that] Eul~afN signifies the fruit of the A^araAk . (Ham p. 196.)

definition: , inf. n. taEoniyqN , He went along and looked down upon it or came in sight of it; expl. by ma$aY waA^a$orafa . (O, K.) ― -b2- En~qt Als~aHaAbapu The cloud emerged from the main aggregate of the...
sourceDefinition: , inf. n. taEoniyqN , He went along and looked down upon it or came in sight of it; expl. by ma$aY waA^a$orafa . (O, K.) ― -b2- En~qt Als~aHaAbapu The cloud emerged from the main aggregate of the clouds, and was seen white by reason of the sun's shining upon it. (TA.) ― -b3- En~qit A@sotuhu His posteriors, or his anus, protruded; syn. xarajat . (O, K.) ― -b4- En~qt kawaAfiyru Aln~axoli The spathes of the palm-trees became long, (O, K,) but had not split open. (O.) ― -b5- En~qt Albusorapu The date that had begun to colour ripened nearly as far as the qimaE [or base ] thereof, (K, TA,) so that there remained of it around that part what was like the finger-ring. (TA.) -A2- En~qhu He took him by his neck, and squeezed his throat, or fauces. (O, * L, K. *) It is related in a trad., that the Prophet said to Umm-Selemeh, when a sheep, or goat, of a neighbour of her's had come in and taken a cake of bread from beneath a jar belonging to her, and she had taken it from between its jaws, maA kaAna yanobagiY laki A^ano tuEan~iqiyhaA i. e. [ It did not behoove thee ] that thou shouldst take hold of its neck and squeeze it: or the meaning is, that thou shouldst disappoint it; (O, K;) from En~qhu signifying he disappointed him; (K;) which is from AlEanaAqu : (O:) or, as some relate it, he said An tuEan~ikiyhaA , (O, K,) i. e., that thou shouldst distress it, and treat it roughly: (O:) and tuEan~ifiyahaA , with f , would be approvable if agreeing with a relation. (O, K. *) And it is also related in a trad., that he said to the women of 'Othmán Ibn-Madh'oon, when he died, Al$~ayoTaAni ↓ Aibokiyna waA_iy~aAkun~a wataEan~uqa , if correct, [meaning Weep ye, but beware ye of the Devil's seizing by the neck, and squeezing the throat, ] from En~qhu as first expl. above: but it is by some related otherwise, i. e. wanaEiyqa Al$yTAn . (L.)
