definition: , with fet-h to the second m , Strong in altercation, not weary of labouring or striving.
sourceDefinition: , with fet-h to the second m , Strong in altercation, not weary of labouring or striving. (S, K.) A'Obeyd cites the following verse: wajadotaniY A^alowaY baEiyda Almusotamaro A^aHomilu maA Hum~ilotu mino xayorK wa$aro [ Thou findest me very contentious, strong in altercation, not weary of labouring or striving, bearing what is imposed on me of good and evil ]. (S, T, A.) IB says, that this rejez is commonly ascribed to 'Amr Ibn-'Ás, but it is said to be quoted by him from Artáh Ibn-Suheiyeh: Sgh says, that it is ascribed to El-'Ajjáj, but is not his; and to En-Nejáshee El-Hárithee; and Aboo-Mohammad ElAarábee says, that it is by Musáwir Ibn-Hind. (TA.)

definition: Camels of Mahreh;
sourceDefinition: Camels of Mahreh; i. e. certain camels, so called in relation to Mahreh Ibn- Heydán, (T, S, Msb, K,) a tribe, (K,) or a great tribe, (TA,) or the father of a tribe of El-Yemen: (S:) or in relation to Mahreh, a district of 'Omán: (Msb:) they are excellent camels, that outstrip horses; and some add, that they are unequalled in quickness of running, understanding what is desired of them with the least training, and having names, by which being called, they answer quickly: (Msb:) [and hence, any such like camels; i. e. any excellent, fleet, camels: (see 4:) n. un. mahoriY~N :] pl. mahaAriY~u [which is irreg. like ZahaAriY~N ] (S, Msb, K) and mahaArK (S, K) and mahaAraY , (K, TA,) written in the L mahaAriY , (TA,) [and so in the CK,] or mahaAraA , the Y being changed into A , (Msb,) [but it generally retains the form of Y , though pronounced A .] See also Huw$iY~N .

definition: A woman dowered;
sourceDefinition: A woman dowered; to whom a dowry has been given; or for whom a dowry has been set apart. (Msb.) It is said in a proverb, kaA@lomamohuwrapi A_iHodaY xadamatayohaA [ Like her who has been dowered with one of her two anklets ]: (S, K:) or A^aHomaqu mina A@lomamohuwrapi A_iHodaY xadamatayohaA [ More stupid than she who has been dowered with one of her two anklets ]: (Mgh:) applied to him who has reached the utmost degree of stupidity: from the following case: (TA:) a stupid woman demanded of her husband her dowry, (K, TA,) when he paid her his first visit, and she said, I will not obey thee unless thou give me my dowry: (TA:) so he pulled off one of her two anklets (K, TA) from her foot, (TA,) and gave it to her, and she was content with it. (K, TA.) In like manner, a certain man gave to another property, and he married with it the daughter of the giver, and then reproached her for the dowry he had given her: so they said, kaA@lomamohuwrapi mino maAli A^abiyhaA [ Like her who has been dowered from the property of her father ]: (K, TA:) [a proverb] applied in relation to him who reproaches for that which is not his own. (TA.)

sourceDefinition: and ↓ AstnbHhu , He made him (a dog) to bark: (S, K:) Alkaloba ↓ AstnbH he excited, or induced, the dog to bark: said of man when, having lost his way, he imitates the bark of that animal, in order that a dog may hear him, and, imagining him to be a dog, may bark, and so guide him. definition: Coming to an end;
sourceDefinition: Coming to an end; coming to nought; perishing; passing away. (TA.) ― -b2- [ Complete: accomplished. ] ― -b3- A promise that has been fulfilled; as also ↓ najiyzN : (TA:) or that has come to pass, and is accomplished. (A, Mgh.) ― -b4- Present; ready; (S, Msb, K, TA;) as also ↓ najiyzN : (K:) and ↓ both, promptly, or quickly, done, or given. (TA.) You say, biEotuhu naAjizFA binaAjizK (S, A, Mgh, Msb) [ I sold it, or I sold to him, ] present, or ready, [merchandise,] for present, or ready, [money,] (TA,) like yadFA biyadK , (S, A, Mgh, Msb,) i. e., taEojiylFA bitaEojiylK . (S.) And laA yubaAEu gaAy^ibN binaAjizK , meaning, A debt to be paid at a future time shall not be sold for ready money. (Mgh.) And naAjizN binaAjizK is a proverb, [meaning Ready merchandise with ready money,] like yadN biyadK , and EaAjilN biEaAjilK . (TA.) It is said in a trad., biyEuwA HaADirFA binaAjizK [ Sell ye present merchandise for ready money ]. (S.) And a poet ('Abeed Ibn-El-Abras, TA, art. klA^ ,) says, waA_i*aA tubaA$iruka Alhumuw mu faA_in~ahaA kaAlK wanaAjizo (S, TA, ubi supra;) [ And when griefs attend thee, know that] they are, some, debts to be payed at future periods, and some, payments in ready money. (TA, ubi supra.) The saying [of 'Abd-Allah Ibn-'Ámir El-Kurashee, owner of a horse named Esh-Shamoos, (TA, art. $ms ,)] jaroYa Al$~amuwsi naAjizFA binaAjizi [app. meaning, Quickly as the running of EshShamoos; ready with ready, or prompt with prompt; ] is explained by IAar, as meaning, Thou hast given an evil recompense and I have recompensed thee in like manner: or, as he says in one place, this is said when one does a thing and thou dost the like thereof; he not being able to go beyond thee in word or in deed. (TA.) [Respecting this saying, Freytag says, in his Arab. Prov., i. 305, (where, for naAjizFA we find naAjizN ,) that it applies to him who is equal to the execution of the things which he undertakes, as well good as bad: and that jaraY is to be supplied before jaroYa .]

sourceDefinition: , (T, S, M, &c.,) aor. , (S, M, Msb,) inf. n. nadorN , (S,) or nuduwrN , (M, Msb, K,) [which latter is the more common, if not the only right, form,] It fell, (T, M, Msb, K,) or went, or came, out, or forth, from another thing, or from other things, (Msb,) or from amid a thing, (T,) or from the inside of a thing, (T, M, K,) or from among things, so as to be apparent, or standing out to view; (M, K;) it fell, and became apart, fell off, fell out, or went, or came, out, or forth, from the generality of things, or the general assemblage, main body, bulk, or common mass, to which it pertained, or from other things: (S, TA:) or, [in some cases,] simply, it fell, or dropped. (TA.) ― -b2- nadara mino qawomihi He went forth [ and became separated ] from his people. (Msb.) And nadara mino bayotihi He went forth from his house or tent. (A.) I heard one say to his wife, A^unoduriY [ Go thou forth and be separate: app. meaning, be thou divorced ]. (Z, in the A, immediately following what here immediately precedes.) ― -b3- nadara AlEaZomu , (A,) or nadara mino mawoDiEihi , (Msb,) The bone became dislocated or displaced. (A, Msb.) It is said of a man, in a trad., EaD~a yada A=xara fanadara vaniy~atahu [or, accord. to another relation, nadarato , meaning, He bit the arm, or hand, of another, and his central incisor dropped out ]. (TA.) ― -b4- nadara TaAy^irN Eano $ajarapK A bird dropped and alighted from a tree. (TA.) ― -b5- nadara naAdirN mina Aljabali A prominence projected, or jutted out, from the mountain. (A.) ― -b6- A^aSaAba AlmaTaru AlHa$iy$a fanadara Alr~uTobu The rain fell upon the dry herbage and the fresh herbage came forth. (A.) And nadara Aln~abaAtu The plant put forth its leaves (M, K) from its uppermost branches. (M.) And nadarati Al$~ajarapu The tree produced its xuwSap [q. v.]; (M, K;) which is the case when the camels are able to pasture upon them: (M:) or became green. (Sgh, K.) ― -b7- nadara fiY EilomK , or faDolK , (IKtt,) and fY faDolihi , (Msb,) (tropical:) He outwent others [or became extraordinary ] (IKtt, Msb) in knowledge or science, or in excellence, (IKtt,) and in his excellence. (Msb.) ― -b8- nadura AlkalaAmu , (tropical:) inf. n. nadaraApN , (Msb, TA,) (tropical:) The speech, or language, was extraordinary or strange, [with respect to usage or analogy or both]: (TA:) it was the contr. of chaste: (Mz, 13th nwE :) [but this explanation requires restriction; for what is extraordinary with respect to usage is the contr. of chaste; but many a word that is extraordinary with respect to analogy is more chaste than a cognate word agreeable with analogy: hence the above phrase is also explained as signifying] the speech, or language, was chaste and good. (Msb.)

definition: [ They mutually threw out, or rejected, a thing from a reckoning ].
sourceDefinition: [ They mutually threw out, or rejected, a thing from a reckoning ]. A poet (namely Aboo-Kebeer El-Hudhálee, TA) says, waA_i*aA AlkumaApu tanaAdaruwA TaEona AlkulaY nadora AlbikaArapi fiY AljazaA='i AlmuDoEafi [ When the courageous men covered with arms mutually throw out from the reckoning the piercing of the kidneys, as the young camels fall out from the reckoning in the doubled compensation ]: he says, that their blood is suffered to be shed unrevenged, like as the young camels are thrown out from the account in the mulct for homicide: (S, TA:) meaning, that the pierced kidneys are thrown out from the reckoning, like as the young camel is thrown out, and not reckoned, in the mulct for homicide that is doubled time after time. (IB, TA.) ― -b2- fulaAnN yatanaAdaru EalayonaA (A, TA) (tropical:) Such a one comes to us [ rarely, or] sometimes. (TA.)

na$ara Alxabara , (S, A, K,) aor. and , (S, K,) inf. n. na$orN , (K,) (tropical:) He spread, or published, the news. (S, A, K.)

He sprinkled water. (A.)

(IAar, K.) ― -b7- na$ara Eanohu , (A, K,) inf. n. na$orN ; (A;) and Eanohu ↓ n$~r , (A, L, TA,) inf. n. tano$iyrN ; (S, A, L, TA;) and in like manner ↓ n$~rhu ; (S, TA;) (tropical:) He charmed away from him sickness, (S, * A, L, K, *) and diabolical possession, or madness, (L, K,) by a nu$orap , i. e., a charm, or an amulet; (S, A, L, K;) as though he dispersed it from him: (A:) and in like manner ↓ n$~rhu he wrote for him a nu$orap . (S.) -A2- na$ara , (El-Hasan, Zj, A, K.) aor. , (TA,) inf. n. na$orN and nu$uwrN ; (K, TA;) or ↓ A^ano$ara ; (I'Ab, Fr, S, A, Mgh, Msb;) or both; (A, K;) (tropical:) He (God, S, A, &c.) raised the dead to life; quickened them; revivified, or revived, them. (Zj, S, A, Mgh, Msb, K, &c.) I'Ab reads [in the Kur, ii. 261,] kayofa nuno$iruhaA [ How we will raise them to life ], and adduces in his favour the words [in the Kur. lxxx. 22,] ↓ vum~a A_i*aA $aA='a A^ano$arahu (tropical:) [ Then, when He pleaseth, He raiseth him to life ]: El-Hasan reads nano$uruhaA : [and others read nuno$izuhaA , with záy:] but Fr says, that El-Hasan holds it to refer to unfolding and folding, and that the proper way is to use An$r [in this sense,] transitively, and na$ara intransitively. (S, TA.) [See also TawaYa , which has the contr. meaning.] ― -b2- Hence, Alr~aDaAEu AlEaZoma ↓ A^ano$ara : i. q. A^ano$aza , with záy: (Msb:) or (tropical:) The sucking strengthened the bone. (Mgh.) -A3- na$ara , (S, A, Msb, K,) aor. , (S,) inf. n. nu$uwrN (S, A, Msb, TA) and na$orN , (Msb,) agreeably with what Fr says, (S,) signifies (tropical:) He (a dead person) lived after death; came to life again; revived; (S, TA;) or lived; came to life; (A, Msb;) as also ↓ Ant$r . (A.) Hence yawomu Aln~u$uwri (tropical:) The day of resurrection. (S.) ― -b2- na$ara , (TA,) inf. n. na$orN , (K, TA,) (tropical:) It (herbage, or pasturage,) became green in consequence of rain in the end of summer after it had dried up. (TA.) ― -b3- (tropical:) It (a plant) began to grow forth in the ground. (K, * TA.) You say, maA A^aHosana na$orahaA (tropical:) How good is its first growth! (TA.) ― -b4- (assumed tropical:) It (a tree) put forth its leaves. (K.) ― -b5- (assumed tropical:) It (foliage) spread. (K.) ― -b6- na$arati AlA^aroDu , (S, A, K,) aor. , (TA,) inf. n. nu$uwrN , (K,) (tropical:) The land being rained upon in the end of summer, its herbage, or pasturage, became green after it had dried up: (S, TA:) or the land, being watered by the rain called Alr~abiyE , put forth its herbage. (A, K.) See na$orN . -A4- na$ara , (S, A, Msb,) aor. , (S,) inf. n. na$orN , (K,) (tropical:) [ He sawed wood;] he cut ( qaTaEa , S, or naHata , K) wood, (S, A, Msb, K,) with a mino$aAr . (S, A, Msb.)

definition: [quasi-pass. of 1,] It spread, expanded, or unfolded; it became spread, expanded, or unfolded; as also ↓ tn$~r : (K:) [or the latter, being quasi-pass. of 2, denotes muchness, &c.] ― -b2- Ant$rt...
sourceDefinition: [quasi-pass. of 1,] It spread, expanded, or unfolded; it became spread, expanded, or unfolded; as also ↓ tn$~r : (K:) [or the latter, being quasi-pass. of 2, denotes muchness, &c.] ― -b2- Ant$rt Aln~axolapu The branches of the palm-tree spread forth. (K.) [And Ant$rt AlA^agoSaAnu The branches spread forth: and the branches straggled. ] ― -b3- Ant$r Alxabaru (tropical:) The news spread, or became published, (S, A, K,) fiY Aln~aAsi among the people. (A.) ― -b4- And Ant$rt Alr~aAy^iHapu (assumed tropical:) [ The odour spread, or diffused itself. ] (K in art. fwH ; &c.) ― -b5- Ant$r Aln~ahaAru (assumed tropical:) The day became long and extended: (K:) and so one says of other things. (TA.) ― -b6- Ant$r AlEaSabu (assumed tropical:) The sinews, or tendons, became inflated, or swollen, (K,) by reason of fatigue: (TA:) A_inoti$aArN is a state of inflation, or swelling, in the sinews, or tendons, of a beast, occasioned by fatigue: (S:) AO says, that the sinew, or tendon, which becomes inflated, or swollen, is the EujaAyap , (S, * TA,) and that what is termed taHar~uku Al$~aZaY is similar to this affection, excepting in its not being so well endured by the horse: by another, or others, it is said, that Ant$Ar of the sinews, or tendons, of a beast, in his fore leg, is a breaking, and consequent displacement, of those sinews. (TA.) ― -b7- Ant$r *akarohu (assumed tropical:) His penis became erect. (TA.) [And hence,] Ant$r Alr~ajulu (tropical:) The man became excited by lust. (S, K.) ― -b8- Ant$r AlmaA='u [In my copy of the A, Astn$r , but this I regard as a mistranscription,] The water became sprinkled; as also ↓ tn$~r : (A:) [or the latter signifies it became much sprinkled. ] ― -b9- Ant$rwA fY AlA^aroDi They became scattered, or dispersed, or they scattered, or dispersed, themselves, in the land, or earth. (A.) ― -b10- Ant$rt Alganama , (Msb, TA,) and AlA_ibilu , (K, TA,) The sheep or goats [and the camels ] became scattered, or dispersed, after having been confined in their nightly resting-place: (Msb:) or the sheep or goats (TA) and the camels (K, TA) became scattered, or dispersed, through negligence of their pastor. (K, TA.) ― -b11- Ant$r AlA^amoru (assumed tropical:) The state of things, or affairs, became dissolved, broken up, decomposed, disorganized, or unsettled; syn. ta$~atata . (TA, art. $t .) -A2- See also 1, latter part of the paragraph. ― -b2- Ant$r also signifies He put himself in motion, and went on a journey. (TA, in art. bsr .) ― -b3- Ant$r Al*~iy^bu fiY Alganami The wolf made an incursion among the sheep or goats. (TA in art. $E .)

(ADk, A, K.) -A2- (tropical:) Herbage, or pasturage, which has dried up and then become green in consequence of rain in the end of summer or spring (see below, and see simaAkN ): (S, K:) it is bad for the pasturing animals when it first appears, and men flee from it with their camels &c.; (S, TA;) which it affects with the [ disease called ] suhaAm when they pasture upon it at its first appearance: [see remarks on a verse cited in art. byD , voce baADa : and see another verse in art. jrb , voce A^ajorabu :] AHn says, that it does not injure animals with the solid hoof; or if it do so, they leave it until it dries, and then its evil quality departs from it: it consists of leguminous plants and of [ the herbage termed ] Eu$ob ; or, as some say, of the latter only: (TA:) [an ex. of the word is cited in art. jrb , voce A^ajarobu :] or herbage, or pasturage, of which the upper part dries up and the lower part is moist and green: (Lth:) or herbage produced by the rain called Alr~abiyE : (A:) and what has come forth, of plants, or herbage. (TA.) -A3- Life. (K.)

definition: is of the measure faEalN in the sense of the measure mafoEuwlN , (Msb, TA,) syn.
sourceDefinition: is of the measure faEalN in the sense of the measure mafoEuwlN , (Msb, TA,) syn. with mano$uwrN , like as qabaDN is with maqobuwDN , (Mgh,) and syn. with munota$irN , (S, Msb, K,) [therefore signifying Spread, expanded, or unfolded: scattered, or dispersed, &c.: and spreading, or being spread, &c.: being scattered, &c.:] and a thing that one has spread, expanded, or unfolded: &c. (O, voce sabalN , q. v.) ― -b2- You say AikotasaY AlbaAziY riy$FA na$arFA The hawk, or falcon, became clad in spreading and long feathers. (S, TA.) ― -b3- And hence na$arN is applied to People in a scattered, or dispersed, state, not collected under one head, or chief; (Msb, K;) as also ↓ na$orN : (K:) and to sheep or goats in a scattered, or dispersed, state, after having been confined in their nightly resting-place: (Msb:) or sheep or goats, and camels, in a scattered, or dispersed, state, through the negligence of their pastor. (TA.) You say, raA^ayotu Alqawoma na$arFA I saw the people in a scattered, or dispersed, state. (S.) And jaA='a Alqawomu na$arFA The people came in a scattered, or dispersed, state. (TA.) ― -b4- Hence also, na$aru AlmaA=' What is sprinkled, of water, (Mgh, TA,) in the performance of the ablution termed AlwuDuwo' . (TA.) It is said in a trad., A^atamoliku na$ara AlmaA='i [ Dost thou possess what is sprinkled of water? ] (S;) or mano yamoliku na$ara AlmaA='i [ Who possesseth what is sprinkled of water? ] (Mgh;) [app. meaning, that it is gone and cannot be recovered.] ― -b5- And hence, A^all~`hum~a A@Domumo na$ariY (assumed tropical:) O God, compose what is discomposed, or disorganized, of my affairs: (K, * TA:) a phrase like lum~a $aEaviY . (TA.) 'Áïsheh says, in a trad., describing her father, farad~a na$ara AlA_isolaAmi EalaY gar~ihi , meaning, (assumed tropical:) And he restored what was discomposed, or disorganized, [lit., what was unfolded,] of El-Islám, to its state in which it was in the time of the Apostle of God, [lit. to its fold, or plait;] alluding to cases of apostacy, and her father's sufficiency to treat them. (TA.) -A2- See also naA$irN .

sourceDefinition: A distortion in a camel's elbow, so that it lacerates his side: (El-'Adebbes El-Kinánee, S, K:) or the cutting of a camel's side by his elbow: (L:) or [ that fault in a camel ] when his elbow makes a mark, or marks, upon his side: in this case you say, bihi nAktN : but when it makes an incision, or incisions, in his side, you say bihi HaAz~N : (IAar) or nAkt is similar to naAHizN , i. e. the elbow's striking, and making a mark, or marks, upon the edge of the callous lump beneath his breast; in the case of which you say bh nAkt : (Lth:) and nearly the same is said in the A. (TA.)

sourceDefinition: , aor. yanuw$u , (S, A, Msb,) inf. n. nawo$N , (S, A, Msb, K,) He took it, or reached it, absolutely, or with the hand, or with the extended hand; (S, A, Msb, K;) as also ↓ tnAw$hu , (A, TA,) inf. n. tanaAwu$N ; (S, Mgh, Msb, K;) and ↓ AntA$hu , (A, TA,) inf. n. A_inotiyaA$N : (S, K:) it is also written with ' ; (A, K, TA, in art. nA^$ ;) and so is tanaAwu$N . (Msb, and K in art. nA^$ .) And He took him, or reached him, to seize his beard, or his head. (ISk, S.) You say, naA$ahu nawo$apF xafiyfapF [ He reached him with a feeble, or slight reach, with his spear or the like]. (A.) And Alr~imaAHu tanuw$uhu The spears reach him: occurring in a poem of Dureyd Ibn-Es-Simmeh. (TA.) And AlZ~ibaA='u tanuw$u AlA^araAka [ The antelopes reach and take with their mouths of the trees called ArAk ]; as also ↓ tanotaA$uhu . (A.) And Aln~aAqapu tanuw$u bifiyahA AlHawoDa [ The she-camel reaches and takes with her mouth of the water of the drinking-trough ]. (TA.) A poet says, (ISk, S,) namely, Gheylán Ibn- Horeyth Er-Raba'ee, (TA,) fahoYa tanuw$u AlHawoDa nawo$FA mino EalaA nawo$FA bihi taqoTaEu A^ajowaAza AlofalaA And she reaches and takes of the drinking-trough, from above it, a copious draught by means of which she traverses [ the middles of the ] waterless deserts without needing other water. (S.) You say also, nu$otu mina AlT~aEaAmi $ayoy^FA I obtained somewhat of the food. (TA.) And AlwaSiy~apu nawo$N mina AlmaEoruwfi [ The testament is a means of an attaining of benefit ]: i. e., the testator gives [for yatanaAwalu in my original I read yunaAwilu ] to the legatee without diminishing his property [during his own life]. (TA.) And it is said in the Kur, [xxxiv. 51,] mino makaAnK baEiydK ↓ waA^an~aY lahumu A@lt~anaAwu$u meaning, [ But how shall ] the attaining of belief [ be possible to them from a distant place, i. e.,] in the world to come, when they have disbelieved in him [namely Mohammad] in the present world? in which passage some read [ Alt~anaAw^u$u ,] with ' . (S.) [See art. nA^$ .] Accord. to Ibn-'Abbád, in this instance, ↓ AltnAw$ signifies Returning. (K, * TA.) And 'Áïsheh said of her father, Ald~iyna binaEo$ihi A_iy~aAhu ↓ faA@notaA$a And he restored the religion, and laid hold upon it and took it from the abyss into which it had fallen; [ by his exalting it; ] in which instance, also, the verb is sometimes pronounced with ' . (TA.) ― -b2- naA$a bihi , aor. as above, He clung, or clave, to him, or it. (TA.) -A2- nu$otuhu xayorFA , (Lth, S,) inf. n. nawo$N , (Lth,) I made him to attain good; (Lth, S;) and $ar~FA evil. (Lth.)

sourceDefinition: and ↓ hiydN and haAdN (S, L, K) and hayodK and hiydi and haAdi (IB, L) and hiydo (L) Cries by which camels are chidden (S, L, K) and urged. (L.) ― -b2- Also hayodN A mode of singing to camels, to urge or excite them: (L:) or the commencement of such singing: (TA:) when a man is about to sing to camels for this purpose, he says hydo hydo , and then sings, or prolongs and modulates his voice. (L, TA.) ― -b3- hayoda maA laka , (T, L, K,) and hiyda mAlk , (Sh, L,) and hiydo mAlk , (L,) [ What is thy state, or condition, or thy affair, or business? ] forms of speech used in inquiring of a man respecting his state, or condition, or his affair, or business; (T, L, K;) like as you say yaA h`*aA maA laka . (T, L.) One says, laqiyahu faqaAla lahu hayoda maA laka [ He met him, and said to him, What is thy state, &c.? ] and laqiytuhu famaA qaAla liY hayoda maA laka [ I met him, and he said not to me, What is thy state, &c.? ] (Lh, L,) and yaA hayoda maA liA^SoHaAbiki , and yaA hayoda maA A^aSoHaAbuka , [ What is the state, &c., of thy companions? ] (Ks, L,) and one says, lawo $atamotaniY maA qulotu hayoda , maAlaka , meaning, [ Hadst thou reviled me, or shouldst thou revile me, I had not said, or would not say, ] What is thine affair? (As, on the authority of 'Eesà Ibn-'Omar.) When a straycamel passes by a man, and he does not turn him aside, nor does he regard it, you say, mar~a baEiyrN famaA qaAla lahu hayoda maA laka , and, as related by an Arab of the desert, hayodi mA lk , with kesr to the d , [ A camel passed by, and he said not to him, What is thy state, &c.? ] (AZ, L.) ― -b4- ↓ maA lahu hayodN walaA haAdN He has no motion: (L, K:) or neither hyd nor hAd is to be said to him; meaning, he is not to be moved, nor withheld from a thing, nor chidden away from it. (S, L.) -A2- hayodN i. q. hayodabN A flabby pubes. (Fr, in TA, voce kaEotabN .)

sourceDefinition: , aor. yatiruhu , inf. n. watorN ; (Msb;) and ↓ Awtrhu ; (S, Msb, K;) He made it, (a number, Msb,) sole; or one, and no more: syn. A^afa*~ahu , (S, K,) or A^aforadahu . (Msb.) It is said that the latter verb only is used in relation to a number; but both are said to be thus used in the M [as well as in the Msb.] (TA.) ― -b2- [And He made it to be an odd number. ] You say, watara Alqawoma , (M, K,) aor. , inf. n. watorN ; (M;) and ↓ A^awotarahumo ; (M, K;) He made the people, they being an even number, to be an odd number. (M, K, TA.) 'Atà says, kaAna Alqawomu witorFA fa$afaEotuhumo wakaAnuwA $afoEFA fawatarotuhumo [ The people were an odd number and I made them an even number, and they were an even number and I made them an odd number ]. (TA.) You say also, watara AlS~alaApa , (Msb, K,) and ↓ A^awotarahaA , (T, S, Msb, K,) and ↓ wat~arahaA , (K,) and fiYAlS~alaApi ↓ A^awotara , (Lh, M,) He made the prayer to be such as is termed witor [i. e., to consist of an odd number of rek'as; as is done in the case of a prayer which is performed in the night, consisting of three rek'ahs, and particularly called SalaApu Alwitori ]; (S, * Msb, K; *) he performed prayers of double rek'ahs, two and two together, and then performed the prayer of one rek'ah at the end, making what he performed an odd number: (T:) and ↓ A^awotara , alone, signifies he performed the prayer called Alwitor [explained above]; (T, M, A, Mgh, K;) or he performed prayers of [ an odd number of rek'ahs, ] two and two together, and then a single rek'ah at the end. (TA.) It is said in a trad. A_in~a A@ll~`ha witorN yuHib~u Alwitora faA^awotiruwA yaA A^ahola A@loquroA=ni [ Verily God is one only: He loveth the odd number: therefore perform ye the prayer of an odd number of rek'ahs, O people of the Kur-án ]. (T.) And in another trad., A_i*aA A@sotajomarota faA^awotiro When thou employest stones in the purification termed A_isotinojaA=' , use an odd number; (TA;) i. e. use three stones for that purpose, or five, or seven, and not an even number. (T.) -A2- watarahu , (T, S, A, Mgh,) aor. yatiruhu , inf. n. watorN (S,) and witorN and tirapN , (T, S,) He slew his relation, and so separated him from him, and rendered him solitary: (A, Mgh:) or he slew a person belonging to him, or related to him, without the latter's obtaining revenge, or retaliation, for the blood of the slain: (S:) or he slew a person belonging to him, or related to him; or took property belonging to him. (T.) It is also doubly trans.: you say, watara fulaAnN fulaAnFA A^aholahu Such a one committed a crime against such a one by slaying his family; or by taking them away: (T:) and watarapu maAlahu (T, M, K) (assumed tropical:) he committed a crime against him by taking away his property: (T:) or (assumed tropical:) he made him to suffer loss or detriment in respect of his property; or he deprived him of it in part, or altogether; syn. naqaSahu A_iy~aAhu : (T, * M, K:) and watarahu Haq~ahu , (S, A, Mgh, Msb,) aor. as above, (Msb,) (tropical:) he made him to suffer loss or detriment in respect of his right or due; or he abridged him, or deprived him, or defrauded him, of it partially, or wholly; syn. nqShu . (S, Mgh, Msb.) It is said in a trad., mano faAtatohu SalaApu AlEaSori fakaA^an~amaA wutira A^aholahu wamaAlahu (T, M, * Msb, * TA) By whomsoever the prayer of the afternoon passeth unobserved, he is as though he had his family slain and his property taken away: or as though he had his family and his property taken away: (T:) or as though he were deprived ( nuqiSa ) of his family and his property, (T, M, Msb, TA,) and remained alone: (T, TA:) the loss of the family and property is thus likened to the loss of the recompense: Ahlh and mAlh being in the accus. case as objective complements: (Msb:) Ahlh is a second objective complement: for the first is understood, as implied in the verb: but if we read A^aholuhu wamaAluhu , accord. to another relation, Ahlh supplies the place of the agent, nothing being understood, and the family and property are the objects to which the loss is made to relate. (TA.) And it is said in another trad., mano jalasa majolisFA lamo ya*okuri A@ll~`ha fiyhi kaAna Ealayohi tirapF (assumed tropical:) He who sitteth in an assembly in which God is not mentioned is obnoxious to detriment, or loss: or, as some say, to a claim of reparation for wrongful conduct. (TA.) And it is said in the Kur, [xlvii. 37,] walana yatirakumo A^aEomaAlakumo (assumed tropical:) And He will not deprive you of aught of the recompence of your deeds: (Zj, T:) or will not make you to suffer loss in respect of your deeds; like as you say daxalotu Albayota , meaning daxalotu fiY Albayoti . (S.) ― -b2- [Also,] watarahu , (M, K,) aor. yatiruhu , (K,) inf. n. watorN (M, K) and witorN (TA) and tirapN , (M, K,) He executed blood-revenge upon him: or did so wrongfully: (M, * K, * TK:) expl. by A^aSaAbahu bi*aHolK . (TK.) ― -b3- He overtook him ( A^adorakahu ) with some displeasing, or abominable, or evil, action. (M, K.) ― -b4- He frightened him; terrified him. (Fr, K.) -A3- watara Alqawosa : see 2, in two places.

sourceDefinition: , (A, and so in some copies of the K,) or ↓ A^awotara , (M, and so in some copies of the K,) and byn kutubihi , (M,) and wAtr A^axobaArahu , (M, K; in the latter of which waAtarahu is put by mistake for waAtarahaA , as is observed in the TA,) and kutubahu , (M, A, K,) inf. n. muwaAtarapN (S, M, K,) and witaArN , (M, K,) He made his tidings, or narrations, and his writings, or letters, to follow one another: (M, A, K:) or with some intervals between them; for mwAtrp between things is only when there is some interval between them; otherwise it is mudaArakapN and muwaASalapN : (S, K:) or wAtr Alkutuba signifies he made the writings, or letters, to follow one another nearly, one by one, without ceasing: (S:) or he made them to follow one another with a small interval between every two: (T:) and waAtr Alxabara he made the tidings, or narration, to follow one part after another: or, accord. to As, with a small space between every two portions thereof: from witorN in the sense of farodN . definition: A man coming to a king, (A,) or governor, (S, A,) [or great man, ] as an ambassador, or envoy, or messenger;
sourceDefinition: A man coming to a king, (A,) or governor, (S, A,) [or great man, ] as an ambassador, or envoy, or messenger; (S, A;) [or to convey gifts, and to ask aid, or assistance: See 1:] pl., (S, L,) or [rather] this first is a quasi-pl. n., (L,) ↓ wafodN (S, A, L, K) and wuf~adN (K) and wuf~aAdN ; (A, Msb;) and pl. of wafodN , A^awoqaAdN and wufuwdN : (S, L, Msb, K:) wafodN is also explained as signifying a party that assembles together and comes to a country or town: and a party that repairs to princes, or governors, to visit, and to ask aid, or assistance, or some benefit, &c.: (L:) and a party that comes to a king respecting an affair of conquest, or for congratulation, or the like: (Mgh:) and a company chosen to go forth for the purpose of having an interview with great men: (En-Nawawee:) and a company of riders: (Jel, xix. 88:) and a company riding and honoured: (Zj, in explanation of the same verse of the Kur-an:) but from the explanations in the K, and other lexicons, it seems to signify a party coming, whether walking or riding, chosen for the purpose of having an interview with great men, or not: the explanations of En-Nawawee and some others may be in accordance with general or conventional acceptations, and those of the rest may be proper, or literal. (TA.) ― -b2- waAfidN (tropical:) A camel, (S, A, K,) or bird, (A,) or bird of the kind called AlqaTaA , (K,) that precedes the others (S, A, K) in pace, and in coming to water. (A.) ― -b3- AlwaAfidaAni (in the poetry of ElAasha, S, L) (tropical:) The parts of the two cheeks which project when one chews, and which become depressed when one grows old. (S, A, L, K.) One says of a very old man, gaAba waAfidaAhu (tropical:) [ The middles of his cheeks have become depressed ]. (A.)

definition: a word like wayolN (S, K) and wayoHN and wayosN : these four words agree in form and meaning, and have no fifth;
sourceDefinition: a word like wayolN (S, K) and wayoHN and wayosN : these four words agree in form and meaning, and have no fifth; although some of the lexicologists differ, in holding that some of them relate to what is good, and others to the falling into destruction. Accord. to what is said by Z, in the Fáïk, wyb and wyH and wys denote compassion: but wyl is used in reviling, and imprecating destruction. (MF.) IKtt says, in the Tahdheeb el-Af'ál, that the invariable verbs are nine in number: niEoma and biy^osu and layosa and EasaY and the verb of wonder and wayoHa zayodK and wayobahu and wayolahu and wayosahu ; but that El-Mázinee asserts the last four to be inf. ns. (TA.) You say wayobaka , (S, K,) and wayobN laka , and wayobN lizayodK , and wayobFA lahu , and wayobK lahu , (K,) with the three different vowel-terminations, both in addressing a person and in speaking of one who is absent, (TA,) and wayobihi , and wayobi gayorihi , (K,) [and wayoba gayorika , (see below,)] and wayoba zayodK , (S, K,) and wayobi zayodK , (TA,) [and wayobu zayodK , (see below,)] and wayobi fulaAnN on the authority of IAar, (K,) who adds, except the bnw Asd , who, it appears, from his saying this, give fet-h to the b : (TA:) the meaning of all which is, May God make woe ( wyl ) to cleave to thee! [and ― -b2- to Zeyd! &c.: or Woe to thee! &c.: but see what is said above.] (S, K.) Dhu-l-Khirak Et-Tuhawee uses wyb in the sense of wyl , addressing to a wolf the ejaculation wayoba gayorika , [which is therefore the same in meaning as wayobaka ]: (TA:) but accord. to what is said by Z, in the Fáïk, wayobaka and wayobN laka &c. signify Mercy on thee! or the like. (MF.) When wyb is put in the acc. case, it is so put as an inf. n. (S.) This is the opinion generally obtaining: the opinion that wayoba is a verb is extraordinary. (TA.) When you use the prep. l , you [generally say] wayobN lizayodK (or wayobFA lizayodK , L): when you use l , it is more elegant to put wyb in the nom. case, as an inchoative, than in the acc. case: but when you use wyb as a prefixed noun, with its complement, the acc. is more elegant than the nom. case: [i. e., it is more elegant to say wayoba zayodK than wayobu zayodK ]. (S, L.) Ks says, Some of the Arabs say wayobaka and wayoba gayorika ; and some of them say wayobFA lizayodK , like wayolFA lizayodK . (TA.) ― -b3- wayobFA liha*aA AlA^amori (K, * TA) i. q. EajabFA lahu , [ I ] wonder at, or with respect to, this thing! (K,) and so wayobahu . (TA.)

definition: A measure consisting of twenty-two, or twenty-four, A^amodaAd (pl.
sourceDefinition: A measure consisting of twenty-two, or twenty-four, A^amodaAd (pl. of mud~N ), which see in art. mk . (K.) Not mentioned by J nor by IF; and IDrd doubted respecting it. In truth it is a post-classical word, used by the people of Syria and Egypt and Africa Proper. (TA.) [At present, the wybp in Cairo is the sixth part of an A_irodab~ , which latter is equivalent, very nearly, to five English bushels.]

sourceDefinition: , aor. yabosiru , [respecting the form of which see the same verb in a different sense below,] inf. n. yasorN and yasarN [and mayosuwrN (see yusorN below)], He was, or became, gentle, and tractable, submissive, manageable, or easy; (M, K;) said of a man, and of a horse: (M:) and yusira [app. signifies the same: and] is said of speech, and of a thing or an affair; signifying, [when relating to the former,] it was gentle, or [when relating to the latter,] easy; like suEida Alr~ajulu [as syn. with saEida ], and nuHisa [as syn. with naHisa ]. (Bd, xvii. 30.) See also tys~r . ― -b2- yasarato , said of a woman: see A^ayosarato -A2- yasura , aor. , It (a thing) was, or became, little in quantity: (A, Msb:) contemptible; paltry; of no weight or worth. (A.) -A3- yasaraniY , aor. yayosiruniY , (AHn, M, K,) inf. n. yasorN , (AHn, M,) He (a man, AHn, M) came on, or from the direction of, my left hand. (AHn, M, K.) See also 3. -A4- yasara , [aor. yayosiru , inf. n. yasorN ,] He divided anything into parts, or portions. (TA.) You say, yasarotu Aln~aAqapa I divided the flesh of the she-camel into parts or portions. (TA.) And yasaruwA Aljazuwra They slaughtered the she-camel and divided its limbs, (S,) or portions, (TA,) among themselves; (S, TA;) as also, accord. to Aboo-'Omar ElJarmee, ↓ A_it~asaruwhaA , aor. yat~asiruwnahaA , inf. n. A_it~isaArN ; and he adds that some people say, yaA^otasiruwnahaA , inf. n. A@notisaArN , with hemz; and humo muw^otasiruwna ; like as they say in the case of A_it~aEada . (S.) Soheym Ibn-Wetheel El-Yarboo'ee says, A^aquwlu lahumo biAl$~iEobi A_i*o yayosiruwnaniY A^alamo tayoy^asuwA A^an~iY A@bonu faArisi zahodami [ I say to them, in the ravine, when they divide me among themselves, deciding what shares they shall severally have in me, Know ye not that I am the son of the rider of Zahdam, and that ye may obtain a great ransom for me?] for capture had befallen him, and they played with [gaming-] arrows for him. (S, TA. [but in the latter, instead of tayoy^asuwA , we find taEolamuwA , which signifies the same.]) You say also, ↓ A_it~asaruwA , aor. yat~asiruwna and yaA^otasiruwna ; (K;) and ↓ tayAasaruwA ; (M, K;) They divided among themselves the slaughtered camel. (M, K.) ― -b2- [Hence,] yasara , aor. yayosiru , (S, M, A, Msb, K,) in the [second] Y is not suppressed as it is in yaEidu and its cöordinates [having w for the first radical], (S,) and yiysaru , like yiyjalu , in the dial. of the Benoo-Asad, (TA,) inf. n. yasorN , (M, TA,) or mayosirN , (A,) He played at the game called Almayosir ; (M, Msb, K;) he played with gamingarrows. (S, A, Msb.)

sourceDefinition: , (inf. n. tayosiyrN , M, &c.) He (God, A, Msb) made it, or rendered it, easy; facilitated it. (M, A, Mgh, Msb, K.) You say, yus~irato EalayohaA AlwilaAdapu The act of bringing forth was rendered easy to her. (A.) ― -b2- He made his circumstances ample; he made his condition, or his way or course [ lika*aA to such a thing ], easy, or smooth: (Sb, M:) he accommodated, adapted, or disposed, him, liloyusoraY [ to easy things, or affairs, or circumstances; or to the easier, or easiest, way ]: (S. A, [in the latter of which this is given as a proper, not tropical, signification:]) (tropical:) he prepared, or made ready, him or it, lika*aA for such a thing. (A [in which this signification is said to be tropical.]) tayosiyrN relates to both good and evil: (M, K:) as in the following instances in the Kur; [xcii. 7, 10;] fasanuyas~iruhu liloyusoraY , and liloEusoraY , (M,) [ We will facilitate, or smooth, his way, or] We will accommodate him, or adapt him, or dispose him, [ to a state of ease, and to a state of difficulty, or (as explained in the TA, art. Esr ,) to punishment, and a difficult case: ] (S, A:) or We will prepare him for paradise, and for hell: (Jel:) or We will prepare him to return to good, or righteous, conduct, [and to persevere in evil, or unrighteous, conduct; the former leading to ease, and the latter to difficulty:] (Fr, TA:) or We will prepare him for that habit of conduct which leads to ease, such as the entering paradise, and for that which leads to difficulty, such as the entering hell: from ys~r Alfarasa , meaning, he prepared the horse for riding, by saddling and bridling. (Bd.) It is said in a trad. waqado yus~ira lahu TahuwrN (assumed tropical:) And water for ablution had been prepared and put for him. (TA.) ― -b3- yas~ara Alr~ajulu , (inf. n. tayosiyrN , K,) The man's camels, and his sheep or goats, brought forth with ease, (IAar, M, K), and none of them perished. (IAar, M.) ― -b4- yas~arati Alganamu The sheep, or goats, abounded in milk, (S, M, A, K,) and in like manner, AlA_ibilu the camels, (M,) and [so in the S, M, A, but in the K or] in offspring: (S, M, A, K:) and they brought forth: and they were ready to bring forth: and they abounded. (TA.) A poet (namely Aboo-Useydeh Ed-Debeeree, TA) says, humaA say~idaAnaA yazoEumaAni wA_in~amaA yasuwdaAninaA A^ano yas~arato ganamaA humaA (S, M) They two are our two chiefs, as they assert; but they are only our chiefs inasmuch as their sheep, or goats, abound in milk and in offspring. (TA.) ― -b5- See also A^ayosarato .

sourceDefinition: , [inf. n. muyaAsarapN ] He was gentle towards him; acted gently towards him; treated him with gentleness; syn. laAyanahu : (M, A, K:) he was easy, or facile, with him; syn. saAhalahu . (S, K.) Ex., cited by Th, from a poem: A_ino yaAsarotahumo yasaruwA If thou treat them with gentleness, they become gently. (M.) And yaAsara Al$~ariyka He was easy, or facile, with the partner. (TA, from a trad.) -A2- yAsr , (inf. n. muyaAsarapN , K,) He took the left-hand side or direction; (S, M, A, Msb, K;) as also ↓ tyAsr ; (S, Msb, K;) which latter is the contr. of tyAmn : (K:) or ↓ tayaAsaruwA they took the lefthand side or direction; contr. of tayaAmanuwA . (A.) You say, yaAsiro biA^aSoHaAbika Take thou the left-hand side or direction with thy companions; (S, A;) as also tayaAsaro ; but some disapprove of this latter. (S.) definition: It (a thing, M, Msb) was, or became, facilitated, or easy;
sourceDefinition: It (a thing, M, Msb) was, or became, facilitated, or easy; (M, A, Msb, K, TA;) contr. of difficult, hard, strait, or intricate; (TA;) as also ↓ Astysr . (M, A, Msb, K.) You say, A^axa*onaA maA tayas~ara , and ↓ maA A@sotayosara , We took what was easy [ of obtainment, or of attainment ]. (TA.) And it is said in a trad., respecting the eleemosinary tax called wayajoEalu mEahaA $aAtayoni A_ini, zakaAp lahu A^awo Ei$ariyna dirohamFA ↓ A@sotayosarataA And he shall put with it, or them, two sheep, or goats, if they be easy to him [ to give ], or twenty dirhems. (TA.) And in the Kur, [ii. 192,] mina AlhadoYi ↓ famaA A@sotayosara What is easy [ to give ], of camels and kine and sheep or goats: or, as some say, either a camel or a cow or a sheep or goat. (TA, from a trad.) ― -b3- tayas~arati AlbilaAdu (tropical:) The countries became abundant in herbage, or in the goods, conveniences, or comforts, of life. (TA, from a trad.)

definition: (TA) and ↓ yasarN , (M, A, K, TA,) [each an inf.
sourceDefinition: (TA) and ↓ yasarN , (M, A, K, TA,) [each an inf. n. (see 1) used as an epithet,] and yaAsirN , (K, TA,) Easy and gentle in tractableness, submissiveness, or manageableness; applied to a man and to a horse: (TA:) or [simply] easy; facile; (M, A, K;) as also ↓ yusorN (TA) and yasiyrN , (Msb), this last being syn. with hay~inN , (S, K,) and signifying not difficult, gayoru EasiyrK , (A,) and ↓ mayosuwrN [respecting which see also EusorN , pl. mayaAsiyru ]. (A.) Hence, ↓ yasaraAtN , pl. of yasorapN and yasarapN , applied to the legs of a beast, signifies Easy: (M:) or light, or active, legs of a beast: (S, TA:) or light, or active, and obedient, legs of a beast of carriage: (A:) or the legs of a she-camel: and you say also, A_in~a qawaAy^ima h`*aA Alfarasi yasaraAtN xifaAfN , meaning, verily the legs of this horse are obedient and light or active. (TA.) [Hence also,] wilaAdapN yasorN [ An easy birth, or bringing forth ]. (A.) And waladato waladahaA yasorFA She brought forth her child easily: (M, K *:) said of a woman: (M:) or ↓ yasarFA . (CK.) And it is said in a trad., ↓ A_in~a h`*aA Ald~iyna yusorN Verily this religion is easy; liberal; one having little straitness. (TA.) You say also, ↓ xu*o mayosuwrahu wadaEo maEosuwrahu [ Take thou what is easy thereof, and leave thou what is difficult ]. (A.) And ↓ mayosuwrN is applied to a saying, or speech: (A:) so in the Kur. xvii. 30; meaning, gentle; (Bd, Jel;) easy: (Jel:) or ↓ quwolN mayosuwrN means prayer for mayosuwr , i. e., for yusor [q. v.]. (Bd.) ― -b2- fatolN yasorN [The twisting a rope or cord towards the left, by rolling it against the body from right to left; or] the twisting downwards, by extending the right hand towards the body [ and so rolling the rope or cord downwards against the body or thigh, which is the usual way of twisting]; (S, A *, K;) contr. of $azorN . (M, A, TA) ― -b3- TaEonN yasorN The thrusting, or piercing, [ straight forward; or] opposite the face: (S, M, K:) opposed to $azorN , which is from one's right and one's left. (TA.) See an ex. voce $azarahu .

sourceDefinition: [ Easiness; facility; ] contr. of EusorN ; (S, M, Mgh, Msb, K;) as also ↓ yusurN ; (S, Msb, TA;) [and ↓ yusoraY ; (see 3, where it is variously explained;)] and ↓ mayosuwrN is the contr. of maEosuwrN , [and therefore signifies as above; or easy; facile; ] (S;) or this last signifies, (accord. to the lexicologists, M,) what is made easy; or facilitated; or (accord. to Sb, M, [but see maEaquwlN ,]) it is an inf. n. of the measure mafoEuwlN , (M, K,) [used in the sense of yusorN as explained above,] of the same kind as [its contr.] maEosuwrN ; and Abu-l-Hasan says, that this is the truth; for it has no unaugmented verb, and inf. ns. of this measure are not of verbs which are in use, but only of imaginary unaugmented triliteral-radical verbs, as in the case of majoluwdN , which is [really] from tajal~ada . (M.) For examples of yusorN , see EusorN . ― -b2- Also, (accord. to the M; but in the K, or; and in both of these lexicons the signification here following is placed first;) and in like manner, ↓ yusurN , (K,) and ↓ yasaArN , (S, M, Mgh, Msb, K,) and ↓ yasaArapN , (S, K,) and ↓ mayosarapN , and ↓ mayosurapN , (S, M, K,) of which last Sb says that it is like masorubapN and ma$orubapN in not being after the manner of the verb, [but after that of the simple substantive,] (M,) and ↓ mayosirapN , (K.) Easiness [ of circumstances ]; (M, K;) competence, or sufficiency; or richness, or wealth, or opulence; (S, M, Mgh, Msb, K;) abundance; (Msb;) [in these senses, also, contr. of EusorN ;] and ↓ yusoraY signifies [ the same; or] easy things or affairs or circumstances; contr. of EusoraY ; as also ↓ mayosarapN . (TA, art. Esr .) You say also, ↓ A^anoZironiY Hat~aY yasaAri [ Grant thou me a delay until I shall be in a state of easiness of circumstances, &c.]; in which the last word is indecl., with kesr for its termination, because it is altered from the inf. n., which is Almayosarapu . (S.) In the Kur. [ii. 280,] some read, ↓ fanaZirapN A_ilaY mayosurihi [ Then let there be a postponement, or delay, until his being in a state of easiness of circumstances ]: but Akh says, that this is not allowable; for there is no noun of the measure mafoEulN [of this kind]: as to makorumN and maEuwnN , [it is said that] they are pls. [virtually though not in the language of the grammarians] of makorumapN and maEuwnapN . (S.) [On this point, see maA^olukN , voce A^aluwkN .] -A2- See also yasorN , in two places. -A3- Euwdu yusorK : see Euwdu A^usorK , in art. A^sr .

sourceDefinition: : see yasorN , first signification. -A2- [ Taking the left-hand side or direction: or coming on, or from the direction of, the left hand of a person:] contr. of yaAminN . (S.) -A3- [ Dividing a thing into parts, or portions. ] ― -b2- [Hence,] The slaughterer of a camel: (K, TA:) because he divides its flesh into portions: (TA:) the person who superintends the division of the slaughtered camel (M, K) for the game called Almayosir : (K:) pl. DariybN [which signifies the same; and the person who is entrusted, as deputy, with the disposal of the arrows in the game above mentioned, and who shuffles them in the ribaAbap :] and, [as quasi-pl. of yaAsirN , like as xadamN is of xaAdimN ,] a party assembled together at the game called Almayosir : (M, K:) pl. A^ayosaArN : (M:) and ↓ yasiyrN and ↓ yasuwrN signify one who contends with another at a game of hazard; syn. qaAmirN : (K:) or ↓ yasarN and ↓ yasuwrN , and also yaAsirN , are applied to one who has, or to whom pertains, a gamingarrow. (IAar, TA.)

definition: The game, or play, with unfeathered and headless arrows;
sourceDefinition: The game, or play, with unfeathered and headless arrows; (M, K;) the game of hazard which the Arabs play with such arrows; (S, Mgh, Msb;) a game of the Arabs, played [ by ten men, ] with ten unfeathered and headless arrows: they first slaughtered a camel, [bought on credit, (see below, in this paragraph,)] and divided it into ten portions, or, as some say, [agreeably with what follows,] into twenty-eight: the first arrow was called Alfa*~u , and had [one notch and] one portion of the slaughtered camel: the second, Alt~awo'amu , and had [two notches and] two portions: the third, Alr~aqiybu , and had [three notches and] three portions: the fourth, AlHilosu , and had [four notches and] four portions: the fifth, Aln~aAfisu , and had [five notches and] five portions; or, as some say, this was the fourth: the sixth, Almusobilu , and had [six notches and] six portions: the seventh, AlmuEal~aY , which was the highest of them, having [seven notches and] seven portions: the eighth and ninth and tenth were called Als~afiyHu and AlmaniyHu and Alwagodu ; and these three had no portions: [the players to whom these three fell had to pay for the slaughtered camel: (see Almusobilu :) whence it appears, that if the camel was divided into ten portions, (see rayomN ,) the game must have continued after all these were won, until it was seen whose were the eighth and ninth and tenth arrows; and it seems to be the general opinion that this was the case:] the camel being slaughtered, they collected together the ten arrows, and put them into the ribaAbap , a thing resembling a quiver ( kinaAnap ), and turned them round about or shuffled them ( A^ajaAluwhaA ): [or they employed a person, whom they called HuroDap , to do this:] then they put them into the hand of the judge ( AlHakam ), who took them forth one after another in the name of one after another of the party; [or they commissioned the HuroDah to do so;] and each took of the portions of the slaughtered camel according to his arrow; but those to whose lots fell the arrows without portions were obliged to pay the price of the slaughtered camel: with the flesh of which they afterwards fed the poor; and him who would not engage with them in the game they reproached, and called a baram : (Sefeenet Er-Rághib, printed at Boolák; p. 637:) [see also raqiybN , and DariybN , and Ea$orN :] or any game of hazard; or play for stakes, or wagers: (K:) so that even the game of children with walnuts is included under this name by Mujáhid in his explanation of verse 216 of chap. ii. of the Kur.: (TA:) or anything in which is risk, or hazard: (Kull, p. 321:) or the game of tricktrack, backgammon, or tables; syn. narodN : (Sgh, K:) and chess was called by 'Alee the mayosir of the Persians, or foreigners: (TA:) or the slaughtered camel for which they played: for when they desired to play, they bought on credit a camel for slaughter, and slaughtered it, and divided it into twentyeight portions, or ten portions; and when one [of the arrows] after another came forth [from the ribaAbap ] in the name of one man after another, the gain of him for whom came forth those to which belonged portions appeared, and the fine of him for whom came forth [any of the arrows called] the gufol : (K:) so called as though it were a place of division: and so used by the poet Lebeed, who speaks of a fat mayosir . (TA.)

sourceDefinition: : ― -b2- zayodN A^aEoqalu mino A^ano yako*ib means mina Al*~aiY yako*ibu (Kull, p. 78) [i. e. Zeyd is more reasonable than he who lies: but, though this is the virtual meaning, the proper explanation, accord. to modern usage, is, that A^ano is here for A^an~a with the adjunct pronoun hu ; for in a phrase of this kind, an adjunct pronoun is sometimes expressed; so that the aor. must be marfooa; and the literal meaning is, Zeyd is more reasonable than that he will lie; which is equivalent to saying, Zeyd is too reasonable to lie. It may be doubted, however, whether a phrase of this kind be of classical authority. The only other instance that I have found is huwa A^aHoSanu mino A^ano yoraAm waA^aEaz~u min A^ano yuDaAm , in the TA, voce A^alo . Accord. to modern usage, one may say, A^anota A^aEoqalu mino A^an~aka tafoEalu ka*aA , which virtually means Thou art too reasonable to do such a thing; and here we cannot substitute A@l~a*in for A^an~ . See A^ano for A^an~a .] ― -b3- A^axozaY A@ll~`hu AlkaA*iba min~iY waminoka : see A^aY~N ― -b4- laqiytu minohu A^asadFA : see A^asodN : and laqiytu ― -b5- minohu baHorFA ; and raA^ayotu minohu baHorFA : see bHr ― -b6- mino in the sense of Einoda : see jad~N ― -b7- jaraY minohu majoraY ka*aA : see 1 in art. jrY ― -b8- mino and Eano , differences between: see Eano ― -b9- mino often means Some. ― -b10- Often redundant: see 1 in art. EyD . ― -b11- Of, or among: see two exs. voce fiY , latter part. ― -b12- HusayonN min~iY waA^anaA minohu Hoseyn and I are as one thing, [as though each were a part of the other,] in respect of the love that is due to us, &c. (Commencement of a tradition in the Jámi' es-Sagheer: thus explained in the Expos. of El-Munáwee.) See Ham, p. 139; and De Sacy's Gr. i. 492. ― -b13- maA A^anaA mano dadK walaA Ald~adu min~iY : see art. dd . IbrD confirms my rendering of this saying. ― -b14- yataEar~aDu A_ilaY $aYo'K layosa minohu [ He applies himself to a thing not of his business to do ]. (TA, art. E$ .) ― -b15- layosa min~aA He is not of our dispositions, nor of our way, course, or manner, of acting, or the like. (TA, art. g$ .) ― -b16- layosa min~iY (Kur, ii. 250) He is not of my followers: (Bd, Jel:) or he is not at one, or in union, with me. (Bd. See 1 in art. TEm .) See a similar usage of mn , voce EiySN . ― -b17- A^anaA minohu kaHaAqini AlA_ihaAlapi : see HaAqinN ― -b18- mino is used in the sense of fY in the phrase mino yawomi AljumoEapi [ In, or on, the day of congregation ] in the Kur lxii. 9. (K, Jel.) So, too, in mino yawomihi In, or on, his, meaning, the same, day: and mino saAEatihi In, or at, his, meaning the same, instant of time. See also De Sacy's Gr., ii. 526.

sourceDefinition: , in grammar, [ A conjunct ]. This is of two kinds; mawoSuwlN HarofiY~N and mawoSuwlN A_isomiY~N . The former term [or conjunct particle ] is applied to the infinitive particles A^ano , A^an~a , kaY , lawo , and maA . The latter term [or conjunct noun ] (I have thus rendered it voce A^alo , and voce A_ino , and voce A_in~a ) is applied to the conjunctive nouns A^al~a*iY , and its fem. Aal~atiY , and mano , and maA , and *uw in the dial. of Teiyi, and to Aalo , which last some incorrectly hold to be a conjunct particle, and others assert to be a determinative particle and not a conjunct, and to *aA after the interrogative maA or mano . (I' Ak, sect. AlmawoSuwlu .)
